Then He described His punishment as severe, saying: God is severe in His punishment to those of His creation who punish Him, because it is a fire whose heat cannot be extinguished, whose embers cannot be extinguished, and whose flames cannot subside. We seek refuge in God from it and from an action that brings us closer to it.

evidence.text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Umaimah, he said, Ibn ʿUmar said about a man who performs Hajj and carries provisions with him, he said: There is nothing wrong with it, and he recited this verse: They seek bounty from their Lord and approval.

Some of the Kufians recited this, namely Yahya bin Waththab and Al-A’mash: what:

Abu Jaʿfar said: What is more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads it: And let him not commit a sin with the opening of the ya’, because of the prevalence of that reading in the readings of the regions, and the anomaly of what differs from it, and that it is the well-known language used by the Arabs, even though it is heard from some of them: ajram yajram according to its anomaly.

Some of them read it as shan’an by moving the sheen and the noon to the fatha, meaning: hatred of a people, directing that to the source that comes in the form of fa’laan, like flying, an-naslaan, aslaan, and ar-ramlaan.

Others read it as: shan’an qawm with a sukoon on the nun and a fatha on the shin meaning: the name, directing its meaning to: do not let the hatred of a people make you bear it, so shan’an is derived on the basis of fa’laan, because fa’l is derived from fa’l, just as it is said: sakran from sakara, and ‘athan from ‘atash, and similar names.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of those who read: Hanan qawm with the fat-ha on the nun, due to the common interpretation of the people of interpretation that its meaning is: hatred of a people, and their referring that to the meaning of the source rather than the meaning of the noun.

Since this was directed to the meaning of the source, the eloquent speech of the Arabs in what came from the sources is on the form of the verb fa’laan with the opening of the fa’, moving the second without making it silent, as described in their saying: darajan and ramlaan, from daraj and ramal, so also hatred from shun’atu ashuhu shanan, and some of the Arabs say: shan’an with the estimation of fa’al, and I do not know of a reader who read it in this way, and from that is the saying of the poet: Life is nothing but what you enjoy and desire, even if the one who has hatred and resentment criticizes it.
Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.

Some of the people of Medina and most of the Kufians read it as: that they prevented you with the opening of the alif of that, meaning: Do not let the hatred of a people for preventing you from entering the Sacred Mosque cause you to transgress.

Some of the readers of Hijaz and Basra used to read it Surat al-Ma’idah 5:2 O you who have believed, do not violate the symbols of God or the sacred month or the offerings or the garlands or those coming to the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and approval.
They claimed that in Ibn Masoud’s reading it was: If they turn you away, so they read it like that, taking into consideration his reading.

Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings that are famous in the readings of the regions, and the meaning of each one of them is correct.

So whoever reads that they prevented you with the opening of the alif of that, its meaning is: Do not let the hatred of a people, O people, because they prevented you on the day of Hudaybiyyah from the Sacred Mosque, lead you to transgress against them.

So God proceeded to the believers - according to the one who read it with a kasra on that - by forbidding aggression against them, if they prevented them from the Sacred Mosque, before that happened from the preventers.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God has forbidden you, O believers, dead animals. Dead: is everything that has a flowing soul from the land animals and birds, which God has permitted to be eaten, whether domestic or wild, and whose soul has departed without being slaughtered.

Some of them said: Dead is everything that has departed from life from the land animals and birds without being slaughtered, and which God has permitted to be eaten. We have explained the reason for the validity of what we have said in this regard in our book, A Book of Delicate Words on Rulings. As for blood, it is spilled blood, not what was not spilled, because God Almighty said: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it, unless it be a dead animal, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine.’ (al-An’am 6:145), but as for what has become like meat, such as the liver and spleen, and what was in the meat that was not spilled, then that is not forbidden, because everyone has agreed on that. As for his saying: and the meat of pigs, he means: And the meat of pigs is forbidden to you, whether domestic or wild. As for dead meat and blood, their apparent meaning is general, but what is meant by them is specific.

As for pork, its appearance is like its interior, and its interior is like its appearance. It is all forbidden, and nothing has been specified. As for his saying: And what is dedicated to other than God, he means: And what is mentioned over it is not the name of God. Its origin is from the baby’s cry of ascent, when he cries when he falls from his mother’s womb. And from it is the pilgrim’s cry of ascent for Hajj, when he responds to it, and from it is the saying of Ibn Ahmar: Its riders arrive at Al-Farqad as a pilgrim arrives for Umrah What he meant by his saying:
h
And what is dedicated to other than God is what is slaughtered for gods and idols

, and is called by a name other than God’s. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation, and we mentioned the narration from those who said that in the past, so we disliked repeating it.

The people of interpretation differed Surat al-Ma’idah 5:3 Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, or that which a wild animal has eaten, unless you slaughter it, or that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, or that you seek to decide by arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired. They disbelieved in your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me this Day. I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
- then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. regarding the description of the strangulation that God Almighty meant by His saying: and the strangled.

Some of them said: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And the strangled one he said: The one who puts her head between two branches of a tree, so she strangles and dies.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak
m: regarding the strangled one, he said: the one who strangles and dies.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: and the strangled, that which dies in its strangulation.

x: Others said: It is the one who is tied up and killed by strangulation.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: and the strangled, he said: The sheep is tied up, and its strangulation kills it, so it is forbidden.

x: Others said: Rather, it is an animal from the blessings, the polytheists used to strangle it until it died, so God forbade eating it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the strangled one is the one who is strangled and dies.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the strangled one, the people of the Age of Ignorance used to strangle the sheep, and when it died, they would eat it. The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: It is the one that is strangled, either by its chains, or by inserting its head into a place from which it is unable to escape, so it suffocates until it dies. We said that this is more correct in interpreting it than anything else, because the one who is strangled is the one described by strangulation, without the strangulation of others. If what was meant by that was that it was the object of the action, it would have been said: and the one who is strangled, so that the meaning of the speech would be what they said.

x: God Almighty means by His saying: and the one who is beaten to death, and the one who is killed by a sword. It is said: He struck him until he was on the verge of death. And from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: A young camel that kicks the young camel with its foot, a prey for the young camels And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the one who is struck with a stick, he said: The one who is struck with a stick is the one who is struck with wood until she is struck with it and dies.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the one who was beaten to death, the people of the Age of Ignorance used to beat it with sticks, until when it died, they would eat it.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And the one who was beaten, he said: They would beat it until they made it vomit, then they would eat it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: and the one who is struck by lightning, that which is struck and dies.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, he said:
m: The one who is beaten to death is the one who is struck.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the one who is struck with a blow, he said: It is the one who is struck and dies.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the one beaten to death, that a sheep or other livestock was beaten with wood for their gods, until they killed it and ate it.

c: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told us, he said, Uqbah bin Alqamah told me, Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla told me, he said, Naim bin Salamah told me, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Sanabhi, he said:
m: The one who is killed is only in Malik, and there is no killing in hunting.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And you are forbidden to eat dead animals that fall from a mountain or into a well, or otherwise. And to throw herself from a high, honorable place to the bottom. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the one who falls down, he said: the one who falls down from the mountain.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the one who falls into the well, she would fall into the well and die, and they would eat her.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The one who fell into the well, he said: The one who fell into the well.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: and the one who falls, he said: It is the one who falls from the mountain, or into the well, and dies.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: The one who falls is the one who falls from the mountain and dies.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the one who falls down, he said: The one who falls into a well, or from the top of a mountain, and dies.

x: What he means by his saying: the gored one, is the sheep that is gored by another one and dies from the goring without being slaughtered. So God, the Most High, has forbidden that to the believers, if they do not slaughter it before its death. The root of the word natiha is mantuha, which was changed from maf’ulah to fa’ila.

How did you prove the feminine ha’ in it, while you know that the Arabs hardly prove the ha’ in similar words when they inflect them like natiha from maf’ul to fa’il, rather they say: a greasy beard, a kohl-lined eye, and a dyed hand, but they do not say: a dyed hand, nor a kohl-lined eye?

The Arabists differed on this - some of the grammarians of Basra said: The ha’ was proven in it, I mean in the word natiha - because it was made like a noun, such as: al-tawila and al-tariqah. It is as if the one who said this statement directed the word natiha to the meaning of nataha. The interpretation of the statement according to his school of thought: And the dead animal that is gored is forbidden to you, as if he meant: The animal that kills from goring is forbidden to you.

Some grammarians of Kufa said: The Arabs only delete the ha’ from the fa’ilah that is declined from the maf’ul if they make it an adjective for a noun that precedes it, so you say:رخَّن َخَخا َخِديًبا,َخِدَخا كخهدًب. But if they delete the kaf and the ‘ayn, and the noun that fa’il is an adjective for it, and they suffice with fa’il from it, they keep the ha’ of femininity in it, so that it is known by its being in it that it is an adjective for the feminine and not the masculine, so you say:كخاًب َخْبَكخهدًبََخِديًباَرخَّن كخهدًب. They said: For this reason the ha’ was inserted in natihah, because it is an adjective for the feminine, and if it were dropped from it, it would not be known whether it is an adjective for the feminine or the masculine. This statement is the more correct of the two statements, because of the common sayings of the people of interpretation, that the meaning of the one who was butted is the one who was butted.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: and the goring, he said: the sheep butts the sheep.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, he said:
m: He used to recite: And the one who was struck by a spear.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: And the butt, is two sheep that butt heads and die.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the one who is gored is the one that is gored by sheep or cows and dies. He says: This is forbidden, because some Arabs used to eat it.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the goring, the two rams would butt heads, and one of them would die, and they would eat it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the goring, the two rams butt heads, and one of them kills the other, and they eat it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the goring, he said: A sheep butts another sheep and it dies.

x: He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: And what the wild beast has eaten, and Surat al-Ma’idah 5:3 Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, or that which a wild animal has eaten, unless you slaughter it, or that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, or that you seek to decide by arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired. They disbelieved in your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me this Day. I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
- then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
He has forbidden you what the wild beast has eaten of the prey that is not trained. And so said the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And what the beast has eaten he said: what the beast has taken.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: And what the beast ate, he said: what the beast took.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And what the beast ate, he said: The people of the Age of Ignorance, if a beast killed something of this or ate some of it, they would eat what was left.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he read: And the lions eat.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Except what you slaughter, is except what you purify by slaughtering which God has made a means of purification. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding what God excluded in His saying: Except what you slaughter.

Some of them said: He excluded from everything that God called forbidden in His saying: And that which is dedicated to other than God, and that which is strangled, beaten to death, or fallen from a fall, or gored, and that which is eaten by a wild beast.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Except what you have slaughtered, he says: Whatever you have slaughtered from all of this, its tail moves, or its eye blinks, so slaughter it and mention the name of God over it, and it is permissible. Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said: Ibn Fadil narrated, on the authority of Ash'ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan: "Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine,
h
and that which has been dedicated to other than God

, and that which has been strangled, beaten to death, fallen from a fall, or gored, and that which a wild animal has eaten, except what you slaughter." Al-Hasan said: That is, if you find that it was slaughtered, then slaughter it and eat. I said: O Abu Saeed, how do I know? He said: If it blinks its eye or strikes with its tail.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except what you slaughter, he said: So everything that God Almighty has named here, except for the flesh of the pig, if you see an eye blinking from it, or a tail moving, or a leg running, and you slaughter it, then God has made that permissible for you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except what you have slaughtered, from all of this. So if you find her blinking her eye, or moving her ear from all of this, then she is lawful for you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham and Ibad told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: If you find the slaughter of an animal that has been struck by a blow, or fallen, or gored, and it is moving a hand or a leg, then eat it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: If a wild animal eats from the game, or the one that was killed, or the one that was gored, or the one that fell, and it was slaughtered, then eat.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Musʿab bin Salam al-Tamimi told us, he said, Jaʿfar bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, he said:
m: If it kicks with its foot, or blinks its eye, and moves its tail, then that is sufficient.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ibn Tawus told me, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: If you slaughter an animal and it bites its tail, or it moves, then it is permissible for you, or he said: That is enough.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: If the animal that was struck by lightning blinks its eyes, or kicks with its foot, or licks its tail, then slaughter it and eat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr:
m: that he heard Ubayd ibn Umair say: If she blinks her eye, or wags her tail, or moves, then she is permissible for you.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to eat this, but God forbade in Islam anything except what was slaughtered from it. So whatever was ripe and moved a leg, tail, or limb, and was slaughtered, it is permissible.

c: Yunus told me, saying, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and His statement, and that which has been strangled, beaten to death, fallen from a fall, or gored, and the verse, And no wild animal has eaten except that which you slaughter. He said: All of this is forbidden, except that which has been slaughtered from this. The interpretation of the verse according to what these people say is: the animal that has been struck by a blow or fallen is forbidden, if it dies from falling, being struck by a blow, or being gored, or from a wild animal’s horse, unless you find its slaughter, and find it before its death, then it is permissible to eat it.

x: Others said: It is an exception to the prohibition, but not an exception to the prohibitions that God Almighty mentioned in His statement: Forbidden to you are dead animals, because dead animals cannot be slaughtered, nor can pigs. They said: Rather, the meaning of the verse is: Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, and everything else that we have mentioned along with that, except what you slaughter from what God has made permissible for you by slaughtering, for it is permissible for you.
Among those who said this were a group of people from Medina.
Some of those who said that said:

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us,
m: Malik said, and he was asked about the sheep whose stomach is torn open by a wild animal until its intestines come out, so Malik said: I do not think that it should be slaughtered, and nothing that is slaughtered from it should be eaten.

c: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ashhab, who said:
m: Malik was asked about a wild animal that attacks a ram and crushes its back. Do you think it should be slaughtered before it dies and eaten? He said: If it reached dawn, then I do not think it should be eaten. But if it only hit its extremities, then I do not think there is anything wrong with that. It was said to him: Did it jump on it and crush its back? He said: I do not like it to be eaten, because it does not live from it. It was said to him: What about a wolf that attacks a sheep and rips open its belly, but does not rip open its intestines? He said: If it rips open its belly, then I do not think it should be eaten. According to this statement, his saying: Except what you slaughter, must be an isolated exception. The interpretation of the verse is: Dead animals, blood, and everything else we mentioned are forbidden to you, but what you slaughter from the animals that were made permissible for you by ritual slaughter is permissible.

x: The first of the two opinions on this matter, in our view, is the more correct opinion, which is that his statement, except what you slaughter, is an exception to his statement,
h
and that which has been dedicated to other than God

, and that which has been strangled, or beaten to death, or fallen, or gored, and that which has been eaten by a wild beast, because all of that is deserved by the description that it has before its death. So it is said that when the polytheists offered it to their gods, they called it that which has been dedicated to other than God, meaning it was called an offering to other than God. Likewise, that which has been strangled, if it has been strangled even if it has not died, then it is strangled. Likewise, all of what God, the Almighty, has forbidden after his statement,
h
and that which has been dedicated to other than God

, except by slaughtering, because it is described by the description that it has before its death, so God has forbidden it to His servants except by lawful slaughtering, not by death by the cause by which it was described.

If that is the case, then the interpretation of the verse is: And what has been dedicated to other than God is forbidden to you, and the strangled, and so on and so on and so on, except what you slaughter of that. So, if that is its interpretation, it is in the accusative case as an exception to what precedes it. It may be permissible to put it in the nominative case. If the matter is as we have described, then everything that has been slaughtered, whether a bird or an animal, before its soul leaves its body, is permissible to eat, if it is among what God has permitted for His servants.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: If that is what you mean, then what is the reason for repeating what he repeated in his saying:
h
And that which has been dedicated to other than God

, and that which has been strangled, or beaten to death, or fallen from a head, and all the rest of what he listed as forbidden in this verse, and he began the verse with his saying: Forbidden to you is dead meat? And you know that his saying:
h
Forbidden to you is dead meat includes every dead animal

, whether its death was a natural death from an illness caused by it without anyone committing a crime against it, or its death was from a blow by someone striking it, or strangulation by it, or goring, or a wild horse? And why was his saying - if the matter is as I have described in that, that he meant by the prohibition in all of that: dead meat by strangulation, goring, spitting, eating by a wild animal or other than that, without his meaning by it its prohibition if he fell or was strangled or his horse was mauled by a wild animal, and that reached him to the point where he knew that he would not live from what he had suffered from it except with a little life - dead meat is forbidden to you, making it unnecessary to repeat what he repeated by his saying:
h
and that which has been dedicated to other than God
and that which has been strangled, and all the rest of what he mentioned with that, and how many of them are there?

The reason for repeating that, even though it was forbidden if it died from the causes for which it is described, and it was mentioned before in His saying: Forbidden to you are dead animals, is that those who were addressed by this verse did not consider dead Surat al-Ma’idah 5:3 Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, or that which a wild animal has eaten, unless you slaughter it, or that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, or that you seek to decide by arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired. They disbelieved in your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me this Day. I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
- then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. animals to be anything except what died from an accidental illness other than strangulation, falling, butting, or the mare of a wild animal.

c: So God informed them that
m: the ruling on that is the ruling on what died from accidental illnesses, and that the reason for forbidding dead animals is not its death from an illness or harm that was in it before its death, but the reason for that is that he did not slaughter it for the sake of his slaughter in the sense in which he made it permissible, like the one who: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And the strangled, and the beaten, and the fallen, and the gored, and what a wild animal has eaten, except what you slaughter, he said: This is forbidden, because some people from among the Arabs used to eat it and not consider it dead, they only considered dead what died from pain. So God forbade it to them, except what they mentioned the name of God over, and they realized that it was slaughtered and still had life in it.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: And that which is slaughtered on altars, is that what is slaughtered on altars is also forbidden to you. So what is in his saying: and what was slaughtered, is in the nominative case, in apposition to what is in his saying: and what the beast ate. And the idols are the idols made of stones, a group of idols that were collected in a place on the ground, so the polytheists would offer sacrifices to them, and they would touch the idols.
Ibn Jurayj used to say about his description:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: The idols are not idols. An idol is made to be depicted and engraved. These are stones that are erected, three hundred and sixty stones. Some say that three hundred of them belong to Khuza’ah. So when they slaughtered, they sprinkled the blood on the opposite side of the House, and they cut up the meat and placed it on the stones. The Muslims said: O Messenger of God, the people of the Age of Ignorance used to venerate the Kaaba with blood, so we have more right to venerate it! It seemed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not dislike that, so God revealed: Never will their meat nor their blood reach God (al-Hajj 22:37). What confirms Ibn Jurayj’s statement that the idols are not the same as the statues is:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And what was slaughtered on the altars, he said: Stones on which the people of the Age of Ignorance used to slaughter.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: The idols, he said: Stones around the Kaaba, on which the people of ignorance would slaughter, and they would replace them if they wished with stones more pleasing to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And what was slaughtered on altars, and altars are stones that the people of the Age of Ignorance used to worship and slaughter for, so God forbade that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And what was sacrificed on altars, meaning: the altars of the Age of Ignorance.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And what was slaughtered on altars, and al-tasb are altars on which they used to slaughter and perform the ritual ablution.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And what was slaughtered on altars, he said: There were stones around the Kaaba on which the people of the Age of Ignorance would slaughter, and they would replace them if they wished with a stone that was more beloved to them than it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim say: The idols were stones to which they would make a vow and slaughter upon them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: And what was slaughtered on altars, he said: What was slaughtered on altars and What was dedicated to other than God, and it is one and the same.

x: What he means by his saying: And that you seek to draw lots with arrows, is that you seek to know what has been allotted to you or not, with arrows. It is an istafʿala from the word oath, which means division of provisions and needs. This is because when one of the people of the Jahiliyyah wanted to travel or go on a raid or something like that, he would swing the arrows, which are the arrows. They were arrows with written on some of them: My Lord has forbidden me, and on others: My Lord has commanded me. If the arrow that had written on it: My Lord has commanded me came out, he would go on with what he wanted of travel or raid or marriage or something else. If the one that had written on it: My Lord has forbidden me came out, he would stop and hold back. So it was said: And that you should seek lots with arrows, because by doing that they were as if they were asking their arrows to divide for them.

From this is the saying of the poet, proud of not seeking lots with them: I did not swear, so the oaths kept me waiting As for the arrows, the singular form is zalam, and it is said: zalam, and they are the arrows whose matter we described. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: And that you cast lots with arrows, he said: The lots. When they wanted to go on a journey, they would draw lots for sitting and going out. If it was time to go out, they would go out. If it was time to sit, they would sit.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And that you cast lots with arrows, he said: White pebbles that they used to strike.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us:
m: It is chess.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Abbad bin Rashid Al-Bazzar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: And that you seek lots by arrows, he said: When they wanted to do something or travel, they would take three lots, on one of which was written: Command me, and on the other: Prohibit me, and they would leave the other one open between them with nothing on it. Then they would not move it around. If the one that had Command me came out, they would go on with their matter. If the one that had Prohibit me came out, they would stop, and if the one that had nothing on it came out, they would repeat it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And that you cast lots with arrows, stones on which they used to write, and they called them arrows.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: with arrows, he said: the lots, they are struck for every journey, conquest, and trade.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And that you cast lots with arrows, he said: The arrows of the Persians with which they gamble, and the arrows of the Arabs.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim Al-Ghafari told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And that you cast lots with arrows, he said: The arrows of the Arabs, and the arrows of the Persians and the Romans, they used to gamble with them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And that you cast lots by arrows, he said: When a man wanted to go out on a journey, he would write on an aral-Saff 61:This one orders me to stay and this one orders me to go out, and he would put with them a gift, something in which he did not write anything, then he would cast lots by it when he wanted to go out. If the one who ordered him to stay went out, he would stay, and if the one who ordered him to go out went out, he would go out, and if the other went out, he would move it around a second time until one of the arrows came out.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And that you cast lots by arrows. When the people of ignorance wanted one of them to go out, he would take a stick and say: This one orders the going out, so if he goes out then he will attain goodness in his journey. And he would take another stick and say: This one orders the staying, so he will not attain goodness in his journey, and the one who is given goodness is between them. So God forbade that and presented it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And that you seek lots with arrows, he said: They used to seek lots with them in matters.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: The arrows were arrows for them. When one of them wanted to do one of those things, he would write on those arrows what he wanted, and he would strike them with it. Whichever arrow came out - even if it was the most hated of those - he would commit to it and act upon it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And that you seek lots by arrows, he said: Arrows are lots that were held by soothsayers in the pre-Islamic era. If a man wanted to travel, or get married, or do something, he would go to the soothsayer and give him something, and he would cast lots for him. If something he liked came out of it, he would order him to do it. If something he disliked came out of it, he would forbid him to do it, and he would stop. Just as Abd al-Muttalib cast lots for Surat al-Ma’idah 5:3 Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, or that which a wild animal has eaten, unless you slaughter it, or that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, or that you seek to decide by arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired. They disbelieved in your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me this Day. I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
- then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Zamzam, and for Abd God and the camels.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, who said:
m: We heard that the people of the Age of Ignorance used to cast lots for setting out and staying, or for something they wanted. The arrow for setting out would come out, so they would set out, and the arrow for staying would come out, so they would stay. Ibn Ishaq said in Al-Azlam:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to me, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Hubal was the greatest idol of the Quraysh in Mecca, and it was on a well inside the Kaaba, and that well was where what was offered to the Kaaba was collected. Hubal had seven cups, each cup had a book on it. One cup had: the intellect, if they disagreed about who among them should carry the intellect, they would cast lots with the seven lots, [and if the intellect came out, then whoever came out should carry it]. One cup had: yes to the matter if they wanted it, they would cast lots with it, and if one cup came out, yes, they would do it. One cup had: no, if they wanted something, they would cast lots with it, and if that cup came out, they would not do it. One cup had: from you. One cup had: attached. One cup had: from others. One cup had: water, if they wanted to dig for water, they would cast lots with that cup in them, and wherever it came out, they would do it. When they wanted to circumcise a boy, or marry someone, or bury a dead person, or they doubted the lineage of one of them, they would go with him to Hubal with a hundred dirhams and a camel, and give it to the one who drew lots. Then they would bring their friend with whom they wanted what they wanted, and say: O our God, this is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and we wanted such-and-such for him, so draw the truth about him. Then they would say to the one who drew lots: Strike, and he would strike. If one of you came out against him, he would be an intermediary. If someone other than you came out against him, he would be an ally. If he came out attached, he would remain in his position among them, with no lineage or alliance. If something other than this came out against him that they acted upon, yes, they would act upon it. But if it came out, they would postpone it for that year until they brought him back another time. They would end their affairs with that which the lots had drawn.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And that you cast lots with arrows, meaning: the lots, they used to cast lots with them in matters.

x: By His saying, That, He, the Most High, meant these matters that He mentioned, and that is: eating dead meat, blood, pork, and all the rest of what is mentioned in this verse that it is forbidden to eat, and casting lots with arrows, is immorality, meaning: going beyond the command of God, the Most High, and obedience to Him, to what He has forbidden and warned against, to disobeying Him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: That is an abomination, meaning: whoever eats all of that is an abomination.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
Today those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion

, is that now the hopes of the parties and the people of disbelief and denial have been cut off, O believers, from your religion, meaning: from your religion that you abandon it and turn away from it, returning to polytheism, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Today those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion
, meaning: that you will ever return to their religion.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Today those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion
, he said: I think, they have despaired that you will turn back from your religion.

x: What day is this, the day on which God said that those who disbelieved despaired of the religion of the believers?
It was mentioned that this was the Day of Arafah, in the year of the Prophet’s farewell pilgrimage, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was after the Arabs had entered Islam.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Mujahid said:
m: This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion, “
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

,” this is when I did. Ibn Jurayj said: And others said, that was on the Day of Arafah, on a Friday, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked and saw only a monotheist, and did not see a polytheist, so he praised God, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to him: This day those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion, that they would return to what they were before.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Today those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion
, he said: This is the Day of Arafah.

x: By that he means: Do not fear, O believers, those who have despaired of your religion, that you will turn back from it from the infidels, and do not fear that they will prevail over you, so they will subjugate you and turn you back from your religion.
And fear, he says: But fear, if you disobey My command and dare to disobey Me, and transgress My limits, that I will bring down My punishment upon you and bring down My torment upon you, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: So do not fear them, but fear Me, so do not fear that they will prevail over you.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you

, is that today I have perfected for you, O believers, My obligations upon you, My limits, My commands to you and My prohibitions, My lawful and unlawful things, and My revelation of that which I have revealed of it in My Book, and My clarification of that which I have clarified to you by My revelation through the tongue of My Messenger, and the evidence that I have established for you regarding all that you need of your religion, so I have completed all of that for you, so there is no increase in it after this day. They said: That was on the Day of Arafah, in the year of the Prophet’s Farewell Pilgrimage. They said: Nothing was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the obligations, nor anything that was lawful or unlawful, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not live after the revelation of this verse except for eighty-one nights.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

, which is Islam. He said, God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers that He had perfected their faith, so they would never need anything more. God, the Mighty and Sublime, had completed it, so it would never be diminished. God was pleased with it, so He would never be displeased with it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you

, this was revealed on the Day of Arafah, and after that nothing was revealed about what was lawful or unlawful. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and died. Asma’ bint Umays said: I performed Hajj with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Hajj, and while we were walking, Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared to him on the mount, and the mount could not bear the weight of the Qur’an on it, so it knelt down. I came to him and covered him with a cloak that I was wearing.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained for eighty-one nights after this verse was revealed, his saying:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: When the verse:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you

was revealed, and that was the day of the greater pilgrimage, Umar wept. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What makes you weep? He said: What makes me weep is that we used to have an increase in our religion, but now that it has been perfected, nothing that is perfected without being diminished! He said: You have spoken the truth.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ahmad Ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Harun Ibn Abi Wakee’, on the authority of his father,
m: and he mentioned something similar to that.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Today I have perfected your religion for you, your Hajj. So you are singled out for the Sacred City to perform Hajj, you believers, without the polytheists. No polytheist will mix with you during your Hajj.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Abi Ghania told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
m: h
This day I have perfected your religion for you
, he said: He perfected their religion for them: that they performed Hajj and no polytheist performed Hajj with them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
This day I have perfected your religion for you
, he said: God made their religion pure for them and banished the polytheists from the House.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
This day I have perfected your religion for you
, he said: The completion of the Hajj and the expulsion of the polytheists from the House.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him that He completed their religion for them on the day He revealed this verse to His Prophet by making the Sacred City theirs alone, to expel the polytheists from it, so that the Muslims would perform Hajj without them, without the polytheists mixing with them. As for the obligatory duties and rulings, there is a difference of opinion regarding them: Was she completed that day or not?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi what we mentioned on their authority before.
m: Surat al-Ma’idah 5:3 Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, or that which a wild animal has eaten, unless you slaughter it, or that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, or that you seek to decide by arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired. They disbelieved in your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me this Day. I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
- then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib
m: that the last verse revealed in the Qur’an was: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning distant relatives”
r
(An-Nisa’: 176)

. No one with knowledge can deny that the revelation did not cease from the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) until he died, but rather the revelation before his death was most continuous. Since that was the case, and His statement, "They ask you for a legal opinion. Say, 'God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are distant from you'" (al-Nisa 4:176) was the last to be revealed, and that was one of the rulings and obligations, it was known that the meaning of His statement,
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you is contrary to the interpretation of those who interpreted it
, I mean: the perfection of acts of worship, rulings and obligations.

x: Why is the statement of the one who said: It was revealed after that as an obligation, more appropriate than the statement of the one who said: It was not revealed?

Because the one who said: It did not come down, is informing that he does not know that an obligation was revealed, and denial is not testimony, and testimony is the statement of the one who said: It came down. And it is not permissible to reject the statement of the truthful in what it is possible for him to be truthful in.

By that, God Almighty means: I have completed my favor, O believers, by giving you victory over my enemy and your enemy from the polytheists, banishing them from your lands, and cutting off their hope of your return and reverting to what you were upon of polytheism. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abdullah told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The polytheists and Muslims used to perform Hajj together, but when Bara’ah was revealed, the polytheists were banished from the House, and the Muslims performed Hajj, and no polytheists shared with them in the Sacred House. This was part of the completion of the blessing: And I have completed My favor upon you.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you

, the verse. He mentioned to us that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of Arafah, a Friday, when God banished the polytheists from the Sacred Mosque and made the Hajj pure for the Muslims.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: This verse was revealed in Arafat, where the beacons of ignorance were demolished and polytheism was eliminated, and no polytheist performed Hajj with them that year.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer,
m: regarding this verse:
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

and completed My favor upon you, he said, it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing at Arafat, and the people had circled around him, and the minarets and rituals of the Age of Ignorance had been demolished, and polytheism had vanished, and no naked person had circled around the House, so God revealed:
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: something similar.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And I am pleased for you to submit to My command, and to obey Me, according to what I have prescribed for you of its limits, obligations, and features, as a religion, meaning by that: obedience from you to Me.
Was God not pleased with Islam for His servants except on the day He revealed this verse?

God has always been pleased with Islam as a religion for His creation, but He, the Most High, has always directed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions through the degrees and ranks of Islam, degree after degree, rank after rank, and state after state, until He completed its laws and features for them, and brought them to its highest degrees and ranks. Then He said when He revealed this verse to them: And I have approved for you Islam in the form in which it is today, and the state in which you are today, as a religion, so adhere to it and do not depart from it. Qatada used to say about that:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the religion of every religion will be presented to the people of every religion on the Day of Resurrection. As for faith, it will give good tidings to its companions and people and promise them good, until Islam comes and says, “O Lord, You are peace and I am Islam.” Then it will say, To You I come today, and with You I will be rewarded today. I think that Qatada directed the meaning of faith in this report to the meaning of belief and acknowledgement with the tongue, because that is the meaning of faith among the Arabs, and he directed the meaning of Islam to the surrender of the heart and its submission to God through monotheism, and the body’s obedience to Him in what He commanded and forbade, so that is why it was said about Islam: You today I come, and through you today I will be rewarded. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed at Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Bashar and Ibn Wakee’ narrated, they said: Abd al-Rahman narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab, he said: The Jews said to Umar: You recite a verse which, had it been revealed concerning us, we would have taken it as a festival! Umar said: I know when it was revealed, where it was revealed, and where the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was when it was revealed: It was revealed on the Day of Arafah, and the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was standing at Arafah - Sufyan said: I am not sure whether it was a Friday or not -
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion. Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ narrated, they said: Ibn Idris narrated, he said: I heard my father, on the authority of Qais Ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq Ibn Shihab, he said: A Jew said to Umar: If we, the Jews, had known when this verse was revealed:
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion, if we had known that day, we would have taken that day as a festival! Umar said: I know the day on which it was revealed, the hour, and where the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was when it was revealed: It was revealed on the night of Friday, and we were with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) at Arafat. The wording of the hadith is from Abu Kuraib, and the hadith of Ibn Wakee’ is similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ja’far ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Abu al-Umais, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Umar,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ammar,
m: the freed slave of Banu Hashim, he said: Ibn Abbas recited:
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

, and a man from the People of the Book was with him and he said: If we knew on which day this verse was revealed, we would have taken it as a holiday! Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed on the Day of Arafah, a Friday.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, Qubaysah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ammar:
m: Ibn Abbas recited:
h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion. A Jew said: If this verse had been revealed to us, we would have taken that day as a holiday! Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed on the day of two holidays: a holiday and a Friday.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ammar bin Abi Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Raja’ ibn Abi Salamah told us, he said: Ubadah ibn Nassi told us, he said: Our leader Ishaq told us
m: - Abu Ja’far said: Ishaq is Ibn Kharshah - on the authority of Qubaysah, he said: Ka’b said: If this verse had been revealed to any other nation, they would have looked to the day on which it was revealed to them, and taken it as a festival on which they would gather! Umar said: Which verse, O Ka’b? He said:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you
. Umar said: I know the day on which it was revealed, and the place in which it was revealed: a Friday, and the Day of Arafah, and both of them, praise be to God, are a festival for us.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Isa bin Jariyah Al-Ansari, he said:
m: We were sitting in the council, and a Christian said to us: O people of Islam, a verse has been revealed to you, and if it had been revealed to us, we would have taken that day and that hour as a festival as long as two of us remained:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you

! None of us answered him, so I met Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi and asked him about that, so he said: Why didn’t you respond to him? He said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said: It was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing on the mountain on the Day of Arafah, and that day will continue to be a festival for the Muslims as long as one of them remains.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of ʿAmir, who said:
m: h
This day I have perfected for you your religion

, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion, was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the eve of Arafah, while he was standing at the station.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdul Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, he said:
m: I said to Amer: The Jews say: How did the Arabs not preserve this day on which God perfected their religion for them? Amer said: Or have you not preserved it? I said to him: On which day? He said: The Day of Arafah. God revealed on the Day of Arafah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It has reached us that it was revealed on the Day of Arafah, and it coincided with Friday. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:3 Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, or that which a wild animal has eaten, unless you slaughter it, or that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, or that you seek to decide by arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired. They disbelieved in your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me this Day. I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
- then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah: that Umar bin al-Khattab said:
m: Surat al-Ma’idah was revealed on the Day of Arafah, and it coincided with Friday.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, he said:
m: Surat al-Ma’idah was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing in Arafat on his mount, and it knelt down because its arm was about to be broken.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid, she said:
m: “The entirety of Surat Al-Ma’idah was revealed while I was holding the reins of the she-camel of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Al-Adhba’. She said: Its weight almost broke the she-camel’s arm.”

c: Abu Amir Ismail bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Hisham bin Ammar told us, he said, Ibn Ayyash told us, he said, Amr bin Qais Al-Sakuni told us:
m: that he heard Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan on the pulpit reciting this verse:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you
, until he finished it, and he said: It was revealed on the Day of Arafah, on a Friday.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse - I mean His statement:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you - was revealed on Monday
. And they said: Surat Al-Ma’idah was revealed in Medina.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Harb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Imran, on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born on Monday, and he left Mecca on Monday, and he entered Medina on Monday, and Surat Al-Ma’idah was revealed on Monday:
h
This day I have perfected your religion for you
, and the remembrance was raised on Monday.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Al-Ma’idah is Medinan.

x: Others said: It was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his journey on the Farewell Pilgrimage.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, he said:
m: Surat Al-Ma’idah was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the road during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and he was riding his mount, and his mount knelt down under its weight.

x: Others said: This is not a day known to people, but rather its meaning is: The day that I know, not my creation, I have perfected your religion for you.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
This day I have perfected your religion for you
, meaning: it is not a known day that people know.

x: The most correct of the sayings about the time of the revelation of the verse is the saying narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab: that it was revealed on the Day of Arafah, a Friday, because of the soundness of its chain of transmission, while the chains of transmission of others are weak.

God Almighty means by His saying: But whoever is forced, that is, whoever is afflicted with hardship, in a state of famine, meaning: in a state of famine. It is mafa’ala, like al-mujbanah, al-mubakhlah, and al-munjabah, from khmas al-batin, which means to be emaciated, and I think that in this context it means to be emaciated from hunger and severe starvation. And in other contexts it may be emaciated from something other than hunger and starvation, but from nature, as Nabigha Bani Dhubyan said in describing a woman with a emaciated belly: The belly is soft and round, and the throat is bulging with a firm breast. It is known that he did not describe her by saying: Khamees as being emaciated and suffering from hunger, but rather he wanted to describe her with the softness of the folds on her hips and thighs of her body, because that is something that is praised in women.

i: But what is in the meaning of the description as being emaciated and suffering from hunger is the saying of A’sha of Banu Tha’labah:
x: You spend the winter with full bellies, while your neighbors go to bed hungry.

He means by this: They go to bed with their bellies emptied from hunger, starvation and distress. Hence the meaning of his saying: in famine. Some Basra grammarians used to say: Al-Mukhmasa, the source of Khamsa Al-Ju’. Other Arab scholars believed that it is a noun for a verbal noun, and not a verbal noun. Therefore, al-Mufa’ala is a noun in verbal nouns for both feminine and masculine. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
But whoever is forced by necessity in a state of famine
, meaning: in a state of famine.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity in a state of famine
, meaning: in a state of famine.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But whoever is forced by necessity in a state of famine
, he said: He mentioned the dead animal and what is in it, so he permitted it in a state of necessity, in a state of famine, he said: in a state of starvation.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His statement: But if someone is forced by severe hunger, he said, severe hunger is starvation.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Whoever is forced, due to famine, to eat what has been forbidden to him from among you, O believers, of dead animals, blood, pork, and all the rest of what has been forbidden to him by this verse, not inclined to sin, meaning: not inclined to sin. Therefore, ghair was made accusative because it was not part of the noun in His statement: So whoever is forced, and it means: No, so it was made accusative with the meaning by which it was made accusative al-mutajanif, so the statement would have come: No, al-mutajanifan. As for the one who leans towards sin, he is the one who sways towards it, deviates towards it. In this context, it means the one who deliberately does it, who intends it, from the people leaned towards me, if they leaned towards it. And every crooked person is ajnaf, according to the Arabs. We have explained the meaning of injustice with evidence in His statement: But whoever fears from a testator deviation (al-Baqarah 2:182), which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

As for the one who eats dead meat avoiding eating it and other things that God has forbidden believers to eat, based on this verse, because of the sin in eating it, it is: his intentionally eating that, not to relieve the necessity that has befallen him, but rather to disobey God and disobey His command in what He commanded him to do, which is to refrain from eating that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
, meaning: to what is forbidden, from what is named at the beginning of this verse, with no inclination to sin, meaning: not intentionally committing a sin.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Not inclined to sin, not intentionally committing sin. He said: To what God has forbidden, what He has forbidden. He permitted the one in need, if he was not intentionally committing sin, to eat it out of his own effort. But whoever transgressed, or transgressed, or went out in disobedience to God, then it is forbidden for him to eat it.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: not inclined to sin, meaning: not exposed to disobedience.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Not inclined to sin, not intentionally committing sin, not exposing oneself to it.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Not inclined to sin, he says: Not exposed to sin, meaning: seeking lust in it, or transgressing in eating it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: not inclined to sin, he does not eat that seeking sin, nor out of audacity to do so.

x: There is something omitted in this statement. I am satisfied with the evidence of what was mentioned in it. That is because the meaning of the statement is: Whoever is forced by famine to do what is forbidden to him from what was mentioned in this verse, not inclined to sin, and eats it, then God is Forgiving and Merciful to him. So he omitted mentioning and eats it, and mentioned for him, because the rest of what was mentioned in the statement indicates them. As for his statement: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, its meaning is: For whoever eats what He has forbidden him to eat in this verse, in a state of famine, not inclined to sin, God is Forgiving and Merciful. He says: He conceals for him what he has eaten of that, by pardoning him from holding him accountable for it, and by overlooking it and from punishing him for it. Merciful, he says: And He is gentle with him.

And from His mercy and gentleness with him, He permitted him to eat what He permitted him to eat of dead meat and Surat al-Ma’idah 5:3 Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, or that which a wild animal has eaten, unless you slaughter it, or that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, or that you seek to decide by arrows. That is grave disobedience. Today those who disbelieve have despaired. They disbelieved in your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me this Day. I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion.
h
But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin
- then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. all that is mentioned with it in this verse, in the case of his fear for himself from the dog of hunger and the harm of need that comes upon his body.
What is the food that God promised to forgive the one who is forced to eat dead meat and other forbidden things with it in this verse if he eats from it?

What: Abdul-A’la bin Wasil Al-Asadi told me, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Qasim Al-Asadi told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan bin Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi, he said: We said: O Messenger of God, we live in a land where famine afflicts us, so what is good for us from dead animals?
He said: If you do not eat green vegetables for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, then do as you please.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Khasib bin Zaid Al-Tamimi, he said, Al-Hasan told us:
m: “A man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Until when will what is forbidden be permissible for me?’ He said: ‘Until your family is satisfied with milk, or their provisions come.’”

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Khasib bin Zaid al-Tamimi told us, he said, al-Hasan told us:
m: A man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Or their provisions are collected.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Urwah narrated to me, on the authority of his grandfather Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of someone who narrated to him:
m: “A man from the Bedouins came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him about what God has forbidden him and what He has permitted him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Good things are permissible for you and bad things are forbidden for you, unless you are in need of food that is not permissible for you, so you eat from it until you are independent of it.’ The man said: ‘What is my poverty that is permissible for me? And what is my wealth that makes me independent of that?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If you hope for a good crop, and you reach your crops with the meat of your livestock, or you hope for wealth that you seek, and you reach some of that, then feed your family whatever you want until you are independent of it.’ The Bedouin said: ‘What is my wealth that I leave behind if I find it?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If you provide your family with a late-night meal, then avoid the food that God has forbidden you. As for your wealth, it is all easy.’” There is nothing forbidden in it.
b.via: on the authority of someone who

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
