m: I found Samurah’s book with Al-Hasan, so I read it to him, and it said: And in case of necessity, a morning or evening meal is sufficient.

c: Hanad and Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, they said, Yahya bin Abi Zaidah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
m: I read in the book of Samra bin Jundub: It is sufficient from necessity - or: from necessity - a morning or evening meal.

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi and Abu Kurayb told me, they said: Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: If a man is forced to eat dead meat, he should eat from it what he needs for his sustenance, meaning: what he needs.

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Ibn Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan bin Atiyah, he said: A man said:
m: O Messenger of God, we live in a land of famine, so what is permissible for us of dead meat? And when is dead meat permissible for us? He said: If you do not eat it in the morning or the evening, and do not eat green vegetables, then do as you please.

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan bin Atiyah, on the authority of a man
m: who was named to us: A man said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We live in a land of famine, so when will carrion be permissible for us? He said: If you do not eat for dinner, or eat for breakfast, or eat green vegetables, then do as you please.

x: This is narrated in four ways: tahtafiwu with a hamza, tahtafiwu with a light ya and ha, tahtafiwu with a shaddah on the fa, and tahtafiwu with a ha and a light ha, and it is possible to have a hamza.

evidence.text: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said: I found Samurah’s book with Al-Hasan, so I read it to him, and it said: And in case of necessity, a morning or evening meal is sufficient.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O Muhammad, your companions ask you: What foods and meals are permissible for them to eat? So say to them: Permissible for you are the good things, which are the lawful slaughtered animals that your Lord has permitted you to eat. Permissible for you is also the game of what you know of the raptors, which are the predatory beasts of prey. Birds of prey are called birds of prey because they wound their owners and earn their livelihood from hunting. It is said: So-and-so wounded his family for good, if he earned them good, and So-and-so is the victim of his family, meaning: he earned them money, and there is no victim for so-and-so, if she has no one to earn it. From this is the saying of A’sha of Banu Tha’labah: A bird with a sharp edge, its brand reminds the victim of what he has done. It means: acquired. He left out from his statement: And what you know, and hunting what you know of the birds of prey, being content with indicating what was mentioned in the speech to what he left out.

c: It has been reported to us that
m: the people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he ordered them to kill dogs, about what they were permitted to keep and hunt. So God Almighty revealed this verse regarding their question. He made an exception for what was forbidden to keep. He ordered the keeping of hunting dogs, livestock dogs, and farm dogs, and permitted them to keep these. The report mentioned that: Abu Kuraib narrated, Zaid bin Habbab Al-Akli narrated, Musa bin Ubaidah narrated, Abaan bin Salih informed us, on the authority of Al-Qaqa bin Hakim, on the authority of Salma Umm Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking permission to enter, and he gave him permission. He said: We have given you permission, O Messenger of God! He said: Yes, but we will not enter a house in which there is a dog! Abu Rafi’ said: Then he ordered me to kill every dog in Madinah, so I killed until I reached a woman who had a dog that was barking at her, so I left it out of mercy for it, then I came to the Messenger of God, Surat al-Ma’idah 5:4 They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is lawful for them. Say, "Lawful to you are [all] good foods and what you have taught of the birds of prey, training them from what God has taught you.
h
So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it

, and fear Allah. Indeed, God is swift in account." may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him, so he ordered me to go back to the dog and kill it. So they came and said: O Messenger of God, what is permissible for us from this nation that you have been ordered to kill? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent, so God revealed: “They ask you, what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful to you are good things and those which you have taught of birds of prey to hunt.”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Rafi to kill dogs, and he was killed! Until he reached Al-Awali, then Asim bin Adi, Saad bin Khaithama, and Uwaim bin Saʿidah entered and said: What is lawful for us, O Messenger of God? Then this verse was revealed: “They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are [all] good foods and what you have taught of birds of prey to hunt.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, he said,
m: they told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the killing of dogs, they said: O Messenger of God, what is permissible for us from this nation? Then the verse was revealed: They ask you, what is permissible for them, the verse. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the organs that God meant by His saying: And what you have taught of the organs.

x: Some of them said: It is everything that is known for hunting and learns it, whether it is an animal or a bird.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Muslim, on the authority of al-Hasan
m: regarding the statement:
h
And what you have taught of the birds of prey that hunt
, he said: Everything that is taught to hunt, from a dog or a falcon or a leopard or other.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Makalbeen, he said: Everything that is known to hunt, such as a dog, a leopard, or something else.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding hunting the cheetah, he said: It is one of the birds of prey.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what you have taught of the birds of prey that hunt
, he said: birds and dogs.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Makalbeen, he said: from dogs and birds.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Of the birds of prey, there are dogs, he said: Of the birds and dogs.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Haytham, on the authority of Talha bin Masraf, he said, Khaithama bin Abd Al-Rahman said:
m: This is what I have explained to you: that the falcon and the hawk are birds of prey.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, he said,
m: I heard al-Haytham narrating, on the authority of Talhah al-Ayami, on the authority of Khaithamah, he said: I explained to you: that the falcon, the hawk, and the dog are among the birds of prey.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Abdullah ibn Umar told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ali ibn Husayn, he said:
m: The hawk and the falcon are birds of prey.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, who said:
m: The hawk and the falcon are among the raptors with docile prey.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what you know of the birds of prey that are hunting dogs
, meaning by birds of prey, the ferocious dogs, leopards, falcons, and the like.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: And what you know of the birds of prey that hunt, he said: of dogs, and other than them, such as falcons and hawks, and the like of that which is known.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And what you have taught of the birds of prey to be trained
, the birds of prey are the trained dogs and falcons.

c: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar,
m: he heard Ubaid bin Umair say regarding His statement: Of the birds of prey, there are two dogs, he said: Dogs and birds.

x: Others said: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And what you have taught of the birds of prey to be trained to hunt
, dogs, not other beasts of prey.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Abu Tamila told us, he said, Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And what you know of the birds of prey that are hunting dogs
, he said: They are dogs.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
And what you have trained of the birds of prey to hunt
, meaning: It is permissible for you to hunt with the dogs that you have trained.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: As for what he hunted from the birds - and the falcons are from the birds - then whatever you catch is yours, otherwise do not feed it.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the one that says: Everything that is hunted from birds and beasts of prey is from birds of prey, and that the prey of all of them is permissible if hunted after being trained, because God Almighty made it general in His statement: And what you have taught of birds of prey as hunters, every bird of prey, and He did not specify any of them. So every bird of prey that has the characteristic that God described from every bird and beast of prey, then eating its prey is permissible.

c: It was narrated from the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what we have said about that, along with what is in the verse of the evidence that we mentioned about the correctness of what we have said about that, which is what: Hanad told us, he said, Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about hunting with a hawk, so he said: Whatever it catches for you, eat it. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted hunting the hawk and considered it a type of bird of prey. This is clear evidence of the corruption of the statement of those who said: God meant by His statement, and what you have taught of birds of prey, what we have taught of dogs in particular, and not of other birds of prey.

x: If someone thinks that his statement, with dogs, indicates that the birds of prey mentioned in his statement, and what you have taught of birds of prey, are dogs in particular, then he has thought incorrectly. The meaning of the verse is: Say: Lawful to you, O people, if you are owners of dogs, are good things and the game of what you have taught them to hunt, from the prey of wild beasts and birds. So his saying: with dogs is a description of the hunter, even if he hunts with something other than dogs sometimes. It is similar to the saying of a speaker addressing a al-Nas 114:
h
Lawful to you are good things and what you have trained of birds of prey to hunt

. It is known that the speaker meant to inform the people that God, the Exalted, has made lawful to them, if they are people of faith, good things and the game of birds of prey that He has informed them that nothing is lawful for them of it except what they hunt with it.
Likewise, his saying:
h
Lawful to you are good things and what you have trained of birds of prey to hunt
, is similar to that, in that the hunting of the hunter - whether by dogs or otherwise - is not an announcement from God, the Exalted, that nothing is lawful of the game except what dogs hunt.

What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: You teach them, is that you discipline the birds of prey and teach them to hunt for you, from what God has taught you, meaning by that: from the discipline with which God has disciplined you, and the knowledge that He has taught you.
Some of the commentators said: The meaning of his saying: From what God has taught you is as God has taught you.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: You teach them from what God has taught you, meaning: You teach them from seeking knowledge as God has taught you. We do not know in the speech of the Arabs the meaning of kaf, because min in their speech means partiality, and kaf means comparison. Rather, a letter is placed in place of another if their meanings are close. However, if their meanings differ, then it is not found in their speech that one of them is placed after the other. The Book of God and His revelation are the most deserving of speech to avoid what has gone beyond the concept and the ultimate in spaciousness from the speech of the one who revealed it in his language.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ismail bin Subaih told us, he said, Abu Hani Omar bin Bashir told us, he said, Amer told us: Adi bin Hatim al-Ta’i said:
m: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him about hunting with dogs, and he did not know what to say to him, until this verse was revealed: You teach them from what God has taught you. It was said: The people of interpretation differed on that.

x: Some of them said: It is that he seeks prey when his owner sends him out, and holds on to it when he catches it and does not eat from it, and responds to it when he calls it, and does not flee from it when he wants it. If he does this repeatedly, then he is a teacher. This is the opinion of a group of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Iraq. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:4 They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is lawful for them. Say, "Lawful to you are [all] good foods and what you have taught of the birds of prey, training them from what God has taught you.
h
So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it
, and fear Allah. Indeed, God is swift in account."
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ata’ said:
m: Everything that your hunter kills before he knows, catches, and hunts, is dead. His killing of it is not considered ritual slaughter until he knows, catches, and hunts. If that happens and then he kills, then it is considered ritual slaughter.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, my father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The trained dog is that it catches its prey and does not eat from it until its owner comes to it. If it eats from its prey before its owner comes to it and realizes its ritual slaughter, then it does not eat from its prey.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If a dog eats, do not eat, for it only held back for its own sake.

c: Abu Kuraib and Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, Ismail ibn Ibrahim told us, Abu al-Mualla told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: If a man sends a dog and it eats from his catch, then he has spoiled it, even if he mentioned the name of God when he sent it - so he claimed that he only caught it for himself - and God says: Of the birds of prey, you teach them from what God has taught you, so he claimed that if it eats from its catch before its owner comes to it, then it is not trained, and that it is necessary for it to strike and become blind until it abandons that behavior.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muammar al-Raqi told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If a dog takes it, kills it, and eats it, then it is considered a wild animal.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told me, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He does not eat from it, because if he had been taught, he would not have eaten from it, nor would he have learned what you taught him. He only held back for himself, and he did not hold back for you.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If a dog eats, do not eat.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Ibn ʿAwn told us:
m: I said to ʿAmir al-Shaʿbi: If a man sends his dog to eat from it, can we eat from it? He said: No, he did not learn what I taught him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: If a dog eats from its prey, hit it, for it is not trained.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: If a dog eats something, it is dead, so do not eat it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: and Sayyar, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, and Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, that they said about a dog that eats from its prey: Do not eat, for it only caught it for its own sake.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Ata’ said:
m: If you find a dog eating from the game, and you do not find it dead, then leave it, because it is one of those who did not catch game for you. It is only a wild animal that caught for itself and did not catch you, even if it knew.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: something similar.

x: Others said something similar to this article, but they limited the dogs’ knowledge that their dog has accepted the training and has become one of the birds of prey that are permissible to hunt: that his dog should do that three times. This is a statement attributed to Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan.

Others who said this statement said: There is no limit to the knowledge of dogs about that from their dog, more than if their dog did what we described as teaching him. They said: If he did that, then he became a teacher whose hunting was permissible. This is the opinion of some of the later scholars. Some of those who said this article differentiated between teaching the hawk and other birds of prey and teaching the dog and other predatory beasts of prey. He said: It is permissible to eat what the hawk has eaten from the game. They said: The hawk is only taught to fly when it is called, to respond when it is called, and not to flee from its owner if he wants to take it. They said: It is not one of the conditions of teaching it that it not eat from the game.
Who said that?

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: There is nothing wrong with hunting a hawk, even if one eats some of it.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said, Abu Ishaq al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said
m: about the bird: If you release it and it kills, then eat. But if you hit the dog, it will not return. Because the bird is taught to return to its owner, and it is not hit if it eats from the hunt and plucks its feathers.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: The hawk and the falcon are not like the dog. If you send them out and they catch up and eat, and you call them and they come to you, then eat from it.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abu Zaid told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Hammad, Ibrahim said:
m: All the prey of the falcon is eaten from it.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim and Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, they said:
m: Everyone who hunts a falcon, even if he eats it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: If the hawk or the falcon eats from the prey, then eat, for it does not know.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim Fal:
m: There is nothing wrong with what the falcon eats.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Hammad: that he said
m: about the falcon when it eats from it, he said: Eat.

x: Others among them said: It is the same as teaching birds, beasts, and wild animals. None of these types is taught except by what all other types are taught. They said: It is not permissible to eat anything from the game that a bird of prey hunted and ate from, regardless of whether that bird of prey was a beast or a bird. They said: Because one of the conditions for its training that makes its game permissible is that it holds back what it hunts for its owner, and does not eat from it.
Who said that?

c: Hanad and Abu Kuraib told us, they said, Ibn Abi Zaida told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Salim told us, on the authority of Amer Fal: Ali said:
m: If the falcon eats from its prey, do not eat.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Mujalid bin Saʿid, on the authority of Al-Shaʿbi, he said:
m: If the falcon eats from it, do not eat from it.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: If the hawk eats, do not eat.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Walid Al-Shani, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: If the hawk eats, do not eat.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Ata’ said:
m: The dog and the hawk are all the same. Do not eat what it has eaten from the game, unless you find it slaughtered, then slaughter it. He said, I said to Ata’: The hawk plucks feathers? He said: So whatever you find and it has not eaten, then eat. He said that more than once.

x: Others said: The training of every animal and bird is one. They said: The training that makes its prey permissible is that it stalks the prey, pulls it out and takes the prey, and its owner calls it and it responds, and does not flee from it if it takes it. They said: So if the bird of prey does that, it is a teacher included in the meaning of which God said: And what you have taught of birds of prey, training them from what God has taught you,
h
so eat of what they catch for you

. They said: It is not a condition of teaching that to someone who does not eat from the prey. They said: How can it be permissible for someone whose condition is that, and he disciplines by eating it?
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed - or Saad - on the authority of Salman, he said:
m: If you send your dog to hunt, and you mention the name of God, and it eats two-thirds of it and one-third remains, then eat what remains.
b.via: Saeed - or Saad - on the authority of Salman

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Humayd told us, al-Qasim ibn Rabiʿah told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Salman - and Bakr ibn ʿAbdullah, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Salman -
m: about the dog that takes prey and eats from it, he said: Eat, even if it eats two-thirds of it, if you send it out and mention the name of God, and it is trained.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, he said:
m: I heard Qatada narrating, on the authority of Saʿid Ibn Al-Musayyab, he said: Salman said: Eat, even if he eats two-thirds of it, meaning: the game if a dog eats from it.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday and Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Samad told us, on the authority of Shu’bah - H and Hannad told us, he said, Abdah told us
m: - all of them, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said, Salman said: If you send your trained dog and mention the name of God, and it eats two-thirds of it and one-third of it remains, then eat.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Salman,
m: something similar.

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Muzani and Al-Qasim: Salman said:
m: If a dog eats, then eat, because it ate two-thirds of it. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:4 They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is lawful for them. Say, "Lawful to you are [all] good foods and what you have taught of the birds of prey, training them from what God has taught you.
h
So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it
, and fear Allah. Indeed, God is swift in account."

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi al-Furat, on the authority of Muhammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, he said: Salman said:
m: If you send your trained dog or your falcon, and you mention the name of God and it eats half of it or two-thirds of it, then eat the rest of it.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Mukhramah ibn Bakir told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Humayd ibn Malik ibn Khathim al-Du’ali:
m: that he asked Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas about hunting that a dog eats from, so he said: Eat, even if nothing remains of it except a shoe - meaning: a piece.
b.via: Humayd ibn Malik ibn Khathim al-Du’ali

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd al-Samad told me, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abd Rabbih ibn Sa’id, he said:
m: I heard Bakir ibn al-Ashja narrating, on the authority of Sa’d, he said: Eat, because he ate two-thirds of it.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abd Rabbih bin Saeed Fal:
m: I heard Bakir bin Al-Ashja, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab - Shu’bah said: I said: Did you hear it from Saeed? He said: No - he said: Eat, even if he ate two-thirds of it. He said: Then Shu’bah said in his hadith: On the authority of Saad, he said: Eat, even if he ate half of it.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: If you send your dog and it eats from it, if it eats two-thirds of it and there is one-third left, then eat.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yazid ibn Harun told us, he said, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: something similar.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Salim bin Nuh Al-Attar told me, on the authority of Omar - meaning:
m: Ibn Aamer - on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman, who said: If you send your dark-skinned dog and it catches and kills, then eat, even if it eats two-thirds of it.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir told us, he said, I heard Ubaidullah -H and Hanad told us, he said, Abdah told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Umar - on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, he said:
m: If you send your dark-skinned dog and mention the name of God, then eat whatever it catches for you, whether it eats or not.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: something similar.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told me: Nafi’ told them:
m: Abdullah bin Omar did not see anything wrong with eating game, if a dog killed it he would eat from it.

c: Yunus told me
m: about it again, saying, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ubayd God ibn Amr, Ibn Abi Tha’lab, and more than one other told me: that Nafi’ told them, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Muhammad bin Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: He saw no harm in what a fierce wolf ate.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of Bakir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Ashja’, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Sa’d, he said:
m: I said to us: Are there ferocious dogs that eat and leave behind? He said: Eat, even if only a few remain.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of Ya’qub ibn Abdullah ibn al-Ashja, on the authority of Hamid, who said:
m: I asked Sa’d, and he mentioned something similar.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, in the interpretation of His statement: You teach them from what God has taught you is that the teaching that God mentioned in this verse for the birds of prey is that a man should teach his bird of prey to sally out when it is caught on prey, to pursue it when it is tempted, or to hold it back if it takes it without eating anything from it, and not to flee from it when it wants it, and to respond to it when it calls it. This is the teaching of all birds of prey, birds and beasts. If a hunter’s bird of prey eats from the prey, then his bird of prey is not trained. If his master finds his prey alive and slaughters it, it is permissible for him to eat it. But if he finds it dead, it is not permissible for him to eat it, because it is something that has been eaten by a wild beast, which God has forbidden by His statement: and that which a wild beast has eaten, and he has not found its slaughter.
We said: This is the most appropriate statement about the trays, because the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are clear:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Sulayman al-Ahwal, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi ibn Hatim:
m: that he asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about hunting, so he said: If you send your dog, mention the name of God over it, and if you find it and it has killed and eaten some of it, then do not eat anything of it, for it has only caught it for its own sake.

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu Hisham al-Rafa’i told us: Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Bayan ibn Bishr, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Adi ibn Hatim, who said:
m: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: We are people who hunt with these dogs. He said: If you send out your trained dogs and mention the name of God over them, then eat what they catch for you even if they kill, unless the dog eats. If it eats, then do not eat, for I fear that it has only kept it for itself.

x: What do you say about what he told you? Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i said, Abdul Aziz bin Musa told us, Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Abu Iyas, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman Al-Farsi, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a man sends his dog to hunt and it catches up with it and has eaten some of it, then let him eat what is left.”

This is a report whose chain of transmission is questionable, because it is not known that Saeed heard it from Salman, and the trustworthy people of the hadiths stop this statement at Salman, and they narrate it from him without it being traced back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the trustworthy hadith masters, if they follow one another in transmitting something with a description, and a single individual who does not have their own memorization contradicts them, then the trustworthy group is more deserving of the authenticity of what they transmitted than the individual who does not have their own memorization.

If the matter with the dog is as you mentioned: that if it eats from the game it is not trained, then the same is the ruling with every animal of prey: that whatever it eats from the game is not trained, and it is not permissible for it to eat its game unless it realizes that it was slaughtered.
What he meant by his saying: Eat of what they catch for you, is that you eat, O people, of what your limbs catch for you.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of this.

Some of them said: This is apparent and general, as God made it general. It is permissible to eat everything that dogs and trained birds of prey catch for us from the game that is permissible to eat, whether the birds of prey and dogs eat from it or not, whether it is slaughtered and slaughtered or not until the birds of prey kill it by wounding it or without wounding it. This is the statement of those who said: Teaching birds of prey that make it permissible to hunt them means teaching them to hunt prey, to pursue it if it is hunted, to take it, and to refrain from running away from its owner, without refraining from eating its prey if it hunts it. We have mentioned the statement of those who said this statement and the narration from them with their chains of transmission mentioned above.

Others said: Rather, it is specific and not general. They said: Its meaning is: So eat of the game that they catch for you, all of it, not some of it. They said: If the birds of prey eat some of it and hold on to some of it, then what they caught is not permissible to eat, and they have eaten some of it, because they only held on to what they caught of that game after what they ate of it, for themselves, not for us. And God, the Most High, mentioned Himself, only permitted us to eat what our trained birds of prey catch for us, by His saying:
h
So eat of what they catch for you

, not what they catch for themselves. This is the saying of those who said: The training of birds of prey that makes their hunting permissible is that they pull out the game when it is untied, then they seek it out and take it, then hold it for its owner and do not eat anything of it, nor do they flee from its owner. We have mentioned many of those who said this in the past, and we will mention another group of them in this place.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And eat of that which they catch for you
, meaning: Eat of that which they kill. Ali said: Ibn Abbas used to say: If it kills and eats, do not eat, but if it catches and you catch it alive, then slaughter it.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If a trained dog eats from its prey before its owner comes to it and catches it alive, then it should not eat from its prey.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
Then eat of that which they catch for you

, if a dog hunts and catches it and kills it but does not eat from it, then it is permissible. But if it eats from it, then it is said: It only caught it for itself, so do not eat anything from it, for it is not trained.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They ask you what is lawful for them until His saying:
h
So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it
, he said: If you send your trained dog or your bird or your arrow, and you mention the name of God, and it takes or kills, then eat.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: If you send your trained dog and mention the name of God when you send it, and it catches or kills it, then it is permissible. But if it eats from it, then do not eat from it, for it only caught it for its own sake.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then eat of that which they catch for you

, he said: I said, O Messenger of God, is my land a hunting land? He said: If you send your dog and say Bismillah, then eat of that which your dog catches for you, even if it kills. But if it eats, then do not eat, for it only caught it for itself. We have already explained the first of the two opinions on this matter as correct, so there is no need to repeat it. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:4 They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is lawful for them. Say, "Lawful to you are [all] good foods and what you have taught of the birds of prey, training them from what God has taught you.
h
So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it
, and fear Allah. Indeed, God is swift in account."

x: What is the reason for the inclusion of min in His statement:
h
So eat of what they catch for you
, when God has made lawful for us the hunting of our lawful birds of prey, and min only enters into the speech as part of what it entered into?
The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of its inclusion in this position.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Min was used in this position for a reason other than meaning, just as the Arabs used it in their saying: Kana min tamār and Kana min ḥadīth. He said: “And from that is His statement: “And He will expiate for you some of your misdeeds” (al-Baqarah 2:271), and His statement: And He sends down from the sky, mountains wherein is hail (al-Nur 24:43), He said: And He sends down from the sky, mountains wherein is hail. He said: “And some of them said: “And He sends down from the sky, mountains wherein is hail” (al-Nur 24:43), meaning: from the sky, hail, by making the mountains of hail in the sky, and making the sending down from it.”

Others among the Arab scholars denied this and said: Min was only used for an understood meaning, and speech is not permissible or valid without it. This is because it indicates partiality. He used to say: The meaning of their saying Qad kan min tammar and Kan min hadith is: Was there any rain in your country? And was there any hadith that happened in your country? And he says: The meaning of: And He will remove from you any evil (al-Baqarah 2:271), is: And He will remove from you any of your evil deeds that He wills and desires. And in His statement: And He sends down from the sky, from mountains, in which is hail (al-Nur 24:43), he allows the deletion of from from from hail, but he does not allow its deletion from mountains. And he interprets the meaning of that as: And He sends down from the sky, like mountains of hail. Then from was inserted into hail, because hail is explained by him from the examples, I mean: the examples of mountains.

And mountains was established in place of the examples and mountains, and they are mountains of hail. So he does not allow the deletion of from from mountains, because it indicates that what is in the sky from which He sent down the hail is like mountains of hail. He permitted the deletion of min from al-bard, because al-bard is an explanation of al-amthal, just as you say: I have two ratls of oil and I have two ratls of oil, but you do not have the ratl, but rather you have the amount. So min enters into the explanation and leaves it. And likewise according to the one who said this: from the sky, from the likes of mountains, and it is not mountains. And he said: And if it was: He sent down from mountains in the sky mountains of cold, then the second al-jabal was deleted, and the first al-jabal is in the sky, it is permissible. You say: I ate from the food, meaning: I ate food from the food, then you delete al-ta’am and do not drop min.

The correct statement in this regard is that min does not enter into speech except for an understood meaning, and it may be permissible to omit it in some speech and in speech there is a need for it, due to the indication of what appears in the speech about it. As for it being in speech for a meaning other than that which it indicates by entering, we have explained previously that it is not permissible for it to be in what is authentic of speech. The meaning of its entering into His statement:
h
So eat of that which they catch for you

, is for partiality, since the birds of prey catch for their owners what God has made lawful for them to eat of its meat, and has forbidden them its excrement and blood, so He, the Most High, said: So eat - from that which your birds of prey catch for you - the good things that I have made lawful for you of their meat, but not what I have forbidden you of its bad things of excrement and blood and the like, which I have not made good for you.

So that is the meaning of min entering into that. As for His statement: And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds (al-Baqarah 2:271), we have explained the reason for its inclusion in it previously, so there is no need to repeat it. As for its inclusion in His statement: And He sends down from the sky mountains (al-Nur 24:43), we will explain it when we come to it, God willing.
He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying:
h
And mention the name of God over it
, over whatever your birds of prey catch for you, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And mention the name of God over it
, meaning: If you send your limbs, say: In the name of God, and if you forget, there is no blame.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And mention the name of God over it
, he said: If you send it out, then mention the name of God over it when you send it out to hunt.

x: He, may His praise be exalted, means: O people, fear God in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you. Beware of doing something contrary to Him, and of eating the game of untrained birds of prey, or of what they have not caught from their game and have caught for themselves, or of eating what God has not mentioned in His name from the game and the slaughtered animals, which were hunted by the idolaters and idol worshippers and those of His creation who did not make God One, or slaughtered, for God has forbidden that to you, so avoid it. Then He frightened them if they did what He forbade them from doing, including that and other things. He said: Know that God is swift in holding to account whoever among you calls Him to account for His blessings upon him, and the grateful among you will thank his Lord for what He has bestowed upon him by obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden, because He is the Guardian of all that among you, and He encompasses it, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, so He rewards the obedient among you for his obedience, and the disobedient for his disobedience, and He has made clear to you the reward of the two groups.

What He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: Today, all good things have been made lawful for you, is that today, O believers, all lawful slaughtered animals and foods have been made lawful for you, but not all impure ones. And His statement:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you

, and the sacrifices of the People of the Scripture from the Jews and Christians, who are those who were given the Torah and the Gospel and it was revealed to them, so they adhered to them or to one of them, are lawful for you, meaning: it is lawful for you to eat it, unlike the sacrifices of the rest of the polytheists who do not have a Scripture from the polytheists of the Arabs and the worshippers of idols and statues. For whoever among them is not one of those who acknowledge the Oneness of God, the Mighty and Sublime, and adheres to the religion of the People of the Scripture, then their sacrifices are forbidden to you.
Then there is a difference of opinion about who God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture
, from the People of the Scripture.

Some of them said: God meant by that the sacrifice of every People of the Book to whom the Torah and the Gospel were revealed, or of those who entered their religion and renounced their religion, and forbade what they forbade, and permitted what they permitted, from them and from others from all the races of nations.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, he said, Khasif told us, he said, Ikrimah told us:
m: Ibn Abbas was asked about the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, so he recited this verse: O you who believe, do not take the Jews as allies until His saying:
h
And whoever among you takes them as allies
, then indeed, he is one of them, the verse (al-Ma’idah 5:51).

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us: on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Uthma told us, he said, Saeed bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ikrimah:
m: that they saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and in marrying their women, and they would recite:
h
And whoever among you takes them as allies
, then indeed, he is one of them (al-Ma’idah 5:51).

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab:
m: that they saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: that he saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and he recited: And your Lord is not forgetful
r
(Maryam 19:64)

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, they said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Ibn Shihab told me
m: about the sacrifice of the Nasar, the Arabs, he said: It is eaten because of the people of the Book among them in religion, and they mention the name of God.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ata’ said:
m: They only acknowledge the religion of that book.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatadah about the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and they said: There is nothing wrong with it. He said: Al-Hakam recited: And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Scripture except wishful thinking (al-Baqarah 2:78).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Eat from the slaughtered animals of Banu Taghlib, and marry their women, for God said in His Book: “O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you, then indeed, he is of them” (al-Ma’idah 5:51). So if they were not of them except through allegiance, then they would have been of them. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:5 Today all good foods have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
h
and your food is lawful for them
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, when
h
you have given them their due compensation
, chaste, not fornicating or taking secret lovers. And whoever disbelieves in the faith - His work has become worthless, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Al-Hasan did not see anything wrong with the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, and he used to say: They adopted a religion, so that is their religion.

x: Others said: What is meant by those who were given the Scripture in this verse are those upon whom the Torah and the Gospel were sent down from among the Children of Israel and their children. As for those who were foreigners among them from among the rest of the nations who followed their religion and were not from among the Children of Israel, then this verse does not mean them, and they are not among those whose slaughtering is permissible to eat, because they are not among those who were given the Scripture by the Muslims. This is a statement that Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi’i used to say, and al-Rabi’ told us about it - and he interprets in that the statement of those who disliked the slaughtering of the Arab Christians from among the Companions and the Followers.
Mention of those who forbade the sacrifices of Arab Christians:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah, he said,
m: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Do not eat the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, for they only cling to Christianity by drinking alcohol.

c: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: Do not eat the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, for they did not adhere to anything of Christianity except drinking wine.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Abdullah bin Bakr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, he said:
m: I asked Ali about the sacrifices of the Arab Christians, and he said: Their sacrifices are not to be eaten, because they have not clung to anything of their religion except drinking alcohol.

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said, Ali bin Abis told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, he said:
m: Ali forbade us from the sacrifices of the Arab Christians.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Qassab, he said:
m: I heard Muhammad Ibn Ali narrating, on the authority of Ali: that he disliked the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said,
m: Do not eat the sacrifices of the Arab Christians, and the sacrifices of the Armenian Christians.

x: These reports from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, only indicate that he forbade the slaughtering of the Christians of Banu Taghlib because they were not Christians, for they did not permit what the Christians permitted and forbade what they forbade, except for wine. And whoever claims to follow a religion but does not adhere to anything of it, is closer to disavowing it than to joining it and its people. Therefore, ʿAli forbade eating the slaughtering of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, not because they were not from the Children of Israel. If this is the case, and it is a consensus of the argument that there is nothing wrong with the sacrifice of every Christian and Jew who follows the religion of the Christian or the Jew, and makes lawful what they make lawful and makes unlawful what they make unlawful, whether from the Children of Israel or from others, then it is clear that what al-Shafi’i said about that is wrong, and his interpretation of what he interpreted in his statement:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you

, that it is the sacrifices of those who were given the Scripture, the Torah and the Gospel, from the Children of Israel, and the correct interpretation of what contradicts that, and the statement of the one who said: The sacrifice of every Jew and Christian is lawful, regardless of the race of the children of Adam.
As for the food about which God said:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture
, it is the sacrifices. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, he said: slaughtered animals.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, he said: Their slaughtered animals.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim and Qubaysah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, he said: The slaughter of the People of the Scripture.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, he said: Their slaughtered animals.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim and Qubaysah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, he said: their slaughtered animals.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Mualla bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, meaning: their slaughtered animals.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
. As for their food, it is the slaughtered animals.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, he said: God has made their food and their women lawful for us.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: As for his statement:
h
And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
, he made their food and their women lawful for us.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I asked him - meaning Ibn Zayd - about what was slaughtered for the churches and mentioned over them, so he said: God has made lawful for us the food of the People of the Book, and He did not exclude anything from it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Abu al-Zahriyyah Hadir ibn Kurayb, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad, on the authority of Umair ibn al-Aswad:
m: That he asked Abu al-Darda’ about a ram that was slaughtered for a church called Girgis, which they gave as a gift to it, can we eat from it? Abu al-Darda’ said: O God, pardon us! They are only people of the Book, their food is lawful for us, and our food is lawful for them! And he ordered him to eat it. As for his saying:
h
And your food is lawful for them
, he means: Your sacrifices, O believers, are lawful for the People of the Book.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: and chaste women from among the believing women, is that it is lawful for you, O believers, to marry chaste women from among the believing women - and they are the free women from among them -
h
and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you

, meaning: and the free women from among those who were given the Scripture, and they are the Jews and Christians who believed in what is in the Torah and the Gospel before you, O believers in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the Arabs and all the people, that you may marry them also, when
h
you have given them their due compensation
, meaning: if you give those whom you marry from among your chaste men and women, their due compensation, which is their dowries.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the chaste women whom God Almighty meant in His saying:
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you

Some of them said: He meant by that free women in particular, whether they were wicked or chaste. The proponents of this statement permitted the marriage of a free woman, whether she was a believer or a woman of the Book from the Jews or Christians, from any race of people, as long as she was a woman of the Book, wicked or chaste. They forbade the female slaves of the People of the Book from marrying in any case, because God Almighty made faith a condition for the marriage of female slaves, as He said:
And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women, then from those whom your right hands possess of your believing slave girls
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Dawood told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And chaste Surat al-Ma’idah 5:5 Today all good foods have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
h
and your food is lawful for them
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, when
h
you have given them their due compensation

, chaste, not fornicating or taking secret lovers. And whoever disbelieves in the faith - His work has become worthless, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers. women from among those who were given the Scripture, he said: free women.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, he said: from among the free women.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab:
m: That a man divorced his wife and his sister proposed to him, and she had become impure. So he went to Umar and mentioned that to him about her, and Umar said: What did you see from her? He said: I have seen nothing but good from her! So he said: Marry her and do not tell.

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said: Abdul Wahid told us, he said: Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, he said: Amer told us, he said:
m: A woman from among us from Hamdan committed adultery. He said: The tax collector of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, flogged her with the prescribed punishment, then she repented. So they went to Umar and said: We will marry her, and what a bad thing happened to her! Umar said: If I hear that you have mentioned anything of that, I will punish you severely.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab:
m: A man wanted to marry his sister, but she said: I fear that I will disgrace my father, for I have been deceived! So he came to Umar and said: Hasn’t she repented? He said: Yes! He said: So he married her.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: That Nabisha, a woman from Hamdan, rebelled and wanted to slaughter herself. He said: So they caught up with her, treated her and she recovered. They mentioned that to Umar, and he said: Marry her as a chaste Muslim woman would.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer:
m: That a man from Yemen committed an indecent act against his sister, so he ran a knife over her jugular vein, and she was caught, and her wound was treated until she recovered. Then her uncle moved with his family until he came to Madinah, and she read the Qur’an and kept quiet, until she was one of the most pious of their women. So she proposed to her uncle, and he hated to deceive her, and he hated to reveal his brother’s daughter’s secret. So he went to Umar and mentioned that to him, and Umar said: If you revealed it, I would punish you! If a righteous man comes to you whom you are pleased with, then marry her to him.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer:
m: That a girl in Yemen called Nabisha committed an immoral act, and he mentioned something similar. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated, Yazid narrated, Ismail narrated, on the authority of Aamir, who said: A man came to Umar and said: I have a daughter who was buried alive during the pre-Islamic era. I extracted her before she died, and she lived to see Islam. When she became Muslim, she committed one of the punishments set by God, so she took a knife to slaughter herself. I found her and she had cut some of her jugular vein, so I treated her until she recovered. Then she came back with a good repentance, and she is asking me for her hand in marriage, O Commander of the Faithful. Tell me about her situation and what happened? Umar said: Will you tell me about her situation? You deliberately reveal what God has concealed! By God, if you tell anyone about her situation, I will make you an example to the people of the cities. Rather, marry her as a chaste Muslim woman.

c: Ahmad bin Mani’ told us, he said, Marwan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: A man came to Omar and mentioned something similar.

c: Mujahid told us, Yazid told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr:
m: A man proposed to his sister, and he told him that she had become impure. report of that reached Umar bin al-Khattab, so he struck the man and said: What do you have to do with this report? Marry and be quiet.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said:
m: I was thinking of not allowing anyone who committed an immoral act in Islam to marry a chaste woman! Ubayy ibn Ka’b said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, polytheism is greater than that, and it may be accepted from him if he repents!

x: Others said: God meant by His statement:
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you

, the chaste women from both groups, whether slave women or free women. So the proponents of this statement permitted marriage to slave women from among the People of the Scripture who owe their debts by this verse, and they forbade prostitutes from among the believers and the People of the Scripture.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, he said: The chaste ones.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Amer:
m: h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, he said: The chastity of the Jewish and Christian women: that she does not commit adultery, and that she washes herself from major ritual impurity.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Amer:
m: h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, he said: The chastity of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she washes herself from major ritual impurity, and that she guards her private parts.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, he said: The chastity of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she does not commit adultery, and that she washes herself from major ritual impurity.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, he said: Her chastity is that she washes herself from major ritual impurity, and that she protects her private parts from adultery.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, he said, Mutraf told us, on the authority of Amer,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us:
m: I heard Sufyan say regarding His statement:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture
, he said: The chaste ones.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, he said: As for chaste women, they are the chaste.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A woman took her slave and said: I have interpreted the Book of God: And those whom your right hands possess. He said: She was brought to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have interpreted a verse of the Book of God in a way other than its meaning. He said: So the slave was exiled and his head was cut off and he said: After him, you are forbidden to every Muslim.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said
m: about the woman who commits adultery before he has consummated the marriage with her: She is not entitled to a dowry, and they should be separated.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding a virgin who commits adultery, he said: She should be lashed one hundred times, banished for a year, and she should return to her husband what she took from him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Ash’ath told us on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: something similar.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus 10:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: If a man sees something indecent from his wife and is certain, then he should not keep her.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, who said:
m: The female slaves of the People of the Book are like their free women. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the ruling of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
. Is it general or specific?

x: Some of them said: It is general for chaste women, because the chaste are chaste women. And a Muslim may marry any free woman or slave woman of the People of the Book, whether she is a combatant or a dhimmi. They based this on the apparent meaning of the Almighty’s statement:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, and that what is meant by them are the chaste women, whoever they may be. This is the statement of those who said: What is meant by chaste women in this context is the chaste women.
Others said: Rather, those whom God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you

, are the free women among them, and the verse is general in its application to all of them. So, the marriage of all free Jewish and Christian women is permissible, whether they are warlike or dhimmi, from any race of Jews and Christians. This is the opinion of a group of the early and late scholars.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Hasan:
m: that they saw no harm in marrying Jewish and Christian women, and they said: God permitted it with knowledge.

x: Others of them said: Rather, he meant by that the Surat al-Ma’idah 5:5 Today all good foods have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
h
and your food is lawful for them
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, when
h
you have given them their due compensation

, chaste, not fornicating or taking secret lovers. And whoever disbelieves in the faith - His work has become worthless, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers. marriage of the Children of Israel to the women of the Book among them in particular, without the rest of the nations who followed Judaism and Christianity. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i and those who said the same.
Others said: Rather, it refers to the women of the People of the Book who have a covenant and protection from the Muslims. As for the people of war, their women are forbidden to the Muslims.

Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Uqbah narrated, he said: Al-Fazari narrated, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the women of the People of the Book are those who are permissible for us, and among them are those who are not permissible for us.

“Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah.”

(al-Tawbah 9:29). So whoever pays the jizyah, his women are permissible for us, and whoever does not pay the jizyah, his women are not permissible for us. Al-Hakam said: So I mentioned that to Ibrahim, and he liked it.
The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by His statement:
h
and chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you

is the free believers and People of the Scripture. Because God, the Most High, did not permit marriage to free slave girls in the situation in which He permitted them to do so, unless they were believers. So He, the Most High, said:
And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free, believing women, then from those whom your right hands possess of your believing slave girls
So He did not permit anyone from among them except the believers. So if what was meant by His statement: and chaste women from among the believers
h
and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture

was the chaste, then the chaste ones among their slave girls would be included in the permissibility, and the unchaste ones among their free women and the free women of the people of faith would be excluded.

God has made lawful for us the free women of the believers, even if they have committed an immoral act, as He says: And marry those among you who are single and those of your male slaves and female slaves who are righteous (al-Tawbah 9:29). We have already demonstrated the corruption of the statement of those who said: It is not lawful for believers to marry those women of the believers and the People of the Book who have committed an immoral act, in a place other than this, so there is no need to repeat it here. Marrying free Muslim women and women from the People of the Book is permissible for believers, whether they have committed an immoral act or not, whether they are dhimmis or non-Muslims, provided that they are in a place where the man who marries does not fear that his child will be forced to disbelieve, based on the apparent words of God Almighty:
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you

As for the statement of the one who said: He meant by that the women of the Children of Israel, especially the women of the Book among them, it is a statement that does not require us to be preoccupied with explaining it, because of its anomaly and departure from what the scholars of the nation are upon, of permitting the women of all Jews and Christians. We have demonstrated the corruption of the statement of the one who said this statement from the aspect of analogy in other than this place sufficiently, so we disliked repeating it.
As for his saying: If you give them their wages, then the wage is the compensation that the husband gives to the woman to enjoy her, which is the dowry, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You have given them their due compensation
, meaning: their dowries.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: It is lawful for you to take chaste women from among the believers
h
and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you

, while you are chaste, not fornicators or taking lovers. What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Chaste, is chaste, not fornicators, meaning: not openly committing fornication with any wicked act, which is immorality, nor taking lovers, meaning: nor alone with one prostitute, whom he has taken as his lover and she has taken as his lover, and he has taken her as a friend for himself with whom he commits fornication.
We have explained the meaning of ihsan and its aspects, and the meaning of saffah and khudn in other places, so that there is no need to repeat it in this place, and it is as follows:
