c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Chaste, not fornicators, meaning: they marry them with a dowry and evidence, not fornicators who openly commit adultery, nor take lovers, meaning: they secretly commit adultery.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: God has made two chaste women lawful for us: a chaste believing woman, and a chaste woman from among the People of the Book, nor those who take lovers: the one with a lover, the one with one close friend.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said:
m: A man asked him: Can a man marry a woman from the People of the Book? He said: What does he have to do with the People of the Book, when God has increased the number of Muslim women! If he must do so, then let him go to her in a chaste manner, not in a fornication. The man said: What is a fornication? He said: It is that which, if a man glances at her with his eyes, she follows him.

x: What he means by his saying, may His praise be exalted: And whoever disbelieves in the faith, is whoever denies what God has commanded us to believe in, of the Oneness of God and the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from God, which is the faith, about which God, may His praise be exalted, said: And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his work has become worthless, meaning: the reward for the work he did in this world, hoping to attain a status with God, has been nullified, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers, meaning: and in the Hereafter he will be among the doomed, those who have cheated themselves of their share of God’s reward by their disbelief in Muhammad and their work in disobedience to God. It has been mentioned that his statement,
h
And whoever disbelieves in faith

, refers to the People of the Book, and that it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the sake of a people who were reluctant to marry women of the People of the Book when it was said to them, “Lawful to you are all good things.
The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
h
and your food is lawful for them
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that some Muslims said: How can we marry their women, meaning: the women of the People of the Book - when they are not of our religion? So God Almighty revealed:
h
And whoever disbelieves in faith

- his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers, so God permitted marrying them with knowledge. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of faith, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
And whoever disbelieves in faith
, his work has become worthless, he said: God, faith.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Wasil, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
And whoever disbelieves in faith
, he said: Faith is monotheism.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And whoever disbelieves in faith
, he said: in God.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves in faith
, his work has become worthless, he said: Whoever disbelieves in God.

c: Muhammad told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves in faith
, he said: Whoever disbelieves in God.

c: Muhammad told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves in faith
, he said: disbelief in God.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And whoever disbelieves in faith

, his work has become worthless, he said: God Almighty informed us that faith is the firmest handhold, and that He does not accept any work without it, and He does not forbid Paradise except to the one who abandons it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What is the interpretation of the meaning of his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves in faith
, to mean: And whoever disbelieves in God?
The way to interpret it is that faith is to believe in God and His messengers and what He sent them with of His religion, and disbelief is to deny that.

They said: So the meaning of disbelief in faith is to deny God and deny His Oneness. So they interpreted the meaning of the word with what was intended by it, and they turned away from interpreting the word according to the reality of its words and its apparent meaning in recitation.
What is its interpretation according to its apparent meaning and the truth of its words?

Its interpretation is: And whoever refuses to believe in God, and refrains from believing in His Oneness and obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden him to do, then his work has been in vain. This is because disbelief is denial in the speech of the Arabs, and faith is belief and acknowledgment. And whoever refuses to believe in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:5 Today all good foods have been made lawful for you. The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you
h
and your food is lawful for them
h
And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you
, when
h
you have given them their due compensation
, chaste, not fornicating or taking secret lovers.

And whoever disbelieves in the faith - His work has become worthless, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers. the Oneness of God and acknowledge it, then he is one of the disbelievers. So this is the interpretation of the speech in its proper form.

evidence.text: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, he said, Khasif told us, he said, Ikrimah told us: Ibn Abbas was asked about the sacrifices of the Christians of Banu Taghlib, so he recited this verse: O you who believe, do not take the Jews as allies until His saying: And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed, he is one of them, the verse (al-Ma’idah 5:51).

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O you who believe, if you stand up to pray, and you are not in a state of ritual purity for prayer, then wash your faces with water and your hands up to the elbows. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding his saying:
h
When you rise to prayer
, meaning every situation in which one rises to prayer, or some of them? And what are the situations in which one rises to prayer?

Some of them said something similar to what we said about it, that it refers to some of the situations in which one performs the ritual prayer, not all of the situations, and that the situation that is meant is the situation in which one performs the ritual prayer without being pure.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaidullah told us:
m: Ikrimah was asked about the statement of God:
h
When you rise to prayer
, wash your faces and your forearms up to the elbows, so does one perform ablution every hour? He said: Ibn Abbas said: There is no ablution except for one who has broken his ablution.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, he said,
m: I heard Masʿud Ibn Ali Al-Shaibani say, I heard ʿIkrimah say: Saʿd Ibn Abi Waqqas used to pray the prayers with one ablution.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Sufyan ibn Habib told us, on the authority of Masʿud ibn Ali, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas used to say: Pray with your purity as long as you do not break your ablution.

c: Ahmad bin Abda Al-Dhabi told us, he said, Salim bin Akhdar told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: I said to Ubaidah Al-Salmani: What necessitates ablution? He said: The state of ritual impurity.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Waqiʿ ibn Suhban, on the authority of Yazid ibn Tarif - or:
m: Tarif ibn Yazid - that they were with Abu Musa on the bank of the Tigris, and they performed ablution, and prayed the noon prayer. When the call to the afternoon prayer was made, some men stood up to perform ablution from the Tigris, and he said: There is no ablution except for one who has broken his ablution.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Tarif ibn Ziyad - or:
m: Ziyad ibn Tarif - on the authority of Waqi’ ibn Suhban: that he witnessed Abu Musa praying the noon prayer with his companions, then they sat in circles on the banks of the Tigris, and the call to the afternoon prayer was made, so men stood up to perform ablution, and Abu Musa said: There is no ablution except for one who has broken his ablution.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, he said:
m: I heard Qatada narrating, on the authority of Waqiʿ Ibn Suhban, on the authority of Tarif Ibn Yazid - or: Yazid Ibn Tarif - he said: I was with Abu Musa on the banks of the Tigris, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Waqi’ Ibn Suhban, on the authority of Tarif Ibn Yazid - or:
m: Yazid Ibn Tarif - on the authority of Abu Musa, the same.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, Abu Khalid told us:
m: I performed ablution at Abu al-ʿAliyah’s house for the noon or afternoon prayer, and then I said: Should I pray with this ablution of mine, for I will not return to my family until the dark? Abu al-ʿAliyah said: There is no blame. And we learned: When a person performs ablution, he is in his state of ablution until something happens.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Ibn Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, who said:
m: Ablution without ritual impurity is an act of aggression.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed,
m: the same.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said:
m: I saw Ibrahim praying with one ablution, the noon, afternoon, and sunset prayers.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us:
m: I was with Yahya, and I would pray the prayers with one ablution. He said: And Ibrahim was like that.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, Yazid bin Ibrahim told us:
m: I heard al-Hasan asked about a man who performs ablution and prays all the prayers with one ablution, so he said: There is nothing wrong with it as long as he does not break his ablution.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: He prays the prayers with one ablution as long as he does not break his ablution.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us,
m: he Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. said, Zaydah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara, he said: Al-Aswad used to pray the prayers with one ablution.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: O you who have believed,
h
when you rise to prayer
, he says: you rise while you are not in a state of purity.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Al-Aswad:
m: He had a cup the size of a man’s water, so he would perform ablution, then pray all the prayers with that ablution. Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Musa narrated, saying: Ziyad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Tufayl al-Bakka’i narrated, saying: Al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashar narrated, saying: I saw Jabir ibn Abdullah praying the prayers with one ablution. Then, if he urinated or broke his ablution, he would perform ablution and wipe his socks with the remaining water from his ablution. So I said: Abu Abdullah, is there something you should do in your opinion? He said: Rather, I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do it, so I do it as I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: O you who believe, when you rise from your sleep for prayer.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us,
m: he told me from someone who heard Malik bin Anas, narrating on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, his saying: O you who have believed,
h
when you rise to prayer
, he said: He means: when you rise from sleep.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us: Malik bin Anas told him on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his saying:
h
When you rise to prayer
, wash your faces. He said: You rose to prayer from sleep.

x: Others said: Rather, it means that whenever a person stands up for prayer, he should renew his purity for it.

Who said that? Humayd ibn Masʿadah narrated, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated, on the authority of Masʿud ibn ʿAli, who said: I asked ʿIkrimah, who said: I said: O Abu ʿAbdullah, should I perform ablution for the dawn prayer, then go to the market and the noon prayer comes, so should I pray? He said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, used to say: O you who have believed,
h
when you rise to prayer
, wash your faces and your forearms up to the elbows.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us,
m: I heard Masʿud ibn Ali al-Shaibani say, I heard ʿIkrimah say: ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, used to perform ablution before every prayer, and he would recite this verse: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces, the verse.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us, he said, Azhar told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: The caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, he said:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab performed ablution in a light, permissible manner, and he said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told me, he said, Shu’bah told me, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Maysarah, on the authority of Al-Nazzal, he said:
m: I saw Ali praying the noon prayer, then he sat for the people in the courtyard, then water was brought to him and he washed his face and hands, then he wiped his head and feet and said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Ali measured a quantity of grain, then performed ablution in which he was allowed to do so, and he said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution.

x: Others said: Rather, this was an order from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him: that they should perform ablution for every prayer, then that was abrogated by making it easier.
Who said that?

c: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad Al-Qatwani told me, he said, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban Al-Ansari told me,
m: then Al-Mazini, Mazen Bani Al-Najjar, he said to Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Omar: Tell me about Abdullah’s ablution for every prayer, whether he was pure or not, from whom? He said: Asma bint Zaid bin Al-Khattab told me: “Abdullah bin Hanzala bin Abi Amir Al-Ghasil told her: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded ablution for every prayer, and that was difficult for him, so he commanded the siwak, and ablution was lifted from him except for one who was in a state of ritual impurity. Abdullah thought that he had the strength to do it, so he would perform ablution.”
b.via: Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban Al-Ansari

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah, he said, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban al-Ansari told me, he said:
m: I said to Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Umar: Tell me about Abdullah’s ablution for every prayer, then he mentioned something similar.
b.via: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban al-Ansari

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer.” Then, in the year of the conquest, he performed the prayers with one ablution and wiped over his socks. Umar said: You have done something that you did not do before! He said: You did it intentionally.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. Then, on the day of the conquest of Mecca, he prayed all the prayers with one ablution.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muharrib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah:
m: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was performing ablution, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed all the prayers with one ablution, and Umar said to him: O Messenger of God, did you do something that you did not do before? He said: I did it intentionally, O Umar.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. When he conquered Mecca, he prayed the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers with one ablution.”

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Dhahir told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar,
m: “On the authority of Ibn Umar: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon, afternoon, sunset, and evening prayers with one ablution.”

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: God meant by His saying:
h
When you rise to prayer

, wash, all the states of the one who stands to pray, except that it is an obligatory command to wash what God has commanded the one who stands to pray to wash, after an impurity that invalidates his purity, and before performing ablution, and it is a recommended command for the one who was previously pure, and did not have an impurity that invalidated his purity. Therefore, the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to perform ablution for every prayer before the conquest of Mecca, then he prayed all the prayers on that day with one ablution, so that his nation would know that what he (peace be upon him) used to do of renewing his purity for every prayer was only from him taking advantage of the virtue, and from him giving preference to the most beloved of the two matters to God, and from him hastening to do what his Lord urged him to do, not because it was an obligatory duty for him.

If someone thinks that in the hadith that we mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Hanzala, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered ablution before every prayer, is evidence of the opposite of what we said, that this was recommended for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions - and he imagines that this was obligatory - then he has thought incorrectly. This is because the statement of the speaker: God commanded his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do such and such, is possible in several ways: it is an obligation, a guidance, a recommendation, a permission, and a generalization. Since it is possible in the ways we mentioned, the more appropriate way to say it is that which the evidence is unanimously agreed upon for its authenticity, rather than that which is not proven authentically by evidence that proves the truth of its claimant.

The evidence is unanimous that God Almighty did not make ablution obligatory for his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor for his servants for every prayer, and then abrogated that. In their consensus on that, there is clear evidence of the correctness of what we have said: that the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was as we have described, of his preference for doing what God Almighty urged him to do and urged his believing servants to do with His saying: O you who have believed,
h
when you rise to prayer

, wash your faces and your forearms up to the elbows Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and that his leaving it in the state in which he left it was a concession for his nation, and an announcement from him to them that that was not obligatory nor binding upon him or them, except for someone who has an event that necessitates the breaking of purity.
There are reports similar to what we have said about this:

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Amir,
m: “On the authority of Anas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a small bucket and he performed ablution. He said: I said to Anas: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution before every prayer? He said: Yes! I said: What about you? He said: We used to pray the prayers with one Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. ablution.”

c: Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqi narrated to us, Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Ifriqi, on the authority of Abu Ghutayf, who said:
m: I prayed the noon prayer with Ibn Umar, and he came to a gathering in his house and sat down, and I sat with him. When the call to the afternoon prayer was made, he called for water for ablution and performed ablution, then he went out to pray, then he returned to his gathering. When the call to the sunset prayer was made, he called for water for ablution and performed ablution. I said: What do I see you doing? He said: No, even though my ablution for the dawn prayer is sufficient for all the prayers as long as I do not break my ablution. But I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity, ten good deeds will be recorded for him, so I only desired that.

c: Abu Saeed Al-Baghdadi told me, he said, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, on the authority of Harim, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Ghatif, on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said,
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity will have ten good deeds recorded for him.

x: Some people said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an announcement from God to him that he does not have to perform ablution unless he stands up for his prayer, and not for all other actions. This is because if he broke his ablution, he would refrain from all actions until he performed ablution. So God permitted with this verse that he do whatever actions he wanted after breaking his ablution except for prayer, whether he performed ablution or not, and He commanded him to perform ablution if he stood up for prayer before entering it.

Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Muawiyah bin Hisham narrated, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Amr bin Hazm, on the authority of Abdullah bin Alqamah bin Al-Fughawa, on the authority of his father, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urinated, we would speak to him but he would not speak to us, and we would greet him but he would not respond to us, until he came home and performed ablution as he did for prayer. So we said: O Messenger of God, we speak to you but you do not speak to us, and we greet you but you do not respond to us? He said: Until the verse of permission was revealed: O you who have believed,
h
when you rise to prayer
, the verse.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the definition of the face that God commanded the one who stands for prayer to wash, in His saying: When you stand for prayer, wash your faces.

Some of them said: It is what is visible from the human skin, from the hair on his head, descending to the end of his chin lengthwise, and what is between the ears widthwise. They said: As for the ear and what is hidden inside the mouth, nose and eye, it is not part of the face. It is not obligatory to wash that or wash any of it in ablution. They said: As for what the hair covers from it, such as the chin that is covered by the hair of the beard, and the temples that are covered by the hair of the beard, then passing water over what is on that of the hair is sufficient for washing what is hidden from it of the skin of the face, because the face, according to them, is what is visible to the eye of the beholder and faces it, and nothing else.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Amr bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The beard is sufficient for whatever water flows from its place.

c: Humayd bin Masʿadah told us, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, Shuʿbah told us, Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: What water flows from his face onto his beard is sufficient for him.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughirah
m: regarding combing the beard, he said: Whatever passes over your beard is sufficient for you.

c: Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamdani told us, Musʿab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Mansur, who said:
m: I saw Ibrahim performing ablution and he did not comb his beard.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Zubaidi, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: What flows over it is sufficient for you to clean it.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Yunus, he said:
m: When Al-Hasan performed ablution, he would wipe his beard and his face.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He did not comb his beard.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: He did not comb his beard when he performed ablution.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: Washing the beard is not from the Sunnah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: That when he performed ablution, the water did not reach the roots of his beard.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Abu Shaiba Saeed bin Abdul Rahman Al-Zubaidi
m: who said: I asked Ibrahim: Should I rinse my beard with water when performing ablution? He said: No, what your hand passes over is sufficient for you.
b.via: Abu Shaiba Saeed bin Abdul Rahman Al-Zubaidi

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said,
m: I asked Shuʿbah about combing the beard during ablution, so he said: Al-Mughira said, Ibrahim said: What water flows from his face onto his beard is sufficient for him.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, Hajjaj bin Rushdin told us, Abdul Jabbar bin Omar told us:
m: Ibn Shihab and Rabia performed ablution and poured water over their beards, and I did not see either of them pass water through his beard.

c: Abu Al-Walid Al-Dimashqi told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us:
m: I asked Saeed bin Abdul Aziz about rubbing the sides of the cheeks during ablution, and he said: That is not obligatory. I saw Makhul performing ablution and he did not do that.

c: Abu Al-Walid Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Qurashi told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Saeed bin Bashir told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Rubbing the sides of the body during ablution is not obligatory.

c: Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told me, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: What water passes over his beard is sufficient for him.

c: Abu Al-Walid Al-Qurashi told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Sulayman bin Abi Zaynab, he said:
m: I asked Al-Qasim bin Muhammad: What should I do with my beard when I perform ablution? He said: I am not one of those who wash their beards.

c: Abu Al-Walid told us, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr said:
m: Combing the sideburns and interlacing the beard is not obligatory in ablution.

x: Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article regarding washing what is inside the mouth and nose.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Bashir, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If it were not for licking my lips during prayer, I would not have rinsed my mouth.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Abdul Malik say: Ata’ was asked about a man who prayed and did not rinse his mouth. He said: What is not mentioned in the book is sufficient for him.

c: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Rinsing the mouth and nose are not obligatory in ablution.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, he said:
m: Ad-Dahhak used to forbid us from rinsing the mouth and nose during ablution in Ramadan.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: If he forgets to rinse his mouth and nose, he said: If he remembers and has started the prayer, then let him continue with his prayer. And if he has not started the prayer, then let him rinse his mouth and nose.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hakam and Qatadah about a man who remembered while he was praying that he had not rinsed his mouth or sniffed water in his nose, so he said: He should continue with his prayer.

x: Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article, that the ears are not part of the face:

c: Yazid bin Mukhallad Al-Wasiti told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ghailan, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Omar say: The ears are part of the head.

c: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told us, Abu Matraf told us,
m: Ghailan, a client of Banu Makhzum, told us: I heard Ibn Umar say: The ears are part of the head.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: The ears are part of the head, so when you wipe the head, wipe them.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us,
m: Ghailan bin Abdullah, a client of Quraysh, told me: I heard Ibn Umar asked a questioner, saying: He performed ablution and forgot to wipe his ears. Ibn Umar said: The ears are part of the head. And he did not see anything wrong with that.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Ayoub bin Suwaid told us, and Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim Abu Al-Nadr, on the authority of Saeed bin Marjana, on the authority of Ibn Omar, that he said: The ears are part of the head. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told me, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: The ears are part of the head.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The ears are part of the head.

c: Humaid bin Mas’adah told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said:
m: The ears are part of the head.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: The ears are part of the head - on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed.

c: Abu Al-Walid Al-Dimashqi told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Abu Amr told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said:
m: The ears are part of the head.

c: Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Isa bin Yazid, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: The ears are part of the head.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzay’ told me, he said, Hammad bin Zayd told us, on the authority of Sinan bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah - or: on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: Ibn Buzay’ was not sure - that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ma’la bin Mansur told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Sinan bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said:
m: The ears are part of the head - Hammad said: I do not know if this is from Abu Umamah or: from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Usama told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told me, he said, Sinan bin Rabi’ah Abu Rabi’ah told me, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head.

c: Abu Al-Walid Al-Dimashqi told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj and others told me, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head.

c: Al-Hasan bin Shabib told us, he said, Ali bin Hashim bin Al-Barid told us, he said, Ismail bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The ears are part of the head.

c: Humaid bin Masada told us, Sufyan bin Habib told us, on the authority of Yunus 10:Al-Hasan said:
m: The ears are part of the head.

x: Others said: The face is everything below the hairline of the head to the end of the chin in length, and from ear to ear in width, what is visible to the eye of the observer and what is hidden from it from the hairline of the beard growing on the chin and on the cheekbones, and what is inside the mouth and nose, and what is in front of the ears on the face. All of that, according to them, is from the face that God commanded to be washed in His saying: So wash your faces. They said: If the one who performs ablution leaves something of that and does not wash it, his prayer with that ablution is not valid.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr and Abu Asim told me, they said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Nafi’ told me:
m: Ibn Umar used to wet the roots of his beard’s hair, and he would put his hand into the roots of its hair until the tar was abundant.

c: Hamid bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Sufyan bin Habib told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Rafiʿ, the freed slave of Ibn ʿUmar, told me: Ibn ʿUmar used to put his hands deep in his beard until the tar was abundant.

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said, Abdul Warith told us, on the authority of Saeed, he said, Laith told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: When he performed ablution, he would comb through his beard until he reached the roots of the hair.

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Ma’la bin Jaber Al-Laqiti told us, he said, Al-Azraq bin Qais told me, he said:
m: I saw Ibn Omar performing ablution and combing his beard.

c: Yaqub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Layth told us, on the authority of Nafi’:
m: Ibn Umar used to wet his beard with water until it reached the roots of the hair.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair told me:
m: That his father Ubayd ibn Umair, when he performed ablution, would insert his fingers into the roots of the hair on his face, inserting them between the hair at its roots, rubbing the skin with his fingers - so Abdullah pointed to me as the man had told him, as he had described about him.

c: Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Amr told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: that when he performed ablution, he would rub his cheeks a little, and sometimes intertwine his beard with his fingers, and sometimes leave it.

c: Abu Al-Walid and Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid told us,
m: Abu Amr said, and Abda told me, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, something similar to that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muslim, he said:
m: I saw Ibn Abi Laila performing ablution, then he washed his beard, and he said: Whoever among you can reach the roots of his hair, let him do so.

c: Humayd bin Masʿadah told us, Sufyan bin Habib told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: It is his duty to wet the roots of his hair.

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said:
m: Mujahid used to comb his beard.

c: Hamid told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: that he used to comb his beard when he performed ablution.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Dawud al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Shabramah, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: Why is the beard washed before it grows, but when it grows it is not washed?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: that he used to comb his beard when he performed ablution.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Tawus:
m: that he used to trim his beard.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: that he used to comb his beard.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said,
m: I asked Shuʿbah about combing the beard during ablution, so he mentioned on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah: that Mujahid used to comb his beard.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Maruf, he said:
m: I saw Ibn Sirin performing ablution and combing his beard.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Zubayr Ibn Adi, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: I saw him combing his beard.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Zaid Al-Khudri, on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi,
m: “On the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing ablution and running his fingers through his beard, so I said: Why did you do this, O Prophet of God? He said: My Lord commanded me to do that.”

c: Tamim told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Salam bin Salm, on the authority of Zaid al-Ami, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra - or:
m: Yazid al-Raqashi - “on the authority of Anas, he said: I performed ablution for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he put his fingers under his chin and combed through his beard and said: This is what my Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, commanded me to do.”

c: Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Salam bin Salm Al-Madini, he said, Zaid Al-Ami told us, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abu Ubaidah al-Haddad told us, he said, Musa bin Tharwan told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is what my Lord commanded me! And he put his fingers in his beard and combed it.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Hisham and Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Ilyas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’,
m: “On the authority of Umm Salamah: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and combed his beard.”

c: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Har told us, he said, Muhammad bin Rabia told us, on the authority of Wasil bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Sura,
m: “on the authority of Abu Ayoub, he said: We saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution and comb his beard.”

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, he said, Omar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib,
m: “on the authority of Abu Umamah: that the Prophet, may God bless him and Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. grant him peace, performed ablution and combed his beard.”

c: Muhammad bin Isa Al-Damaghani told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim Abu Umayya:
m: Hassan bin Bilal Al-Muzni saw Ammar bin Yasir performing ablution and combing his beard, so he was asked: Do you do this? He said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do it.

c: Abu al-Walid told us, al-Walid told us, Abu Amr told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi and Qatadah:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, he would rub his cheeks and interlock his beard with his fingers.”

c: Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Mahdi Saeed bin Sinan told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriya, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Tanafisi Abu Abdullah told us, he said, Wasil Al-Raqashi told me, on the authority of Abu Sawda - this is how Al-Ahmasi
m: said it - on the authority of Abu Ayoub, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, he would rinse his mouth and wipe his beard from underneath with water.
b.via: Abu Sawda - this is how Al-Ahmasi

x: Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article regarding washing the inside of the nose and mouth:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say: Rinsing the nose is half of ablution.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, he said:
m: I asked Hammad about a man who remembered while he was praying that he had not rinsed his mouth or sniffed water in his nose. Hammad said: He should turn away, rinse his mouth and sniff water in his nose.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, he said:
m: I went to Kufa and went to Hammad and asked him about that - meaning: about someone who left rinsing the mouth and nose and prayed - and he said: I think he must repeat the prayer.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, Shuʿbah told us:
m: Qatada used to say: If he leaves out rinsing his mouth, or inhaling water, or his ear, or a part of his foot, until he enters his prayer, then he should turn away, perform ablution, and repeat his prayer.

x: Mention of those who said what we have narrated from the people of this article, that what is in front of the ears is from the face, and what is behind is from the head:

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: What is in front of the ears is from the face, and what is behind it is from the head.

c: Humayd bin Masʿadah told us, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, Shuʿbah told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam and Hammad, on the authority of Al-Shaʿbi,
m: regarding the ears: their inner parts are part of the face, and their outer parts are part of the head.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi, he said:
m: The front of the ears is part of the face, and the back of them is part of the head.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam and Hammad, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: similarly, except that he said: the inside of the ears.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Al-Shaʿbi,
m: similarly, except that he said: the inside of the ears.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Al-Shaʿbi,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: The inner parts of the ears are part of the face, and their outer parts are part of the head.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Abu Tamila told us, and Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us,
m: they both said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah told me, on the authority of Ubayd God al-Khawlani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Shall I not perform ablution for you as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did? He said: We said: Yes! So he performed ablution, and when he washed his face, he put his thumbs in the front of his ears. He said: Then when he wiped his head, he wiped his ears from the backs of them.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: The face that God Almighty commanded the one who is standing for prayer to wash is everything that descends from the hairline of the head to the end of the chin in length, and between the ears in width, of what is apparent to the eye of the observer, without what is hidden of the mouth, nose, and eyes, and without what is covered by the hair of the beard, cheeks, and moustache, concealing it from the sight of observers, and without the ears. We said that this is more correct, even if what is under the hair of the beard and moustache was a face that must be washed before the growth of hair covering the eyes of onlookers, for the one who is standing for his prayer, because they all agree that the eyes are part of the face. Then, with their agreement on that, they are unanimous that washing what is above them of the eyelids without letting the water reach what is under the eyelids of them is sufficient.

If this was a consensus from them, by the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, informing his nation of this, then similar to that is everything that is covered by something from the places of ablution on the body of the son of Adam from his very creation, covering it, the water does not reach it except with cost, effort, and treatment, by analogy to what we mentioned about the ruling on the eyes in this regard. If this is the case, then there is no doubt that the same as the eyes in terms of the difficulty of getting water to them when performing ablution, is what is inside of the nose, mouth, beard hair, temples, and moustache, because water cannot reach all of that except through treatment to get water to it, such as the cost of treating the pupils to get water to them or worse. If this is the case, it is clear that those of the Companions and Followers who washed what was under the hairline of the beard, the cheeks, and the moustache, and what was inside the nose and mouth, were only preferring the more difficult of two matters for him: washing that, and leaving it, just as Ibn Umar preferred washing what was under the eyelids with water by pouring water into that, not because that was an obligatory duty for him.

As for the one who thought that their action was obligatory and mandatory, he has contradicted them in that by saying it is their method, and he has neglected the path of analogy, because analogy is what we have described of representing the disputed matter in that, with the agreed upon principle of the ruling on the eyes, and that there is no report from one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that obligated the one who neglected to let the water reach the roots of the hair of his beard and his cheeks in his ablution, and the one who neglected rinsing the mouth and nose, to repeat his prayer if he prayed with that purity. In that is the clearest evidence of the correctness of what we said, that their action, what they did, was a preference on their part for the better of the two actions, of neglecting and washing. If someone thinks that in the report that was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: If one of you performs ablution, let him blow his nose.

As evidence of the obligation of istinsar, the consensus of the argument is that it is not an obligatory duty, and that whoever leaves it must repeat the prayer that he prayed before washing, which makes it unnecessary to say much about it. As for the ears, the consensus of all of them is that leaving them out, or washing what is in front of them with the face, does not invalidate the prayer of the one who prays with the purity in which he left them out, along with their consensus that if he left out washing something that he must wash of his face in his ablution, then his prayer is not valid with that purity, which indicates that the statement in that is what the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, whose statement we mentioned: that they are not part of the face, not what Al-Sha’bi said.

The people of interpretation differed regarding elbows. Are they part of the hand that must be washed, or not? After all of them agreed that washing the hand to them is obligatory. Malik bin Anas said, and he was asked about the statement of God: So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, do you think that the elbows should be left behind in ablution? He said: What was commanded is to reach the elbows, God the Blessed and Exalted said: So wash your faces, so this one went to wash behind him!! So it was said to him: So he should only wash up to the elbows and the ankles and not go beyond them?
He said: I do not know what does not go beyond them, as for what he was commanded to reach it is this:

c: to the elbows and the ankles - Yunus told us, on the authority of Ashhab,
m: on his authority. Al-Shafi’i said: I do not know of anyone who disagrees that the elbows are among what should be washed. It seems that he believes that its meaning is: Wash your faces and hands until you wash the elbows.

c: Al-Rabi’ told us
m: about that from him.

x: Others said: God made obligatory in His statement:
h
And your hands to the elbows

, washing the hands to the elbows. The elbows are the limit of what God made obligatory to wash from the end of the hand, and the limit is not included in the definition, just as He changed the night from what God made obligatory for His servants to fast with His statement:
h
Then complete the fast until the night (al-Baqarah 2
:187). Because the night is the limit of the fast of the fasting person, if he reaches it he has fulfilled what is required of him. They said: Likewise the elbows in His statement:
h
Then wash your faces and your hands to the elbows
, are the limit of what God made obligatory to wash from the hand. This is the statement of Zafar ibn al-Hudhayl.

The correct statement regarding this matter, according to us, is that washing the hands up to the elbows is an obligation, and if one leaves it or part of it, his prayer will not be valid if he leaves it out. As for the elbows and what is beyond them, washing that is recommended, which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged his nation to do by saying: My nation will have radiant faces and white foreheads Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it.

God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. from the effects of ablution. So whoever among you can lengthen his radiance, let him do so. The prayer of one who neglects to wash them and what is behind them is not invalidated, because we have explained previously in what came before: that every purpose that is limited to to may in the speech of the Arabs include the purpose in the definition or its exclusion from it. If the speech includes that, then it is not permissible for anyone to rule that it is included in it, except for someone whose disagreement is not permissible in what is between him and a ruling and a ruling that the elbows are included, so what must be washed according to us is from someone whose ruling must be accepted.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the wiping that God commanded in His saying:
h
And wipe over your heads
Some of them said: Wipe whatever you want to wipe on your heads with water when you stand up for prayer.
Who said that?

c: Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us, Hammad bin Masada told us, on the authority of Isa bin Hafs, who said:
m: Wiping the head was mentioned in the presence of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, so he said: O Nafi’, how did Ibn Umar wipe? He said: One wipe. And he described that he wiped the front of his head to his face, so Al-Qasim said: Ibn Umar is the most knowledgeable and most learned of us.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said:
m: I heard Yahya bin Saeed say: Nafi’ told me: When Ibn Omar performed ablution, he would return his hands to the water and put them in it, then wipe the front of his head with his hands.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakir told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Nafi’ told me:
m: Ibn Umar used to place the palm of his right hand on the water, then he would not shake it, then he would wipe with it the area between his horns to the forehead once, then he would not do more than that. In each of that, he would wipe once, moving from the forehead to the horn.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed Al-Ansari, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: that when he performed ablution, he would wipe the front of his head.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abd Al-A’la Al-Tha’labi, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, he said:
m: It is sufficient for you to wipe the front of your head if you are performing Umrah. And the woman should do the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abdullah Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Nafi’, he said:
m: I saw Ibn Umar wipe his forehead once. Sufyan said: If he wiped a hair, it would suffice him, meaning one.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Abd al-Salam bin Harb told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Whichever side of your head you touch the water on, that is sufficient for you.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ali bin Dhibyan told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Whichever side of your head you touch the water on, that is sufficient for you.

c: Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Azraq, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, he said:
m: Ibn Umar used to wipe his head like this, so Ayoub placed his palm in the middle of his head, then he passed it over the front of his head.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said:
m: If he wipes his head with one finger, that is sufficient for him.

c: Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi told us, he said, al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said:
m: I said to Abu Amr: What is sufficient for wiping the head? He said: I prefer wiping the front of your head to the back of your head.

c: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me, on the authority of his father,
m: on his authority, something similar.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Wipe your entire head. They said: If he does not wipe his entire head with water, his prayer with that ablution is not valid.
Who said that?

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said, Malik said:
m: Whoever wipes part of his head but does not wipe it completely, must repeat the prayer, just as if he washed part of his face or part of his arm. He said: Malik was asked about wiping the head, he said: He begins from the front of his face, then moves his hands to the back of his head, then returns them to where he started.

x: Others said: Wiping the head with less than three fingers is not sufficient. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad.

The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, commanded wiping one’s head while standing for prayer, along with everything else that He commanded one to wash or wipe with it, and He did not set a limit for that which it is not permissible to fall short of or exceed. Since that is the case, then whatever the person performing ablution wipes from his head deserves to be said: He wiped his head, for he has fulfilled what God has enjoined upon him in wiping that, because it is included in what is required of him by the name of one wiping his head when he stands for prayer.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: God said about dry ablution: Then wipe over your faces and your hands
r
(An-Nisa’: 43)
, so is wiping part of the face and hands sufficient in dry ablution?

Everything that is wiped with dirt, in what the scholars disputed, some of them said: It is sufficient for him as dry ablution, and some of them said: It is not sufficient for him, so it is sufficient for him, because it is included in the name of those who wipe with it. And whatever of that was agreed upon as not being sufficient, then it is accepted because of what the proof brought from its Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And no one has any proof against us in that, since it was from our saying: What came in the verses of the Book is general in meaning, so the rule is that it is general, until what must be accepted is made specific to it. So if something is made specific from it, then what was made specific from it is outside its apparent meaning and the rule for the rest of it is general. We have explained the reason for the validity of this statement in other places, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
The head that God Almighty commanded us to wipe with His saying:
h
And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
, is the hair on the head, not including what goes beyond that to the nape of the neck, and not including what descends from that, facing the face to the forehead.
The reading of this differed.
A group of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as:
h
And your feet to the ankles
, in the accusative case. Its interpretation is: When you stand up for prayer, wash your faces
h
and your hands to the elbows
h
and your feet to the ankles

, and wipe your heads. If it is read like this, it is from the deferred meaning of bringing forward, and the feet would be in the accusative case in apposition to the hands. The reciters of this interpreted it like this, that God, the Most High, only commanded His servants to wash the feet, not wipe them. It was mentioned that he said: God meant by His saying:
h
And your feet to the ankles
, washing.

c: Humayd bin Masʿadah told us, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, Khalid Al-Hadhaʿ told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah,
m: that a man prayed and there was a nail spot on the back of his foot. When he finished his prayer, Umar said to him: Repeat your ablution and your prayer.

c: Hamid told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Israel told us, Abdullah bin Hassan told us, Hazil bin Sharhabil told us, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said:
m: Wet your fingers with water, do not wet them with fire.

c: Abdullah bin Al-Sabah Al-Attar told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar Al-Hawdi told us, he said, Marji told us
m: - meaning: Ibn Raja Al-Yashkari - he said, Abu Ruh Amara bin Abi Hafsa told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Hunayn: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man performing ablution while he was washing his feet, so he said: This is what I was commanded to do.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Waqid,
m: the freed slave of Zayd ibn Khalidah, he said: I heard Musʿab ibn Saʿd say: Umar ibn al-Khattab saw some people performing ablution, so he said: Make vinegar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said:
m: I heard Yahya say, I heard Al-Qasim say: Ibn Omar used to take off his shoes, then perform ablution, wash his feet, then interlace his toes.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn Adi, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: I said to al-Aswad: Did you see Umar washing his feet? He said: Yes.

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, he said, Muhammad bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Maysarah, on the authority of Umar bin Abdul Aziz:
m: He said to Ibn Abi Suwaid: We have been informed of three people, all of whom saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, washing his feet, the closest of them being your cousin Al-Mughira.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Muhammad -
m: who is Ibn Aban - on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: Wash the feet up to the ankles.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Abu Qilabah:
m: That Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a man who had left something like a fingernail on the back of his foot, so he ordered him to repeat his ablution and prayer.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Shaiba ibn Nasah, he said:
m: I accompanied Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad to Mecca, and I saw him, when he performed ablution for prayer, put his toes in and pour water over them. I said: O Abu Muhammad, why do you do this? He said: I saw Ibn Umar do it.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us:
m: I heard my father, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement:
h
So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows and wipe over your heads and your feet up to the ankles
, he said: The matter returned to washing.

c: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hafs Al-Ghadiri, on the authority of Amer bin Kulayb, on the authority of Abu Surat al-Ma’idah 5:
m: 6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. Abd Al-Rahman, he said: Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, recited to me, and they recited:
h
And your feet to the ankles
, so Ali, may God be pleased with him, heard that - and he was judging between people - so he said: And your feet, this is from the introduction and the delay of speech.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he read it:
h
And wipe over your heads
and your feet in the accusative case, and he said: The matter returned to washing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father:
m: that he read it: and your feet, and he said: The matter returned to washing.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: that he used to read: and your feet, in the accusative case.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles
. As for and your feet up to the ankles, he says: Wash your faces, wash your feet, and wipe your heads. This is an example of advancing and delaying.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Shaiban, he said:
m: It was proven to me on the authority of Ali that he read: And your feet.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father:
m: And your feet, the matter goes back to washing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said:
m: The companions of Abdullah used to recite it: And your feet, and they would wash them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: Wash the feet up to the ankles.

c: Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told me, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Sawda, on the authority of Ibn Abd Al-Khair, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I saw Ali perform ablution and wash the tops of his feet, and he said: If I had not seen the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do that, I would have thought that the bottom of the foot was more deserving than the top of it.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: I did not see anyone wiping over the feet.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that he read:
h
And your feet to the ankles
, and he put it in the accusative case and said: It refers back to washing.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said,
m: I heard Al-A’mash read: And your feet, in the accusative case.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said:
m: Malik was asked about the statement of God,
h
And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles

, is it: your feet or: your feet? He said: It is only washing, not wiping. Do not wipe the feet, they are washed. It was said to him: What do you think of someone who wipes? Is that sufficient for him? He said: No. Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
And wipe over your heads
and your feet, he said: Wash them thoroughly.

x: Others from the Hijaz and Iraq recited it as: And wipe your heads and your feet, lowering the feet. The reciters of this interpreted it as: God only commanded His servants to wipe the feet during ablution without washing them, and they made the feet in apposition to the head, so they lowered them for that reason.
Mention of those who said that from the people of interpretation:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muhammad bin Qais Al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Ablution is two washings and two wipings. Humayd ibn Masʿadah narrated, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, on the authority of Humayd, and Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated, saying: Humayd narrated, saying: Musa ibn Anas said to Anas while we were with him: O Abu Hamza, al-Hajjaj delivered a sermon to us in Ahwaz and we were with him, and he mentioned purification and said: Wash your faces and your hands, and wipe your heads and your feet. There is nothing in the son of Adam closer to his filth than his feet, so wash their insides, their backs, and their heels. Anas said: God has spoken the truth and al-Hajjaj has lied. God said: And wipe your heads and your feet. Anas used to wet his feet when he wiped them.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Muammil told us, Hammad told us, Asim al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Anas, who said:
m: The Qur’an was revealed regarding wiping, and the Sunnah is washing.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Musa ibn Anas, he said:
m: Al-Hajjaj delivered a sermon and said: Wash your faces, your hands, and your feet, their backs, their palms, and their heels, for that is closer to the most impure among you. Anas said: God spoke the truth and Al-Hajjaj lied. God said:
h
And wipe over your heads
and wipe over your feet to the ankles.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ubayd God al-Atki told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: There is no washing required of the feet, only wiping was revealed concerning them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, who said:
m: Wipe over your head and your feet.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Gabriel came down with the wiping. He said: Then Al-Sha’bi said: Do you not see that dry ablution is to wipe what was washed and nullify what was wiped?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: He was commanded to perform dry ablution as he was commanded to perform full ablution.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told me, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, that he said:
m: It is only wiping over the feet. Do you not see that what was required to be washed, was required to be wiped, and what was required to be wiped was neglected?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, that he said:
m: He was commanded to wipe in dry ablution what he was commanded to wash in ablution, and he invalidated what he was commanded to wipe in ablution: the head and the feet.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: He was commanded to wipe with earth in dry ablution what he was commanded to wash with water, and he neglected what he was commanded to wipe with water.

c: Ibn Abi Ziyad told us, Yazid told us, Ismail told us:
m: I said to Amerah, some people say that Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with washing the feet! He said: Gabriel came down with wiping.

c: Abu Bishr Al-Wasiti Ishaq bin Shahin told us, he said, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Yunus, he said, someone who accompanied Ikrimah to Wasit told me:
m: I did not see him wash his feet, he only wiped over them, until he came out of it.
b.via: someone who accompanied Ikrimah to Wasit

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: O you who have believed,
h
when you rise to prayer
, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
, God has made two washings and two wipings obligatory.
