c: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of Alqamah:
m: that he read: And your feet, with the lam in the lowered position.

c: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Al-Hussein Al-Akli told us, on the authority of Abdul-Warith, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: that he used to recite: And your feet.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, he said,
m: Al-Sha’bi used to recite: And your feet, in the accusative case.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saleh, on the authority of Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Jaafar:
m: that he read: And your feet, in the accusative case.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: that he read: And your feet, with a kasra.

x: The correct opinion in our view on this matter is that God, the Exalted, commanded the general wiping of the feet with water in ablution, just as He commanded the general wiping of the face with earth in dry ablution. If the person performing ablution does that to them, he deserves the name of a washer-washer, because washing them means passing water over them or touching them with water, and wiping them means passing the hand or something that takes the place of the hand over them. So if someone does that to them, then he is a washer-washer. Therefore - due to the possibility of wiping the two meanings described as general and specific, one of which is wiping with some, and the other wiping with all - the reading of the recitation differed in his saying: and your feet, so some of them put it in the accusative case, directing that to the fact that the obligation in them is washing, and denying wiping over them, with the apparent narrations from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the generality of wiping them with water.

Some of them lowered it, indicating that wiping is obligatory in both cases. And since we said in the interpretation of that - that it means the generality of wiping the feet with water - those who disliked the one performing ablution to suffice with putting his feet in the water without wiping them with his hand or with what takes the place of the hand, directed his saying:
h
And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles

, to wiping all of them in general with the hand, or with what takes the place of Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity
, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it.
So wipe over your faces and your hands with it.

God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. the hand, without some of them, with washing them with water, as:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us
m: - Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar - on the authority of al-Ahwal, on the authority of Tawus that he was asked about a man who performs ablution and puts his feet in the water, he said: I do not consider that to be a great sin. And those who permitted it permitted it, indicating that it is meant for ablution, as:

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard Hisham mention, on the authority of Al-Hasan, about a man performing ablution on a ship, he said: There is nothing wrong with him immersing his feet in it.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said: Abu Hura told me, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding a man who performs ablution on the edge of a ship, he said: He shakes his feet in the water. If the two meanings of wiping that we have described are: the generality of the feet with water, and the specificity of some of them with it, and it is correct with the indicative evidence that we will mention later, that what God intended by wiping them is generality, and their generality has the meaning of washing and wiping, then it is clear that the correctness of reading both readings, I mean the accusative for the feet and the genitive for the feet, is clear. Because in the generality of the feet by wiping them with water is washing them, and in passing the hand and what takes the place of the hand over them is wiping them. The correct reading of those who read it in the accusative case is that it is general in meaning by passing water over them. The correct reading of those who read it in the lowered form is because that involves passing the hand over them, or what takes the place of the hand, wiping them. However, even if that is the case, and both readings are good and correct, the reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who reads it with a dhammah, because of what I described of wiping combining the two meanings that I described, and because it is after His saying: And wipe your heads, so linking it to the heads, despite its proximity to it, is more appropriate than linking it to the hands, and it was prevented from it by His saying: And wipe your heads.

x: What is the evidence that what is meant by wiping the feet is general, without being specific, similar to what you said about wiping the head?

The evidence for that is the apparent hadiths “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Woe to the heels and soles of the feet from the Fire.” If wiping part of the foot was sufficient for its generality, then there would be no woe for it for leaving what it left to wipe with water after wiping part of it. Because whoever fulfills God’s obligation upon him in what he is required to wash of it, does not deserve woe, rather he should have a great reward. In the obligation of woe for the heel of one who leaves out washing his heel in his ablution, there is the clearest evidence for the obligation of the generality of wiping the entire foot with water, and the correctness of what we said about that, and the invalidity of what contradicts it. Mentioning some of the report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as we mentioned:

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said:
m: Abu Hurayrah would pass by while we were performing ablution in the water-tub, and he would say: Perform ablution thoroughly, perform ablution thoroughly! Abu al-Qasim said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar, except that he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, he said:
m: “Abu Hurairah used to pass by people who were performing ablution but were not doing it properly, and he would say: Perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard Abu Al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said something similar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, he said, Sulayman bin Bilal told me, he said, Suhayl told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen and Ismail bin Musa told me, they said, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Saleh, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said,
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire, and Ismail said in his hadith: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, Husayn al-Muʿallim told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Salim al-Dawsi, who said:
m: I entered with Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr upon Aisha, and he asked for water for ablution. Aisha said: O Abd al-Rahman, perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ikrimah ibn Ammar told us, he said, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, he said, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, he said,
m: Abu Salim, the freed slave of al-Mahri told me - this is how Umar ibn Yunus said - he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr and I went out for the funeral of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas. He said: Abd al-Rahman and I passed by the room of Aisha, the sister of Abd al-Rahman, and Abd al-Rahman asked for water for ablution, and I heard Aisha calling out to him: O Abd al-Rahman, perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Amer told us, he said, Ali Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Salim,
m: the freed slave of Dos, he said: I heard Aisha say to her brother Abd Al-Rahman: O Abd Al-Rahman, perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Yaqub and Suwar bin Abdullah told me, they said: Yahya al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Saʿid bin Abi Saʿid, on the authority of Abu Salamah,
m: that Aisha saw Abd al-Rahman performing ablution and she said: Perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said:

c: Ibn Uyaynah and Yahya ibn Saeed al-Qattan narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Saeed, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said:
m: Aisha saw Abd al-Rahman performing ablution, and she said: Perform ablution thoroughly, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: Abu Zur’ah Wahb God ibn Rashid told us: Haywah ibn Shuraih told us: Abu Al-Aswad told us:
m: Abu Abdullah, the freed slave of Shaddad ibn Al-Haad told him: He entered upon Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abd Al-Rahman was with her. Abd Al-Rahman performed ablution, then stood up and turned away. Aisha called out to him and said: O Abd Al-Rahman! So he turned to her, and she said to him: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yahya ibn Saʿid told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, he said, Abu Ishaq told me, on the authority of Saʿid - or Shuʿayb - ibn Abi Karb, he said:
m: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.
b.via: Saʿid - or Shuʿayb - ibn Abi Karb

c: Khallad bin Aslam told us, he said, Al-Nadr told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said,
m: I heard Ibn Abi Karb say, I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say, I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Woe to the heels - or: the heels - from the Fire.”

c: Ismail bin Mahmoud Al-Hujairi told me, he said, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said,
m: I heard Saeed say, I heard Jabir say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah bin Muharrib told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Aban, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: I heard with my own ears from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Sabah bin Muharib told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Aban, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: I heard with my own ears from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform ablution thoroughly.

c: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man performing ablution and something remained from his heel, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.”

c: Ali bin Muslim told me, he said,
m: Abd al-Samad bin Abd Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. al-Warith told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution, but the water did not reach their heels, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.”

c: Abu Sufyan al-Ghanawi Yazid bin Amr told us, he said, Khalaf bin al-Walid told us, he said, Ayoub bin Utbah told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Mu’ayqib, he said,
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution, and he saw their heels shining, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform the prayer perfectly.”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal Ibn Yassaf, on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-Aʿraj, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution but they had not completed it, so he said: Perform the prayer perfectly, woe to the heels - or: the heels - from the Fire.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of a man from the people of Mecca, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution but they did not complete it, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution and their heels were shining, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform ablution thoroughly.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Abu Yahya,
m: the freed slave of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, between Mecca and Medina, and some people preceded us and performed ablution. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and saw their feet white from the traces of ablution, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform ablution thoroughly.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Mutrah bin Yazid, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Zahr, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! He said: There was no noble or lowly person left in the mosque except that I looked at him turning his heels and looking at them.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Layth, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah - or:
m: Abu Umamah’s brother - “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution, and on the heel of one of them - or: the heel of one of them - there was a spot the size of a dirham - or: the spot of a fingernail - that had not been touched by water, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire! So he said: So if a man saw something on his heel that the water had not touched, he would repeat his ablution.”

x: If someone says: What do you say about what he told you? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’, on the authority of his father, “On the authority of Aws bin Abi Aws, he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution and wipe over his shoes, then he stood up and prayed.” What he told you: Abdullah bin Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal said, my father told me, he said, Jarir bin Hazim told us, he said, I heard Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s sandal and urinated on it while standing, then he called for water, performed ablution and wiped over his shoes.” What he told you: Al-Harith said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, Hisham told us, Yaʿla bin Ataʿ told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aws bin Abi Aws, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, come to the courtyard of a people, perform ablution, and wipe over his feet.

What is similar to this from the hadiths indicating that wiping part of the feet during ablution is sufficient? It was said to him: As for the hadith of Aws ibn Abi Aws, there is no evidence in it for the authenticity of that, since there was no mention in the report that was narrated from him that he saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution after an impurity that required him to perform ablution for his prayer, so he wiped over his shoes or his feet.

It is possible that his wiping over his feet, which Aws mentioned, was in an ablution that he performed without an impurity that required him to renew his ablution, because the report from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that if he performed ablution for something other than an impurity, he would do the same, is indicated by what:

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me, he said, Abu Malik Al-Junbi told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Habbah Al-Arni, he said:
m: I saw Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, drinking in the courtyard while standing, then he performed ablution and wiped over his shoes. He said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. This is what I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do. This report has confirmed the correctness of what we said about the meaning of the hadith of Aws.

x: The hadith of Aws, even if it is possible in meaning what I said, is also possible in meaning what was said by the one who said that it is meant to be wiping over the shoes or feet in an ablution that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed after a state of ritual impurity?

The best cases of the report are those that carry what I said, if what was claimed of its possibility is accepted, what was mentioned about wiping the foot or the shoe after the impurity, even if that is not possible according to us, since it is not permissible for the obligations of God and the Sunnahs of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be contradictory and conflicting, and it has been authenticated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, the command to wash the feet in ablution with water in general, by the widespread transmission that conclusively excuses whoever reaches it and is informed of it. And since that is authentic from him, it is not permissible for it to be authentic from him permitting the omission of washing some of what he obligated to wash obligatorily, in one case and at one time. Because that is obligating an obligation and invalidating it in one case. And that is absent from the rulings of God and the rulings of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. However, if we accept what was claimed in the hadith of Aws, that it is possible that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped his foot while performing ablution after a major ritual impurity, out of our confidence in his argument that he has no proof for that, we say: If what you claimed is possible, is what we said possible, that it was done by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while performing ablution after a major ritual impurity?

If he said no, his stubbornness is proven, because there is no statement in the hadith of Aws that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that in the ablution of someone who had become impure. And if he said: Rather, it is possible for what I said, and possible for what we said. He was asked: What is the proof that your interpretation, which you claimed, is more appropriate than our interpretation? He will not claim evidence for the validity of his claim in this regard, except that it will be countered by something similar in opposition to his claim. As for the hadith of Hudhayfah, the trustworthy preservers of hadith from the companions of Al-A’mash narrated it, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the courtyard of a people and urinated while standing, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks.”

c: Ahmad bin Abda Al-Dhabi told us that.
m: He said: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Abu Kuraib and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Issa bin Othman bin Issa Al-Ramli told me, he said, my uncle Yahya bin Issa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah. H, Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah. All of these people narrate this from Al-A'mash with the chain of transmission we mentioned from Hudhayfah: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped over his socks." They are the companions of Al-A'mash. No one narrated this hadith from Al-A'mash except Jarir ibn Hazim. If no one had disagreed with him on this, it would have been necessary to verify it because of its anomaly. So how about when the trustworthy companions of Al-A'mash disagree with him in his narration of what he narrated of this!! If this was authentic from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it would have been permissible for him to have wiped over his shoes while they were worn over his socks. If this was permissible, then no one could have diverted the report to one of the possible meanings of the report except with an argument that must be accepted.

x: The people of interpretation differed Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. regarding the heel.

Some of them said: Ahmad bin Hazim Al-Ghafari told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Al-Qasim bin Al-Fadl Al-Hadani told us, he said, Abu Jaafar said: Where are the ankles? The people said: Here. He said: This is the top of the leg, but the ankles are at the joint.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said, Malik said:
m: The heel towards which ablution must be performed is the heel attached to the leg, parallel to the heel, and not the one visible on the outside of the foot.

x: Others said: Al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Al-Shafi’i said: I do not know of anyone who disagrees that the two heels that God mentioned in His Book regarding ablution are the two protruding ones, and they are the joint of the shin and foot.
The correct statement about this is that the heels are the two bones in the joint of the leg and foot, which the Arabs call the ankles.

Some scholars of Arabic speech used to say: They are the two bones of the leg at its end. Scholars differed about the obligation of washing them in ablution, and the extent to which washing should reach on the feet, similar to their difference of opinion about the obligation of washing the elbows, and the extent to which washing should reach on the hands. We have mentioned that and provided evidence for the correct opinion with its reasons in what has passed before, so there is no need to repeat it.
What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, is that if you are in a state of major ritual impurity before you stand up for your prayer and you stand up for it, then purify yourselves, meaning: purify yourselves by washing yourself before you enter into the prayer that you have stood up for. The word al-Janub is a noun that is used to describe all of them, because it is a noun that is used as a verb, as is said: A just man and just people, “A false man and false people,” and the like. The wording of one, all, two, male, and female is one. It is said: the man became impure, became impure, and avoided. The action is impurity and impurity. He heard in his collection of Ajnab, and this is not widespread in the speech of the Arabs, but rather the eloquent of their speech is what came in the Qur’an.

What He, the Most High, means by His saying: If you are wounded or sick, and you are in a state of major ritual impurity. We have already explained that this is the case in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his statement: or on a journey, he is saying: And if you are travelling and you are in a state of major ritual impurity, or one of you comes from the toilet, meaning: or one of you comes from the toilet and has relieved himself in it while he is travelling. What he meant by mentioning his coming from it is relieving himself in it, or you have touched women, meaning: or you have intercourse with women while you are travelling. We have already mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differed in the past regarding touching, and we have explained the most correct of the opinions on that in the past, so there is no need to repeat it.
What is the reason for repeating his statement: or you have touched women, if the meaning of touching is sexual intercourse, and what is required of him has already been mentioned in his statement:
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity
, then purify yourselves?
The reason for repeating this is that the meaning that the Most High obligated him to do in his statement:
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity
, purify yourselves, is not the meaning that he obligated him to do in his statement: or have touched women. That is because he explained his ruling in his statement:
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves, if he has access to water that purifies him, so he obligated him to perform ablution with it. Then he explained his ruling if he lacked water and could not find access to it and he was a traveler, not a sick resident, so he informed him that tayammum with earth would purify him in that case.
What God, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
But if you find no water

, then perform tayammum with clean earth, is that if you do not find any, O believers, when you stand up for prayer and you are sick and resident, or on a journey and healthy, or one of you has come from relieving himself, or has had intercourse with his wife while travelling! Water, then perform tayammum with clean earth, meaning: then deliberately and aim to touch the surface of the earth, clean, meaning: pure and clean, not dirty or impure, permissible and lawful for you, and wipe your faces and your hands with it, meaning: then strike with your hands the earth that you performed tayammum with and deliberately struck with your hands, then wipe your faces and hands from what has stuck to your hands, from it, meaning: from the earth that you struck with your hands, from its dust and dirt. We have previously explained how to wipe the faces and hands with it, and the differences of opinion among those who differ on that, and the statement on the meaning of the ground and dry ablution, and we have provided evidence for the correct statement on all of that, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
What God Almighty means by His statement,
h
God does not want to place any difficulty on you

, is that God does not want, by what He has imposed on you of ablution when you stand up for your prayer, and ritual washing after sexual impurity, and dry ablution with clean earth when you do not have water, to place any difficulty on you, to impose upon you hardship in your religion and not to make you suffer in it. And what we said about the meaning of hardship, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Dinar, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, and on the authority of Abu Makin, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: from difficulty, they said: from tightness.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: From hardship, from tightness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: But He wants to purify you, is that God wants to purify you, by what He has imposed upon you of ablution from ritual impurity, ritual washing from major ritual impurity, and dry ablution when there is no water, so that you may clean and purify your bodies from sins, as:

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, Saʿid told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, ablution expiates what came before it, and then the prayer becomes voluntary. I said: “Did you hear that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” He said: Yes, not once, not twice, not three, not four, not five.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah Siddi bin Ajlan, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti told us:

c: Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Mardanbah al-Qurashi told us: Ruqabah ibn Musaqala al-Abdi told us, on the authority of Shamr ibn Atiyah, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then stands up to pray, his sins will leave his hearing, sight, hands, and feet.’”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Jaʿd, on the authority of Kaʿb bin Murrah, he said,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is no man who performs ablution, washing his hands or arms, except that his sins come out of them. So when he washes his face, his sins come out of his face. So when he wipes his head, his sins come out of his head. So when he washes his feet, his sins come out of his feet.’”

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed narrated to us, he said, Hatim narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Abu Ubaid,
m: the freed slave of Sulayman bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Amr bin Abasa, that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When a believer washes his hands, his sins fall from his hands. When he rinses his mouth and nose, his sins come out of his mouth and nostrils. When he washes his face, they come out of his face until they come out from the eyelashes. When he washes his hands, they come out of his hands. When he wipes his head and ears, they come out from his head and ears. When he washes his feet, they come out until they come out from the nails of his toes. When he has finished his ablution, that is his portion of it. If he stands and prays two rak’ahs, turning his face and heart to his Lord, his sins will be as if they were on the day his mother bore him.

c: Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi told us, he said, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, he said, Malik ibn Anas told me, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When a Muslim servant - or a believer - performs ablution and washes his face, every sin he has looked at with his eyes will leave his face with the water - or with the last drop of water, or something like that - and when he washes his hands, every sin his hands have committed will leave his hands with the water - or with the last drop of water - until he emerges pure from sins.”

c: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told us, he said, Ali bin Ayyash told us, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Zaid bin Aslam told us, on the authority of Hamran,
m: the freed slave of Uthman, he said, I brought Uthman bin Affan some ablution water while he was sitting, so he performed ablution three times, three times, then he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing ablution like this ablution of mine, then he said: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, his sins will be as if they were on the day his mother bore him, and his steps to the mosques will be voluntary. And His statement: And that He may complete His favor upon you, means that He says: And your Lord wants, along with purifying you from your sins by your obedience to Him in what He has enjoined upon you of ablution and ritual washing when you stand up for prayer, with water if you find it, and your dry ablution if Surat al-Ma’idah 5:6 O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows
h
and wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles
h
And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity

, purify yourselves. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe yourselves with it. So wipe over your faces and your hands with it. God does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. you do not find it, to complete His favor upon you by permitting you to perform dry ablution and making pure earth a means of purification for you, as a concession from Him to you in that, along with all the other favors that He has bestowed upon you, O believers, that you may be grateful, meaning: so that you may thank God for the favors that He has bestowed upon you, by your obedience to Him in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you.

evidence.text: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us, I heard Masʿud ibn Ali al-Shaibani say, I heard ʿIkrimah say: ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, used to perform ablution before every prayer, and he would recite this verse: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces, the verse.

Tamim told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Salam bin Salm, on the authority of Zaid al-Ami, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra - or: Yazid al-Raqashi - “on the authority of Anas, he said: I performed ablution for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he put his fingers under his chin and combed through his beard and said: This is what my Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, commanded me to do.”

Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Salam bin Salm Al-Madini, he said, Zaid Al-Ami told us, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.
Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.
A group of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as: And your feet to the ankles, in the accusative case.
If it is read like this, it is from the deferred meaning of bringing forward, and the feet would be in the accusative case in apposition to the hands.
The reciters of this interpreted it like this, that God, the Most High, only commanded His servants to wash the feet, not wipe them.

Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he read it: And wipe over your heads and your feet in the accusative case, and he said: The matter returned to washing.

Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father: that he read it: and your feet, and he said: The matter returned to washing.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: The companions of Abdullah used to recite it: And your feet, and they would wash them.
Others from the Hijaz and Iraq recited it as: And wipe your heads and your feet, lowering the feet.

The reciters of this interpreted it as: God only commanded His servants to wipe the feet during ablution without washing them, and they made the feet in apposition to the head, so they lowered them for that reason.

Therefore - due to the possibility of wiping the two meanings described as general and specific, one of which is wiping with some, and the other wiping with all - the reading of the recitation differed in his saying: and your feet, so some of them put it in the accusative case, directing that to the fact that the obligation in them is washing, and denying wiping over them, with the apparent narrations from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the generality of wiping them with water.
The correct reading of those who read it in the accusative case is that it is general in meaning by passing water over them.
The correct reading of those who read it in the lowered form is because that involves passing the hand over them, or what takes the place of the hand, wiping them.

However, even if that is the case, and both readings are good and correct, the reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who reads it with a dhammah, because of what I described of wiping combining the two meanings that I described, and because it is after His saying: And wipe your heads, so linking it to the heads, despite its proximity to it, is more appropriate than linking it to the hands, and it was prevented from it by His saying: And wipe your heads.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And remember the blessing of God upon you, O believers, in the contracts that you made for God upon yourselves, and remember His blessing upon you in that, in that He guided you from the contracts to what is pleasing, and granted you success in what is your salvation from misguidance and ruin, in addition to many other blessings, such as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And remember the favor of God upon you, he said: The favors are the blessings of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. As for his saying:
h
And His covenant with which He has bound you
, it means: And remember also, O believers, in the blessings of God that He has bestowed upon you, His covenant with which He has bound you, which is His promise that He has made to you.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the covenant that God mentioned in this verse. Which of His covenants did He mean?

Some of them said: He meant by it the covenant of God that the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were confident in, when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear and obey him in what they liked and disliked, and to do everything that God and His Messenger commanded them to do.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you when you said

, “We hear and we obey, the verse, meaning: when God sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and revealed the Book to him, and they said: We believe in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the Book, and we acknowledge what is in the Torah, so God reminded them of His covenant which they acknowledged upon themselves, and He commanded them to fulfill it.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you with when you said, ‘We hear and we obey,’ for He took our covenant and we said, We hear and we obey, on the basis of faith and acknowledgment of Him and His Messenger.

x: Others said: Rather, what He, may His praise be glorified, meant was His covenant that He took from His servants when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we testify.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And His covenant with which He bound you
, he said: The covenant with which He bound the children of Adam in the back of Adam.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, which is that its meaning is: And remember, O believers, the favor of God upon you, which He bestowed upon you by guiding you to Islam, and His covenant by which He bound you, meaning: and His covenant by which He made a covenant with you when you pledged allegiance to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear and obey him in ease and hardship, in difficulty and ease, when you said, ‘We hear,’ what you said to us, and you took from us the covenants, and we obeyed you in what you commanded us to do and what you forbade us from doing. And He also bestowed upon you success in accepting that from Him by saying to Him: We hear and we obey. He says: So fulfill to God, O believers, His covenant with which He has bound you, and His favor which He has bestowed upon you in that by your acknowledging upon yourselves that you will hear Him and obey what He has commanded you to do and what He has forbidden you from doing.

He will fulfill for you what He has guaranteed you to fulfill if you fulfill His covenant with Him, by completing His favor upon you, and by admitting you into His Paradise, and granting you eternal life in the abode of His honor, and saving you from His punishment and painful torment. Rather, we said that this is more correct than the statement of those who said that it meant the covenant that was taken from them in the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, because God, the Most High, mentioned after reminding the believers His covenant with which He bound them, His covenant with which He bound the People of the Torah - after He revealed His Book to His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, in what He commanded them and forbade them - in it, so He said:
And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders and the verses after that

thereby alerting the companions of the Messenger of God, Muhammad, peace be upon him, to the places where they have the opportunity to fulfill God’s covenant with them, and informing them of the evil end of the People of the Book in their neglect of what they neglected of His covenant with which He bound them in His commands and prohibitions, and strengthening His prophets and messengers, deterring them from breaking their covenants, so that what He had done to the covenant-breakers among the People of the Book before them would happen to them.

So - since what he mentioned to them, admonished them with it, and forbade them from committing such an act was the covenant of a people whose covenant was taken after the Messenger was sent to them and the Book was revealed to them - it was necessary that the situation in which the covenant was taken and the admonished should be similar to the situation of those who were admonished. And if that is the case, then it is clear that what we said about that is correct, and the opposite of it is invalid. As for his saying: “
h
And fear God

. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts,” it is a threat from God, the Most High, to the believers who were among his companions in his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a warning to them that they would break the covenant of God with which he made them secure in his Messenger, and the promise they made to him in it, by harboring for him something other than what they expressed to him with their tongues.
He, the Most High, says to them:
h
And fear God

, you believers, and fear Him lest you change His covenant and break His pledge with which He has bound you, or go against what you have guaranteed to Him by saying, We hear and we obey, by harboring for Him something other than fulfilling that in your souls. For God is aware of the secrets of your hearts, and knows what your souls conceal. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will bring upon you a punishment that you cannot bear, like what befell those Jews before you of transformation and various kinds of punishments, and you will become in your return to the wrath of God and His painful punishment.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O you who believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad, let your morals and characteristics be to stand up for God as witnesses to justice in your friends and enemies, and do not be unjust in your rulings and actions, so that you transgress what I have specified for you regarding your enemies because of their enmity towards you, and do not fall short in what I have specified for you of My rulings and limits regarding your friends because of their allegiance to you, but abide by My limits in all of them, and act in them according to My command. As for his saying:
h
And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just

, he is saying: And let not the enmity of a people cause you to not be just in your judgment of them and your conduct among them, so that you transgress against them because of the enmity between you and them.
We have mentioned the narration from the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of His statement:
h
Be persistently standing firm in justice
, witnesses for God
r
(An-Nisa’: 135)
, and regarding His statement:
h
And let not the hatred of a people prevent you (al-Ma’idah 5

:2), and the differences of those who differed regarding the reading of that, which is more correct than the statement about it and the reading, with the evidence indicating its correctness, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. It has been said that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Jews intended to kill him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Kathir:
m: “O you who have believed,
h
be persistently standing firm in justice
, witnesses for God.
h
And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just

. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.” It was revealed about the Jews of Khaybar, who wanted to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said, Abdullah bin Kathir said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the Jews to ask for their help in paying blood money, and they intended to kill him. That is what His statement,
h
And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just
, is meant.

x: By His saying, Be just, O believers, He means, “to treat everyone equally, whether they are your friends or enemies. So hold them to what I have commanded you to hold them to of My rulings, and do not transgress against any of them.” As for his saying: It is closer to piety, he means by his saying: It is, that justice towards them is closer to you, O believers, to piety, meaning: that you will be, with God, by using it, among the people of piety, and they are the people of fear and caution from God lest they disobey Him in any of His commands, or commit any of His sins. God Almighty described justice as closer to piety than injustice, because whoever is just is obedient to God through his justice, and whoever is obedient to God is undoubtedly one of the people of piety, and whoever is unjust is disobedient to God, and whoever is disobedient to God is far from his piety. Rather, he used the word it is closer as a metaphor for the verb.

The Arabs use metaphors for verbs when you refer to them with it and that, as God, the Most High, said: It is better for you (al-Baqarah 2:271) and That is purer for you (al-Baqarah 2:232). If there was no it in the word it is closer, it would have been accusative, and it would have been said: Be just, it is closer to righteousness, as it was said: It is better for you to desist (al-Nisa’ 4:171). As for His statement: “And fear God. Indeed, God is Aware of what you do,” it means: Beware, O believers, of being unjust to His servants and transgressing His judgment and decree concerning them that He has made clear to you, lest His punishment befall you and you deserve His painful retribution. Indeed, God is Aware of what you do, meaning: God is All-Knowing and All-Aware of what you do, O believers, in what He has commanded you to do and what He has forbidden you to do, whether you act upon it or oppose it.
He has examined all of that against you, so that He may reward you with it as you are rewarded, the good-doer among you for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil, so beware of doing evil.

evidence.text: We have mentioned the narration from the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of His statement: Be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God (An-Nisa’: 135), and regarding His statement: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you (al-Ma’idah 5:2), and the differences of those who differed regarding the reading of that, which is more correct than the statement about it and the reading, with the evidence indicating its correctness, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying:
h
God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds

, is the promise of God, O people, to those who believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged what he brought to them from their Lord, and acted according to what God entrusted them with, and fulfilled the contracts that He made with them by saying: We will surely hear and obey God and His Messenger. So they heard God’s command and prohibition and obeyed Him, so they acted according to what God commanded them to do, and refrained from what He prohibited them from doing. What He means by His statement:
h
For them is forgiveness

, for those who fulfilled the contracts and covenant that their Lord made with them, forgiveness, which is covering and concealing their past sins, by His pardoning them for them, and leaving their punishment and disgrace for them, and a great reward, He says: And for them, along with His pardoning them for their past sins, as a reward for the deeds that they did, and their fulfillment of the contracts that they made with their Lord, is a great reward.
The greatness of His goodness is unlimited in extent, and no one knows its end except Him, the Most High.
God Almighty informed in this verse that He promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, but He did not inform them of what He promised them, so where is the information about the promised?
Yes, He informed about the promised, and the promised is His statement:
h
For them is forgiveness and a great reward
His statement:
h
For them is forgiveness and a great reward

, is the report of a subject, and if it were the promised, it would have been said: God promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward, and He did not include them in that, and in including that in it, there is evidence of the beginning of the speech and the end of the report of the promise!

Even if its appearance is as you mentioned, it is one of the things that sufficed with the indication of what appeared from the speech to what was hidden from its meaning, from some that he left out mentioning in it. That is because the meaning of the speech is: God promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that He will forgive them and reward them with a great reward, because it is the nature of the Arabs to accompany the promise with an and to apply it in it, so an was left out since the promise is a statement.

And it is the nature of the statement that what follows it from the sentences of report is the subject, and the sentence of report is mentioned after it to suffice with the indication of the appearance of the speech to its meaning, and to divert the promise that agrees with the statement in its meaning, even if its wording is different, to its meaning, so it is as if it was said: God said: For those who believe and do righteous deeds is forgiveness and a great reward.
Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It was said:
h
God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds
forgiveness and a great reward in reference to the promise that they were promised. So the meaning of the statement, according to the interpretation of the one who said this, is:
h
God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds
forgiveness and a great reward in what He promised them.

What He, the Most High, means by His saying: And those who disbelieved, and those who denied the Oneness of God and broke His covenant and contracts that they made with Him, and denied Our signs, meaning: and denied the proofs and arguments of God indicating His Oneness that were brought by the Messengers and others, those are the companions of Hellfire, meaning: those who have this description, are the people of Hellfire, meaning: the people of the Fire who will remain in it forever and will never come out of it.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
O you who have believed

, O you who have acknowledged the Oneness of God and the message of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought to them from their Lord, Remember the favor of God upon you, remember the favor that God bestowed upon you, so thank Him for it by fulfilling His covenant with which He bound you, and the contracts that you made with your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He described His favor that He, the Most High, commanded them to thank Him for, along with all of His other favors, and said: It is His restraining from you the hands of the people who intended to attack you, so He turned them away from you, and prevented them from what they intended for you. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of this blessing that God Almighty mentioned to the companions of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and commanded them to thank Him for it.

Some of them said: It is God’s rescue of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from what the Jews of Banu Nadir intended to do when they came to them demanding that they pay the blood money for the two Amris who were killed by Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, they said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Banu Nadir to ask for their help in paying the blood money for the two ‘Amiris whom Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri had killed. When he came to them, some of them spoke to each other privately and said: ‘You will not find Muhammad closer than him now! Who is the man who will appear at this house and throw a rock at it and relieve us of him?’ Amr ibn Jahash ibn Ka’b said: ‘I will.’ So the report reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he turned away from them, so God, the Mighty and Sublime, revealed about them and what he and his people intended: ‘
h
O you who have believed
, remember the favor of God upon you
h
when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you
,’” the verse.
b.via: Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: When a people were about to stretch out their hands against you, he said: The Jews. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon them in their garden with his companions from behind its wall, so he sought their help in paying the blood money that he had paid, then he got up from them, and they conspired among themselves to kill him. So he went out walking backwards, looking at them, then he called his companions, man by man, until they gathered around him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Remember the favor of God upon you
h
when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you

, but He withheld their hands from you, the Jews, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered their garden, and his companions were behind their garden, so he sought their help in a fine, in the blood money that he had paid, then he got up from them and they conspired among themselves to kill him, so he went out walking, crossing his arms, looking at them in fear. Then he called his companions, man by man, until they gathered around him, God the Almighty said: So withhold their hands from you and fear God, and in God let the believers put their trust.

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, Abu Maʿshar narrated to me, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Banu An-Nadir to ask for their help in a matter of insanity that he had suffered, and with him were Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali. He said: Help me in a matter of insanity that I have suffered. They said: Yes, O Abu Al-Qasim, it is time for you to come to us and ask us for something! Sit down so that we may feed you and give you what you ask of us! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions sat waiting for him, and Huyayy bin Akhtab came, and he was the head of the Surat al-Ma’idah 5:11
h
O you who have believed

, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah, and upon Allah let the believers rely. people, and he was the one who said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he said. Huyayy said to his companions: You do not see him closer than he is now. Throw stones at him and kill him, and you will never see any evil! So they came to a large millstone of theirs to throw them at him, but God held back their hands from it until Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and set him up from there. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed: ‘
h
O you who have believed

, remember the favor of God upon you when they were a people who were about to They stretch out their hands against you, so restrain their hands from you and fear God, and upon God let the believers put their trust.” So God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what they intended for him.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Kathir:
m: h
O you who have believed

, remember the favor of God upon you when a people were about to stretch out their hands against you, the verse. He said: The Jews entered upon them in a garden and asked them for help in a debt he had lost, so they conspired among themselves to kill him, so he got up from them and went out, looking at them in fear, then he called his companions, man by man, until they gathered around him.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Mundhir bin Amr Al-Ansari - one of the Banu Al-Najjar, and he was one of the leaders on the night of Al-Aqaba - and he sent him with thirty riders from the Muhajireen and Ansar, so they went out and met Amir bin Al-Tufayl bin Malik bin Ja’far at the well of Ma’unah, which is from the waters of Banu Amir, and they fought. Al-Mundhir and his companions were killed except for three men who were searching for something they had lost, and they were not startled until birds were circling in the sky, and blood clots were falling from between their trunks. One of the men said: Our companions have been killed, by the Most Merciful! Then he turned and ran until he met a man, and they exchanged two blows, and when the blow was mixed with his, he raised his head to the sky and opened his eyes and then said: God is Great, Paradise and the Lord of the Worlds!! So he was called Anqab to die, and his two companions returned and met two men from Banu Salim, and between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was a truce between them and their people, so they attributed themselves to them from Banu Amir, and killed them. Their people came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking for blood money. He went out with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, until they entered upon Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and the Jews of Nadir, and he asked for their help in blood money for them. He said: The Jews gathered to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and they made an excuse by making food. Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him with what the Jews had agreed upon, which was treachery. He went out, then called Ali and said: Do not leave your place, and if any of my companions revolt against you and ask you about me, say: Go to Medina, and catch up with him. He said: So they passed by Ali, and he ordered them to do what he ordered, until the last of them came to him, then he followed them, and that is what His saying: “And you will not cease to find treachery among them” (al-Ma’idah 5:13).

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you, he said: It was revealed about Ka’b ibn Al-Ashraf and his companions, when they intended to betray the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: Rather, the blessing that God mentioned in this verse, and commanded the believing companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to thank Him for it, is that the Jews intended to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, over a meal to which they had invited him, so God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they intended to do, so he and his companions stopped responding to him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, remember the favor of God upon you until his statement: and restrain their hands from you, that is because a group of Jews prepared food for the Messenger of God and his companions, in order to kill him when the food came, so God revealed to him about them, but the food did not come, and he ordered his companions, but they did not come to him.

x: Others said: God Almighty meant by that: the blessing that He bestowed upon the believers by informing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what his enemy and their enemy, the polytheists, were up to on the day of Batn Nakhl, of their deceiving them and their attack on them, when they were distracted from them by their prayer and prostrated in it, and His informing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the need to beware of his enemy in his prayer, by teaching him the prayer of fear.
Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, remember the favor of God upon you
h
when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you

Al-Baqarah 2:177. He mentioned to us that it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Batn Nakhl during the seventh battle. Banu Tha’labah and Banu Muharib wanted to kill him, but God informed him of that. He mentioned to us that a man volunteered to kill him, so he came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his sword was laid out. He said: Shall I take it, O Prophet of God? He said: Take it! He said: Shall I draw it? He said: Yes! Ask him. He said: Who can protect you from me? He said: God can protect me from you! So the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threatened him and spoke harshly to him, so he drew his sword, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions to depart, and the prayer of fear was revealed to him at that time.

Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he mentioned it on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Jabir: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped at a place, and the people dispersed among the wild trees to seek shade under them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hung his weapon on a tree, and a Bedouin came to the sword of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and took it and drew it, then he turned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who can protect you from me? And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying: God! So the Bedouin drew the sword, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called his companions and told them what had happened to the Bedouin, while he was sitting beside him and did not punish him.

Muammar said: Qatada used to mention something similar to this, and he mentioned that some Arabs wanted to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they sent this Bedouin, and he interpreted: Remember the favor of God upon you
h
when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you
, the verse.

The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this is the saying of those who said: God meant by the blessing mentioned in this verse, His blessing upon the believers in Him and His Messenger, which He bestowed upon them, in rescuing their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what the Jews of Banu Nadir intended to do, which was to kill him and those with him, on the day the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched to them regarding the blood money that he was carrying for the two men killed by Amr ibn Umayya. We said that this is more correct in interpreting it because God, the Most High, after mentioning that, accused the Jews of their deeds and ugly actions, and their betrayal of their Lord and their prophets, then He commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pardon them and overlook their great ignorance.
So it was known from this that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not commanded to pardon and overlook them immediately after His statement:
h
When a people intended to stretch out their hands against you

, and he extended his hands to others. Because if those who intended to stretch out their hands to them were not them, then it would have been more appropriate for the command to pardon and overlook them, not to those who were not mentioned about that, and the description of betrayal would have been in describing them in this place, not in describing those whose betrayal was not mentioned. So in that is what indicates the correctness of what we have decided to be correct from the interpretations in that, not what contradicts it.

He, the Most High, means: O believers, beware of God, lest you disobey Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you, and break the covenant with which He has bound you, so that you deserve from Him a punishment that you cannot bear. And in God let the believers put their trust, meaning: and to God let them face the reins of their affairs, and submit to His judgment, and trust in His victory and support, acknowledging the Oneness of God and the message of His Messenger, acting according to His commands and prohibitions, for that is from the perfection of their religion and the completion of their faith, and that if they do that, He will protect them and watch over them, and preserve them from those who intended to harm them, just as He preserved and defended you, O believers, the Jews who intended to do what they intended to do by extending their hands to you, as a protection from Him for you, since you were from the people of faith in Him and in His Messenger, and none other, for none other than Him is able to repel the evil that your Lord intended for you, nor bring you any benefit that He did not decree for you.

This verse was revealed as an announcement from God, may His praise be glorified, to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in him, about the character of those Jews who intended to extend their hands to them, such as the one who:

c: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel

, he said: The Jews are from the People of the Book. And that what they intended to do of treachery and breaking the covenant between them and him, is from their characteristics and the characteristics of their forefathers and their morals and the morals of their ancient ancestors, and as an argument for his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the Jews, by informing him of what he knew of them but not of the Arabs, of the hidden matters of their affairs and the hidden knowledge of their sciences, and as a rebuke to the Jews for their persistence in error and their insistence on disbelief, despite their knowledge of the error of what they were establishing. God says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not consider the matter of those Jews who intended to extend their hands to you as too great, nor the matter of the treachery that they attempted and intended for you, for that is from the morals of their forefathers and ancestors, and they are no more than following the path of their forefathers and the way of their ancestors. Then the Almighty began the story of some of their treachery and betrayal, their audacity towards their Lord, and their breaking of the covenant that their Creator had bound them to, with His blessings that He had bestowed upon them, and His honors for which they were grateful. He said: And God had taken a covenant from those who had extended His hand to you from the Jews of the Children of Israel, O company of believers, to fulfill His covenants and obey Him in what He commanded them and forbade them, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, he said: God took their covenants that they would be sincere to Him and not worship anyone other than Him.
h
And We sent from among them twelve leaders

, meaning: And We sent from among them twelve guarantors, who guaranteed them the fulfillment of the covenants that We had entrusted to Him regarding what He had commanded them to do and what He had forbidden them to do. In Arabic, the naqib is like the arif chief of a people, except that he is above the arif. It is said: So-and-so dug into the Banu so-and-so, so he dug. If it is meant that he was not a naqib and became a naqib, it is said: he dug, so he dug a niqab. And from the arif: he dug into them, he is known as a fortune-teller. As for the manakib, they are like helpers who are with the arifs, one of them is mankab.

x: Some scholars of Arabic say: He is the trustworthy guarantor of the people. As for the people of interpretation, they differed among themselves in its interpretation.
Some of them said: He is a witness against his people.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel and raised up from among them twelve leaders
, from each tribe a man to bear witness over his people.

x: Others said: The captain, the trustee.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hassan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, who said: The leaders are the trustees.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: the same. God, the Almighty, commanded His Prophet Moses, peace and blessings be upon him, to send twelve leaders from his people, the Children of Israel, to the land of the giants in the Levant, to find out for Moses their report, since he wanted to destroy them, and to inherit their land and homes for Moses and his people, and to make them dwellings for the Children of Israel, after he had saved them from Pharaoh and his people, and brought them out of the land of Egypt. So Moses sent those whom God had commanded him to send to it from the leaders, as follows:
