c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: God commanded the Children of Israel to march to Jericho, which is the land of Jerusalem, so they marched until they were close to them, then Musa sent twelve leaders from all the tribes of the Children of Israel, so they marched intending to bring him report of the giants, but a man from the giants called Aaj met them, so he took the twelve and put them in his cloak, and on his head were bearers of firewood. He went with them to his wife and said: Look at these people who claim that they want to fight us!! So he threw them in front of her, and said: Shall I not crush them with my feet! His wife said: Rather, leave them alone until they tell their people what they saw. So he did that. When the people went out, some of them said to one another: O people, if you tell the Children of Israel the report of the people, they will turn away from the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, but keep it secret and tell the Prophet of God, so that they will be the ones who make up their own minds! So some of them took a covenant from one another to keep it secret, then they returned. Ten of them went and broke the covenant, and a man began to tell his brother and his father what he had seen of the ivory, but two of them kept it secret.

c: Then they came to Moses and Aaron and told them
m: the story, and that is when God says:
h
And God had taken a covenant from the Children of Israel
, and We raised up among them twelve leaders.
b.via: Then they came to Moses and Aaron and

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Twelve chiefs, from each tribe of the Children of Israel, a man. Moses sent them to the giants, and they found them, with two of them entering into the sleeve of each one of them, throwing them down, and no one would carry a bunch of grapes except five of them on a piece of wood, and five or four people would enter into the half of a pomegranate if its seeds were removed. So the chiefs returned, each of them forbidding his tribe from fighting them, except for Joshua ibn Nun and Kalb ibn Yafnah, who commanded the tribes to fight the giants and wage jihad against them, but they disobeyed these two and obeyed the others.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: in a similar manner - except that he said: From the Children of Israel are men - and he also said: They will meet them. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that Moses was commanded to march with the Children of Israel to the Holy Land, and he said: I have written it down for you as a home, a settlement, and a place of residence. So go out to it and fight the enemy in it, for I will support you against them. And take from your people twelve leaders, from each tribe a leader who will be over his people by fulfilling what they were commanded to do, and say to them: God says to you: “I am with you.
h
If you establish prayer

and give zakat” until His saying: then the right path has gone astray. And Moses took from them twelve leaders whom he chose from the tribes to be guarantors over their people in what they were in, by fulfilling his covenant and his pact. And from each tribe he took the best and most loyal of them a man - God Almighty says: And God had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders - so Moses marched with them to the Holy Land by God's command, until when he reached the desert between Egypt and Syria, a land where there was neither wine nor shade, Moses called upon his Lord when the heat harmed them, so He shaded them with clouds, and he called upon Him for provision, so God sent down upon them manna and quails. And God commanded Moses, saying: Send men to explore the land of Canaan which I gave to the Children of Israel, from each tribe a man. So Moses sent all the leaders who were among them, so God Almighty sent from the wilderness of Paran with the word of God, and they were the leaders of the Children of Israel. These are the names of the group whom God, the Most High, sent from the Children of Israel to the land of Ash-Sham, as the people of the Torah mention, to traverse it for the Children of Israel: From the tribe of Reuben: Shamon son of Zaccur, and from the tribe of Simeon: Shaphat son of Hari, and from the tribe of Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh, and from the tribe of As: Jegael son of Joseph, and from the tribe of Joseph, which is the tribe of Ephraim: Joshua son of Nun, and from the tribe of Benjamin: Pelet son of Rephon, and from the tribe of Zebulun: Gidi son of Sodi, and from the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph: Gidi son of Susa, and from the tribe of Dan: Hamlael son of Gamal, and from the tribe of Asher: Sathur son of Malkiel, and from the tribe of Naphtali: Nehi son of Povsi, and from the tribe of Gad: Golael son of Micah. These are the names of those whom Moses sent to feel out the land for him. On that day, Hoshea, son of Nun, was called Joshua, son of Nun. So he sent them and said to them, “Get up before the sun, leave the mountain, and see what is in the land, and what kind of people they have who inhabit it are: are they strong or Surat al-Ma’idah 5:12 And Allah had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you.
h
If you establish prayer

and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow." Beneath it are rivers. So whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way. weak, are they few or many? And see the land they inhabit: is it fat or lean? Does it have trees or not? Pass on, and bring us some of the fruit of that land!” And that was when the first fruits of the grapes were first harvested.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We sent from among them twelve leaders

, they were from the Children of Israel, Moses sent them to look for the city for him, so they went and looked at the city and brought back a grain of their fruit, and a man was knocked down, so they said: Estimate the strength of a people and their might, this is their fruit!! At that point they were tempted and said: We are not able to fight, So go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here (al-Ma’idah 5:24).

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj Al-Marwazi
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid say regarding His statement:
h
And We sent from among them twelve leaders

, God commanded the Children of Israel to march to the Holy Land with their Prophet Moses, peace be upon him. When they were close to Medina, Moses said to them: Enter it! But they refused and were cowardly, and sent twelve leaders to look at them. So they went and looked, and they brought a grain of their fruit the size of a man’s udder. They said: Appreciate the strength and might of a people; this is their fruit!! At that point they said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight (al-Ma’idah 5:24).

x: God Almighty says: And God said to the Children of Israel: I am with you, meaning: I will support you against your enemy and My enemy whom I have commanded you to fight, if you fight them and fulfill My covenant and pledge that I took from you. There is something omitted in the speech, and what was apparent in the speech was dispensed with in what was omitted from it. That is because the meaning of the speech is: And God said to them, I am with you. So He left out mentioning them, dispensing with His saying:
h
And God had taken a covenant from the Children of Israel

, since the report had preceded about a people named specifically, so it was known that what was in the context of the speech of the report was about them, since the speech was not diverted from them to others. Then our Lord, may He be glorified, began the oath, saying: I swear that if you, the Children of Israel, establish prayer, give zakat, meaning: give it to those I have commanded you to give it, and believe in My messengers, meaning: and believe in what My messengers brought you of the laws of My religion.
Al-Rabi’ bin Anas used to say: This is a speech from God to the twelve leaders.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas: That Moses, peace be upon him, said to the twelve leaders: Go to them - meaning: to the tyrants - and tell me their story and what they commanded, and do not fear, for God is with you as long as you establish prayer and give zakat and believe in My messengers and support them, and lend God
h
a good loan

x: What Al-Rabiʿ said about this is not far from the truth, except that it is part of God’s decree for all of His creation that He supports those who obey Him, and takes care of those who follow His command, avoid disobeying Him, and avoid their sins. So since that is the case, and part of His obedience is establishing prayer, paying zakat, believing in the messengers, and all that He has urged the people to do, it is known that the expiation of sins and entering Paradise by it was not specific to the leaders and not to the rest of the Children of Israel. So it was more appropriate and fitting that it be an exhortation for all of the people and an urging for them to do what He urged them to do than it being an exhortation for some and an urging for a specific person and not a general one.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement: And you punished them.
Some of them said: The interpretation of that is:
h
And you supported them
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And you supported them
, he said: you aided them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you supported them
, he said: You aided them with the sword.

x: Others said: It is obedience and support.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd say regarding His statement: And you honored them, he said: Honor and respect, obedience and support. The Arabs differed in their interpretation of it. It was mentioned on the authority of Yunus Al-Harmari that he used to say: The interpretation of that is: You praised them. I narrated this on the authority of Abu Ubaidah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna on his authority. Abu Ubaidah used to say: The meaning of this is: you supported them, helped them, honored them, glorified them, and supported them. And he recited in this regard: How many noble and generous are there among them, and how many lions are there who are honoured in the gathering. Al-Farra’ used to say: Al-‘azr is the response. I excused him, I responded to him, if I saw him committing injustice and I said: Fear God, or I forbade him, then that is al-‘azr.

x: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: You supported them. That is because God, the Most High, said in Surat al-Fath 48:Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner * That you may believe in God and His Messenger and support him and respect him (al-Fath 48:8-9). So respect is veneration. Since that is the case, then the saying in that is only some of what we mentioned from the sayings that we narrated from those we narrated from. If it is corrupted that its meaning is veneration, and victory may be by hand and tongue, as for the hand, it is defending it with the sword and other things, and as for the tongue, it is good praise and defending honor, then it is correct that it is victory, since victory contains the meaning of every speaker who said a saying about it from what we narrated from him.
As for his statement:
h
And you have loaned to God a good loan
, he is saying: And you have spent in the way of God, and that is in the struggle against His enemy and your enemy,
h
a good loan

, he is saying: And you have spent what you have spent in His way, so you have attained the truth in your spending what you have spent in that, and you have not transgressed in it the limits of God and what He has urged you to do and urged you to do, and so on.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How did he say: And you have loaned God
h
a good loan
, and not say:
h
a good loan
, and you know that the source of I loaned is lending?
If that had been said, it would have been correct, but his saying:
h
A good loan

, he extracted a source from its meaning, not from its wording. That is because in his saying: I lend, there is the meaning of I loan, as in the meaning of I gave there is I took. So the meaning of the statement is: And you have loaned God
h
a good loan
Similar to that is: And God caused you to grow from the earth a plant
r

, since in I caused you to grow there is the meaning of: So you grew, and as Imru’ al-Qais said: I was satisfied and was humiliated in a difficult way Since the word raḍat means I humiliated, then humiliation is derived from its meaning, not from its wording.
By that, He, the Most High, means the Children of Israel. He, the Most High, says to them:
h
If you establish prayer

, O people who gave Me their covenant to fulfill their obedience to Me and follow My command, and pay the zakat, and do all the rest of what I promised you, My Paradise, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds, meaning: I will cover with My pardon for you - and My forgiveness of your punishment, for your previous crimes that you committed between Me and you - your sins that you committed in the past, such as worshipping the calf and other deadly sins of yours, and I will admit you, while I cover that from you with My grace on the Day of Resurrection, into gardens beneath which rivers flow. In the gardens and orchards. I said that the meaning of his saying: I will certainly disbelieve is I will cover up, because disbelief means denial, covering up, and concealment, as Labid said: On a night when the stars are covered in clouds It means: he covered it, so takfir is the active participle of kufr.
The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of the letter lam in the phrase laakfarna.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The first lam has the meaning of an oath, meaning the lam in his saying:
h
If you establish prayer
. He said: The second has the meaning of another oath.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Rather, the first lam is in the place of an oath, so it is sufficient for the oath, meaning with the first lam:
h
If you establish prayer
. He said: And the second lam, meaning his saying:
h
I will surely expiate your sins from you
, is an answer to it, meaning the lam in his saying:
h
If you establish prayer
. And he justified his saying that by saying:
h
If you establish prayer
is not complete, and does not dispense with his saying:
h
I will surely expiate your sins from you
. Since that is the case, it is not permissible for his saying:
h
I will surely expiate your sins from you to be an introductory oath

, rather it is obligatory for it to be an answer to the oath, since it does not dispense with it. And His saying: Rivers flow beneath it, means: Rivers flow beneath the trees of these gardens that I have brought you into.

The Almighty says: Whoever among you, O children of Israel, denies anything that I have commanded him to do and abandons it, or commits what I have forbidden him to do and does it, after I have taken a covenant from him to fulfill my obedience and avoid disobeying me, has certainly strayed from the right path, meaning: he has missed the clear path and strayed from the straight path. And misguidance is riding without guidance, and we have explained that with evidence in other places. His saying equally means: middle, and the way means the road. We have explained the interpretation of all of this in another place, so there is no need to repeat it here. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:12 And Allah had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you.
h
If you establish prayer
and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow."
Beneath it are rivers. So whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.

The Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do not be surprised by these Jews who intended to extend their hands to you and your companions, and broke the covenant between you and them, out of treachery towards you and your companions, for that is part of their customs and the customs of their ancestors, and part of that is that I took a covenant from their ancestors during the time of Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, to obey me, and I sent from them twelve leaders who were chosen from all of them to investigate the report of the tyrants, and I promised them victory over them, and that I would inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, after I showed them the lessons and signs - the destruction of Pharaoh and his people in the sea, and the splitting of the sea for them, and all the lessons - that I showed them, but they broke their covenant that they had pledged to me, and broke my covenant, so I cursed them for breaking their covenant. If this was done by their best, with their own hands, then do not find it strange that their scum did the same.

There is an omission in the speech, so I sufficed with the apparent meaning of it. That is because the meaning of the speech is: So whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the right path - so they broke the covenant, so I cursed them, So
h
because they broke their covenant
We cursed them, so I sufficed with his statement:
h
So because they broke their covenant from mentioning So they broke
. What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
Because they broke their covenant
, is
h
because they broke their covenant
, as Qatada said.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So
h
because they broke their covenant
, We cursed them, meaning: So
h
because they broke their covenant
, We cursed them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
Because they broke their covenant

, he said: It is a covenant that God took from the people of the Torah, but they broke it. We have mentioned the meaning of cursing in other places. The ha and the mim in his saying: Because of their breach, refer to the mention of the Children of Israel before.

x: The reading of this differed. The people of Medina, some of the people of Mecca, Basra and Kufa read it as Qasiyyah with an alif.

i: On the assumption of the agent of the hardness of the heart, from the saying of the speaker: his heart hardened, so it hardens, and he is hard, and that is when it becomes thick and intense and becomes dry and hard, as the rajaz poet said:
x: I was cruel and cruel to myself The interpretation of the statement according to this reading is: So We cursed those who broke My covenant and did not fulfill My covenant from among the Children of Israel, by breaking their covenant that they had pledged to Me, and We made their hearts hard, rough and dry from believing in Me and being guided to obey Me, stripped of compassion and mercy.
The majority of Kufian readers read this as: And We made their hearts hard. Then those who read it differed in their interpretation.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is the meaning of cruelty, because fa’ila is more eloquent in censure than fa’ila, so we chose to read it as qasiyya instead of qasiyya, for that reason.

Others among them said: Rather, the meaning of Qasiyyah is not the meaning of Qaswat, and rather Qasiyyah in this context is: the hearts whose faith in God is not sincere, but whose faith is mixed with disbelief, like Qasiyyah dirhams, which are those whose silver is mixed with adulteration of copper or lead or something else, as Abu Zubayd al-Ta’i said: She neighs in the deafening silence, as the cruel ones neigh in the hands of the money changers. This describes the impact of the surveyors who dug Uthman's grave on the rocks, which are peace.
The reading that I like the most in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: And We Surat al-Ma’idah 5:13 So
h
because they broke their covenant

, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their [proper] usages and have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded. And you will not cease to uncover treachery among them, except for a few of them.
h
So pardon them and overlook

. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good. made their hearts hard, with the letter faʿilah, because it is more expressive in denouncing the people than qasiyyah. And the more correct of the two interpretations in this regard is the interpretation of the one who interprets it: faʿilah from qaswa, as it was said: a pure soul and a pure woman, and a witness woman and a martyr, because God, may He be praised, described the people as having broken their covenant and disbelieved in Him, and He did not describe them with any faith, so their hearts are described as having faith mixed with disbelief, like hard dirhams mixed with adulteration of silver.

God the Almighty says: And We made the hearts of those who broke Our covenants from the Children of Israel hard, from which goodness was removed, and guidance was taken away from them, so they neither believed nor were guided. So because God the Almighty removed guidance and faith from their hearts, they distorted the words of their Lord that He sent down to their Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, which is the Torah, and they changed it and wrote with their own hands other than what God the Almighty sent down to their Prophet, then they said to the ignorant al-Nas 114:This is the word of God that He sent down to His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, and the Torah that He revealed to him. This is from the description of the generations that came after Moses from the Jews, some of whom lived during the time of our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

However, God the Almighty included them among those about whom the story began from among those who lived during the time of Moses, since they were from their descendants, and they followed their method of lying about God, slandering Him, and breaking the covenants that He took from them in the Torah, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: They distort words from their proper places, meaning: the limits of God in the Torah, and they say: If Muhammad commands you to do what you are upon, then accept it, and if he contradicts you, then beware. God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And they forgot a portion

, and they left a share, and it is like His saying: They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67), meaning: they abandoned God’s command, so God abandoned them. This has been explained with evidence in other places, so there is no need to repeat it. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded
, meaning: they left a portion.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded
, he said: They abandoned the bonds of their religion, and the duties of God, may He be glorified, without which deeds are not accepted...

x: The Blessed and Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And you, O Muhammad, will continue to see among the Jews, whose report I have informed you of, their breaking of My covenant and their breach of My agreement, despite their good deeds and My blessings upon them - despite such treachery and betrayal - ‘
h
except a few of them
h
except a few of them

who did not betray.” The traitor in this context: betrayal, and it was placed - which is a noun - in the place of the source, as it was said: a sinner, for the sin, and a narrator for the nap. His saying:
h
Except a few of them
, is an exception to the ha’ and mim in his saying: On a traitor among them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And you will not cease to find treachery among them, he said: treachery, lying, and immorality.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: And you will not cease to find out about treachery on their part, he said: They are Jews, like what they intended to do to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the day he entered their garden.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid and Ikrimah said, his statement:
h
And you will not cease to discover treachery among them
, from the Jews, like the one who intended to harm the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the day he entered upon them.

x: Some of the speakers said: The meaning of this is: And you will continue to find a traitor among them. He said: The Arabs add the letter ha’ to the end of the masculine, like their saying: He is a narrator of poetry, and a man of knowledge.
You told yourself to be loyal, and you were not a traitor to treachery, with your finger tied.
He said: A traitor, while addressing a man.

The correct interpretation of this is the statement we have narrated from the people of interpretation. Because God meant by this verse the people of the Jews of Banu Nadir who intended to kill the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to them seeking their help in the blood money of the ʿAmiris, so God, the Exalted, informed him of what they intended to do. Then He, the Exalted, said after informing him of the report of their predecessors and informing him of the path of their ancestors, and that their last will follow the path of their first in treachery and betrayal, lest their action be considered too great for the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so He, the Exalted, said: And you will not cease to find out about treachery, betrayal, and breaking of covenant from the Jews, and He did not mean that He will not cease to find out about a traitor among them.

This is because the report began with them about their group, so it was said: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people were determined to stretch out their hands against you, then it was said:
h
And you will not cease to discover treachery among them
, so since the beginning was about the group, then ending with the group is more appropriate.

This is a command from God, the Almighty, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pardon these people who intended to extend their hands to him from the Jews. God, the Almighty, says to him: Pardon, O Muhammad, these Jews who intended to do what they intended to do, to extend their hands to you and your companions to kill you, and forgive them for their crime by refraining from exposing yourself to their harm, for I love the one who is good at pardoning and forgiving those who have wronged him. Qatada used to say: This is abrogated. He said: It was abrogated by the verse of Bara’ah: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, the verse (al-Tawbah 9:29).

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So pardon them and overlook
, he said: It was abrogated by: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have made unlawful (al-Tawbah 9:29).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So pardon them and overlook

. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.” He was not commanded that day to fight them, so God, the Exalted, commanded him to pardon them and overlook them. Then He abrogated that in Bara’ah, saying: “Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture - until they pay the jizyah with willing submission while they are subdued.” (al-Tawbah 9:29), and they are the People of the Book, so God, the Exalted, commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight them until they submit or acknowledge the jizyah.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I read on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, something similar.

x: What Qatada said is not possible. However, the abrogating verse that is undoubtedly in the command is that which negates all the meanings of the opposite of what came before it. As for that which does not negate all of it, there is no way to know that it is abrogating except by a report from God Almighty or from His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in His statement:
h
Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9

:29), there is no indication of the command to negate the meanings of forgiveness and pardon for the Jews. And since that was the case, and it was permissible, with their acknowledgment of their humiliation and their payment of the jizya after the fighting, to order pardon for them in the treachery they intended to commit, or the breach they resolved to commit, as long as they did not set up spears without paying the jizya, and refrain from the rulings required of them, it was not necessary to rule, according to His statement:
h
Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9
:29) the verse, that it abrogated His statement: “
h
So pardon them and overlook
Indeed, God loves the doers of good.”

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.
The people of Medina, some of the people of Mecca, Basra and Kufa read it as Qasiyyah with an alif.

On the assumption of the agent of the hardness of the heart, from the saying of the speaker: his heart hardened, so it hardens, and he is hard, and that is when it becomes thick and intense and becomes dry and hard, as the rajaz poet said: I was cruel and cruel to myself The interpretation of the statement according to this reading is: So We cursed those who broke My covenant and did not fulfill My covenant from among the Children of Israel, by breaking their covenant that they had pledged to Me, and We made their hearts hard, rough and dry from believing in Me and being guided to obey Me, stripped of compassion and mercy.
The majority of Kufian readers read this as: And We made their hearts hard.
Then those who read it differed in their interpretation.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is the meaning of cruelty, because fa’ila is more eloquent in censure than fa’ila, so we chose to read it as qasiyya instead of qasiyya, for that reason.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that I like the most in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: And We Surat al-Ma’idah 5:13 So because they broke their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard.

x: The Almighty says: And We took from the Christians a covenant to obey Me, perform My duties, follow My messengers, and believe in them. But they followed in My covenant that I took from them the path of the misguided nation of the Jews.
So they changed their religion and broke it as they broke it, and they abandoned their share of My covenant that I took from them to fulfill My covenant, and they wasted My command, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And of those who said, ‘We are Christians,’ We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. They forgot the Book of God among them, and the covenant of God that He made with them, and the command of God that He commanded them with.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: The Christians said what the Jews said, and they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of.

x: God Almighty means by His statement,
h
So We stirred up discord among them

, that We stirred up discord among them and cast discord, as one thing stirs up discord. God Almighty says: When these Christians, from whom I took a covenant to fulfill My covenant, abandoned their share of what I had entrusted to them of My commands and prohibitions, I stirred up enmity and hatred among them. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of God Almighty’s temptation of enmity and hatred among them.
Some of them said: His temptation among them was due to the desires that occurred between them.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We stirred up among them enmity and hatred
, he said: These are the different desires and hatred, so it is the temptation.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, he said:
m: I heard Al-Nakha’i say:
h
So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred
, he said: He stirred some of them up against each other with disputes and arguments about religion.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Al-Taimi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred
, he said: I do not see the temptation in this verse except for different desires. And Mu’awiyah bin Qurra said: Disputes over religion nullify deeds.

x: Others said: Rather, this is the enmity and hatred between them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection the verse, because the people abandoned the Book of God, disobeyed His Messengers, neglected His obligations, and neglected His limits, He cast enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection, because of their evil deeds, and if the people had taken the Book of God and His command, they would not have separated nor hated one another.

x: The most correct of the two interpretations of this, in our view, is the interpretation of the one who said: He incited them among themselves with the desires that arose among them, as Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi said, because the enmity of the Christians among themselves is only due to their differences in what they said about the Messiah, and that is desires, not revelation from God.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the letters ha and mim in His statement:
h
So We stirred up discord among them

Some of them said: He meant the Jews and Christians. So the meaning of the speech according to their statement and interpretation is: So We stirred up discord between the Jews and Christians, because they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: He also said
m: about the Christians: So they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded. So when they did that, God Almighty instilled enmity and hatred between them and the Jews until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Then We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection
, he said: They are the Jews and the Christians. Ibn Zayd said: Just as you cast enmity between two animals.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred
, he said: The Jews and the Christians.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: They are the Jews and Christians, God has instilled enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection.

x: Others said: Rather, God meant by that the Christians alone. They said: The meaning of that is: So We stirred up discord among the Christians, as a punishment for them forgetting a portion of what they were reminded of. They said: And upon it returned the ha and the mim in among them, not the Jews.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said:
m: God, the Mighty and Sublime, said to the Children of Israel: Do not exchange the verses of God for a small price, and learn wisdom and do not take payment for it! But only a few of them did that, so they took bribes in judgment and exceeded the limits. So He said about the Jews when they ruled other than what God had commanded: And We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection (al-Ma’idah 5:64), and He said about the Christians: But they forgot a portion of that of which they had been reminded, so We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.

x: The most correct of the two interpretations of the verse, in my opinion, is what Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas said, which is that what is meant by the temptation among them is the Christians, in this verse specifically, and that the ha and the mim refer to the Christians and not the Jews, because the mention of the temptation in God’s statement about the Christians, after He had completed His statement about the Jews, and after He had begun His statement about the Christians, so it is more appropriate for it to be meant for the Christians specifically than for it to be meant for both parties together, for what we have mentioned.
What is the enmity between Christians, so that it is specifically meant by that?

This is the enmity between the Nestorians and the Jacobites, the royalists, and the royalists, the Nestorians and the Jacobites. And what was said by the one who said: (What is meant by that is: God’s temptation between the Jews and the Christians) is not far-fetched, but this is closer to me, and more similar to the interpretation of the verse, for what we mentioned.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Forgive those who intended to extend their hands to you and your companions and pardon them, for God Almighty is behind taking revenge on them. God will inform them when they come to Him in their place of resurrection, of what they did in this world, of breaking His covenant, violating His promise, altering His book, and distorting His commands and prohibitions. He will punish them for that according to what they deserved.

evidence.text: And Mu’awiyah bin Qurra said: Disputes over religion nullify deeds.

x: The Almighty says to the group of the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, who were in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, Our Messenger has come to you, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: O People of the Book, there has come to you Our Messenger, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: He makes clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Book, meaning: Muhammad, our Messenger, makes clear to you much of what you used to conceal from the people and not make clear to them of what is in your Book. And among what they used to conceal from their Book, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made clear to the al-Nas 114:stoning married adulterers. It was said: This verse was revealed to clarify this to the people by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had hidden it from their book.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Whoever disbelieves in stoning has disbelieved in the Qur’an without expecting it. His statement:
h
O People of the Scripture
, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture, so stoning was among what they concealed.

c: Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwaih told us, Ali bin Al-Hassan told us, Al-Hussein told us, Yazid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
O People of the Scripture

, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you, to His statement: a straight path, he said: The Jews came to the Prophet of God and asked him about stoning, and they gathered in a house. He said: Who among you is the most knowledgeable? They pointed to Ibn Suriya, so he said: Are you the most knowledgeable of them? He said: Ask whatever you wish! He said: Are you the most knowledgeable of them? He said: They claim that! He said: So he implored him by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, and the One who raised the mountain, and he implored him by the covenants that were taken from them, until he was overcome by fear. Then he said: Our women are beautiful women, and the killing among us has increased, so we shortened the hair, and we flogged a hundred, and shaved our heads, and we divided the heads among the animals - I think he said: camels - he said: So he ruled that they should be stoned, and God revealed about them:
h
O People of the Scripture

, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you, the verse, and this verse: And when some of them are alone with others, they say, ‘Do you tell them what God has revealed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?’ (al-Baqarah 2:76). And His saying:
h
And He pardons
much, means by His saying:
h
And He pardons

, and He leaves you from being held accountable for much of what you were concealing from your book that God revealed to you, which is the Torah, so you do not act upon it until God commands him to take you by it.

x: God Almighty says to those whom He addressed from the People of the Book: There has come to you, O People of the Torah and the Gospel, a light from God, meaning by the light Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, through whom God illuminated the truth, made Islam manifest, and destroyed polytheism. He is a light for those who are illuminated by him, clarifying the truth. And part of his illumination of the truth is his clarification to the Jews of much of what they had hidden in the Book. And His statement:
h
And a clear Book
, God Almighty says: There has come to you from God Almighty the light with which He has illuminated for you the landmarks of truth,
h
and a clear Book

, meaning a book in which there is an explanation of what they differed about among themselves: of the oneness of God, what He has permitted and forbidden, and the laws of His religion, and it is the Qur’an that He revealed to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, explaining to the people everything they need of their religious affairs, and clarifying it for them, so that they may know its truth from its falsehood.
He, may His remembrance be glorified, means: He guides with this clear book that came from God, may He be glorified and exalted, and by His saying:
h
God guides with it
, He means that
h
God guides with it

and directs with it, and the ha’ in His saying: with it refers back to the book, whoever follows His pleasure, he says: whoever follows God’s pleasure. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of satisfaction from God Almighty.

Some of them said: His satisfaction with something, acceptance of it, praise and commendation. They said: He accepts faith, purifies it, commends the believer for faith, and describes faith as light, guidance and separation.

Others said: The meaning of satisfaction from God, the Almighty and Majestic, is an understood meaning, it is the opposite of discontent, and it is one of His attributes according to what is understood from the meanings: satisfaction which is the opposite of discontent, and that is not praise, because praise and commendation are words, and only that which is pleased is praised and commended. They said: So satisfaction is a meaning, and praise and commendation are a meaning that is not it. What he means by his saying: (paths of peace) are the ways of peace, and (peace) is God Almighty.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “Whoever follows His pleasure, the paths of peace,” the path of God that He has prescribed for His servants and called them to it, and with which He sent His messengers, which is Islam, and He does not accept any action from anyone except with it, neither Judaism, nor Christianity, nor Zoroastrianism.

x: The Almighty says: God guides with this clear Book, whoever follows the pleasure of God to the paths of peace and the laws of His religion, and brings them out, meaning: and brings out whoever follows His pleasure, and the ha’ and meem in: and brings them out refers to whoever is mentioned, from darknesses into the light, meaning: from the darkness of disbelief and polytheism, to the light and radiance of Islam, by His permission, meaning: by the permission of God, the Almighty and Majestic. And His permission in this place: His making him love faith by removing the seal of disbelief from his heart, and the seal of polytheism from him, and enabling him to see the paths of peace.
What He, the Almighty, meant by His statement:
h
And guides them
, and directs them and directs them, to a straight path, is that He says: to a straight path, which is the upright religion of God in which there is no crookedness.

This is a condemnation from God Almighty for the Christians, men and women, who have strayed from the paths of peace, and an argument from Him for His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their slander against him by claiming that he had a son. God Almighty says: I swear, those who said: God is the Messiah, son of Mary, have disbelieved. Their disbelief in that is their covering up the truth by abandoning the denial of a son for God Almighty, and their claim that the Messiah is God, a slander and a lie against Him. We have explained the meaning of the Messiah previously, so there is no need to repeat it here.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the Christians who have slandered me and have strayed from the right path by saying: God is the Messiah, son of Maryam 19:Who has control over anything from God? He says: Who is able to repel anything from the command of God Almighty, so that He may return it when He decrees it? From the saying: I have given control over so-and-so’s affairs, if he is unable to carry out an order except through it. And his saying:
h
If He willed to destroy the Messiah
, son of Mary, and his mother, and everyone on earth, he says: Who is it that can prevent anything from God’s command,
h
if He willed to destroy the Messiah

, son of Mary, by eliminating him from the earth, and eliminating his mother Mary, and eliminating everyone on earth from creation altogether. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these ignorant Christians: If the Messiah were as you claim - that he is God, and he is not - he would have been able to repel God’s command when it came to him to destroy him and his mother.

And he destroyed his mother, but he was not able to repel His command when it came down. So in that there is a lesson for you if you consider, and an argument against you if you understand: that the Messiah was a human being like all the children of Adam, and that God the Almighty is the One who cannot be defeated or subdued and whose command cannot be repelled, rather He is the Ever-Living, the Eternal, the Self-Sustaining, who gives life and causes death, creates and destroys, and He is the Living One who does not die.

By that, the Blessed and Exalted means: God has control over what is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them - meaning: what is between the heaven and the earth - He destroys whomever He wills of that and keeps whatever He wills of it, and creates what He wills and eliminates what He loves. Nothing prevents Him from doing what He wills of that, and nothing repels Him from it. He executes His judgment upon them, and His decree is carried out upon them - not the Messiah, who, if his Lord wanted to destroy him and destroy his mother, would not have the power to repel what his Lord wanted for him of that. God Almighty says: How can there be a god to be worshipped who is unable to repel the evil that others intended for him, and unable to avert the destruction that befell him? Rather, the god who is worshipped is the one who owns everything, and in whose hand is the control of everything in the heavens and the earth and everything in between.

So He, the Most High, said: And what is between them. He mentioned the heavens in the plural form, and did not say: And what is between them, because the meaning is: And what is between these two types of things, as Al-Ra’i said: Knocks, that is my concern, I read them to you, fertile camels like bows and squints He said: Knocks, informing about two things, then he said: These are my concerns, so he returned to the meaning of the speech. And His statement:
h
He creates what He wills
, the Most High says: And
h
He creates what He wills

and brings it into existence, and brings it out from a state of nonexistence into a state of existence, and none is able to do that except God, the One, the Subduer. What He means by that is that He has the management of the heavens and the earth and everything in between and its disposition, its annihilation and its destruction, and the creation of whatever He wills of what does not exist and has no origin.

He says: That is not for anyone but Me, so how did you claim, you liars, that the Messiah is a god, while he is not capable of any of that, rather he is not able to ward off harm from himself or his mother, nor Surat al-Ma’idah 5:17 They have certainly disbelieved who say, "God is the Messiah, the son of Mary." Say, "Then who can have any control over God
h
if He willed to destroy the Messiah
, the son of Mary, and his mother, and whoever is on the earth, all together?" And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them.
h
He creates what He wills
, and God is over all things competent. bring any benefit to her except with My permission?

God Almighty says: God is the worshipped, He is able to do all things, and He owns all things, for whom nothing He wills is impossible, and nothing He seeks can overcome, He is able to destroy the Messiah, his mother, and everyone on earth, not the helpless one who is unable to prevent himself from the harm that has befallen him from God, nor to prevent his mother from destruction.

evidence.text: He mentioned the heavens in the plural form, and did not say: And what is between them, because the meaning is: And what is between these two types of things, as Al-Ra’i said: Knocks, that is my concern, I read them to you, fertile camels like bows and squints He said: Knocks, informing about two things, then he said: These are my concerns, so he returned to the meaning of the speech.

x: This is report from God Almighty about a group of Jews and Christians who said this statement. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas the name of the Jews who said that.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying, Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq,
m: saying, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, narrated to me, saying, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, saying: “Nu’man bin Ada’, Bahri bin Amr, and Shas bin Adi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to them, and called them to God and warned them of His wrath. They said: What do you fear, O Muhammad? By God, we are the sons of God and His beloved!! Like the Christians say. So God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed about them: ‘And the Jews and the Christians say, “We are the sons of God and His beloved,”’ until the end of the verse. Al-Saddī used to say about this:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “And the Jews and Christians said, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved.’ As for ‘the sons of God,’ they said, ‘God revealed to Israel that a child of yours will enter the Fire, and they will be in it for forty days until it purifies them and consumes their sins. Then a caller will call out, ‘Bring out every circumcised person from the children of Israel.’ So bring them out. That is what He said, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.’”
r
(Al Imran 3:24)

. As for the Christians, a group of them said about the Messiah, ‘He is the son of God.’ The Arabs may present the report, if they boast, as a report about the group, even if what they boast about is the action of one of them, so they say: We are the generous and noble ones, and the generous one among them is only one of them, and the subject is not the speaker, as Jarir said: We stab Abu Mandusa, the blacksmith, with a spear, and the blood of a neighbor flows from his well He said: We infiltrated, and the infiltrator was a man from the people of Jarir other than him, so he reported the report as a report from a group of people, one of whom was one of them.

c: Thus God Almighty informed us
m: about the Christians that they said that, in this manner, God willing. And his saying:
h
And his beloved ones

, which is the plural of beloved. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say to these liars who slander their Lord, Why has your Lord punished you? He says: Why would your Lord punish you for your sins, if the matter is as you claim, that you are His sons and beloved ones, for the Beloved does not punish His Beloved, and you admit that He will punish you? This is because the Jews said: God will punish us for forty days, the number of days in which we worshipped the calf, then He will bring us all out of it. So God said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say to them: If you are, as you say, the sons of God and His beloved ones, then why has He punished you for your sins? He, the Mighty and Sublime, teaches them that they are people of slander and lies against God, the Mighty and Sublime.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them: The matter is not as you claim, that you are the sons of God and His beloved, but you are human beings from among those He created. He says: He was created from the children of Adam. God created you like all the children of Adam. If you do good, you will be rewarded for your goodness, just as all the children of Adam are rewarded for their goodness. And if you do evil, you will be rewarded for your evil, just as others are rewarded for it. You have nothing with God except what others of His creation have, for He forgives whomever He wills of the people of faith in Him, so He pardons them with His grace and covers them for them with His mercy, so He does not punish them for them. We have explained the meaning of forgiveness in a place other than this with its evidence, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

And He punishes whomever He wills, meaning: He is just with whomever He wills of His creation, punishing him for his sins and disgracing him for them in front of all witnesses, so He does not conceal them from him. This is a warning from God, the Almighty, to those Jews and Christians who rely on the status of their chosen ancestors with God, whom God, the Almighty, the Almighty, preferred because of their obedience to Him, and chose them because of their hastening to please Him, and their patience in the face of what befell them. He says to them: Do not be deceived by the status of those with Me and their status with Me, for they only attained what they attained from Me through obedience to Me, and preferring My pleasure over their own desires, not through wishful thinking. So strive to obey Me, and desist from My command, and refrain from what I have forbidden them, for I only forgive the sins of whomever I wish to forgive from among the people of My obedience, and I punish whomever I wish to punish from among the people of My disobedience, not for those whose fathers were close to Me, but who are My enemies and oppose My commands and prohibitions.
Al-Saddī used to say about this:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He forgives whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills
, meaning: He guides whomever He wills among you in this world and forgives him, and He causes whomever He wills among you to die in his disbelief and punishes him.

x: He says: To God belongs the management and control of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them. In His hand is its command, and His is its kingdom. He disposes of it as He wills and manages it as He likes. He has no partner in anything of it, and no one has dominion over it with Him. So know, O you who say: We are the children of God and His beloved, that if He punishes you for your sins, you will have no one to prevent Him from doing so, nor will you be able to defend Him from it, because there is no kinship between anyone and Him that would favor him for that reason, and no one has dominion over anything below Him, that would stand between Him and Him if He wanted to punish him for his sins. To Him is the destination and return of everything. So fear, O slanderers, His punishment of you for your sins after you have returned to Him, and do not be deceived by hopes and the virtues of your fathers and ancestors.
By His saying,
h
O People of the Book

, He, the Most High, meant the Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day this verse was revealed. That is because they - or: some of them, according to what was mentioned - when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to believe in him and in what he brought to them from God, they said: God did not send a prophet after Moses, nor did He send down a book after the Torah! Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, who narrated, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, who narrated, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Muadh bin Jabal, Saad bin Ubadah, and Uqbah bin Wahb said to the Jews: O group of Jews, fear God, for by God you know that he is the Messenger of God!

You used to mention him to us before his mission, and you used to describe him to us with his characteristics! Rafi bin Huraymila and Wahb bin Yahudah said: We did not say this to you, and God did not send down any book after Moses, nor did He send a bearer of good tidings or a warner after him! So God, the Almighty, revealed regarding that from their words: “O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you [what is] clear [to the truth] after a hiatus among the messengers - lest you should say, ‘There has come to us no bearer of good tidings or a warner.’ But there has come to you a bearer of good tidings and a warner. And God is over all things competent.”
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
Our Messenger has come to you

, is that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, our Messenger, has come to you, making clear to you, meaning: making the truth known to you, clarifying to you the signs of guidance, and guiding you to the approved religion of God, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you the truth after a hiatus among the messengers

, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He came with the Criterion by which God distinguished between truth and falsehood. In it is God’s clarification, His light and His guidance, and protection for whoever takes it. After a period of messengers, he says: after a cessation of messengers, and the period in this place means cessation, he says:
h
Our Messenger has come to you

explaining to you the truth and guidance, after a cessation of messengers. The active period is from the saying of the speaker: This matter became calm and quiet, meaning it became still and quiet. Likewise, the period in this place means: stillness, meaning the stillness of the arrival of the messengers, which is its cessation. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the length of that period, and there was a difference in the narration of that from Qatada. Muammar narrated on his authority:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
After a period of time between the messengers
, he said: There were five hundred and sixty years between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Saeed bin Abi Aruba narrated on his authority:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both, he told us was six hundred years, or whatever he wanted of that, and God knows best.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of his companions,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Our Messenger has come to you

, making clear to you the truth after a hiatus from the messengers. He said: There were five hundred and forty years between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both. Muammar said, Qatadah said: Five hundred and sixty years.

x: Others said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid, who said:

c: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
After a period of time between the messengers

, he said: The period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both, was four hundred and thirty-some years. What he means by his saying: That you should say, ‘No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us,’ Surat al-Ma’idah 5:19 O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you [what is] [the Qur’an] after a period of messengers, lest you say, "No bringer of good tidings or warner came to us." But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent. is that you should not say, and so that you should not say, as God Almighty said: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray
r
(An-Nisa’: 176)
, meaning: that you should not go astray, and so that you should not go astray. The meaning of the words is:
h
Our Messenger has come to you

, explaining to you after a period of messengers, so that you will not say, No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us. The Almighty informs them that He has cut off their excuse with His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and has conveyed to them the argument. By Al-Bashir, he means the bearer of good tidings, the one who obeys God and believes in Him and His Messenger, and does what He has given him from God, with great reward in the Hereafter. And by Al-Nadhir, he means the one who warns, the one who disobeys Him and belies His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and does other than what God has given him of His commands and prohibitions, with what he cannot bear of painful punishment in the Hereafter, and severe torment on the Day of Resurrection.

x: God Almighty says to these Jews whose characteristics we have described: We have excused you, and we have argued with you through our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we have sent him to you to explain to you what is unclear to you about your religion, so that you will not say: No Messenger has come to us from you to explain to us what misguidance we are upon. A Messenger has come to you from Me, giving good tidings to whoever believes in Me and does what I have commanded him and refrains from what I have forbidden him, and warning whoever disobeys Me and opposes My command. I am the One who is capable of all things. I am the One who is capable of punishing whoever disobeys Me and rewarding whoever obeys Me. So fear My punishment for your disobedience to Me and your denial of My Messenger, and seek My reward for your obedience to Me and your belief in My good tidings and My warner, for I am the One for whom nothing I desire is impossible, and nothing I seek escapes from Him.

This is also from God, a definition for His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, of the long-standing persistence of these Jews in error, their distance from the truth, their poor choices for themselves, their severe opposition to their prophets, and their slowness in returning to the right path, despite the abundance of God's blessings upon them, and the succession of His favors and blessings upon them, thereby comforting His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, for what befalls him in terms of their treatment, and what befalls him in terms of their suffering for the sake of God. God says to him, peace and blessings be upon him: Do not grieve over what has befallen you from them, for turning away from God, and being far from the truth, and what is in it for them is their share in this world and the hereafter, from their customs and the customs of their ancestors and their forefathers - and be comforted by what your brother Moses, peace and blessings be upon him, suffered from them - and remember when Moses said to them: O my people,
h
remember the favor of God upon you
, meaning: Remember the favors of God upon you, and His favors before you, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah:
m: Remember the blessings of God upon you, he said: God’s favors upon you and His days.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Remember the favor of God upon you
, meaning: the well-being of God Almighty.

x: We chose what we said because God did not specify any of the blessings, but rather made it general by mentioning the blessings, so that applies to well-being and other things, since well-being is one of the meanings of blessings.

By this, may His praise be glorified, He meant that Moses reminded his people, the Children of Israel, of the days of God with them, and of His blessings before them, urging them thereby to follow God’s command in fighting the tyrants. He said to them: Remember the blessing of God upon you, that He favored you, by placing among you prophets who bring you His revelation, and inform you of report of the unseen, and He did not give that to anyone other than you in your time. It was said: The prophets whom Moses mentioned that they were made among them are those whom Moses chose when he went to the mountain, and they are the seventy whom God mentioned when He said: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time (al-A’raf 7:153).
h
And He made you kings
, He made others serve you as servants. It was said: Moses said that to them because at that time there was no one other than them who served him from the sons of Adam.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when Moses said to his people
, ‘O my people,
h
remember the favor of God upon you
when He made prophets among you
h
and made you kings
,’ he said: We used to say that they were the first of the sons of Adam to whom servants were made subservient and they became kings.

x: Others said: Everyone who owns a house, a servant, and a woman is a king, whoever he is among the people.
Who said that?

c: Yunus bin Abdul A'la told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Hani told us:
m: that he heard Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Habli say: I heard Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, and a man asked him and said: Are we not among the poor emigrants? Abdullah said to him: Do you have a wife to whom you can take refuge? He said: Yes! He said: Do you have a house to live in? He said: Yes! He said: Then you are among the rich! He said: I have a servant. He said: Then you are among the kings.

c: Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar told us, he said, Abu Damrah Anas bin Ayyad told us, he said:
m: I heard Zaid bin Aslam say:
h
And He made you kings
, so I do not know except that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a house and a servant is a king.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: that he recited this verse:
h
And He made you kings
, and he said: Is a king anything but a mount, a servant, and a house?

x: Those who said this statement said: Moses only said that to them because they owned houses and servants, and had women and husbands.
Who said that?

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur - he
m: said: I think it was on the authority of Al-Hakam -
h
And He made you kings
, he said: When a man from the Children of Israel had a house, a wife, and a servant, he was considered a king.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: H, and Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
h
And He made you kings
, he said: the house, the woman, and the servant. Sufyan said: Or, two of the three.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He made you kings
, he said: the house and the servant.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam or someone else, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He made you kings
, he said: the wife, the servant, and the house.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
And He made you kings
, he said: He made for you wives, servants, and houses.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Tamim, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And He made you kings
, he said: If a man from the Children of Israel had a wife, a servant, and a house, he was called a king.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And made you kings
, he said: He made servants their kings. Qatada said: They were the first to have servants as kings.

c: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Aban told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And He made you kings
, he said: He made for you wives, servants, and houses.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying:
h
And made you kings is that they own themselves
, their families, and their money.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And He made you kings
, a man among you owns himself, his family, and his money.

x: There is a difference of opinion about who was meant by this address.
Some of them said: He meant the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds
, they said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
b.via: Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair

x: Others said: It refers to the people of Moses, peace be upon him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They are the people of Moses.

c: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Aban told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: They will be among him on that day. Then they differed about what God gave them that He did not give to anyone in the worlds.

x: Some of them said: It is manna, quails, stones, and clouds.
Who said that?

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: manna, quails, stones, and clouds.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, meaning: the people of that time, manna, quails, stones, and clouds.

x: Others said: It is the house, the servant, and the wife.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Sarri told us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds
, he said: A man will have a house, a servant, and a wife.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, the manna, the quails, the stones, and the Surat al-Ma’idah 5:20
h
And when Moses said to his people
, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He made among you prophets
h
and made you kings
and gave you that which He had not given to anyone in the worlds." clouds.

x: The most correct of the two interpretations in this regard, in my opinion, is the statement of the one who said: And He gave you what He did not give to anyone in the worlds, in the context of His statement:
h
Remember the favor of God upon you
, and it is connected to it. There is no indication in the speech that his statement,
h
And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds

, is diverted from addressing those whom He began by addressing at the beginning of the verse. Since that is the case, then it is more appropriate for it to be addressed to them than to say that it is diverted from them to others. If someone thinks that his statement,
h
And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds

, cannot be addressed to them, since the nation of Muhammad had been given from the honor of God, the Almighty and Majestic, through their Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, what was not given to anyone else - and they are from the worlds - then he has thought incorrectly.
That is because his statement,
h
And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds

, is an address from Moses, peace be upon him, to his people at that time, and he meant by that the scholars of his time, not the scholars of every time. And no one in the world had been given at that time from the blessings and honor of God what his people, peace be upon him, had been given. So the speech came from him, peace be upon him, in that regard, not to all scholars of every time.

evidence.text: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: that he recited this verse: And He made you kings, and he said: Is a king anything but a mount, a servant, and a house?
