x: This is report from God Almighty about what Moses, peace be upon him, said to his people from the Children of Israel, and his command to them - based on God’s command to him - to command them to enter
h
the Holy Land
. Then the people of interpretation differed about the land that he meant by
h
the Holy Land
Some of them said: He meant the mountain and what is around it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The Holy Land
is Al-Tur and what is around it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Enter
h
the Holy Land
, he said: Al-Tur and what is around it.

x: Others said: It is the Levant.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Holy Land
, he said: It is the Levant.

x: Others said: It is the land of Jericho.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you
, he said: Jericho.

c: Yusuf bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: It is Jericho.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It is Jericho. It was said that
h
the Holy Land
is Damascus, Palestine and some of Jordan. By his saying: the holy, he meant the purified and blessed, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The Holy Land
, he said: The blessed one.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: The most correct of the sayings about this is to say: It is
h
the Holy Land

, as the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, said, because the saying about it that it is a land apart from a land, the truth of its correctness cannot be known except by report, and no report about that can be used as a definitive testimony. However, it will not be outside of being from the land between the Euphrates and the Arish of Egypt, because of the consensus of all the people of interpretation, biography, and scholars of report on that. What he means by his saying: which God has written for you is that which He has established in the Preserved Tablet as being for you dwellings and homes, without the tyrants in it.

How could He say: which God has ordained for you, when you know that they did not enter it by His saying: It is forbidden to them? How could it be established in the Preserved Tablet that they are dwellings for them, but it is forbidden for them to inhabit them?
It was written for the Children of Israel as a home and dwellings, and they inhabited it and settled in it and it became theirs, as God Almighty said. And Moses said to them: Enter
h
the Holy Land

which God has written for you, meaning by that: God wrote it for the Children of Israel, and those whom Moses commanded to enter it were from the Children of Israel, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not mean that God Almighty wrote it for those whom He commanded to enter it specifically.

If someone were to say: It was written for some of them and for a specific one of them, then he would make the statement general, and what is meant by it is the specific one, since Joshua and Caleb had entered, and they were among those addressed by this statement, then it would also be a correct view. Ibn Ishaq said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq,
m: which God has written for you, which God has given you. Al-Suddi used to say: The meaning of wrote in this context is: ordered.

c: Musa bin Harun told us that, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Enter
h
the Holy Land
that God has written for you, which God has commanded you to do.

x: This is report from God Almighty about what Moses, peace be upon him, said to his people from the Children of Israel, when he ordered them, according to the order of God Almighty to him, to enter
h
the Holy Land
, that he said to them: Go, O people, to the order of God that He ordered you to do, to enter
h
the Holy Land

, and do not turn back, he says: do not go back, turning back, on your heels, meaning: behind you, but go forward to the order of God that He ordered you to do, to enter upon the people whom God ordered you to fight and attack in their land, and God Almighty has written it for you as a dwelling and a place of settlement. What he means by his saying:
h
Then you will return as losers
, is that you will leave disappointed and destroyed. We have explained the meaning of loss in other places, with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
What was the reason for what Moses said to his people when he ordered them to enter
h
the Holy Land
: Do not turn back and become losers, or does he deserve loss if he does not enter a land that was made for him?

God Almighty had commanded them to fight those in it who disbelieved in Him and imposed on them entering it, so the people deserved the loss by abandoning it when God imposed it on them for two reasons: One of them: wasting the obligation of jihad that God Almighty had imposed on them, and the second: their disobedience to God’s command in abandoning entering the land, and their saying to their prophet Moses, peace be upon him, when he said to them: Enter
h
the Holy Land
: We will not enter it until they leave it, so if they leave it, then we will enter. Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O my people
h
enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you
, they were commanded to do so, just as they were commanded to perform prayer, zakat, Hajj, and Umrah.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about the response of the people of Moses, peace be upon him, when he ordered them to enter the Holy Land: that they refused to answer him to what he ordered them to do, and they argued with him about that by saying: In the Holy Land that you are ordering us to enter, there are a mighty people whom we have no strength to fight, nor do we have any power over. And they called them mighty because, due to the severity of their violence and the greatness of their character, as we have been told, they had subdued all other nations. The root of the word al-Jabbar is the one who reforms his own affairs and the affairs of others. Then it was used for anyone who brings benefit to himself, whether rightly or wrongly, seeking to reform it, until it was said of the one who transgresses against what is not his, out of oppression of people, and insolence towards them, and insolence towards his Lord, al-Jabbar.

It is actually a verb from their saying: So-and-so repaired this fracture, if he repaired it and fixed it. From this is the saying of the rajaz poet: The religion has mended God, so mend the blindness of the Merciful, whoever turns to the blindness He means: God has reformed the religion, so it has been reformed. And among the names of God Almighty is the Compeller, because He is the one who reforms the affairs of His servants, the one who subdues them with His power.
Among the greatness of their creation that I mentioned is:

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to me, he said, Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in a story he mentioned
m: about the matter of Moses and the Children of Israel, he said: Then he ordered them to march to Jericho - which is the land of Jerusalem - so they marched, until they were close to them, Moses sent twelve leaders from all the tribes of the Children of Israel, so they marched intending to bring him report of the giants, but a man from the giants called Aaj met them, so he took the twelve and put them in his cloak, and on his head were loads of firewood, and he went with them to his wife and said: Look at these people who claim that they want to fight us!! So he threw them down in front of her, and said: Shall I not crush them with my feet? His wife said: No, rather leave them alone until they tell their people what they saw! So he did that.
b.via: Al-Suddi in a story he mentioned

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, Sufyan told us, Abu Saeed told us, Ikrimah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Moses was commanded to enter the city of the giants. Moses and those with him set out until they stopped near the city - which was Jericho - and he sent twelve spies to them, one from each tribe, to bring him report of the people. He said: So they entered the city and saw something terrible about their appearance, bodies, and size. So they entered a garden belonging to one of them. The owner of the garden came to pick the fruits from his garden, so he began to pick the fruits and look at their tracks, and followed them. Whenever he found one of them, he would take it and put it in his sleeve with the fruits, and he went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said: You have seen our situation and our matter, go and inform your master. He said: So they returned to Moses and told him what they had seen of their situation.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, therein are a people of mighty men, he mentioned to us that they had bodies and character that no one else had.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: who said: Moses, peace be upon him, said to his al-Nas 114:I will send men to bring me their report. He took a man from each tribe, and they were twelve chiefs. He said: Go to them and tell me their story and what they have been commanded to do, and do not fear. Indeed, God is with you as long as you establish prayer, give zakat, believe in His messengers, support them, and lend God a good loan. The people went until they attacked them, and they saw people with bodies that were amazing in size and strength. And - according to what was mentioned - one of the tyrants saw them, and they did not spare themselves from hiding themselves when they saw the wonder. So that tyrant took men from them, and he came to their leader and threw them in front of him, and they were amazed and laughed at them. Then one of them said: These people claimed that they wanted to attack you!! And that if it were not for what God had protected them from, they would have been killed, and that they returned to Moses, peace be upon him, and told him the wonder.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Twelve leaders, from each tribe of the Children of Israel, a man. Moses sent them to the giants, and they found them, two of them entering into the sleeve of one of them, throwing them down, and no one would carry their bunch of grapes except five people between them on a piece of wood, and five people, or four, would enter into half of the pomegranate when its seeds were removed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Wazir bin Qais told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: There are tyrants in it. He said: lowly people who have no morals.

x: This is report from God Almighty about what the people of Moses said to Moses, in response to his saying to them: Enter the Holy Land which God has written for you. They said: We will not enter it until they leave it, meaning: until the tyrants who are in it leave the Holy Land, out of cowardice and fear of fighting them. And they said to him: If these tyrants leave it, we will enter it, otherwise we will not be able to enter it while they are in it, because we have no power over them and no ability to fight them. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that Caleb bin Yufna silenced the people from Moses, peace be upon him, and said to them: We will ascend the land and inherit it, and we will have power through them! As for those who were with him, they said: We cannot reach that people, because they are bolder than us! Then those spies told the Children of Israel the report and said: We passed through a land and felt it, and behold, it devoured its inhabitants, and we saw its men as huge, and we saw giants, the sons of giants, and we were like locusts in their eyes!

So the group of the Children of Israel became alarmed, and they raised their voices in weeping, and the people wept that night, and whispered to Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Oh, if only we had died in the land of Egypt! Oh, if only we had died in this wilderness, and God had not brought us into this land to fall into war, so that our women, children, and burdens would be spoils! If we had remained in the land of Egypt, it would have been better for us! The man said to his companions: Come, let us appoint a leader and go back to Egypt.

This is report from God Almighty about the two righteous men from the people of Moses: Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yufana, that they were faithful to what Moses had entrusted them with, which was to leave informing his people, the Children of Israel - whom he had ordered to enter the Holy Land against the tyrants of the Canaanites - of what they had seen and witnessed of the severity of the tyrants’ brutality and the greatness of their creation, and God Almighty described them as being among those who fear God and observe Him in His commands and prohibitions, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us,
m: H, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, H, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God bestowed favor, said, he said: Kilab ibn Yafna and Joshua ibn Nun.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God bestowed His favor, said, he said: Joshua ibn Nun and Kilab ibn Yafna, and they were among the leaders.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid in a story he mentioned, he said:
m: So the leaders returned, each of them forbidding his tribe from fighting them, except for Joshua bin Nun and Kalb bin Yafnah, who ordered the tribes to fight the tyrants and struggle against them, but they disobeyed them and obeyed the others, so they are the two men upon whom God bestowed His blessings.
b.via: Mujahid in a story he mentioned

c: Ibn Hamid and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: like the hadith of Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, except that Ibn Hamid said in his hadith: They are among the twelve leaders.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said,
m: Abu Saeed said, Ikrimah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas in a story he mentioned. He said: So they returned - meaning the twelve leaders - to Moses and told him what they had witnessed of their situation. Moses said to them: Keep their affair secret, and do not tell anyone from the army about it, because if you tell them this report, they will fail and will not enter the city. He said: So each man of them went and told his relative and cousin, except for these two men - Joshua bin Nun and Kalb bin Yufnah - because they kept it secret and did not tell anyone about it, and they are the ones about whom God the Almighty said: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, until His saying: and among the wicked people.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God bestowed His favor, said, and they were the ones who concealed them: Joshua bin Al-Nun, the young man of Moses, and Calub bin Juphnah, the son-in-law of Moses.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: “Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said: Caleb and Joshua bin al-Nun, the young man of Moses.”

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Two men from among those who feared said
, upon whom God bestowed favor, and the two men upon whom God bestowed favor from among the Children of Israel were: Joshua bin al-Nun, and Calub bin Yufnah.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said, he told us that the two men were Joshua bin Nun and Caleb.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ: That Moses said to the leaders when they returned and told him
m: the wonder: Do not tell anyone what you have seen, for God will open it for you and make you prevail over it after what you have seen. And the people have spread the report among the Children of Israel, so two men from those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, stood up - one of them, as we heard, was Joshua bin Nun, who was the young man of Moses, and the other was Caleb - and they said: Enter upon them through the gate to if you are believers.
b.via: That Moses said to the leaders when they returned and

x: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: Two men from among those who fear said. This was read by the people of Hijaz, Iraq and Syria: Two men of those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said, with the opening of the ya of they feared, according to the interpretation that we mentioned from the one we mentioned earlier, that they were Joshua bin Nun and Caleb, from the people of Moses, among those who feared God, and upon whom God had bestowed success. Qatada used to say: In some readings: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: H, and Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Two men from among those who feared God’s favor upon them said, in some versions: They feared God’s favor upon them. This also indicates the correctness of the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as we mentioned about him, that he said: Joshua and Caleb.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair
m: that he used to recite this: Two men from those who fear said, with the dammah on the ya’, God has bestowed His blessings upon them.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub - and we do not know
m: that he heard it from him - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: that he used to read it with a dammah on the ya’ from yakhāfuun. It is as if Saeed went in this reading to the fact that the two men whom God told about who said to the Children of Israel: Enter upon them through the gate, and when you enter it, you will be victorious, were from the tribe of giants, and they had converted to Islam and followed Moses. So they were from the sons of giants whom the Children of Israel feared, even though they were opposed to them in religion. A similar interpretation was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
b.via: Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub - and we do not know

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you and do not turn back and become losers

, he said: It is the city of the tyrants. When Moses and his people descended there, he sent twelve men from among them - they are the leaders whose mission he mentioned - to bring him report of them. So they set out, and a man from the tyrants met them, so he put them in his cloak, and carried them until he came to the city, and called out to his people, so they gathered around him, and said: Who are you? They said: We are the people of Moses, we were sent to you to bring him report of you! So they gave them a grape the size of a man’s udder, and they said to them: Go to Moses and his people and tell them: Estimate the size of their fruit! So when they came to them, they said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here! Two men from among those who feared God, upon whom God had bestowed favor, and who were from the people of Medina, became Muslims and followed Moses and Aaron. They said to Moses, “Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will be victorious. And upon God rely, if you should be believers.”

x: According to this reading and interpretation, none of the twelve leaders concealed from the Children of Israel what Moses had ordered them to conceal from them of what they had seen and witnessed of the greatness of the giants’ bodies, the severity of their violence, and the wonders of their affairs. Rather, they disclosed all of that. The one who said to the people and to Moses, Enter upon them through the gate, were two men from the sons of those whom the Children of Israel feared and dreaded the giants entering upon them. They had converted to Islam and followed the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who reads: Of those who fear, God has bestowed His favor upon them both, due to the consensus of the reciters of the regions on it, and that what is widely recited from them is an argument that cannot be contradicted, and what is recited by one person alone, error and forgetfulness are permissible in it. Then in the consensus of the argument in interpreting it that they are two men from the companions of Moses from the Children of Israel and that they are Joshua and Kalb, there is no need to cite evidence for the correctness of the reading with the opening of the ya’ in that, and the corruption of others. And it is the correct interpretation in our view, due to what we have mentioned of their consensus on it. As for his saying:
h
God bestowed His favor upon them
, it means:
h
God bestowed His favor upon them

by obeying God in obeying His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, and their adherence to his command, and their abstention from what he, peace be upon him, forbade them from, of divulging what they witnessed of the strange matter of the tyrants to the Children of Israel, which their other companions who were with them from the leaders had told about.
It has been said that the meaning of this is: God bestowed fear upon them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said,
m: Surat al-Ma’idah 5:23 Two men from among those who feared, upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, said, "Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious. And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers."

c: Khalaf bin Tamim told us, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Sahl bin Ali,
m: his saying:
h
Two men from among those who feared said
, upon whom God bestowed His favor, he said:
h
God bestowed His favor upon them
with fear. Al-Dahhak and a group of others said something similar to what we said about that.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: “
h
Two men from among those who feared said
: God has bestowed His favor upon them,” with guidance, so He guided them, and they were on the religion of Moses, and they were in the city of the tyrants.

x: This is report from God Almighty about the words of the two men who feared God to the Children of Israel, when they were cowardly and afraid to enter upon the tyrants, when they heard their report, and the leaders who spread what they had seen of their affair informed them, and they said: Indeed, there are tyrants in it, and we will not enter it until they leave it.
So they said to them: Enter upon them, O people, through the gate of their city, for God is with you, and He is your supporter, and if you enter the gate, you will defeat them, as:

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge of the first book, he said:
m: When the children of Israel were about to return to Egypt, when the leaders informed them of what they had been told about the giants, Moses and Aaron fell on their faces in prostration before the assembly of the children of Israel, and Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yufana tore their clothes, and they were spies of the land, and they said to the assembly of the children of Israel: We passed through the land and found it to be good, our Lord was pleased with it for us and gave it to us, and it . . . flows with milk and honey, but do one thing: Do not disobey God, and do not fear the people who are in it, for they are our bread and are given into our hand. Their pride has gone from them, and God is with us, so do not fear them. So the assembly of the children of Israel wanted to stone them.
b.via: some of the people of knowledge of the first book

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that they sent twelve men, one from each tribe, as spies for them, and to bring them report of the people. As for ten, they were cowardly towards their people and disliked them entering upon them. As for the two men, they ordered their people to enter it, and to follow the command of God, and they desired that, and they informed their people that they would be victorious if they did that.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Upon them is the door, the village of the tyrants.

x: This is also report from God, the Almighty, about the words of the two men who feared God, that they said to the people of Moses, encouraging them with that and encouraging them to follow God’s command to enter upon the tyrants in their city: O people, trust in God in your entry upon them. They said to them: Trust in God, for He is with you if you obey Him in what He has commanded you to do in jihad against your enemy. And what they meant by their words: If you are believers is if you believe your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he informed you about from your Lord about victory and triumph over them, and in other things of his information about his Lord, and believe that your Lord is able to fulfill what He promised you of empowering you in the lands of His enemy and your enemy.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: Two men from among those who fear said.

This was read by the people of Hijaz, Iraq and Syria: Two men of those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said, with the opening of the ya of they feared, according to the interpretation that we mentioned from the one we mentioned earlier, that they were Joshua bin Nun and Caleb, from the people of Moses, among those who feared God, and upon whom God had bestowed success.
It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he used to recite this: Two men from those who fear said, with the dammah on the ya’, God has bestowed His blessings upon them.

Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub - and we do not know that he heard it from him - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: that he used to read it with a dammah on the ya’ from yakhāfuun.

It is as if Saeed went in this reading to the fact that the two men whom God told about who said to the Children of Israel: Enter upon them through the gate, and when you enter it, you will be victorious, were from the tribe of giants, and they had converted to Islam and followed Moses.

Abu Jaʿfar said: According to this reading and interpretation, none of the twelve leaders concealed from the Children of Israel what Moses had ordered them to conceal from them of what they had seen and witnessed of the greatness of the giants’ bodies, the severity of their violence, and the wonders of their affairs.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who reads: Of those who fear, God has bestowed His favor upon them both, due to the consensus of the reciters of the regions on it, and that what is widely recited from them is an argument that cannot be contradicted, and what is recited by one person alone, error and forgetfulness are permissible in it.

Then in the consensus of the argument in interpreting it that they are two men from the companions of Moses from the Children of Israel and that they are Joshua and Kalb, there is no need to cite evidence for the correctness of the reading with the opening of the ya’ in that, and the corruption of others.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about the words of the leaders of Moses’ people to Moses, when they desired to fight their enemy, and promised them victory from God if they opposed them and entered upon them through the gate of their city, that they said to him: We will never enter it, meaning: We will never enter their city. The letter ha and the letter alif in his saying:
h
We will not enter it are from the mention of the city

. And by their saying: Forever, they mean as long as they are in it, meaning: as long as the tyrants were residing in that city that God had written for them and which they had been commanded to enter, “So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here,” we will not come with you, O Moses, if you go to them to fight them, but we will leave you to go alone, you and your Lord, and fight them.

Some of them said about that: The meaning of the words is not: Go, you, and let your Lord go with you and fight, but rather it means: Go, you, O Moses, and let your Lord help you, and that is because God Almighty is not permitted to go. This would only require seeking a way out if the report was about a group of believers. As for a group of people who disagree with God Almighty and His Messenger, there is no reason to seek a way out for their words in what they said about God Almighty and slandered Him, except in what resembles their disbelief and misguidance. It was reported that Al-Miqdad said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something contrary to what the people of Moses said to Moses.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mukhariq, on the authority of Tariq:
m: that Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We do not say as the Children of Israel said: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, we are sitting here, but we say: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, we are with you fighting.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the day of Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists prevented the sacrificial animals and they were prevented from performing their rituals: I am going with the sacrificial animals and slaughtering them near the House! Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad said to him: By God, we will not be like the leaders of the Children of Israel when they said to their prophet: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, and we are sitting here. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight, and we are fighting with you! When the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard it, they followed one another in that. Ibn Abbas, Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, and a group of others said: They only said this to Moses, peace be upon him, when the matter of the tyrants and the severity of their violence became clear to them. Al-Husayn narrated, he said: I heard Abu Muadh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say:

c: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard al-Dahhak say: God, the Almighty and Majestic, commanded the Children of Israel to march to the Holy Land with their Prophet Moses, peace be upon him. When they were close to Medina, Moses said to them: Enter it. They refused and were cowardly. They sent twelve leaders to look at them. They went and looked and brought a piece of their fruit the size of a man’s udder. They said: Estimate the strength and might of a people; this is their fruit! Then they said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will stay here.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

x: This is report from God, the Almighty, about what the people of Moses said to him when his people said to him what they said, of their saying: "We will never enter it as long as they are in it, so go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will remain right here." He said at that time, and became angry at what they said to him, supplicating: O Lord, I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother. He meant by that: I have no power over anyone to compel them to do what I love and want of obeying You and following Your commands and prohibitions, except over myself and my brother. From the saying: I do not have control over anything of the matter except such and such, meaning: I am not able to do anything other than that. What he means by his saying:
h
So separate us from the wicked people is separate us from them by a judgment from You that You will carry out in us and in them
, and distance them from us.

i: From the saying of the poet:
x: I separated between these two things, meaning: I separated between them, from the saying of the rajaz poet: Oh God, separate him from me as much as you separate two people.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
So separate us from the wicked people
, he said: Judge between me and them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
So separate us from the wicked people
, meaning: Judge between us and them.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Moses, peace be upon him, became angry when the people said to him: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will stay here.” So he called down curses on them and said: My Lord, I have no control over anyone but myself and my brother,
h
so separate us from the wicked people
. And it was a haste on the part of Moses that he hastened.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
So separate us from the wicked people

, meaning: Judge between us and them, and resolve between us and them - all of this is the man saying: Judge between us - so the judgment of God, may His praise be exalted, between him and them is that He called them wicked. By his saying: the wicked, he meant those who have departed from faith in God and in Him to disbelief in God and in Him. We have already demonstrated that the meaning of wickedness is to depart from one thing to another, in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the one who opposes the forty.

Some of them said: The one who made it an enemy is his saying: forbidden. God Almighty forbade the people who disobeyed Him and went against His command from the people of Moses and refused to fight the tyrants from entering their city for forty years. Then He conquered it for them and settled them in it, and He destroyed the tyrants after they fought them, after the forty years had passed and they had left the wilderness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: When the people said to them what they said, and Moses invoked God against them, God revealed to Moses: “
h
It is forbidden to them for forty years

, while they wander in the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.” And they were, as he mentioned, on that day six hundred thousand fighters. So He made them defiantly disobedient because they disobeyed. So they remained for forty years in six farsakhs or less, walking every day in order to get out of it until they became tired and stopped, and behold, they were in the house from which they had departed, and that they complained to Moses about what had been done to them, so he sent down manna and quails upon them, and they were given as much clothing as was available for them, and the young one would grow up and it would be with him in his form. And Moses asked his Lord to give them drink, so He brought the Stone of Mount Tur, which is a white stone. When the people descended, he would strike it with his staff, and twelve springs would come out of it, one for each tribe, and each people would know their drinking place. Then, when forty years had passed, and they were torments because of their transgression and disobedience, it was revealed to Moses: Tell them to go to the Holy Land, for God has sufficed them against their enemy, and tell them, when they come to the mosque, to go to the gate, and prostrate themselves when they enter, and say: Forgiveness - and their saying Forgiveness means that their sins would be forgiven - but most of the people refused and disobeyed, and prostrated on their cheeks, and said: Wheat. So God, the Most High, said: But those who did wrong substituted a statement other than that which was said to them to: because they were defiantly disobedient (al-Baqarah 2:59).

x: Others said: Rather, the object of the forty is they wander in the land. They said: The meaning of the statement is: He said, It is forbidden to them forever, they wander in the land for forty years. They said: And none of those who said, We will never enter it as long as they are in it, so go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here, entered the city of the tyrants. This is because God, the Exalted, forbade it to them. They said: And only Joshua and Kalb entered it from those people, who said to them, Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be victorious, and the children of those whom God forbade entering it, so God wandered them and none of them entered it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: It is forbidden to them, he said: Forever.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, he said, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God: They wander in the land, he said, forty years.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Harun al-Nahwi told us, al-Zubayr bin al-Kharit told me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is forbidden to them for forty years
, while they wander throughout the land, he said: Prohibition means wandering.

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Moses became angry with his people and supplicated against them, saying: My Lord, I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother verse. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, said: Then
h
it is forbidden to them for forty years

, while they wander in the land. When the wilderness was imposed upon them, Moses regretted it. His people who were with him and obeyed him came to him and said to him: What have you done to us, O Moses? So they remained in the wilderness. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:26 He said, "Then
h
it is forbidden to them for forty years

while they wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people." When they came out of the wilderness, the manna and quails were taken away and they ate from the vegetables. Then Moses and Ij met, and Moses ascended ten cubits into the sky, and his staff was ten cubits long, and his height was ten cubits, so he struck Ij’s heel and killed him. None of those who refused to enter the city of the giants with Moses remained, except that he died and did not witness the conquest. Then, when the forty years had passed, God Almighty sent Joshua bin Nun as a prophet. He informed them that he was a prophet and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants. They pledged allegiance to him and believed him. He defeated the tyrants and they attacked them, killing them.

x: A group of the Children of Israel would gather around a man’s neck and strike it, but they would not cut it off.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said,
m: Abu Saeed said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God the Almighty said: When Moses called,
h
It is forbidden to them for forty years

, while they wander in the land. He said: So they entered the wilderness, and everyone who entered the wilderness who was over twenty years old died in the wilderness. He said: So Moses died in the wilderness, and Aaron died before him. He said: So they remained in their wandering for forty years, and Joshua and those who remained with him confronted the city of the giants, and Joshua conquered the city.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God Almighty said:
m: h
It is forbidden to them for forty years

, [the villages] were forbidden to them, so they would not descend into a village nor would they be able to do so, but they would follow the valleys for forty years, and it was mentioned to us that Moses, peace be upon him, died at the age of forty, and that none of them entered the Holy House except their sons and the two men who said what they said.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said, some of the people of knowledge of the first book told me:
m: When the Children of Israel did what they did, of disobeying their prophet and their intention to attack Caleb and Joshua, when he ordered them to enter the city of giants, and they said to them what they said, the greatness of God appeared in the clouds over the door of the Tabernacle of the Cities over all the Children of Israel, and He, the Most High, said to Moses: How long will this people disobey Me? And how long will they not believe in all the signs that I have placed among them? I will strike them with death and destroy them, and I will make for you a people stronger and greater than them. Then Moses said, “The people of Egypt, from whom you have brought this people out by your power, will hear, and the inhabitants of this country, who have heard that you are God among this people, will say, ‘If you had slain all this people as one man, the nations who have heard of your name would have said, ‘This people was slain because they were not able to enter the land for which you created them.’ So they slew them in the wilderness. But let your hand be lifted up and your recompense be great, O LORD, as you have spoken and said to them. For your patience is long-suffering, your graciousness is abundant, and you forgive iniquities and do not repent. You reserve the iniquity of the fathers for the children and the children’s children for three generations and four years. Therefore, O LORD, forgive the iniquities of this people according to the abundance of your graciousness, as you have forgiven them since you brought them out of the land of Egypt until now.” Then God Almighty said to Moses, peace be upon him: I have forgiven them by Your word, but as I live, My praise has filled the entire earth. The people who have seen My praise and My signs that I performed in the land of Egypt and in the deserts, and who have tested Me ten times and have not obeyed Me, will not see the land that I swore to their fathers, nor will those who angered Me see it. As for My servant Caleb, whose spirit was with Me and who followed My desire, I will bring him into the land which he entered and he will see it behind him. Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites were sitting in the mountains, and they set out into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea. And the Lord spoke to Moses and Haran and said to them, How long will this evil company whisper against me? I have heard the whispering of the children of Israel. And he said, "I will do to you as I said to you, and you will cast your corpses into these wildernesses, and according to your reckoning from me, twenty years and more, because you whispered against me. You shall not enter the land to which I raised my hand, nor shall any of you dwell in it except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. And your burdens shall be, as you were, spoil. But your children this day, who did not know good from evil, they shall enter the land, and I know them; they shall have the land that I intended for them. And your corpses shall fall in these wildernesses, and you shall wander in these wildernesses according to the number of days that you counted the land for forty days, instead of each day a year, and you shall be killed for your sins for forty years, and you shall know that you whispered before me." I, God, will do this to this congregation, to this congregation of the children of Israel, who promised before me that they would wander in the wilderness and die there. As for the group that Moses had sent to probe the land, and they stirred up the congregation and spread evil report among them, they all died suddenly, but Joshua and Caleb the son of Joseph lived from the group that had gone out to probe the land. When Moses, peace be upon him, said all these words to the children of Israel, the people were very sad, and they went up to the top of the mountain and said: We will ascend the land of which God Almighty has spoken, because we have sinned. Moses said to them: Why do you transgress against the word of God? For that reason no work will be right for you, and you will not ascend, because God is not with you. Now you will be defeated by your enemies, because of the Amalekites and the Canaanites who are before you. Do not fall into battle because you have turned against God, and God was not with you. So they began to ascend the mountain, and the ark in which were the covenants of God Almighty and Moses did not leave the camp, meaning from the tent, until the Amalekites and the Canaanites descended to that wall, and burned them and chased them out and killed them. So God Almighty caused them to wander in the wilderness for forty years because of their disobedience, until those who deserved disobedience from God in that case perished. He said: When their descendants grew up and their fathers perished and the forty years in which they wandered had passed, Moses set out with them, accompanied by Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yufana, who was, as they claim, the wife of Mary, the daughter of Imran, the sister of Moses and Aaron, and was their son-in-law. Joshua bin Nun came to Jericho with the Children of Israel, and entered it with them, and killed the giants who were in it. Then Moses entered it with the Children of Israel, and he stayed in it as long as God willed him to stay, then God took him to Himself, and no one among creation knows his grave.
b.via: some of the people of knowledge of the first book

x: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is the opinion of those who said: The forty are the object of the prohibition, and that His statement:
h
Forbidden to them for forty years refers to all of the people of Moses

, not some of them but not others. This is because God, the Exalted, mentioned that people in general and did not specify some of them but not others. God, the Exalted, fulfilled what He promised them of punishment, so He made them wander for forty years, and He forbade all of them, during the forty years in which they remained wandering, from entering the Holy Land. None of them entered it, neither young nor old, neither righteous nor wicked, until the years in which God, the Exalted, forbade them from entering it had passed. Then He permitted those who remained of them and their descendants to enter it with the Prophet of God, Moses, and the two men upon whom God had bestowed His favor.

The city of the giants was conquered, God willing, by the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, and Joshua was at his head. This is due to the consensus of the scholars of the reports of the ancients that Og bin Anaq was killed by Moses, peace be upon him. If he had killed him before his fate in the wilderness, and he was one of the greatest tyrants in creation, the Children of Israel would not have been so terrified by the tyrants as they were. But that was, God willing, after the annihilation of the nation that had been terrified and disobeyed its Lord, and refused to enter the city of the tyrants. Moreover, the people of knowledge of the stories of the ancients agree that Balaam bin Ba'ur was among those who aided the tyrants by praying against Moses. It is impossible that this happened while the people of Moses were refraining from fighting and struggling against them, because aid is only needed by those who are sought after.
As for those who are not seeking, there is no reason to need it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf, he said:
m: Og’s bed was eight hundred cubits long, and Moses’ height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits, and he jumped into the sky ten cubits, and he struck Og and hit his heel, and he fell dead, and it became a bridge for people to walk over.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Atiyah told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Moses’ staff was ten cubits long, and his jump was ten cubits long, and his height was ten cubits, so he jumped and hit the heel of Awj and killed him, and it was a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year. The meaning of: They wander in the land is that they are confused and go astray. Hence, the man who has strayed from the path of truth is called a wanderer. Their wandering was that they would spend forty years every day walking a distance of six farsakhs to get out of it, and they would end up in the place from which they had begun their journey.

c: Al-Muthanna told me that.
m: He said, Ishaq told us. He said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The Children of Israel wandered for forty years, going to bed where they had gone to bed in their wanderings.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Do not despair
, do not be sad.

So-and-so is sad about such-and-such, he is sad and I am saddened by such-and-such, meaning I am sad. From this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: My companions stood there on their mounts and said: Do not perish in sorrow and be patient.
Meaning: Do not perish with grief. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So
h
do not despair
, he said: So do not be sad.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: So do not grieve over the wicked people, he said: When the wilderness struck them, Musa, peace be upon him, regretted it, and when he regretted it, God revealed to him: So do not grieve over the wicked people, do not grieve over the people whom you called wicked, so he did not grieve.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And recite to these Jews who intended to stretch out their hands against you, and to your companions with them, and make them aware of the evil consequences of injustice and deceit, and the evil consequences of treachery and breaking a covenant, and the reward of the treacherous and the faithful, the story of the two sons of Adam, Abel and Cain, and what happened to the one of them who obeyed his Lord and fulfilled his covenant, and what happened to the one of them who disobeyed his Lord and broke his covenant. So let the Jews know by this the terrible consequences of their treachery and their breaking of their covenant between you and them, and their intentions of what they intended to do of stretching out their hands against you and your companions, for you and them, in the goodness of My reward and the greatness of My recompense for fulfilling the covenant with which I rewarded the murdered one of the sons of Adam who fulfilled his covenant, and punished the murderer who broke his covenant, a beautiful consolation.
Scholars differed about the reason for the two sons of Adam offering sacrifices, the reason for God Almighty accepting what He accepted from them, and who were the two who offered sacrifices.

Some of them said: It was by the command of God Almighty to them to bring it near, and the reason for acceptance was that the one who was accepted brought near the best of his wealth, and the other brought near the worst of his wealth. And the two who were brought near were the two sons of Adam, one of them: Abel, and the other: Cain.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Saad, on the authority of Ismail bin Rafi’, he said:
m: It has reached me that when the two sons of Adam were commanded to offer sacrifices, one of them was a shepherd, and a lamb had been born to him among his sheep, and he loved it so much that he would give it precedence at night, and he would carry it on his back out of love for it, until he had no wealth more beloved to him than it. So when he was commanded to offer sacrifices, he offered them to God, and God accepted them from him, and they continued to graze in Paradise until the son of Abraham, may God bless them both, was ransomed by it. Ibn Bashar narrated, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, Awf narrated, on the authority of Abu al-Mughira, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The two sons of Adam who offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them and not from the other, one of them was a farmer and the other was a sheep owner. They were both commanded to offer a sacrifice, and the sheep owner offered the most noble, fattest and best of his sheep, pleased with them, while the farmer offered the worst of his crops, the darnel and the tares, but he was not pleased with them. And God accepted the sheep owner’s sacrifice, but He did not accept the sacrifice of the farmer. And of their story is what God has related in His Book. And he said: By God, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but he was prevented from extending his hand to his brother by his shame.

x: Others said: This was not their command, as God commanded them to do.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It was their custom that no poor person would be given charity, but rather the offering would be offered by a man. While the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said: If we offer an offering, and if a man offered an offering and God was pleased with him, He would send fire to him and consume him. And if God was not pleased with him, the fire would go out. So they offered an offering, and one of them was a shepherd and the other was a farmer. The owner of the sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crops. Then the fire came and descended between them, and it consumed the sheep and left the crops. And the son of Adam said to his brother: Do you walk among the people and they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you and rejected me? By God, people will not look at me and you, although you are better than me!! He said: I will kill you! His brother said to him: What is my sin? God only accepts from the righteous.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: When they offered a sacrifice, he said: The two sons of Adam, Abel and Cain, from the loins of Adam. So one of them offered a sheep, and the other offered a vegetable, and it was accepted by the owner of the sheep, so its owner killed it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth

, when they offered a sacrifice, he said: Abel and Cain. Abel offered a young goat from the best of his sheep, and Cain offered a crop from his crop. He said: The fire consumed the young goats but did not consume the crops, so he said: I will kill you! He said: God only accepts from the righteous.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said,
m: a man heard Mujahid tell us about his statement:
h
And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth

, when they offered a sacrifice, he said: It is Abel and Cain from the loins of Adam. They offered a sacrifice. One of them offered a sheep from his flock, and the other offered green vegetables, and it was accepted from the owner of the sheep. He said to his companion, I will kill you! So he killed him. So God tied one of his legs with its shin to its thigh until the Day of Resurrection, and he made his face to the sun wherever it turned. He had a fence of snow over him in the winter, and a fence of fire over him in the summer. He had seven angels with him, and whenever one of them went away another would come.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: H, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth

, when they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. He said: This one offered a ram, and this one offered a heap of food, and it was accepted from one of them. He said: It was accepted from the owner of the sheep, but it was not accepted from the other.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth
, when they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. There were two men from the sons of Adam, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Atiyyah:
m: h
And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth

. He said: One of them was called Qabil, and the other Abel. One of them was a shepherd, and the other a farmer. So this one brought a lamb from the best of his sheep, and this one brought a lamb from the worst of his crops. He said: Then the fire came down and consumed the lamb, and he said to his brother: I will kill you! Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the scholars of the first book: That Adam ordered his son Cain to marry his twin sister, Abel, and ordered Abel to marry his twin sister, Cain, so he submitted to that. Abel was pleased, but Cain refused and disliked that, out of respect for Abel’s sister, and he preferred his sister over Abel, and said: We are the offspring of Paradise, and they are the offspring of Earth, and I have more right to my sister!

x: Some of the scholars of the first book say: Cain’s sister was one of the best people, but he was stingy with her for his brother and wanted her for himself. And God knows best which of them it was. His father said to him: O my son, she is not lawful for you! But Cain refused to accept that from his father, so his father said to him: O my son, offer a sacrifice, and let your brother Abel offer a sacrifice, so whichever of you God accepts his sacrifice is more entitled to her. Cain was in charge of sowing the land, and Abel was in charge of tending the livestock. Cain offered wheat, and Abel offered the firstborn of his sheep - and some say: he offered a cow - so God Almighty sent a white fire that consumed Abel’s offering, and left Cain’s offering, and thus the offering was accepted if he accepted it.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: as mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: No child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him, so he would marry the boy of this womb to the girl of this other womb, and he would marry the girl of this womb to the boy of this other womb. Until two sons were born to him, they were called: Qabil and Abel. Qabil was a farmer, and Abel was a milker. Qabil was the older of them, and he had a sister who was more beautiful than Abel’s sister. Abel asked to marry Qabil’s sister, but he refused and said: She is my sister, she was born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I have more right to marry her! So his father ordered him to marry her to Abel, but he refused. They both offered a sacrifice to God, which of them had more right to the girl? Adam had gone away from them to Mecca to look at her. God, the Almighty, said to Adam: O Adam, do you know that I have a house on earth? He said: O God, no! He said: I have a house in Mecca, so go to it. Adam said to the sky: Keep my son in trust, but it refused. He said to the earth, but it refused. He said to the mountains, but it refused. He said to Cain, but it said: Yes, you can go and come back and find your family as you please. When Adam set out, they offered a sacrifice, and Cain was proud of him and said: I have more right to her than you, she is my sister, and I am older than you, and I am my father’s successor! When they offered it, Abel offered a fat young tree, and Cain Surat al-Ma’idah 5:27 And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "God only accepts from the righteous." offered a bundle of ears of corn. He found a large ear of corn in it, so he rubbed it and ate it. Then the fire came down and consumed Abel’s sacrifice, and left Cain’s sacrifice. He became angry and said: I will kill you so that you will not marry my sister! Abel said: God only accepts from the righteous.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the two sons of Adam in truth

, he mentioned to us that they were Abel and Cain. As for Abel, he was a herder, so he took the best of his herd and offered it as an offering, but a fire descended upon it and consumed it - and if an offering was accepted from them, a fire descended upon it and consumed it. And if it was returned to them, the birds and wild beasts would eat it - as for Cain, he was a farmer, so he took the worst of his crops and offered it as an offering, but the fire did not descend upon him. So he became envious of his brother and said: I will kill you! He said: God only accepts from the righteous.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the two sons of Adam in truth

, he said: They are Abel and Cain. He said: One of them was a farmer and the other a livestock owner. So one of them came with the best of his wealth and the other came with the worst of his wealth. Then the fire came and consumed the sacrifice of one of them, which was Abel, and left the sacrifice of the other. So he envied him and said: I will kill you!

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: When they offered a sacrifice, he said: This one offered crops, and that one offered a young goat, and the fire left the crops and consumed the young goats.

x: Others said: The two who offered a sacrifice, and God Almighty narrated their stories in this verse: two men from the Children of Israel, not from the descendants of Adam through his loins.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: The two men mentioned in the Qur’an, about whom God said:
h
And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth
, were from the Children of Israel, and they were not the sons of Adam by his loins, but rather the sacrifice was among the Children of Israel, and Adam was the first to die.

x: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is that the two who offered the sacrifice were Adam’s two sons from his loins, not from his descendants from the Children of Israel. This is because God Almighty is too exalted to address His servants with what does not benefit them, and those addressed by this verse knew that offering the sacrifice to God was only for the children of Adam, not the angels, devils, and all other creation. So since this was known to them, it is reasonable that if what was meant by the two sons of Adam whom God mentioned in His Book were not his two sons from his loins, He would not have benefited them by mentioning them with a benefit that they did not have. Since it was not permissible for him to address them in a way that did not give them any meaning, it is known that he meant by the sons of Adam the sons of Adam by his loins, not the sons of his sons who were descended from him, despite the consensus of the people of report, biographies, and knowledge of interpretation that they were the sons of Adam by his loins, and in the time and era of Adam, and that is sufficient as evidence.
We have mentioned many of those who have stated this, and we will mention many of those who have not, God willing.

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hussam bin Al-Mask told us, on the authority of Ammar Al-Dahni, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, who said:
m: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam remained sad for a hundred years, not laughing. Then he came and it was said to him: May God give you life and happiness! He said: May God make you laugh.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ghiyath bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, he said,
m: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam cried and said: The country and its people have changed, the color of the earth is dusty and ugly Everything changed in color and taste, and the pretty face became less cheerful. So Adam, peace be upon him, was answered: Abel's father and father were all killed, and the living became like the dead slaughtered. And Bashara came, whom he had been afraid of, so he brought her, shouting: Abu Jaʿfar said: As for the statement about their bringing them near as they brought them near, the correct statement is to say that God, the Mighty and Sublime, informed His servants about them that they had brought them near, and He did not inform them that bringing them near as they brought them near was by God’s command to them, nor by other than His command. It is possible that it was by God’s command to them to do that, and it is possible that it was by other than His command. However, whichever of the two it was, they did not bring that near except to seek nearness to God, God willing. As for the interpretation of his statement: He said, ‘I will kill you,’ its meaning is: The one whose offering was not accepted said to the one whose offering was accepted: I will kill you. So he omitted mentioning the one whose offering was accepted and the one whose offering was rejected, because what had already been mentioned of them sufficed without repeating it. Likewise, he omitted mentioning the one whose offering was accepted with his statement, He said, ‘God only accepts from the righteous.’ In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He said, ‘I will kill you.’ His brother said to him: What is my sin? God only accepts from the righteous.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
God only accepts from those who fear Him

, he said, he says: If you feared God in your offering, it would be accepted from you. You came with an offering adulterated with the worst of what you have, and I came with a pure offering with the best of what I have. He said: And he said: God accepts from you but does not accept from me! What he means by his saying: of the righteous is those who fear God and are in awe of Him, by performing the duties He has charged them with, and avoiding the acts of disobedience He has forbidden them.

x: A group of interpreters said: The pious in this context are those who avoid polytheism.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God only accepts from those who fear Him

, those who fear polytheism. We have previously explained the meaning of Qurban, and that it is the two verbs from the saying of the speaker: Quran as the two verbs from faraq and adwan from ‘ada. The offerings of the nations before our nation were like the alms and zakat among us. However, their offerings were known to be accepted and not accepted - as mentioned - by eating the fire of what was accepted from it, and leaving the fire of what was not accepted from it. The offerings in our nation are righteous deeds, such as prayer, fasting, charity to the poor, and paying the obligatory zakat. There is no way for them to know in the immediate future what was accepted from it and what was rejected. It was mentioned about Amer bin Abdullah Al-Anbari: When death approached him, he cried. It was said to him: What makes you cry? I was and was! He said: What makes me cry is that I hear God say:
h
God only accepts from those who fear Him

c: Muhammad bin Omar Al-Muqaddami told me that.
m: He said: Saeed bin Amer told me, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of someone who mentioned him, on the authority of Amer.

x: Some of them said: The sacrifice of the pious is prayer.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Imran bin Sulayman, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, who said:
m: The sacrifice of the pious was prayer.

x: This is report from God Almighty, mentioned about the one who was killed from the sons of Adam, that he said to his brother - when his brother the killer said to him: I will kill you -: By God, if you stretch out your hand against me, meaning: you stretch out your hand against me, to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you, meaning: I will not stretch out my hand against you, to kill you. There is a difference of opinion as to why the murdered man said that to his brother, and why he did not object to what was done to him.
Some of them said: He said that to inform his murderous brother that he did not consider it permissible to kill him or to extend his hand to him in a way that God Almighty did not permit him to do.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that he said:
m: By God, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but he was prevented from extending his hand to his brother due to his embarrassment.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me
, I will not stretch out my hand against you, I will not be victorious, and I will withhold my hand from you.

x: Others said: He did not prevent him from what he wanted to kill, and he said what he said to him from what God narrated in His Book: except that God Almighty imposed on them that whoever wanted to kill him should not prevent whoever wanted to kill him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, a man told us that
m: he heard Mujahid say about His statement:
h
If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me
, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Mujahid said: It was written for them, if a man wanted to kill a man, you would see him and not resist him.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is that it is said that God, the Mighty and Sublime, had forbidden them to kill a soul for another soul unjustly, and that the one killed said to his brother: I will not extend my hand to you if you extend your hand to me. Rather, it was forbidden for him to kill his brother just as it was forbidden for his brother, the killer, to kill him. As for refraining from killing him when he wanted to kill him, there is no evidence that when the killer wanted to kill him and resolved to do so, the one killed was aware of what he was determined to do and was trying to kill him, so he left it to himself. Rather, a group of scholars have stated that he killed him by treachery, he assassinated him while he was sleeping, and smashed his head with a rock. So since that is possible, and there is no evidence in the verse that he was commanded not to prevent his brother from killing him, it is permissible to claim what is not in the verse, except with proof that must be accepted.

As for the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the Worlds, it is: I fear God in extending my hand to you if I extend it to kill you, Lord of the Worlds, meaning: Owner of all creation, lest He punish me for extending my hand to you.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is:
h
I want you to bear my sin
of killing me, your sin of disobeying God, and other sins of yours.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi
m: in his hadith, on the authority of Abu Malik and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, he said: the sin of killing me, in addition to your sin that is around your neck, and you will be among the companions of the Fire.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, he said: by killing me, and your sin before that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, he said: the sin of killing me and your sin.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed,
h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, he said: I want your sin and my blood to be upon you, so that you bear both of them.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, he said:
h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, he said: for what happened from you before that.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
