. He said: As for your sin, it is the sin that he committed before killing the soul - meaning his brother - and as for his sin, it is killing his brother. The authors of this article interpreted his statement:
h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, as: I want you to bear the sin of killing me. So he omitted killing and was satisfied with mentioning the sin, since its meaning was understood by those addressed by it.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
I want you to bear my sin

, so you bear its burden and your sin in killing me. This is a statement I found on the authority of Mujahid, and I fear that it may be a mistake, because the correct narration on his authority is what we mentioned before.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin
, he said: I want my sin and my blood to be upon you, so you bear both of them.

x: The correct statement about this is to say that its interpretation is: I want you to turn away from your sin in killing me, and that is the meaning of his saying:
h
I want you to bear my sin

. As for the meaning of and your sin, it is his sin other than killing him, and that is his disobedience to God, may He be glorified, in the actions of others. We said that this is correct, because the people of interpretation have agreed upon it.

c: Because God Almighty has informed us that
m: every worker will be rewarded for his work or against it. If this is His ruling regarding His creation, then it is not permissible for the sins of the one killed to be taken from the killer. Rather, the killer will be taken for his sin of the forbidden killing and all the sins of his transgressions that he committed himself, not for what his victim committed.

x: Is not killing the murdered person from among the sons of Adam a protection for God from the murderer?
Yes, and it is a greater sin!
If there is a sin against God, the Almighty and Majestic, how is it permissible for the murdered person to want that from him, and say:
h
I want you to bear my sin
, and you have mentioned that the interpretation of that is: I want you to bear the sin of killing me?

Its meaning is: I want you to bear the sin of killing me if you kill me, because I will not kill you. If you kill me, then I want you to bear the sin of disobeying God in killing me. And if he kills him, then he will inevitably bear it in God’s judgment, so his desire for that does not require him to enter into error. He means by his saying:
h
Then you will be among the people of the Fire
, and that is the reward of the wrongdoers.

He says: Then by killing me you will be among the inhabitants of Hell, and the fuel of the Fire, abiding therein eternally. “And that is the reward of the wrongdoers.” He says: And the Fire is the reward of those who abandon the path of truth, who deviate from the straight path, who transgress what was made for them to what was not made for them. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:29 Indeed,
h
I want you to bear my sin and your sin

and be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers. This indicates that God Almighty had commanded and forbidden Adam after He sent him down to Earth, and had promised and warned. And were it not for that, the murdered man would not have said to the murderer:
h
Then you will be among the people of the Fire

, for killing me, nor would he have told him that this is the reward of the wrongdoers. So Mujahid used to say: One of the murderer’s legs will be suspended by its shin to its thigh from that day until the Day of Resurrection, and his face will be in the sun wherever it turns, with a fence of fire over him in the summer and a fence of snow over him in the winter.

c: Al-Qasim told us that, he said, Al-Hussein told us that, Hajjaj told me that,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said that - he said: And Abdullah bin Amr said: And we find the son of Adam, the murderer, dividing the people of Hell in a correct division of punishment, with half of their punishment upon him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, a story.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, and Sufyan told us, he said, Jarir and Abu Muawiyah told us,
m: H, and Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah and Waki’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no soul that is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear some responsibility for it, because he was the first to institute killing.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us,
m: H, and Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hasan ibn Salih, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, who said:
m: There is no one who is killed unjustly, except that the first son of Adam and the devil have a share of it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hakim:
m: that he told on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr: that he used to say: The most wretched of people is a man, the son of Adam who killed his brother. No blood has been shed on earth since he killed his brother until the Day of Resurrection, except that some of it has been inflicted on him, and that is because he was the first to institute killing.

x: This report that we have mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shows that the statement that Al-Hasan made about the two sons of Adam whom God mentioned in this place, that they are not the sons of Adam by his loins, but rather they are two men from the Children of Israel, and that the statement that was reported from him, that the first to die was Adam, and that the sacrifice that the fire consumed was only from the Children of Israel, is a mistake, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed about this murderer who killed his brother: that he was the first to establish killing. And, without a doubt, killing occurred before Israel, so how about before his descendants! So it is a mistake to say: The first to establish killing was a man from the Children of Israel. Since this is the case, it is known that the correct statement is the statement of the one who said: He is the son of Adam through his loins, because he was the first to establish killing, so God made obligatory for him the punishment that we narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

What He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: So I obeyed, was that I came to him and helped him with it. It is an action of obedience, from the saying of the one who says: This matter obeyed me, if he submitted to it.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of it.
Some of them said, meaning: So his soul encouraged him to kill his brother.
Who said that?

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi and Muhammad bin Hamid told me, they said, Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: His soul was willing to do it, he said: I was encouraged.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So his soul was willing to do it, he said: So I encouraged him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, he said: It encouraged him to kill his brother.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: It was decorated for him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: His soul made it easy for him, he said: His soul made the killing of his brother seem attractive to him, so he killed him. Then they differed about the manner in which he killed him, how it was, and the reason for which he killed him.

x: Some of them said: He found him sleeping and smashed his head with a rock.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: as mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then his soul prompted him to kill his brother. So he sought him out to kill him, and the young man finished him off on the mountaintops. One day he came to him while he was tending his sheep on a mountain, and he was asleep, so he lifted a rock and smashed his head with it, and he died, and he was left in the open.

x: Some of them said: Muhammad bin Omar bin Ali told me, he said, I heard Ash’ath al-Sijistani say, I heard Ibn Jurayj say: The son of Adam who killed his companion did not know how to kill him, so Satan appeared to him in the form of a bird, so he took a bird and cut off its head, then put it between two stones and smashed its head, so he taught it how to kill.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: He killed him while he was tending the sheep. He came to him and did not know how to kill him, so he twisted his neck and took hold of his head. Then Satan came down and took an animal or a bird and placed his head on a rock. Then he took another rock and crushed his head with it, while the killer, the son of Adam, was watching. Then he took his brother and placed his head on a rock, and took another rock and crushed his head with it.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, a man told us
m: who heard Mujahid say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the fire consumed the sacrifice of the son of Adam whom you killed! His sacrifice, the other said to his brother: Do you walk among the people and they know that you offered a sacrifice and it was accepted from you and returned to me? By God, people do not wait for me and you when you are better than me! He said: I will kill you. His brother said to him: What is my sin? God only accepts from those who fear Him. So he frightened him with the fire, but he did not stop or refrain, so his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers.

c: Al-Qasim told me, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim told me:
m: I came with Saeed bin Jubair to throw the pebbles at the Jamarat, and he was covering his face and leaning on my hand, until we reached the place of Samurah al-Sawwaf.

c: He stopped and told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: It was forbidden for a woman to marry her twin brother, and for another of her brothers to marry her. And in every pregnancy there was a man and a woman. So she gave birth to a beautiful woman, and she gave birth to an ugly, ugly woman. So the brother of the ugly woman said: Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister. He said: No, I have more right to my sister. So they made a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the owner of the ram, but it was not accepted from the owner of the crops, so he killed him. And that ram remained with God, the Almighty, until He brought it out in ransom for Isaac, and slaughtered it on this Safa in Thabir, at the place of Samurah al-Sawwaf, and it is on your right when you throw the pebbles. Ibn Jurayj said, and others said something similar to this story. He said: The children of Adam continued to do this until four fathers passed away, and he married his cousin, and the marriage of sisters was no longer permissible.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God, the Mighty and Sublime, has informed us that the killer killed his brother, and we do not have any information that would excuse him for the manner in which he killed him. It is possible that it was as al-Suddi mentioned in his report, and it is possible that it was as Mujahid mentioned, and God knows best which of them it was. However, the killing undoubtedly took place. As for His statement:
h
So he became one of the losers

, its interpretation is: So the killer became his brother from the sons of Adam, from the party of the losers, and they are those who sold their afterlife for their worldly life, by preferring it over it - so they were deceived in their sale, were cheated in it, and were disappointed in their deal.

This is also one of the proofs that the statement regarding the two sons of Adam is contrary to what Amr narrated from Al-Hasan, because if the two men whose description God described in this verse had been from the Children of Israel, the killer would not have been ignorant of burying his brother and covering his brother's body, but they were from the descendants of Adam through his loins, and the killer of his brother was not one of them. He knew God's law regarding His dead servants, and he did not know what to do with his murdered brother. So he mentioned that he carried him on his shoulder for a while until his corpse was at rest, so God wanted to make him aware of the law regarding the dead of His creation, so He provided him with the two ravens whose description He described in His Book. Mentioning the report from the people of interpretation about what the killer of the two sons of Adam did to his murdered brother, after killing him.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahs bin Abi Rawq Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: He continued carrying his brother in a bag on his neck for a year, until God Almighty sent the two crows. He saw them searching, so he said: Am I unable to be like this crow? So he buried his brother.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Then God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to hide the shame of his brother, God Almighty sent a living raven to a dead raven, and the living raven began to hide the shame of the dead raven, so the son of Adam who killed his brother said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven? The verse.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: as mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the boy died, he left him in the open, and he did not know how to bury him. Then God Almighty sent two ravens, brothers, and they fought, and one of them killed the other, so he dug a grave for him and threw it over him. When he saw it, he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover my brother’s private parts? This is what God says: Then God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to cover his brother’s private parts.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Searching, he said, God sent a raven until it dug a hole for another dead person next to it - and the son of Adam, the killer, was looking at him - then it searched for him until it hid him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: A crow digging in the ground, until it dug for another dead person next to it, and hid him, and the son of Adam, the killer, was looking at him, searching for him until he hid him, and he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow, the verse.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then God sent a crow scratching the ground

, he said: God sent a crow to a crow, and they fought, and one of them killed the other, and he began to throw dirt on him, and he said: Woe to me, am I unable to be like this crow and cover the shame of my brother, so that I may become one of the regretful ones?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told me, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Then God sent a crow scratching the ground
, he said: A crow came to a dead crow and threw dirt on it until it covered it, so the one who killed his brother said: Woe to me! I am unable to be like this crow, the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah, who said:
m: When he killed him, he regretted it, so he hugged him until he died, and the birds and beasts of prey swarmed around him, waiting for him to throw him away so they could eat him.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then God sent a crow scratching the ground to show him

, that God Almighty sent him scratching the ground. He told us that they were two crows who fought, and one of them killed the other, and that - meaning the son of Adam was looking - and the living one began to throw dirt on the dead one, and then he said what he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow? The verse, until His saying: among the regretful ones.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Surat al-Ma’idah 5:
m: 31 Then God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to hide his brother's shame. He said, "Woe to me! I could not be like this raven and hide my brother's shame!" So he became one of the regretful. Qatada, he said: As for his statement:
h
Then God sent a crow

, he said: A crow killed another crow, and it began to throw dirt at it. So the son of Adam who killed his brother said when he saw it: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and cover my brother’s shame? Then I became one of the regretful ones.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to hide his brother’s private parts

, he said: The raven hid the raven. He said: He carried it on his shoulder for a hundred years, not knowing what to do with it, carrying it and putting it on the ground, until he saw the raven burying the raven, so he said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and hide my brother’s private parts? I have become one of those who regret it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding the statement of God: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow? He said: God Almighty sent a crow, and it began searching for a dead crow in the dirt. He said: Then it said: Am I unable to be like this crow and cover the shame of my brother? So I became one of the regretful ones.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Then God sent a crow

, scratching the ground, God sent a living crow to a dead crow, and the living crow began to cover the dead crow’s private parts. Then the son of Adam who had killed his brother said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow? The verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, according to what is mentioned by some of the people of knowledge of the first book, he said:
m: When he killed him, he was dismayed and did not know how to bury him. That is because he was, as they claim, the first of the sons of Adam to be killed and the first to die. He said: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and cover the shame of my brother? The verse, until His saying:
h
Then indeed many of them after that are transgressors upon the earth

. He said: The people of the Torah claim that when Cain killed his brother Abel, God Almighty said to him: O Cain, where is your brother Abel? He said: I do not know, I was not a watcher over him! Then God Almighty said to him: The sound of your brother’s blood calls to me from the earth. Now you are cursed from the earth that opened its mouth and swallowed your brother’s blood from your hand. So when you work the earth, it will no longer yield its crops to you until you are a wandering, terrified person on the earth. Cain said: My sin is too great for you to forgive it! Today you have brought me out from the face of the earth, and I will hide myself from your presence, and I will be a wanderer in fear on the earth, and everyone who meets me will kill me! God Almighty said: It is not so, and whoever kills a person will not be rewarded with seven for one, but whoever kills Cain will be rewarded with seven. And God made a sign in Cain so that everyone who finds him will not kill him, and Cain went out from before God Almighty from the east of Eden, Paradise.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Khathima, he said:
m: When the son of Adam killed his brother, the earth dried up his blood, so it was cursed and the earth did not dry up any blood after that.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: So God raised up for the killer, since he did not know what to do with his murdered brother, a crow digging in the ground, meaning: digging in the ground and stirring up its soil, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother, meaning: to show him how to hide the corpse of his brother. It may be possible that what he meant by the private parts is the vagina, but the most likely meaning is what I mentioned about the corpse, and that is how the people of interpretation interpreted it.

There is something omitted in that which was not mentioned, as the indication of what was mentioned was sufficient, which is: “So he showed it to him by searching in the ground for another dead crow and hid it in it. Then the one who killed his brother said at that time: Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow, who hid the other dead crow, “and hid the shame of my brother,” so he hid it at that time, and he became among the regretful, for what he had neglected, of disobeying God Almighty in killing his brother. And everything that God the Almighty mentioned in these verses, is an example that God the Almighty gave to the children of Adam, and with it He urged the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to use forgiveness and pardon for the Jews - who intended to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and kill them - from Banu Nadir, when they came to them seeking their help in the blood money for the two dead of Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri, and God the Almighty knew the bad nature of their forefathers, and their poor adherence to the path of truth, despite the many favors and blessings He bestowed upon them.

And He gave an example of their treachery, and an example of the believers in their loyalty to them and their pardon for them, with the two sons of Adam, who were close relatives to them, whom God mentioned in these verses. Then that is an example for them to follow the example of the virtuous among them rather than the wicked.
And with that came the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said,
m: I said to Bakr bin Abdullah, Have you not heard that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty has given you an example of the two sons of Adam, so take the better of them and leave the worse of them? He said: Yes.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two sons of Adam are an example for this nation, so take the best of them.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said,
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has given you an example of the two sons of Adam, so take from the good among them and leave the evil.

x: God Almighty means by His statement, Because of that, from the crime and offense he committed.

Whoever caused the murderer of his brother from the two sons of Adam - whose story we have related - the crime he committed and the offense he committed, We prescribed for the Children of Israel. It is said: I postponed this matter, meaning: I dragged him towards it and earned it, I postponed it for him for a period, like you say: I took it, and from that is the saying of that poet: The people of Salih’s tent fought among themselves over an urgent matter that I will postpone.

By his saying: I will postpone it, he meant that I will punish them and the aggressor. The meaning of the statement: From the crime of the son of Adam who killed his brother unjustly, We ruled upon the Children of Israel that whoever among them killed a soul unjustly, unless it was a soul that was killed, then he was killed in retaliation, or corruption in the land, meaning: or he killed a soul among them without corruption that was on its part on the land, so it deserved to be killed. And its corruption in the land is only by war against God and His Messenger, and frightening the wayfarer.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Those who said that mentioned:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
For that reason We decreed upon the Children of Israel
, he said: For the sake of the son of Adam who killed his brother unjustly. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: “
h
Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land
- it is as if he had killed mankind entirely.
h
And whoever saves a life
- it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.”

x: Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he killed all of humanity, and whoever supports a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he saved all of humanity.
Who said that?

c: Abu Ammar Al-Hussein bin Harith Al-Marwazi told us, he said, Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Waqid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land
h
it is as if he had slain mankind entirely
h
And whoever saves a life

, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely,” he said: Whoever strengthens the arm of a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land -
h
it is as if he had slain mankind entirely
, meaning: Whoever kills a single soul that I have made sacred, is like someone who has killed all of mankind.
h
And whoever saves a life
, he said: Whoever refrains from killing a single soul that I have made sacred out of fear of Me, and spares it from killing it, it is like sparing all of mankind, meaning by that the prophets.

x: Others said:
h
Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land
, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, when the one killed is guilty of sin,
h
and whoever saves a life
, when rescuing it from destruction, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, when rescuing it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: in what was mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his saying:
h
Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land

, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, in reference to the one killed, he says: in sin, and whoever saves it, so he rescues it from destruction, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, in reference to the rescuer.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: The one who kills a soul in a state of forbidden killing will burn in Hell just as he would burn in it if he killed all people.
h
And whoever saves a life
, whoever is saved from killing it, is saved from killing all people.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
Whoever saves a life

, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said: Whoever refrains from killing it has saved it, Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, he said: And whoever destroys it.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Whoever kills a soul, it is as if he had killed all of humanity.
h
And whoever saves a life
and is saved from its oppression and does not kill it, then he has been saved from killing all of humanity.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: It is as if he had killed all of humanity,
h
and whoever saves a life
, it is as if he had saved all of humanity. He did not kill her, and all of the people were saved from him. He did not kill anyone.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, who said, Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah told us:
m: I asked Mujahid - or I heard him ask - about his statement: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land -
h
it is as if he had killed all of mankind
. He said: If he had killed all of mankind, his recompense would be Hell, wherein he would abide eternally, and God would be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: reading it on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
It is as if he had slain mankind entirely

, he said: Whoever kills a believing soul intentionally, God will make his recompense Hell, and God will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment. He says: If he had killed all of mankind, it would not have increased the punishment like that. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: And whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said: Whoever does not kill anyone, then the people are relieved of him.

c: Sufyan told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: He destroyed himself.

c: Sufyan told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: In sin.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land
, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely. And His statement:
h
And whoever kills a believer intentionally
, his recompense is Hell
r
(An-Nisa’: 93)
, he said: He will go to Hell by killing a believer, just as if he had killed all of mankind, he would have gone to Hell.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that
h
whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land
, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely. He said: It is as he said. And he said:
h
And whoever saves a life

, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. So saving it means not killing a soul that God has forbidden, so that is what saves mankind entirely, meaning: whoever has forbidden killing it except for a right, saves mankind entirely from it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And whoever revives it, he said: And whoever forbids it and does not kill it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say:
h
Whoever saves a life
, it is as if he saved all of humanity. He said: Whoever refrains from killing it has saved a life.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
It is as if he had killed all of mankind
, he said: It is like what is in An-Nisa’:
h
And whoever kills a believer intentionally
, his recompense is Hell
r
(An-Nisa’: 93)
, regarding his recompense.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
It is as if he had killed all of mankind
, like what is in Surat An-Nisa,
h
And whoever kills a believer intentionally
in his punishment,
h
And whoever saves a life
, and did not kill anyone, then the people have been saved by him.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whoever saves a life
h
it is as if he had saved all of mankind
, he said: He turned to his companions and said: It is this and this.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption on earth,
h
it is as if he had killed all of mankind
, because he must be subject to retaliation and retribution for his killing, just as he must be subject to retaliation and retribution if he had killed all of mankind. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:32
h
For that reason We decreed upon the Children of Israel
that
h
whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land
- it is as if he had killed mankind entirely.
h
And whoever saves a life
- it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And indeed Our messengers came to them with clear proofs; then indeed many of them, after that, are transgressors upon the earth.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land - it is as if he had killed mankind entirely, he said: He must be killed as if he had killed all of mankind. He said: My father used to say that.

x: Others said that the meaning of his saying: And whoever saves it is whoever pardons someone from whom retaliation is due and does not kill him.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And whoever saves a life
, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said:
h
Whoever saves a life

, God, the Almighty, the Majestic, will give him a reward equal to that if he had saved mankind entirely. He saved a life, he did not kill it and pardoned it. He said: And that is because the one who was killed, and the one who was killed himself is pardoned before he dies. He said: My father used to say that.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever saves a life
, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, he said: Whoever pardons.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
And whoever saves a life
h
it is as if he had saved all of mankind
, he said: Whoever kills a close relative of his and pardons his blood.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And whoever saves a life
h
it is as if he had saved all of mankind
. He said: Forgiveness comes after power.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying:
h
And whoever saves one life
h
it is as if he had saved all of mankind
, is whoever saves one life from drowning or burning.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And whoever saves a life
, it is as if he saved all of mankind. He said:
h
Whoever saves a life
from drowning, burning, or destruction.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And whoever saves a life
, it is as if he saved all of mankind, he said: whoever drowned, burned, or demolished.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And whoever saves it, he said: He saved it. Al-Dahhak said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Aamer, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: Whoever kills a soul without a soul, he said: Whoever is pious or does not have any piousness.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
It is as if he had saved all of mankind
, that he said: If he had not killed him, he would have saved all of mankind, and he would not have made permissible what is forbidden. Qatada and Al-Hasan said about this:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption on earth, he said: That is a great sin!

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul the verse, whoever kills it unless for a soul or for corruption it has caused, “
h
it is as if he had slain mankind entirely
h
And whoever saves a life

it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.” Great is its reward, and great is its sin! So save it, O son of Adam, with what you have, and save it with your forgiveness if you are able, and there is no power except with God. We do not know of anyone who makes the blood of a Muslim man from the people of this Qiblah permissible except in one of three cases: a man who disbelieves after his conversion to Islam, in which case he must be killed; or he who commits adultery after being married, in which case he must be stoned; or he who kills intentionally, in which case he must be subject to retaliation.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said:
m: Qatada recited: “Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption done in the land - it is as if he had killed mankind entirely.
h
And whoever saves a life
- it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.” He said: By God, her reward is great, and by God, her sin is great!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Salam bin Maskeen, he said, Sulayman bin Ali Al-Rab’i told me, he said:
m: I said to Al-Hasan: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul the verse, is it for us, O Abu Saeed, as it was for the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, by the One besides Whom there is no god, as it was for the Children of Israel! And what made the blood of the Children of Israel more precious to God than our blood?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Zaid, who said:
m: I heard Khalid Abu Al-Fadl say: I heard Al-Hasan recite this verse: And his soul prompted him to kill his brother until His saying:
h
And whoever saves a life

, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. Then he said: By God, the sin is great as you hear, and by God, the reward is desired as you hear! If you think, O son of Adam, that if you killed all of humanity, you would have from your deeds what would win you from the Fire!! By God, your soul has lied to you, and Satan has lied to you.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is as if he had killed all of mankind
, he said: A sin,
h
And whoever saves a life
h
it is as if he had saved all of mankind
, he said: A reward.

x: The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The interpretation of that is that whoever kills a believing soul for a reason other than a soul that he killed, and did not deserve retaliation or killing in retaliation, or for corruption on earth, by war against God and His Messenger and the war of the believers in it, then it is as if he killed all of mankind in what he deserves of great punishment from God, the Most High, as his Lord has promised him for his action in His saying:
h
And whoever kills a believer intentionally
- his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and God has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment
As for his statement:
h
And whoever saves a life

, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, the most appropriate interpretation of it is the statement of the one who said: Whoever forbade killing someone whom God the Almighty has forbidden to kill for himself, and did not precede killing him, then he has saved mankind from him by their being safe from him, and that is his saving it.
This is similar to the report of God the Almighty about the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord when Abraham said to him: “My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. He said:
h
I give life
and cause death” (al-Baqarah 2:258). So the meaning of the disbeliever in his saying:
h
I give life
, is that I leave whoever I am able to kill - and in his statement: and cause death, he killed whoever killed him. Likewise the meaning of revival in his statement:
h
And whoever saves a life

, is that people are safe from his killing them, except for those whom God has permitted to be killed from them, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. We said that this is the most appropriate interpretation of the verse, because no soul whose killing in the immediate harm is equivalent to killing all souls, nor its revival is equivalent to reviving all souls in the immediate benefit. Thus it was known that the meaning of revival is the safety of all souls from it, because whoever does not advance on a single soul, all souls are safe from it - and that the one of them whose killing is equivalent to all of them is only in sin, because there is no soul of the sons of Adam whose loss is equivalent to the loss of all of them, even if the loss of some is more harmful than the loss of some.

This is an oath from God, the Most High, by which He swore: that His messengers, may God’s prayers be upon them, came to the Children of Israel, whose stories God related and whose report He mentioned in the verses that preceded, from His saying: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people were about to stretch out their hands against you to this place, with clear proofs, meaning: with clear signs and evident arguments on the truth of what they were sent with to them, and the correctness of what they called them to of belief in them, and performing God’s obligations upon them. God Almighty says: Then many of them, after that, were transgressors upon the earth, meaning: many of the Children of Israel. The ha and the mim in his saying:
h
Then many of them are from the mention of the Children of Israel
, and likewise in his saying: And there came to them.

“After that,” meaning: after the coming of God’s messengers with clear proofs. On the earth are transgressors, meaning: they are on earth committing sins against God, disobeying God’s commands and prohibitions, and defying God and His messengers, following their whims and disobeying their prophets. That was their transgression on the earth.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Zaid, who said: I heard Khalid Abu Al-Fadl say: I heard Al-Hasan recite this verse: And his soul prompted him to kill his brother until His saying: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.

x: This is a statement from God, the Exalted, about the ruling on corruption on earth, which He mentioned in His statement: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption on the earth, He informed His servants: What punishment and humiliation the corrupter on earth deserves, so He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: There is no recompense for him in this world except killing, crucifixion, cutting off a hand and a foot from opposite sides, or exile from the land, as a disgrace for them. As for in the Hereafter, if he does not repent in this world, then there is a great punishment. Then the people of interpretation differed about who this verse was revealed to.

Some of them said: It was revealed about a group of the People of the Book who had a truce with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they broke the covenant and spread corruption on earth, so God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the ruling regarding them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land

, he said: There were people from the People of the Book who had a covenant and a pact with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they broke the covenant and spread corruption in the land, so God gave His Messenger the choice: If He wished, he could kill them, or if He wished, he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: There were people between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a covenant, so they broke the covenant and cut off the way and spread corruption on the earth, so God Almighty gave His Prophet the choice regarding them, if He wished he could kill him, if He wished he could crucify him, and if He wished he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told me: I heard Al-Dahhak say: and he mentioned something similar.

x: Others said: It was revealed about a group of polytheists.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said:
m: h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

to Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. This verse was revealed regarding the polytheists. So whoever among them repents before you are able to overpower him, there will be no punishment against him. This verse does not protect a Muslim man from the prescribed punishment. If he kills or spreads corruption in the land or wages war against God and His Messenger, then joins the disbelievers before he is able to overpower him, that will not prevent him from having the prescribed punishment carried out against him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Surat al-Ma’idah 5:
m: 33 The only reward of those who make war upon God and His Messenger and strive after corruption upon earth is that they be killed or crucified or their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides or they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a great punishment. Al-Hasan:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
, he said: It was revealed about the polytheists.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about a people from Uraynah and Ukl, who apostatized from Islam and fought God and His Messenger.

Who said that? Ibn Bashar narrated, saying: Ruh ibn Ubadah narrated, saying: Saeed ibn Abi Arubah narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas: A group of people from Ukl and Uraynah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we are people of udder, and we were not people of the countryside, and we find Medina unpleasant. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered for them a flock of sheep and a shepherd, and ordered them to go out with them and drink from their milk and urine. So they killed the shepherd of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and drove away the flocks, and they disbelieved after their Islam. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought them, cut off their hands and feet, gouged out their eyes, and left them in the lava field until they died. He told us that this verse was revealed about them:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
is that they will be killed or be disgraced.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ruh told us, he said, Hisham bin Abi Abdullah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, with a story similar to this. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq narrated, he said, I heard my father say:

c: Abu Hamza narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Karim,
m: and he was asked about camel urine, so he said: Saeed bin Jubair narrated to me on the authority of the warriors, he said: There were people who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We pledge allegiance to you on Islam! So they pledged allegiance to him, and they were liars, and they did not want Islam. Then they said: We are going to Medina! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These camels come to you in the morning and in the evening, so drink from their urine and milk. He said: While they were like that, the cry came, and it was cried out to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: They killed the shepherd and drove the camels away! So the Prophet of God ordered that it be called out to the al-Nas 114:O horses of God, ride! He said: So they rode, and no horseman waited for another horseman. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode after them, and they kept pursuing them until they brought them to their place of safety. Then the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and had taken some of them as prisoners. They brought them to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

(al-Baqarah 2:17). He said: So their exile was that they were exiled until they brought them to their place of safety and their land, and they were exiled from the land of the Muslims. The Prophet of God killed some of them, crucified them, cut off their eyes, and gouged out their eyes. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had never mutilated anyone before or after. He said: He forbade mutilation, and said: Do not mutilate anything. He said: Anas bin Malik used to say the same, except that he said: He burned them with fire after he killed them. He said: Some of them say: They are people from Bani Salim, some from Uraynah, and some from Bajila.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said, Al-Hasan bin Hammad told us, on the authority of Amr bin Hashim, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Jarir, who said:
m: A group of people from Uraynah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, barefoot and injured, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave orders to them. When they recovered and became strong, they killed the shepherds of the camels, then they went out with the camels, intending to go to the land of their people. Jarir said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me with a group of Muslims until we caught up with them after they had reached the land of their people, so we brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he cut off their hands and feet from opposite sides, and gouged out their eyes, and they kept saying: Water! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fire! Until they perished. He said: God, the Almighty, disliked the gouging out of eyes, so He revealed this verse:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
to the end of the verse.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr,
m: H, and Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yahya ibn Abd God ibn Salim, Sa’id ibn Abd al-Rahman and Ibn Sam’an told me, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said: Some people from ‘Uraynah raided the camels of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they drove them away and killed one of his slaves in them, so he sent after them, and they were captured, so he cut off their hands and feet and gouged out their eyes.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar - or:
m: Amr, Yunus was uncertain - on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that, and the verse of fighting was revealed about them. Ali bin Sahl narrated, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated, Al-Awza’i narrated, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas, who said: Eight men from Ukl came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they converted to Islam. Then they settled in Madinah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go to the camels of charity and drink their urine and milk. So they did, and they killed their shepherds and drove away the camels. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a tracker after them, and they were brought to him. He cut off their hands and feet and left them without cauterizing them until they died.

c: Ali told us, Al-Walid told us, Saeed told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said:
m: There were four men from Uraynah and three from Ukl. When they were brought to him, he cut off their hands and feet, put out their eyes, did not cauterize them, and left them to throw stones at Al-Harrah. Then God Almighty revealed regarding that:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
Al-Madinah 1:17.

c: Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib:
m: That Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to Anas asking him about this verse, so Anas wrote to him informing him that this verse was revealed about those people from Arniyah, who were from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove away the camels, frightened the travelers, and committed unlawful sexual intercourse.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

and strive after corruption on earth He said: It was revealed about the blacks of Uraynah. He said: They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had yellow water, and they complained about that to him, so he ordered them to go out to the camels of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the charity, and he said: Drink from their milk and urine! So they drank from their milk and urine, until when they recovered and were well, they killed the shepherds and drove away the camels.

x: The most appropriate statement in this regard, in my opinion, is to say: God revealed this verse to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform him of His ruling on those who fight God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption on earth, after what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did to the two tribes of Arnayin. We said that this is the most correct of the sayings in this regard, because the stories that God Almighty told before and after this verse are stories of the Children of Israel and their report, so it is more appropriate and more appropriate for this to be in the middle, in defining the ruling on them and their peers. We said: This was revealed after what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did to the two Arnayin, because the reports from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are consistent with this.

And since that was more appropriate for the verse because of what we have described, then its interpretation is: For that reason We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul, or strives to cause corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs; then indeed many of them after that were transgressors upon the earth. He says: Striving to cause corruption upon the earth, and fighting souls unless for a soul, and not striving to cause corruption upon the earth, in war against God and His Messenger. So whoever among them does that, O Muhammad, his recompense is only that they be killed, or crucified, or their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides, or they be exiled from the land.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How is it possible that the verse was revealed in the situation you mentioned: the situation of a disbeliever from the Children of Israel breaking his covenant, and from your saying that the ruling of this verse is a ruling from God regarding the people of Islam, not the people of war from the polytheists?

It is permissible for that to be the case, because the ruling on those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption on earth are from among the people of our covenant and one religion. And those meant by the verse were people of a covenant and a protection, even though every dhimmi and religion is included in its ruling. And it is not invalidated by the inclusion of those who are included in the ruling of the verse from the people, that it was correct to reveal it regarding those about whom it was revealed. Scholars have differed about abrogating the Prophet’s ruling, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Arabs.
Some of them said: This is an abrogated ruling, abrogated by His prohibition of mutilation in this verse, I mean His statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption Al-Ma’idah 2
:17. They said: This verse was revealed as a rebuke to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he did to the two Arabs.

Some of them said: Rather, what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did with the Arniyyin is a ruling that is always valid for their peers, it has not been abrogated or changed. And His statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger 3

:17, is a ruling from Surat al-Ma’idah 5:33 The only reward of those who make war upon God and His Messenger and strive after corruption upon earth is that they be killed or crucified or their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides or they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a great punishment. God regarding those who wage war and strive to spread corruption in the land through banditry. They said: The Arniyyin apostatized, killed, stole, and waged war against God and His Messenger, so their ruling is different from the ruling of the one who wages war and strives to spread corruption in the land from among the people of Islam or the covenant.

Others said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not blind the eyes of the Arabs, but he wanted to blind them, so God Almighty revealed this verse to His Prophet, informing him of the ruling on them, and forbidding him from blinding their eyes.
Mention of those who said what we described:

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us:
m: I mentioned to Al-Layth bin Saad what happened when the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) blinded their eyes and left them cauterized until they died, so he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ajlan say: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) as a reprimand for that, and he taught him the punishment for those like them: cutting off, killing, and banishment, and no one else was blinded after them. He said: This statement was mentioned to Abu Amr, so he denied that it was revealed as a reprimand, and he said: Yes, the punishment for those people was in their persons, then this verse was revealed regarding the punishment for others who fought after them, so the blinding was lifted from them.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told me, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent, and they were brought to him - meaning the Arabs - and he wanted to put out their eyes, but God forbade him from that and ordered him to implement the limits on them, as God had revealed them to him. Scholars differed about who deserves the title of one who fights against God and His Messenger, and who is subject to the ruling of this.

x: Some of them said: He is the thief who cuts off the road.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and Ata al-Khurasani,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption the verse
, they said, this is the thief who cuts off the road, so he is a highway robber.

x: Others said: He is the thief who openly commits his theft, who is stubborn in Egypt and elsewhere.
Among those who said this is Al-Awza’i.

c: Al-Abbas told us
m: this, on the authority of his father, on his authority. On his authority, and on the authority of Malik, Al-Layth bin Saad, and Ibn Lahi’ah.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us:
m: I said to Malik bin Anas: Is there a war in the city? He said: Yes, and the warlord among us is the one who carries arms against the Muslims in the city or in the open, and he does that without any conflict between them, nor any enmity or hostility, cutting off the way, the road, and the homes, frightening them with his weapon, and he kills one of them, the Imam kills him like the killers of the warlord, and the guardian of the one killed has no pardon or retaliation.

c: Ali told me, Al-Walid told us:
m: I asked Al-Layth bin Saad and Ibn Lahi’ah about that. I said: Will the fighting take place in the homes of cities, towns and villages? They said: Yes, if they enter upon them openly with swords, or at night with fire. I said: So they kill, or take the money and do not kill? He said: Yes, they are the combatants. If they kill, they are killed, and if they do not kill and take the money, they are cut off on opposite sides if they leave the house with it. The one who fights the Muslims in the open and on the road is not more severe in fighting than the one who fights them in their harems and homes!

c: Ali told me, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr said:
m: And the war in the city is a month of fighting with his people with his weapon, day or night. Ali said, Al-Walid said:

c: And Malik told me:
m: Killing by treachery is in his view the same as fighting. I said: And what is killing by treachery? He said: It is a man who deceives a man or a boy and brings him into a house or is alone with him, and kills him, and takes his money. So the imam is the guardian of killing this one, and the guardian of the blood and the wound has no right to retaliation or retribution. This is what Al-Shafi’i said.

c: Al-Rabi' told us
m: about it.

x: Others said: The warrior is a highway robber. As for the stubborn person in the cities, he is not a warrior who is subject to the same ruling as warriors.
Among those who said this were Abu Hanifa and his companions.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, who said:
m: We discussed Al-Muharib while we were with Ibn Hubayrah, among some people from Basra, and their opinion was unanimous: Al-Muharib had not left the city. Mujahid said: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption
, he said: Adultery, theft, killing people, and destroying crops and offspring.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And they strive to spread corruption in the land, he said: Corruption means murder, adultery, and theft. The most correct of these sayings, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The one who fights against God and His Messenger is the one who fights against the Muslims’ paths and their protection, and raids them in their cities and wages war against them. We said: This is the most correct statement, because there is no disagreement among the proofs that whoever wages war against the Muslims due to his injustice towards them, is a combatant against them, and there is no disagreement about that. The one whose description we have described, there is no doubt about him waging war against them unjustly. Since that is the case, then whether he wages war against them in their cities and villages, or on their roads and paths, he is a combatant against God and His Messenger, by waging war against those whom God and His Messenger have forbidden from waging war against. As for his saying: And they strive to cause corruption in the land, it means: And they commit sins in the land of God: by frightening the paths of His believing servants, or the paths of their protection, and cutting off their roads, and taking their money unjustly and aggressively, and attacking their sanctuaries with immorality and wickedness.

x: God Almighty says: “He who wages war against God and His Messenger, and strives to spread corruption on earth, from among the people of the religion of Islam or their protection, has nothing but some of these characteristics that God Almighty mentioned.” Then the people of interpretation differed regarding these characteristics. Is the warrior obligated to deserve the name warrior, or is he obligated to do what is obligatory for him according to the extent of his crime, varying according to the differences in his crimes?

Some of them said: The combatant must be punished according to the extent of his entitlement, and he must bear what is due to him according to the extent of his crime, varying according to the severity of his crimes.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger until His statement

: or be banished from the land, he said: If he wages war and kills, then he must be killed if he is defeated before he repents. And if he wages war and takes property and kills, then he must be crucified if he is defeated before he repents. And if he wages war and takes property and does not kill, then he must have his hand and foot cut off from opposite sides if he is defeated before he repents. And if he wages war and frightens the wayfarer, then he must be banished.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

is that if he goes out and frightens people on the road and takes money, his hand and foot are cut off on opposite sides. And if he frightens people on the road, but does not take money and kills, he is crucified.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim - as I see it -
m: regarding a man who goes out to fight, he said: If he cuts off the road and takes money, his hand and foot are to be cut off. If he takes money and kills, he is to be killed. If he takes money and kills and mutilates, he is to be crucified.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse

, he said: If he kills, takes money, and threatens the wayfarer, he is crucified. And if he killed, it was no longer that, he killed. And if he took the money, it was no longer that, he cut off. Why was he corrupting, he was banished.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
until His saying: or be banished from the land, he said: If he frightens on the road and does not kill or take money, he is banished.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, he said:
m: It was said: Whoever fights and frightens the wayfarers and takes money but does not kill, his hand and foot will be cut off on opposite sides. And if he takes money and kills, he will be crucified.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: that he used to say regarding His statement,
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger to His statement

, or be banished from the land, are four limits that God has revealed: As for the one who sheds blood and property together, he is crucified. As for the one who sheds blood but refrains from property, he is killed. Whoever gains wealth and refrains from shedding blood shall have his hand cut off. Whoever does not gain any of this shall be banished. Muhammad bin Al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad bin Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: God forbade His Prophet, peace be upon him, from blinding the eyes of the Arabs who raided his camels, and He ordered him to implement the prescribed punishments on them as God had revealed them to him. So he looked at the one who took the money but did not kill, so he cut off his hand and foot from opposite sides, his right hand and his left Surat al-Ma’idah 5:33 The only reward of those who make war upon God and His Messenger and strive after corruption upon earth is that they be killed or crucified or their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides or they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a great punishment. foot. And he looked at the one who killed but did not take the money, so he killed him. And he looked at the one who took the money and killed, so he crucified him. And this is how it is appropriate for everyone who frightens the Muslims on the road and cuts off, if he took and took money, his hand was cut off for taking the money, and his foot for frightening the road. And if he killed but did not take the money, he was killed. And if he killed and took the money, he was crucified.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Suddi asking Atiyah Al-Awfi about a man who fights and goes out and seizes but does not seize any money or shed any blood. He said: Banishment by the sword. If he seizes money, his hand is to be cut off with the money, and his foot is to be cut off with what he feared the Muslims. If he kills but does not take any money, he is to be killed. If he kills and seizes the money, he is to be crucified. I think he said: His hand and foot are to be cut off.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ata al-Khurasani and Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse

, he said: This is the thief who robs the road, so he is a combatant. If he kills and takes money, he is crucified. If he kills and does not take money, he is killed. If he takes money without killing, his hand and foot are cut off. If he takes it before doing any of that, he is banished.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: Whoever goes out in Islam fighting against God and His Messenger, and kills and seizes wealth, he is to be killed and crucified. Whoever kills but does not seize wealth, he is to be killed as he killed. Whoever seizes wealth but does not kill, his hand is to be cut off from opposite sides. If he terrifies the Muslims, he is to be banished from his country to another, because God the Almighty says: or be banished from the land.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
, he said: There were people who were spreading corruption in the land, killing and cutting off roads, so those were crucified.

x: Others fought and made property lawful but did not transgress that, so their hands and feet were cut off.
Others fought and withdrew but did not transgress that, so those were expelled from the land.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hilak, he said, Qatada told us, on the authority of Muwarriq al-Ajli,
m: regarding the warrior, he said: If he went out and killed and took the money, he is crucified. If he killed but did not take the money, he is killed. If he took the money but did not kill, his hand is cut off. If he went out to cause trouble for the Muslims, he is banished.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Atiyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If a warrior goes out and frightens people on the road and takes money, his hand and foot are to be cut off on opposite sides. If he goes out and kills and takes money, his hand and foot are to be cut off on opposite sides and then he is crucified. If he goes out and kills but does not take money, he is to be killed. If he frightens people on the road but does not kill or take money, he is to be banished.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ ibn Yazid told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding this verse:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

and strive after corruption in the land, they said: If he frightens the Muslims and seizes wealth but does not shed it, he is to be cut off. If he sheds blood, he is to be killed and crucified. If he combines both and seizes wealth and sheds blood, he is to be cut off, then killed, then crucified. Crucifixion is mutilation. It is as if the cutting off is: As for the male thief, male or female, cut off their hands, and killing is: A life for a life. If he refuses, then it is the right of the leader and the Muslims to seek him out until they seize him, and implement upon him the ruling of the Book of God: or be banished from the land, from the land of Islam to the land of disbelief.

x: The proponents of this statement based their argument on their statement by saying: God has made retaliation obligatory for the murderer, and amputation for the thief. They said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
h
