The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases

: a man who killed and was killed, a man who committed adultery after being married and was stoned, and a man who disbelieved after becoming a Muslim. They said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of a Muslim man except in one of these three cases. As for killing for frightening people on the road without killing or taking money, this is precedence over God and His Messenger by disagreement over their ruling. They said: The meaning of the statement of those who said: The imam has the choice, if he killed and frightened people on the road and took money, then there is the choice of the imam according to their statement between killing, or killing and crucifixion, or cutting off the hand and foot from opposite sides.
As for crucifixing him in the name of fighting, without doing anything like killing or taking money, this is something that no scholar has said.
Others said: The imam has the choice: to do these things that God mentioned in His Book.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ata’ and on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding the warrior: that the imam has a choice in it, whichever he wants he does.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: The imam has a choice regarding the combatant, he can do whatever he wants. If he wants, he can kill, if he wants, he can cut off his hand, if he wants, he can banish, or if he wants, he can crucify.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
, to his statement: or be exiled from the land, he said: The imam takes whichever he prefers.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
, he said: The imam has a choice in it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Saʿd, he said, Ata’ said:
m: The imam can do whatever he wants in this regard. If he wants, he can kill, or cut off, or exile, based on the statement of God: that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off on alternate sides or that they be exiled from the land, so that is up to the ruling imam, and he can do whatever he wants in it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

, the verse, he said: Whoever draws a weapon in the sanctuary of Islam, and frightens the wayfarer, then he is captured and overpowered, then the Imam of the Muslims has the choice regarding him: if he wants, he can kill him, if he wants, he can crucify him, and if he wants, he can cut off his hand and foot.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Usama told us, he said, Abu Hilal told us, he said, Qatada told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: that he said
m: about the warrior: that is up to the imam, if he takes him he does with him what he wants.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abu Osama told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding Al-Muharrib, he said: That is up to the Imam, he does with him as he wishes.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger
, he said: That is up to the Imam.

x: Those who said this statement argued that we found the conjunction with or in the Qur’an to mean choice in everything that God has made obligatory from it, such as His statement regarding expiation for an oath: Then its expiation is feeding ten poor people from the average of that with which you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave (al-Ma’idah 5:89), and His statement: But if any of you is ill or has an ailment in his head, then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice (al-Baqarah 2:96), and His statement: “
h
Then the penalty of an animal like that which he killed

, as judged by two just men among you, is an offering delivered to the Kaʿbah, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or the equivalent of that in fasting” (al-Ma’idah 5:95). They said: If the conjunction with or in the Qur’an, in everything that God has made obligatory from it in the rest of the Qur’an, means choice, then it is the same in the verse of the warriors, the imam has a choice in what he sees fit to rule on the warrior if he is able to do so before repentance.

The more correct of the two interpretations in this regard, in our view, is the interpretation of those who impose punishment on the combatant according to the extent to which he deserves it, and make the ruling on combatants different according to their actions. So he imposes on those who are terrifying others - if he is overpowered before repentance, and before taking money or killing - exile from the land. And if he is overpowered after taking money and killing a soul that is forbidden to be killed, he is to be crucified, for the reason I mentioned earlier for those who say this statement. As for what those who say that the imam has the choice have argued, that or in conjunction means giving a choice in the case of a supposition, this is a statement that has no meaning, because or in the speech of the Arabs may have various meanings, and if it were not for the dislike of prolonging the book by mentioning them, I would have mentioned them.

I have explained many of their meanings in the past, and we will come to the rest of them in the future in their places, God willing. As for this passage, its meaning is a follow-up, and that is similar to the statement of the one who says: The reward of the believers with God on the Day of Resurrection is that He will admit them into Paradise, or raise their status in the highest place, or make them dwell with the prophets and the truthful. It is known that the one who says that does not mean by his statement that the reward of every believer who believes in God and His Messenger is in one of these ranks, and one of these stations, by his faith. Rather, what is understood from him is that its meaning is: The reward of the believer with God, the Mighty and Sublime, will not be devoid of some of these stations. The moderate one’s status is lower than the status of the one who is foremost in good deeds, and the one who is foremost in good deeds is higher than him in status, and the one who wrongs himself is lower than them both, and everyone is in Paradise as God, the Most High, said:
Gardens of Eden which they will enter
Likewise, the meaning of the conjunction with or in His statement:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger (Fatir 35

:33) is a follow-up. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:33 The only reward of those who make war upon God and His Messenger and strive after corruption upon earth is that they be killed or crucified or their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides or they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a great punishment. Its interpretation is: He who wages war against God and His Messenger and strives to spread corruption on earth will not be without deserving punishment for one of these four characteristics that God the Almighty mentioned - not that the Imam is the judge over him and has a choice in his matter - whatever his condition, whether his crime is great or small, because if that were the case, the Imam would have the right to kill and crucify whoever brandishes a weapon and frightens the wayfarer, even if he did not take money or kill anyone, and he would have the right to exile whoever kills, takes money, and frightens the wayfarer.
This is a statement, if anyone says it, contrary to what is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying:
h
The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases

: a man who kills a man and is killed in return, or commits adultery after being married and is stoned, or apostatizes from his religion, and contrary to his saying: Cutting off the hand for a quarter of a dinar or more, and other than what is known of its rulings. If someone says: These rulings that I mentioned were from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding someone other than the combatant, and the combatant has a ruling other than that that is unique to him. He was asked: What is the ruling that Al-Muharrib has isolated in his Sunnah?

If he claims that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, issued a ruling that is contrary to what we have mentioned, all scholars will call him a liar, because that is not found in a single transmission or group. If he claims that this is what is in the apparent meaning of the Book, it is said to him: The best way for you to do this is if we accept that the apparent meaning of the verse may include what you said and what those who disagreed with you said. So what is your proof that your interpretation is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse than his interpretation? And then, since the Imam had a choice in ruling on the combatant, in order to or in the sense of choice in this situation with you, then he could crucify him alive, and leave him crucified on the wood until he dies without killing him. If he said: That is for him, he would be contradicting the nation in that. If he claims that this is not his right, but rather he has the right to kill him and then crucify him, or crucify him and then kill him, he leaves out his reason that the imam only had the choice in ruling on the combatant because or comes with the meaning of choice.

How did he have the choice of killing, exile, or amputation, but he did not have the choice of crucifixion alone, so that another punishment could be added to it? It was said to him: Is there a difference between you and the one who gave him the option where you refused, and he refused it where you gave it to him, based on principle or analogy? He will not say something about one of them without being obligated to say something similar about the other.

c: It was narrated from the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that what we said about that was correct, including that in its chain of transmission there is doubt, and that is what: Ali bin Sahl narrated to us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi'ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib: That Abdul Malik bin Marwan wrote to Anas bin Malik asking him about this verse, so Anas wrote back to him informing him that this verse was revealed about those people from Arniyah, who were from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove the camels, frightened the wayfarers, and violated the forbidden vagina. Anas said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, peace be upon him, about the ruling on those who wage war, so he said: Whoever steals and frightens the wayfarers, cut off his hand for his theft, and his foot for frightening him. Whoever kills, kill him. Whoever kills, frightens the wayfarers, and violates the forbidden vagina, crucify him. As for his statement: Or their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides, what He, may He be glorified, means by this is that their hands are cut off in a way that is different from the way their feet are cut off. That is, their right hand is cut off, and their entire foot is cut off. That is the difference between them in the cutting off. If the place of min in this position was ala or ba, then it would have been said: or their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides - or: on opposite sides, and they would have conveyed the meaning conveyed by min.

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning of the negation that God mentioned in this place.
Some of them said: It is to seek until he is able to do so, or to flee from the House of Islam.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: Or they are banished from the land, he said: The imam pursues them with horses and men until he seizes them and establishes judgment over them, or they are banished from the land of the Muslims.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: His denial, is that he is asked.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Or are they banished from the land? He said. Or they flee until they leave the abode of Islam for the abode of war.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of the letter of Anas bin Malik to Abdul Malik bin Marwan:
m: that he wrote to him: And his exile, that the imam should seek him out until he takes him, and when he takes him, he should establish over him one of these positions that God Almighty mentioned with what he deemed permissible.
b.via: letter of Anas bin Malik to Abdul Malik bin Marwan

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said:
m: I mentioned that to Al-Layth bin Saad, so he said: His exile, his pursuit from country to country until he is captured, or his pursuit takes him out of the abode of Islam to the abode of polytheism and war, if he is a combatant who has apostatized from Islam. Al-Walid said: I asked Malik bin Anas, and he said the same.

c: Ali told me, Al-Walid told us:
m: I said to Malik bin Anas and Al-Layth bin Saad: And likewise, the warrior who remains a Muslim is sought after, forcing him to be sought from country to country until he reaches one of the borders of the Muslims or the furthest part of the Muslim territory. If they seek him, does he enter the land of polytheism? They said: A Muslim is not forced to do that.

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Or they are banished from the land, he said: That they seek him until they are unable to do so.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told me, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Or they are banished from the land, he said: They are banished until they cannot be controlled.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas,
m: regarding his statement: or they are banished from the land, he said: They were expelled from the land. Wherever they are found, they are taken out until they reach the enemy's land.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding his statement: Or they are banished from the land, he said: His banishment means that he is sought after but is not able to find him, whenever he hears about him in a land he is sought after.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Saeed told me, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or they are banished from the land, he said: If he did not kill or take money, he is sought until he is unable to do so.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ bin Yazid told me, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr:
m: or they are banished from the land, from the land of Islam to the land of disbelief.

x: Others said: The meaning of exile in this context is that if the imam has power over him, he exiles him from his town to another town.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays ibn Saʿd, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: or are banished from the land. He said: Whoever frightens the Muslims’ way, is banished from his country to another, because God Almighty said: or are banished from the land.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Salih told us, Al-Layth told me, Yazid bin Abi Habib and others told me, on the authority of Hayyan bin Surayj:
m: that he wrote to Umar bin Abdul Aziz about the thieves, and described to him their thievery and their imprisonment in prisons. He said: God said in His Book: “
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

and strive to cause corruption through the land is that they shall be killed or crucified or their hands and feet shall be cut off on opposite sides,” and he left out the words: or they shall be exiled from the land. So Umar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to him: As for what follows, you wrote to me mentioning the words of God, the Almighty and Majestic: “
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

and strive to cause corruption through the land is that they shall be killed or crucified or their hands and feet shall be cut off on opposite sides,” and you left out the words of God: or they shall be exiled from the land. So, a prophet! You, Hayyan! Do not move things from their places. You have prepared yourself for killing and crucifixion as if you were a slave of Banu Uqayl, without any resemblance to him? When this letter of mine reaches you, understand the commotion.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yazid and others,
m: a hadith similar to this, except that Yunus said in his hadith: It is as if you are a slave of the Banu Abi Uqal, without me resembling you to him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib:
m: That Al-Salt, the scribe of Hayyan ibn Shurayj, told them: Hayyan wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: That some Copts were proven to have fought God and His Messenger and spread corruption in the land, and that God says:
h
The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger

and spread corruption in the land is that they will be disgraced. So he read until he reached: and their feet are on opposite sides, and he stopped at the denial. And he wrote to him: If the Commander of the Faithful sees fit to carry out God’s judgment concerning them, then let him write that. So when Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz read his letter, he said: Hayyan has satisfied himself! Then he wrote to him: Your letter has reached me and I have understood it, and I have been content, as if I had Surat al-Ma’idah 5:33 The only reward of those who make war upon God and His Messenger and strive after corruption upon earth is that they be killed or crucified or their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides or they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a great punishment. written according to the letter of Yazid ibn Abi Muslim, or the foreigner of Iraq, without likening you to them. So I wrote according to the beginning of the verse, then I was silent about the end of it. And God says: Or they are banished from the land. So if the evidence has been established against them as you have written, then tie iron chains around their necks, then hide them to a tumultuous and violent place.

x: Shaghab and Bada are two places.
Others said: The meaning of banishment from the land in this context is imprisonment.
Mention of those who narrated this from him: It is the saying of Abu Hanifa and his companions.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of exile from the land, in this context, is his exile from one country to another country, and his imprisonment in the prison in the country to which he was exiled, until his repentance from his immorality becomes clear, and his turning away from his disobedience to his Lord. I said that this is the most correct of the sayings, because the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that in one of the three aspects that I mentioned. Since that is the case, and it is known that God, the Most High, made the punishment of the warrior: killing, crucifixion, or cutting off the hand and foot from opposite sides, after being able to do so, not in a state of his refusal, it is known that the banishment is also his punishment after being able to do so, not before.

If his fleeing from being pursued was his banishment from the land, then cutting off his hand and foot from opposite sides in a state of his refusal and his war in the form of combat, meaning carrying out the punishment on him after being able to do so. And in the consensus of all that this does not take the place of his banishment that God, the Most High, made a punishment for him after being able to do so, it is invalid that his banishment from the land was his fleeing from being pursued. Since this is the case, it is known that there are only two other options left, which are exile from one town to another, or imprisonment. Since this is the case, there is no doubt that if he is exiled from one town to another, he is not exiled from the land, but rather he is exiled from one land rather than another. Since this is the case - and God, may He be glorified, only commanded his exile from the land - it is known that there is no way to exile him from the land except by confining him to a spot in it, away from the rest of it.

In that case, he would be exiled from all of it, except from that from which there is no way to exile him. As for the meaning of negation, in the speech of the Arabs, it is expulsion, and from that is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: They deny the ways of the generous as hammers deny what follows the monkey. Hence, the word nafaya refers to bad dirhams and other things. As for the source of nafaya I banished, it means banishment and waste. It is also said: The bucket banishes the water. And what is said about the water that flies from the bucket is nafaya. Hence, the saying of the rajaz poet: His back was from the banishment like the birds’ places on the pure water. And from this it is said: He banished his hair, if it fell. It is said: Your color has changed, and He banished your hair.

By His saying, That, He, the Most High, means that this is the punishment with which I have rewarded those who fought God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption in the world, by killing, crucifixion, or cutting off a hand and a foot from opposite sides. For them, meaning for these fighters, is disgrace in this world. He says: It is evil, shame, humiliation, punishment, and punishment for them in this world before the Hereafter. It is said: I have disgraced so-and-so, so he was disgraced with disgrace. And His statement: And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment, the Almighty says: For those who fought God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption in the land, and did not repent from their actions until they perished, in the Hereafter, along with the disgrace with which You rewarded them in this world, and the punishment with which You inflicted upon them in it, a great punishment, meaning: the punishment of Hell.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Except for those who repent from their polytheism and their war against God and His Messenger and their endeavor to spread corruption on earth, by Islam and entering into faith, before the believers have power over them, for there is no way for the believers to be punished by any of the punishments that God has made a recompense for those who wage war against Him and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption on earth, such as killing, crucifixion, or cutting off a hand and a foot from opposite sides, or exile from the land, so no one has the right to be sold before him for what he took during his state of disbelief and war against the believers, in money, blood, or honor. They said: As for the Muslim, if he wages war against the Muslims or those with whom he has a treaty, and does some of what requires punishment, his repentance will not remove the punishment for his sin, rather his repentance is between him and God, and the Imam must implement the punishment that God has made obligatory upon him, and take the rights of the people.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said:
m: His statement, The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon the earth until His statement, So
h
know that God is Forgiving and Merciful

, this verse was revealed regarding the polytheists. So whoever among them repents before he is overpowered, there is no punishment against him. This verse does not protect a Muslim man from the prescribed punishment if he kills, or spreads corruption on earth, or wages war against God and His Messenger, then joins the disbelievers before he is overpowered. The prescribed punishment that he committed will be carried out against him.

c: Bashar told us, he said, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Except for those who repent before you have them in your power
. So
h
know that God is Forgiving and Merciful
.” He said: This is for the people of polytheism, if they do something in their polytheism, then God is Forgiving and Merciful, if they repent and submit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption is adultery, theft, killing a person, and destroying crops and offspring,
h
except for those who repent before you have them in your power
, during the time of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: There were people between whom and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a covenant, but they broke the covenant, cut off the way, and spread corruption on the earth. So God gave His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the choice concerning them: If He wished, He could kill him, or if He wished, He could crucify him, or if He wished, He could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. Whoever repents before you are able to seize him, that will be accepted from him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse, then he mentioned something similar to what Al-Dahhak said, except that he said: If he comes repentant and enters Islam, it is accepted from him, and he is not held accountable for what came before.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except for those who repent before you are able to seize them, he said: This is for the people of polytheism, if they did something like this in their polytheism, then repented and submitted, then God is Forgiving and Merciful.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Qatadah:
m: As for his statement:
h
Except those who repent before you are able to overpower them

, this is for the people of polytheism. So whoever among the polytheists attacks something from the Muslims while they are at war with them, and takes property and sheds blood, then repents before you are able to overpower him, what has passed is waived for him.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse is meant by the ruling, the warriors of God and His Messenger: the warriors of the people of Islam, whoever of them cuts off the road while he is residing in his Islam, then he seeks protection and is granted protection for the crimes he committed, and he is at war with the Muslims, and whoever of them does that while apostatizing from Islam, then he goes to the land of war, then he seeks protection and is granted protection. They said: So if the Imam grants him protection for his previous crimes, then no one has a responsibility against him in blood or money that he took before his repentance, and before the Imam grants him protection.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Osama told me, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Suwar, on the authority of Amer Al-Sha’bi:
m: That Haritha bin Badr went out as a warrior, and he frightened the wayfarers, shed blood, and seized money, then he came repentant before he was overpowered, so Ali bin Abi Talib, peace be upon him, accepted his repentance, and granted him a security extended for whatever he had taken of blood or money.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: That Haritha bin Badr fought during the reign of Ali bin Abi Talib, so he went to Al-Hasan bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, and asked him to seek protection from Ali, but he refused. Then he went to Ibn Ja’far, but he refused him. Then he went to Saeed bin Qais Al-Hamdani, and he granted him protection and took him close to him, and said to him: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, sought protection for me. He said: When Ali prayed the morning prayer, Saeed bin Qais came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is the punishment for those who wage war against God and His Messenger? He said: That they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. Then he said: Except for those who repent before you are able to seize them. Saeed said: Even if it was Haritha bin Badr? He said: Even if it was Haritha bin Badr! He said: So this Haritha bin Badr has come repentant, is he safe? He said: Yes! He said: So he brought him and pledged allegiance to him, and he accepted that from him, and wrote him a guarantee of safety.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Haritha ibn Badr had spread corruption on earth and waged war, then he repented. Ali spoke to him, but he did not grant him security. So he went to Sa’id ibn Qays and spoke to him. Sa’id ibn Qays went to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you say about one who wages war against God and His Messenger? - and he recited the entire verse - and said: What do you think of one who repents before you are able to overpower him? He said: I say as God said. He said: Then he is Haritha ibn Badr! Ali said: So he granted him security. Haritha said: Shall I not reach Hamdan? If I meet it far away, no enemy will be safe who finds fault with it. By the life of her father, Hamdan fears God and her suitor judges by the Book.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
Except for those who repent before you have them in your power

, and his repentance before he is in your power is that he writes to the Imam asking him for protection from what he killed and corrupted on earth. If he does not give me protection from that, I will increase in corruption, killing, and taking of wealth more than I did before. So it is the right of the Imam to give him protection from that. So if the Imam gives him protection, he comes until he places his hand in the hand of the Imam. No one among the people has the right to follow him, nor to seize him for the blood he shed, nor for the wealth he took. And whatever wealth he had is his, so that he does not kill the believers and cause corruption as well. So if he returns to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, then He is his guardian, and He will seize him for what he did, and his repentance is between him, the Imam, and the people. So if the Imam takes him, and he has repented, as he claims, to God, the Almighty, before the Imam gives him protection, then let the prescribed punishment be carried out on him.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, Makhul told me that he said:
m: If the imam gives him security, then he is safe, and the punishment for what he did will not be carried out on him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever comes repentant from war before he is able to overpower him, seeks protection from the Imam who grants him protection or does not seek protection from him, after he comes surrendering and abandoning war.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash'ath, on the authority of Amir, he said:
m: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa, while he was in Kufa during the reign of Uthman, after he had prayed the obligatory prayer and said: O Abu Musa, this is the place of one who seeks refuge with you. I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so al-Muradi. I fought against God and His Messenger, and I spread corruption in the land, but I repented before you could overpower me! So Abu Musa stood up and said: This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and he fought against God and His Messenger, and he spread corruption in the land, but he repented before you could overpower him. Whoever meets him should not treat him except with good. So the man stayed as long as God willed, then he went out and God, the Almighty and Majestic, caught up with him because of his sins and killed him.

c: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Surat al-Ma’idah 5:34 Except for those who repent before you are able to overpower them. So
h
know that God is Forgiving and Merciful

. A man came to Abu Musa and mentioned something similar. Ali ibn Sahl narrated that al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated: I said to Malik: What do you think of this warrior who has frightened the people and taken blood and property, and has fled to the land of war or has resisted in the lands of Islam, then has come repentant before he is overpowered? He said: His repentance is accepted. I said: Is he not to be prosecuted for any of his incidents? He said: No, unless he has specific property with him, which is returned to its owner, or the guardian of the one who was killed in his war seeks it, which is proven by evidence or confession, and he is executed for it. As for the blood that he has taken but whose guardians have not sought it, the Imam is not to be prosecuted for anything. Ali said: al-Walid said: I mentioned that to Abu Amr, and he said: His repentance is accepted if he was a warrior against the common people and the Imams, and has harmed them in his war, so he has drawn his weapon, and taken blood and property, and has had a means of protection or a group to whom he can take refuge, or he has fled to the land of war and apostatized from Islam, or he was residing there, then he has come repentant before he is overpowered, his repentance is accepted, and he is not to be prosecuted for anything of it.

c: Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Amr said:
m: I heard Ibn Shihab Al-Zuhri say that.

c: Ali bin Sahl Tal told me, Al-Walid told us:
m: I mentioned the statement of Abu Amr and Malik to Al-Layth bin Saad on this issue, and he said: If he declares a general war against the Imams, and seizes blood and property, and the government is prevented by his war against him, or he goes to the land of war, then he comes repentant before he is overpowered, his repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for any of his events in his war of blood, whether specific or general, because his guardian is seeking it.

c: Ali told me, Al-Walid told us,
m: Al-Layth said, and Musa bin Ishaq Al-Madani, who was the emir among us, also told me: Ali Al-Asadi fought and frightened the wayfarers and took blood and property, so the imams and the common people sought him out, but he refused, and they could not find him until he came repentant. That was because he heard a man reciting this verse: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ (al-Zumar 39:53), so he stopped and said: O servant of God, recite it again. So he repeated it to him, then he sheathed his sword, then he came repentant. Until he arrived in Madinah at dawn, washed himself, then he came to the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and prayed the dawn prayer, then he sat with Abu Hurairah in the midst of his companions. When dawn broke, the people recognized him and stood up to him, so he said: You have no way with me, I have come repentant before you could find me! Abu Hurairah said: He has spoken the truth. Abu Hurairah took him by the hand until he came to Marwan bin Al-Hakam when he was in charge of Medina during the time of Muawiyah, and he said: This is Ali who has come repentant, and you have no way against him or killing him. He said: So he left all of that. He said: And Ali went out repentant, fighting in the way of God at sea, and they met the Romans, so they brought his ship close to one of their ships, so he attacked the Romans in their ship, and they were defeated from him to their other ship, so it capsized with them and him, and they all drowned.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Mutraf bin Muqal told us, he said,
m: I heard Ata’ say about a man who stole something and came back repentant without being caught, is there any punishment for him? He said: No! Then he said:
h
Except for those who repent before you have them in your power
, the verse.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ ibn Yazid told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, they said:
m: If someone comes repentant and has not seized any money or shed any blood, he is left alone. This is what God said:
h
Except for those who repent before you have them in your power
, meaning that he has not shed any blood or seized any money.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by the exception in that is the one who repents from his war against God and His Messenger and his striving to spread corruption on earth after joining his war in the land of disbelief. But if his war and his fighting were while he was residing in the land of Islam and entering the midst of the nation, then his repentance does not remove from him anything of the limits of God, the Exalted, the Majestic, nor of the rights of the Muslims and those with whom he has a treaty, rather he is held accountable for that.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Ismail told me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah: that he told him that
m: they asked Urwah about someone who steals in Islam and commits a crime, then comes back repentant, so he said: His repentance is not accepted, if that were accepted from them they would be emboldened against him, and it would be a great corruption. But if he flees to the enemy, then comes back repentant, I do not see any punishment for him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Urwa
m: that this statement is different, which is: Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, someone who heard Hisham bin Urwa told me, on the authority of Urwa, he said: The punishment for what he fled from will be carried out on him, and no one is allowed to be safe in it - meaning, the one who commits a punishment, then flees and joins the infidels, then comes back repentant.

x: Others said: If his fighting and warfare was in the land of Islam, and he was not protected by a group to which he could resort, then he came repenting before he was able to overpower him, then his repentance does not remove from him any of the punishment or the rights of the people. If his fighting and warfare was in the land of Islam, or he was going to the land of disbelief, but in all of that he was resorting to a group that would protect him from whoever wanted him from the authority of the Muslims, then he came repenting before he was able to overpower him, then his repentance removes from him all of the incidents that he did during those days of his fighting, unless he committed a prescribed punishment, or ordered the company to do something that included a punishment, or fined a Muslim or a covenanted person while he was not resorting to a group that would protect him, then he is held accountable for what he did of that while he was like that, and that does not remove from him his repentance.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Abu Amr said:
m: If a thief or a group of thieves cut off the road, and they took what they took of blood and money, and they had no group to turn to or protection, and they were not safe except by entering the midst of their nation and the masses of their people, then he came repentant before he was overpowered, his repentance would not be accepted, and his punishment would be carried out on him, whatever it was.

c: Ali told me, Al-Walid told us:
m: I mentioned to Abu Amr what Urwah said: The prescribed punishment for what he fled from shall be carried out on him, and no one shall be granted security for him. Abu Amr said: If someone fled from his incident in the land of Islam, and an imam gave him security, his security is not permissible. If he went to the land of war, then asked an imam for security for his incidents, the imam should not give him security. Because the imam gave him security even though he was unaware of his incidents, he is safe. If someone comes demanding him for blood or money, he is returned to his place of safety. If he refuses to return, he is safe and no one shall interfere with him. He said: If he gave him security for his incidents even though he was aware of them, the imam is responsible and must pay blood money for what he had taken of blood or money, and he is sinful for neglecting those prescribed punishments and blood money, and his matter is up to God, the Almighty and Majestic. He said: Abu Amr said: If he does that, and he has a means of protection or a group to which he can take refuge, or he goes to the land of war and apostatizes from Islam, or he was residing there, then he comes repentant before he is overpowered, his repentance is accepted, and he is not followed by any of the incidents that he committed in his war, unless something is found with him that is still there, in which case it is returned to its owner.

c: Ali told me, he said, Al-Walid told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Rabia, he said:
m: His repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for anything he did during his war, unless someone demands that he be punished for blood that he had taken in peace before his war, then he is to be retaliated for.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Muammar Al-Raqi told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, who said:
m: May God kill Al-Hajjaj! If he was knowledgeable! He gave a man security from fighting him, so he said: Look, did he do anything before he went out?

x: Others said: His repentance removes the punishment imposed on him by God for fighting him, but does not remove the rights of the children of Adam.
Among those who said this was Al-Shafi’i.

c: Al-Rabi' told us
m: about it.

x: The most correct of these statements in my opinion is the statement of the one who said: The repentance of the warrior who abstains by himself or with a group with him before he is overpowered removes from him the worldly consequences that were incumbent upon him during his days of war and rebellion, from the limits of God, and the necessary fines, fuel, and retaliation, except for what was in his hand of the money of the Muslims and those with whom he had a treaty, which is returned to its people, due to the consensus of all that this is the ruling on the group that abstains and wages war against God and His Messenger, and seeks to spread corruption on earth in the manner of apostasy from Islam. So too is the ruling on every one who abstains and seeks to spread corruption on earth, whether they are a group or one. As for the one who steals in secret, or sneaks in to take advantage of the one he stole from, or brandishes a weapon in the open at some passerby, and is unable to refrain when asked, then the judgment of God upon him - whether he repents or not - is carried out, and the rights of the one whose money he stole, or whose guardian he harmed with blood or deceit are taken, and his repentance is between him and God, the Mighty and Sublime, based on the consensus of all that if he steals something of that nature while it belongs to the Muslims, he is safe, then he becomes at war with them: that his war against them will not remove from him a right of God, the Mighty and Sublime, nor of a human being.

So too is his judgment if he commits that in the open or in secret, and he is not able to resist the ruler himself if he wants to, nor does he have a group to which he can resort to protect him. In His statement:
h
Except those who repent before you have them in your power

, is clear evidence for those who are guided to understand that the ruling that God, the Exalted, mentioned regarding those who are at war, applies to Muslims and those with whom we have a treaty, not to the polytheists who have waged war against the Muslims. This is because if this were a ruling regarding the polytheists who are at war, not to the Muslims and not to their protection, then their Islam would not have been removed from them - if they converted to Islam or repented after We had power over them - what they had before their conversion to Islam and repentance of being killed, and what the Muslims have regarding the polytheists at war.

And in the consensus of the Muslims is that the conversion of the polytheist at war removes from him, after the Muslims have power over him, what his conversion to Islam removed from him before the power over him, Surat al-Ma’idah 5:34 Except for those who repent before you are able to overpower them. So
h
know that God is Forgiving and Merciful

. which indicates that the correct statement regarding this is the statement of the one who said: What is meant by the verse about those who are at war in this place is the wars of the people of the religion or the protection, not from the polytheists other than them who are at war. As for his saying:
h
Know that God is Forgiving and Merciful

? Its meaning is: Know, O believers, that God will not hold accountable anyone who repents from among the people of war against God and His Messenger, who strive to spread corruption on earth, and others for their sins, but He pardons him and conceals them from him, and does not disgrace him for them with punishment in this world or the next, and He is Merciful to him in His pardon of him and His leaving him to be punished for them.

evidence.text: (al-Zumar 39:53), so he stopped and said: O servant of God, recite it again.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger in what He has informed you of and promised of reward and threatened of punishment, fear God, meaning: answer God in what He has commanded you and forbidden you by obeying Him in that, and realize your faith and belief in your Lord and your offspring through your righteous deeds, and seek the means of approach to Him, meaning: seek closeness to Him by doing what pleases Him. Al-Wasila is the active participle of the saying: I sought the help of so-and-so with such-and-such, meaning: I approached him. From this comes the saying of Antarah: Men have a way to get to you. If they take you, put on kohl and dye your hair. It means the means, the proximity, and from it the saying of the other: If the informers are absent-minded, we will return to our connection and the reconciliation between us and the means will return And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us,
m: H, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Wa’il:
h
And seek a means of approach to Him
, he said: drawing near to Him in deeds.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us,
m: H, and Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Ata’:
h
And seek a means of approach to Him
, he said: closeness.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: O you who have believed, fear God and seek the means to Him, he said: It is asking and drawing near.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And seek a means of approach to Him
, meaning: draw near to Him by obeying Him and doing what pleases Him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And seek a means of approach to Him
, drawing near to God Almighty.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And seek a means of approach to Him
, he said: closeness.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And seek a means of approach to Him
, he said: closeness.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And seek a means of approach to Him
, he said: Love, endear yourself to God. And he recited: Those are the ones who call upon God, seeking a means of approach to their Lord (al-Isra’ 17:57).

x: God Almighty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: And strive, O believers, against My enemies and your enemies, in My cause, meaning in His religion and law that He has legislated for His servants, which is Islam. He says: Exhaust yourselves in fighting them and compelling them to enter into the true Islamic faith, that you may succeed, meaning: so that you may succeed and attain eternal life and immortality in His Paradise. We have demonstrated the meaning of success in the past with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

The Almighty says: Those who denied the Lordship of their Lord and worshipped other than Him, from among the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf, and from others who worshipped idols and statues, and were destroyed for that before repenting, if they had the kingdom of all that is on the earth and double it with it, to ransom themselves with it from the punishment of God upon them for abandoning His command and worshipping other than Him on the Day of Resurrection, and ransomed themselves with all of that, God would not accept that from them as ransom and compensation for their torment and punishment, but rather He will torment them with scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, a painful torment for them. This is an announcement from God, the Most High, to the Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they and all the other polytheists are equal before Him in their painful torment and great retribution.
This is because they used to say, The Fire will not touch us except for a few days
r
(Al Imran 3:24)

, being deceived by God, the Most High, and lying about Him. So God, the Most High, denied them with this verse and the one after it, and put an end to their hope, so He said to them and to all the disbelievers in Him and His Messenger: “Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment. They want to get out of the Fire, but they will never get out of it, and theirs is an enduring punishment.” God, the Most High, says to them: Do not hope, O disbelievers, for the ransom to be accepted from you, nor for your exit from the Fire through the means of your fathers after you have entered it, if you die in your disbelief, but repent to God with sincere repentance.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
They want to get out of the Fire

, is that He wants those who disbelieved in their Lord on the Day of Resurrection to get out of the Fire after entering it, and they will not get out of it, and for them is a lasting punishment, meaning: for them is a permanent, fixed punishment that will never leave them or be transferred, as the poet said: For on the Day of the People, you will have from me a permanent torment that will last for you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Nafi’ bin Al-Azraq said to Ibn Abbas, may God have mercy on him: Blind of sight and blind of heart, he claims that people will come out of the Fire, and God Almighty said: And they will not come out of it? Ibn Abbas said: Woe to you, read what is above it! This is for the disbelievers.

x: God Almighty says: And whoever drives a man or woman, then cut off, O people, his hand. That is why He raised the male and female thief, because they are not specified. If what was meant by that was a male and female thief specifically, then the correct way of speaking would have been to put it in the accusative case.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud
m: that he used to recite: And the male and female thieves.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: In our reading - he said:
m: and perhaps he said: in the reading of Abdullah - And the male and female thieves, cut off their hands.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: In our reading: And the male and female thieves, cut off their hands. This is evidence of the correctness of what we have said about its meaning, and the correctness of the nominative case in it, and that the male and female thief are nominative by their action as I have described, for the reasons that I have described. And God Almighty said: Then cut off their hands, meaning: their right hands, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then cut off their hands, the right one.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: In Abdullah’s recitation:
h
And the male thief
, male or female, cut off their hands. Then they differed about the thief that God Almighty meant.

x: Some of them said: He meant by that the one who steals three dirhams or more. This is the opinion of a group of the people of Medina, including Malik bin Anas and those who said the same. They provided evidence for their opinion by saying that: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off a shield worth three dirhams.
Others said: Rather, he meant by that the one who steals a quarter of a dinar or its value.

Among those who said that is Al-Awza’i and those who said the same. They supported their saying by the report that was narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cutting off the hand for a quarter of a dinar or more.
Others said: Rather, he meant by that the one who steals ten dirhams or more.

Among those who said that was Abu Hanifa and his companions. They provided evidence for that with the report narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr and Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off the hand of a shield worth ten dirhams.

Others said: Rather, he meant by that the thief of little or much. They argued for that by saying that the verse is clear, and that no one has the right to specify anything from it, except with an argument that must be accepted. They said: There is no authentic report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that this is for a specific thief. They said: The reports regarding what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off his hand are confused and different, and no one narrated from him that a thief of a dirham was brought to him and he let him go. Rather, they narrated from him that he cut off his hand for a shield worth three dirhams. They said: It is possible that if a thief of a daniq were brought to him, he would cut off his hand. They said: Ibn al-Zubayr cut off his hand for a dirham.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said:
m: The verse is general.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Abdul-Mumin told us, on the authority of Najdah al-Hanafi, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement:
h
And the male thief
, male or female. Is it specific or general? He said: Rather, it is general.

x: The correct statement regarding this matter, in our view, is the statement of those who said: The verse is specifically intended for thieves, and they are those who steal a quarter of a dinar or more or its value, due to the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Cutting off the hand for a quarter of a dinar or more. I have exhaustively mentioned the statements of those who differed on this matter, along with the reasons they used for their statements, and the statement of which of them is most correct, with its supporting evidence, in our book The Book of Theft, so we disliked making the book long by repeating it in this place. His saying:
h
A punishment for what they have earned
, a punishment from God, means: a reward for their theft and their work of stealing in disobedience to God. A punishment from God, means: a punishment from God for their theft.
Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And as for the male thief
, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, an exemplary punishment from God.
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise

.” Do not feel sorry for them by implementing the prescribed punishments on them, for by God, God has never commanded anything except that it is good, nor has He ever forbidden anything except that it is corruption. Omar bin Al-Khattab used to say: Be harsh on thieves, and cut off their hands hand by hand and foot by foot. And His saying:
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise

, God Almighty says: And God is Exalted in Might, in His vengeance against this male and female thief and others who disobey Him, Wise, in His judgment and decree over them. He says: O believers, do not be excessive in implementing My judgment on thieves and other criminals for whom I have imposed punishments in this world, for I have decreed that upon them, with My wisdom, and My knowledge of what is good for them and for you.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: In our reading - he said: and perhaps he said: in the reading of Abdullah - And the male and female thieves, cut off their hands.
Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim: In our reading: And the male and female thieves, cut off their hands.

x: God Almighty says: So whoever repents, of these thieves, meaning whoever returns from what God hates of disobeying Him, to what He is pleased with of obeying Him, after his wrongdoing, and his wrongdoing is his aggression and doing what God forbade him from doing of stealing people’s money, and reforms, meaning: and reforms himself by carrying it to what it hates in obedience to God, and repenting to Him for what he was doing of disobeying Him.

c: Mujahid - as he told us
m: - used to say: His repentance in this situation is the punishment that will be carried out on him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, then God forgives him, he says: the limit. Abu Kuraib narrated: Musa ibn Dawud narrated: Ibn Lahi’ah narrated: Huyayy ibn Abdullah narrated: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli narrated: Abdullah ibn Amr said: A woman stole jewelry. Those whom she had stolen from came and said: O Messenger of God, this woman stole from us! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cut off her right hand. The woman said: Is there any repentance? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are today as free from your sin as the day your mother bore you! Then God, the Almighty, revealed: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and amends, then indeed, God will turn to him in forgiveness. And his saying: Then God will accept his repentance, means: God Almighty will return him to what He loves and is pleased with, from what He hates and is displeased with in His disobedience. And His saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, means: Indeed, God, the Almighty, will cover the sins of whoever repents and turns from his sins to His obedience, by pardoning his punishment, making it lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection, and leaving him disgraced by it in front of all witnesses. Merciful, to him and to His servants who repent to Him for their sins.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do these people - meaning those who say: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days, who claim that they are the sons of God and His beloved ones - not know that God is the Manager of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and its Disposer and Choker, and nothing in either of them is prevented from what He wills, because all of that is His property, and His command is to Him, and there is no relation between Him and anything in them or in either of them, so He favors him because of his kinship to Him, so He saves him from His punishment, even though he is a disbeliever in Him, and opposes His command and prohibition, or He sends him to the Fire while he is obedient to Him because of his distant kinship to Him, but He punishes whomever He wills of His creation in this world for disobeying Him by killing, swallowing up, transforming, and other types of His punishment, and He forgives whomever He wills of them in this world by repenting to Him for his disbelief and disobedience, so He saves him from destruction and rescues him from punishment, and God is over all things competent. He says: God Almighty is able to punish whomever He wants to punish from among His creation for disobeying Him, and to forgive whomever He wants to forgive from among them by rescuing them from destruction through repentance and other than that of all matters, because creation is His creation, and the kingdom is His kingdom, and the servants are His servants.
His statement,
h
Do you not know that to God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth

? was addressed to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it are those mentioned from the groups of the Children of Israel who were in the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those around it. We have explained the Arabs’ use of something similar to that in their speech with its evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
The people of interpretation differed about who was meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It was revealed about Abu Lubaba bin Abdul Mundhir, because of his saying to Banu Qurayzah when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them: It is only slaughter, so do not accept the judgment of Saad.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief - of those who say, “We believe with their mouths but whose hearts do not believe,” he said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar - they claimed that he was Abu Lubaba - whom Banu Qurayzah pointed to on the day of the siege, what is the matter? And why was it revealed? So he pointed to them that it was slaughter.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about a Jewish man who asked a Muslim man to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his ruling on a person he had killed.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Aamer:
m: h
Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you

, he said: There was a Jewish man who was killed by a man from his religion, so the killer said to their Muslim allies: Ask Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for me, for if he sends the blood money, we will dispute before him, but if he orders us to kill, we will not go to him.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Abdullah bin Suriya, because he apostatized after converting to Islam.
Who said that?

c: Hannad and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Az-Zuhri narrated to me, saying:
m: I heard a man from Muzaynah narrating, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurairah narrated to them: The rabbis of the Jews gathered in Bayt Al-Madras when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina. A man from among them had committed adultery with a Jewish woman who had been married after his marriage. They said: Take this man and this woman to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him what the ruling is regarding them. And bring him the ruling regarding them. If he does with them what you do with regard to stoning, which is flogging with a rope of palm fiber coated with tar, then blackening their faces, then carrying them on two donkeys, and turning their faces towards the donkey’s back, then follow him, for he is a king. But if he rules that they should be stoned, then beware of him taking away from you what is in your hands. So they came to him and said: O Muhammad, this man has committed adultery with a married woman after his marriage. So rule regarding them, for we have appointed you to rule regarding them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked until he reached their rabbis at the school house, and said: O group of Jews, bring out to me your most knowledgeable one! So they brought out to him Abdullah bin Suriya the one-eyed - and some of Banu Qurayzah narrated that they brought out to him that day with Ibn Suriya, Abu Yasir bin Akhtab, and Wahb bin Yahudah - and they said: These are our scholars! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them until their matter was resolved, until they said to Ibn Suriya: This is the most knowledgeable of those remaining in the Torah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was alone with him, and he was a young boy, one of the newest of them in walking. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him the question, saying: O Ibn Suriya, I ask you by God and I remind you of His favors to the Children of Israel, do you know that God ruled in the Torah for those who commit adultery after being married that they should be stoned? He said: By God, yes! By God, O Abu al-Qasim, they know that you are a prophet sent by God, but they envy you! Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and ordered them to be stoned at the door of his mosque, in the tribe of Banu Ghanim ibn Malik ibn al-Najjar. Then Ibn Suriya disbelieved after that, so God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten into disbelief - those who say, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths but whose hearts do not believe. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: My father narrated, H, and Hannad narrated, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated, on the authority of Al-A’mash, H, and Hannad narrated, he said: Ubaidah ibn Hamid narrated, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a Jew who had been flogged and had been bathed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called one of their scholars and said: Is this how you find the punishment for adultery among you? He said: Yes! He said: I ask you by He who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery among you? He said: No, and had you not asked me about this, I would not have told you. But stoning is the Surat al-Ma’idah 5:41 O Messenger,
h
let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you

- from among those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts do not believe - and from among the Jews are listeners to falsehood, listeners to another people who have not come to you, distorting words from their [proper] usages, saying, "If you were given this, you would not be able to do so." So take it, but if you do not give it to him, then beware. And he whom Allah intends to test - you will not possess for him anything from Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah does not intend to purify. For them is disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. punishment. However, adultery has become widespread among our nobles, so if we seized a noble person, we would leave him, and if we seized a weak person, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: Come, let us meet and you can put something in place of stoning, so it can be for the noble and the lowly. So we put bathing and flogging in place of stoning! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the first to revive your matter after they killed it! So he ordered him to be stoned, and God revealed:
h
Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you
, the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said:
m: I was sitting with Saeed bin al-Musayyab, and with Saeed was a man whom he respected, and he was a man from Muzaynah whose father had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah, and he was one of the companions of Abu Hurayrah. He said: Abu Hurayrah said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. H, and Al-Mughni told me, he said, Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said:

c: A man from Muzaynah who follows knowledge and comprehends it told me,
m: he told on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurairah said: While we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a Jewish man came to him, and they had consulted about a friend of theirs who had committed adultery after he had become married.
b.via: A man from Muzaynah who follows knowledge and comprehends it

x: Some of them said to one another: This prophet has been sent, and you know that stoning has been imposed upon you in the Torah, but you concealed it and agreed among yourselves on a lesser punishment. So go and ask this prophet, and if he gives us a fatwa with what was imposed upon us in the Torah of stoning, we will leave that, for we left that in the Torah, and it is more deserving of being obeyed and believed! So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Abu Al-Qasim, a friend of ours who had become married committed adultery, so what do you think should be the punishment for him? Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) did not return to them until he had risen and we had risen with him. He set off to lead the schools of the Jews until he came to them and found them studying the Torah in the school house. He said to them: O group of Jews, I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah as punishment for one who commits adultery while he is married?

They said: We find him being bathed and flogged! Their rabbi was silent in the corner of the house. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) saw his silence, he insisted on asking him. Their rabbi said: O God, since you ask us, we find stoning upon them! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to him: What was the first concession you sought from God? He said: The cousin of a king committed adultery and he did not stone him. Then another man committed adultery in a family of people, and the king wanted to stone him, but his people stood up to protect him and said: By God, you will not stone him until you stone so-and-so, the cousin of the king! So they agreed among themselves on a punishment less than stoning and left off stoning. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then I will judge according to what is in the Torah! So God revealed regarding that: O Messenger,
h
let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you
until His saying:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
Others said: Rather, he meant the hypocrites.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer,
m: regarding his statement: O Messenger,
h
let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you
- those who say, ‘We believe’ with their mouths but whose hearts do not believe, he said: They are the hypocrites.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We believe with their mouths, he said, he says: they are the hypocrites, listening to another people, he said: they also listen to the Jews.

x: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is to say: What is meant by His statement,
h
Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you

, of those who say, “We believe, with their mouths, but whose hearts do not believe,” are a group of hypocrites. It is possible that Ibn Suriya was among those included in this verse, or Abu Lubabah, or someone else. However, the most reliable thing that has been narrated about this is what we mentioned before from the narration on the authority of Abu Hurayrah and al-Bara’ ibn ʿAzib, because that was on the authority of two men from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If that is the case, then the correct thing to say about it is to say: What is meant by it is ʿAbdullah ibn Suriya. If this is true, then the interpretation of the verse is: O Messenger, do not let those who hasten to deny your prophethood and to reject that you are a prophet grieve you, from those who said: We believe in you, O Muhammad, that you are a messenger sent to God, and we know that with certainty, because of your existence and description in our book.

This is because in the hadith of Abu Hurairah, which was narrated by Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Al-Zuhri: Ibn Suriya said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: By God, O Abu Al-Qasim, they know that you are a prophet sent by God, but they envy you. This was - according to this report - from Ibn Suriya, out of faith in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his mouth, but he did not believe it in his heart. So God Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, knowing the conscience of Ibn Suriya and that he did not believe in his heart, he says: And his heart did not believe that you are a messenger sent by God.

God, the Most High, says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger, do not be saddened by the haste of these hypocrites - who show with their tongues that they believe in you, but they believe in lying - to disbelieve in you, and do not let the Jews be hasty to deny your prophethood. Then God, the Most High, the Most Great, described their characteristics to him, and described them to him with their reprehensible descriptions and their vile actions, and informed him, comforting him for the sadness that befell him because of their denial of him, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness, that they are people who make permissible what is forbidden and bad foods and vile meals, such as bribes and ill-gotten gains, and that they are people of slander and lies against God, and distortion of His Book.

c: Then he informed him that
m: he would bring them shame in this worldly life and punishment in the Hereafter. He said: They are listeners to falsehood, meaning these hypocrites from among the Jews. He said: They are listeners to falsehood, and their hearing of falsehood is their hearing of the words of their rabbis: The ruling for the married adulterer in the Torah is to be burned and flogged.
