They are listeners to other people who have not come to you, he said: They listen to the people of the adulterer who wanted to resort to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the other people who had not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were determined to come to him, as Mujahid said:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Mujahid said:
m: listening to other people who did not come to you, with those who came to you.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the listeners of lies and the listeners of other people.
Some of them said: They are listening to other people, the Jews of Fadak. The other people who did not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were the Jews of Medina.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Zakariya and Mujalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among those who are Jews are some who listen to falsehood
, some who listen to another people, he said: The Jews of Medina, They did not come to you altering words from their [proper] usages, he said: The Jews of Fadak, they say to the Jews of Medina:
h
If you are given this
, then take it.

x: Others said: What is meant by this is a group of Jews who were the family of the woman who committed adultery. They sent them to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the ruling on her. And those who sent them were the other people, who were the family of the immoral woman. They had not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: his statement:
h
And among those who are Jews are some who listen to falsehood

, some who listen to other people who have not come to you, distorting [their] truth, for God revealed to the Children of Israel: If anyone among you commits adultery, stone him. They continued to do that until one of their best committed adultery. When the Children of Israel gathered to stone him, the best and nobles stood up and prevented him. Then a man from the elite committed adultery, so they gathered to stone him. The elite gathered and said: Do not stone him until you bring your companion and stone them both! The Children of Israel said: This matter has become too much for us, so come, let us set it right! So they abandoned stoning, and replaced it with forty lashes with a strong rope, and they carried him on a donkey with his face to his tail, and they blackened his face and paraded him around. They continued to do that until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent and arrived in Madinah. A woman from the noble Jews called Busra committed adultery. Her father sent some of his companions to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Ask him about adultery and what was revealed to him about it, for we fear that he will disgrace us and tell us what we did. If he gives you flogging, take it, but if he orders you to stone, beware of him! So they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him. He said: Stoning! Then God the Almighty revealed: “And among the Jews are some who listen to falsehood, listening to other people who have not come to you. They distort words from their [proper] usages,” when they distorted stoning and made it flogging.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The listeners of lies are the listeners of other people. It may be possible that those were from the Jews of Medina, and what was heard from them was from the Jews of Fadak, or it may be possible that they were from others. However, whichever of these was, it is from the description of a group of Jews who heard the lie against God in the ruling on the woman who Surat al-Ma’idah 5:41 O Messenger,
h
let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you

- from among those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts do not believe - and from among the Jews are listeners to falsehood, listeners to another people who have not come to you, distorting words from their [proper] usages, saying, "If you were given this, you would not be able to do so." So take it, but if you do not give it to him, then beware.

And he whom Allah intends to test - you will not possess for him anything from Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah does not intend to purify. For them is disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. rebelled among them while she was married, and that her ruling in the Torah was to be burned and flogged, and they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the ruling that was required of her, and they heard what the people of the wicked woman were saying about her before they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to judge him about her. They only asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that for them, so that the people of the wicked woman would know what his answer would be to them. If his ruling was not stoning, they would accept it as a ruling on them. If his ruling was stoning, they would warn him and refrain from accepting it and his ruling.
Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we said.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: listeners to falsehood, listeners to another people, he said: to another people who did not come to him from the People of the Book, these are listeners to those other people who did not come to him, they say to them falsehood: Muhammad is a liar, and this is not in the Torah, so do not believe in him.

x: God the Almighty says: These listeners to lies, the listeners of another people among them who have not yet come to you from the Jews, distort the words. And their distortion was that they changed the ruling of God the Almighty - which He revealed in the Torah regarding the chaste men and women who committed adultery by stoning - to flogging and blackening. So God the Almighty said: They distort the words, meaning: these Jews, and the meaning is the ruling of the words, so He was satisfied with mentioning the report of the distortion of the words instead of mentioning the ruling, so that the listeners would know its meaning. Likewise His statement: After their [proper] places, meaning: after God placed them in their proper places, so He was satisfied with mentioning the report of their places, instead of mentioning the placement of that, as God the Almighty said:
But righteousness is of he who believes in God and the Last Day
and the meaning is: But righteousness is of he who believes in God and the Last Day.

It may be possible that its meaning is: they distort the words from their places, so after is placed in place of about, just as one says: I came to you after I finished work, meaning: after I finished work. What he means by his saying:
h
If you are given this

, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware, is that these aggressors who listen to lies say: If Muhammad issues a fatwa to you regarding flogging and burning our companion, then take it, meaning: accept it from him, and if he does not issue a fatwa regarding that and issues a fatwa regarding stoning, then beware. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Al-Zuhri told me, he said:
m: I heard a man from Muzaynah telling Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: Abu Hurairah told them - in a story he mentioned -
h
And among those who are Jews are some who listen to falsehood

, some who listen to another people who have not come to you, he said: meaning those who were sent from among them who were sent and stayed behind, and they ordered them to do what they were ordered to do of distorting words from their places, so he said: They distort words from their places, saying, ‘
h
If you are given this
, then take it,’ for the sake of collecting, And if you are not given it, then beware, meaning stoning.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
If you are given this
, if this agrees with you, then take it. The Jews say it to the hypocrites.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
If you are given this
, then take it. If this suits you, then take it, and if it does not suit you, then beware of it. The Jews say this to the hypocrites.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They distort words from their proper places, when they distorted stoning and made it flogging, They say, ‘
h
If you are given this
, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Zakariya and Mujalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir:
m: They distort words from their proper places, saying, ‘
h
If you are given this
, then take it.’ The Jews of Fadak said to the Jews of Medina:
h
If you are given this
flogging, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware of stoning.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you are given this

, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware, they are the Jews. A woman among them committed adultery, and God had ruled in the Torah that adultery should be punished by stoning. They wanted to stone her, and they said: Go to Muhammad, perhaps he has a dispensation. If he has a dispensation, then accept it! So they went to him and said: O Abu al-Qasim, a woman among us has committed adultery, so what do you say about her? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: How did God rule in the Torah regarding the adulterer? They said: Leave the Torah alone, but what do you have regarding that? He said: Bring me the most knowledgeable of you about the Torah that was revealed to Moses! He said to them: By He who saved you from the people of Pharaoh, and by He who split the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh, will you not tell me what is the ruling of God in the Torah regarding the adulterer? They said: His ruling is stoning! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered it. And he stoned her to death. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
They have not come to you, distorting words from their [proper] usages, saying, If you are given this, then take it, but if you are not given it, then beware.

It was mentioned to us that this was regarding a man killed from Banu Qurayzah, killed by Nadir. Whenever Nadir killed a man from Banu Qurayzah, they would not put him in retaliation, but would rather give them blood money because of their superiority over them. Whenever Qurayzah killed a man from Banu Qurayzah, they would not accept anything less than retaliation because of their superiority over them in their eyes, out of pride. So the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina to collect this man killed, and they wanted to report this to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). A hypocrite said to them: This man killed by you was intentionally killed, whenever you report him to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I fear for you retaliation, so if he accepts the blood money from you, then take him, otherwise be on your guard!

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, They distort the words from their [proper] usages, he said: These people who did not come to you distort the words from their [proper] usages, they do not place them as God revealed them. He said: And all of these are Jews, some of them from others.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah and Ubaidah bin Hamid told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib:
m: “They say, ‘
h
If you are given this

, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’ They say, ‘Go to Muhammad, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding the burning and flogging, then take it, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding the stoning, then beware.’”

x: This is a consolation from God, the Most High, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his grief over the haste of those whose story he told of the Jews and hypocrites in this verse. God, the Most High, says to him: Do not be saddened by their haste to deny your prophethood, for I have decreed that they will not repent from their misguidance, nor will they turn back from their disbelief, because of My previous wrath upon them. And your grief over what you see of their haste to do what I have made a cause for their destruction and their deserving of My warning will not benefit them. The meaning of fitnah in this context is: straying from the right path. God Almighty says: And whoever God, O Muhammad, wants to return due to his straying from the path of guidance, you will not be able to rescue him from God from what God wants for him of confusion and straying.
So do not feel sad about what you missed of his guidance to the truth, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And whomever God wants to test, you will not possess for him anything from God.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not let those who hasten to disbelief from among the Jews, whose description I have described to you, grieve you. Because their hastening to do so is because God has willed to tempt them and has sealed their hearts, so that they will never be guided. Those are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify, meaning: These are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify from the filth of disbelief and the dirt of polytheism, with the purity of Islam and cleanliness of faith, so that they would repent. Rather, He intended for them disgrace in this world - and that is humiliation and disgrace - and in the Hereafter the torment of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. In a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of shame, the statement was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar and others, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: Those are the ones whose hearts God did not want to purify - for them in this world is disgrace, he said: A city in Rome will be conquered and they will be taken captive.

x: God Almighty says: These Jews, whose description I have described to you, O Muhammad, listen to falsehood and lies, from what some of them say to others: Muhammad is a liar, he is not a prophet, and some of them say: The punishment for the married adulterer in the Torah is flogging and burning, and other falsehoods and slander, and they accept bribes and eat them in exchange for their lies about God and their slander against Him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Abu Aqil told us, he said,
m: I heard Al-Hasan say regarding His statement: They are listeners to falsehood and devourers of unlawful gain, he said: That is for the rulers, they heard a lie and ate bribes.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: listeners to lies, devourers of unlawful gain, he said: This was with the Jewish rulers before you, they used to listen to lies and accept bribes.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Those who consume unlawful gain, he said: Bribery in judgment, and they are Jews.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father and Ishaq al-Azraq told us, and Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: Those who consume ill-gotten gains, he said: ill-gotten gains are bribes.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ and Wasil ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said:
m: It was said to Abdullah: What is sahh? He said: Bribery. They said: In the ruling? He said: That is disbelief.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Ghundar and Wahb bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Irreligious gain means bribery.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Harith, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: We said to Abdullah: We did not see ill-gotten gains as anything but bribery in judgment! Abdullah said: That is disbelief.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: Is ill-gotten gain, bribery? He said: Yes.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAmmar Al-Dahni, on the authority of Salim Ibn Abi Al-Jaʿd, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah about ill-gotten gains, and he said: A man seeks a need from another man, so he fulfills it, and he gives it to him, and he accepts it.

c: Suwar told us, he said, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur and Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said:
m: Irreligious gain means bribery.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: Al-Saht, he said: Bribery in religion.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah, he said, Umar said:
m: What was from the ill-gotten gains, bribes and the dowry of the adulteress.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Al-Saht is bribery.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who consume what is unlawful
, he said: bribes.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: The dowry of a prostitute is ill-gotten, the semen of a stallion is ill-gotten, the earnings of a barber are ill-gotten, and the price of a dog is ill-gotten.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Al-Saht is a bribe in a ruling.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubair, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Masoud about ill-gotten gains, he said: Bribery. I said: In the ruling? He said: That is disbelief.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They consume ill-gotten gains, meaning bribes.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hasan narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman informed us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Masruq and Alqamah:
m: They asked Ibn Masoud about bribery, and he said: It is ill-gotten gain. They said: In the judgment? He said: That is disbelief! Then he recited this verse: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers (al-Ma’idah 5:44).

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Bakir bin Abi Bakir, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, who said:
m: Masruq interceded for a man in need, so he gave him a slave girl. He became extremely angry and said: If I had known that you would do this, I would not have spoken to you about your need, nor will I speak to you about what remains of your need. I heard Ibn Mas’ud say: Whoever intercedes to restore a right or remove an injustice, and a gift is given to him and he accepts, then it is ill-gotten. It was said to him: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, we did not see that as anything other than taking a judgment! He said: Taking a judgment is disbelief.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: They listen to falsehood and devour what is unlawful. That is because they took bribes in judgment and ruled with lies.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Masoud about saht, is it bribery in judgment? He said: No, whoever does not rule by what God has revealed is a disbeliever, and whoever does not rule by what God has revealed is a wrongdoer, and whoever does not rule by what God has revealed is a sinner. But saht is when a man seeks your help in wronging him and you help him in it, then he gives you a gift and you accept it.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hubayrah al-Saba’i, who said:
m: There are three types of ill-gotten gains: the dowry of a prostitute, bribery in a ruling, and what was given to soothsayers in the pre-Islamic era.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Mut’i’ told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib: that he said
m: about the earnings of a cupper, the dowry of a prostitute, the price of a dog, the bribe in a judgment, the fee of a soothsayer, the sperm of a stallion, the bribe in a judgment, the price of wine, and the price of a dead animal: they are from ill-gotten gains.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who consume what is unlawful
, he said: Bribery in judgment.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Mawwal told me, on the authority of Umar ibn Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn Umar:
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every flesh that is grown by ill-gotten gains, the Fire is more deserving of it. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is ill-gotten gains? He said: Bribery in judgment.
b.via: Umar ibn Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn Umar

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abdul-Jabbar bin Omar told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abdullah, he said:
m: Anas bin Malik said to me: If you go back to your father, say to him: Beware of bribery, for it is ill-gotten. His father was the police chief of Medina.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Bribery is ill-gotten. Masruq said: So we said to Abdullah: Is it in the ruling? He said: No. Then he recited: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers (al-Ma’idah 5:44), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers (al-Ma’idah 5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient (al-Ma’idah 5:47). The root of the word saht is the dog of hunger. It is said from it: So-and-so has a saht al-madah, if he is a glutton who is never found except hungry. The bribe is called saht, in imitation of that, as if the one who is being bribed is greedy for taking what is given to him, like the one who has a saht al-madah for food. It is said from it: Sahtah and Asahtah, two dialects transmitted from the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq bin Ghalib: There was a time, O Ibn Marwan, when nothing was left of money except what was wiped out or wasted. It means that he has eradicated it by eating it and spoiling it. Hence the Almighty’s saying: He will destroy you with a punishment
r
. The Arabs say to the one who shaves: He has eradicated the hair, meaning: he has eradicated it. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:42 Listeners to falsehood, devourers of illicit gain. So
h
if they come to you
, either judge between them or turn away from them.
h
And if you turn away from them
, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
If they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them

, that if these other people who have not yet come to you - and they are the people of the prostitute - come to you seeking arbitration, then judge between them if you wish with the truth that God has made His judgment for those of them who have done the act of the prostitute, or turn away from them and leave the judgment between them if you wish, and the choice in that is yours. And a group of interpreters said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Or turn away from them, the Jews. A man from among them of lowly lineage committed adultery, so they stoned him. Then a noble man from among them committed adultery, so they humiliated him and paraded him around. Then they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a fatwa to agree with them. He said: So he gave them a fatwa regarding it, stoning, but they denied it. So he ordered them to call their rabbis and monks, and he implored them by God: Do you find it in the Torah? So they concealed it, except for a man from the youngest of them who was one-eyed. So he said: They have lied to you, O Messenger of God, it is in the Torah!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: The verse in Surat Al-Ma’idah, So
h
if they come to you
, judge between them, was about stoning.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: They came to him - meaning the Jews - about a woman among them who had committed adultery, asking him about her punishment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: How do you find it written in your Torah? They said: We are commanded to stone the adulteress! So the Messenger of God commanded her to be stoned. And God Almighty said: “But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if they come to you

, judge between them or turn away from them, he said: They used to punish for adultery, until a young man of honor among them committed adultery, and some of them said to each other: His people will not let you stone him, but flog him and mutilate him! So they flogged him, and made him ride on a saddled donkey, and made his face face to the tail of the donkey, until another lowly man of no honor committed adultery, and they said: Stone him! Then they said: How come you did not stone the one before him? But do as you did to him! So when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, they said: Ask him, perhaps you will find a dispensation with him! So the following was revealed:
h
But if they come to you
, judge between them or turn away from them, until His saying: Indeed, God loves those who act justly.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed about a man who was killed among the Jews, and was killed by some of them.
Who said that?

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq Fal, Dawud bin Al-Hussain told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that the verses in Al-Ma’idah, His saying:
h
Then judge between them or turn away from them

, to His saying: those who are just, were revealed regarding the blood money in Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayzah. That is because the slain of Banu Nadir, who had honor, were paid the full blood money, while Qurayzah paid half the blood money. So they brought their case to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed that regarding them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them right in that, and made the blood money equal in that. And God knows best which of them it was. Abu Kuraib narrated, he said, Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated, on the authority of Ali bin Salih, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: There were Qurayzah and Nadir, and Nadir were more noble than Qurayzah, so if a man from Qurayzah killed a man from Nadir, he was killed in his place. And if a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, he was given one hundred wasqs of dates. When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was sent, a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, so they said: Give him to us! They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). So the verse was revealed: And if you judge, judge between them with justice.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: “Ibn Zayd said: In the ruling of Huyy ibn Akhtab, there were two blood-moneys for the Nadirites, and one blood-money for the Quraziites, because he was from the Nadirites. He said: And God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what was in the Torah, He said: “And We ordained for them therein that a life is for a life” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), to the end of the verse. He said: When the Qurayzah saw that, they were not satisfied with the ruling of Ibn Akhtab, so they said: Let us go to Muhammad for judgment! So God, the Blessed and Exalted, said:
h
But if they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them

, so He gave him a choice, And how can they make you judge while they have the Torah in which is the judgment of God, the entire verse. And if the noble man committed adultery with a lowly woman, they would stone her, and they would blacken the face of the noble man, and they would carry him on a camel, and they would make his face face towards the tail of the camel. And if the lowly man committed adultery with a high-ranking woman, they would stone him, and they did that to her. So they went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for judgment, and he stoned her. He said: And The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Who is the most knowledgeable among you about the Torah? They said: So-and-so, the one-eyed man! So he sent for him and he came to him and said: Are you the most knowledgeable among them about the Torah? He said: That is what the Jews claim! The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: I ask you by God and by the Torah that He revealed to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai, what do you find in the Torah about adulterers? He said: O Abu al-Qasim, they stone the lowly, and they carry the noble on a camel, and they blacken his face, and they make his face face towards the camel’s tail, and they stone the lowly if he commits adultery with the noble, and they do that to her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: I ask you by God and by the Torah that He revealed to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai, what do you find in the Torah? He kept evading, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked him by God and by the Torah that He revealed to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai, until he said: O Abu al-Qasim, if an old man and an old woman commit adultery, stone them both. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “That is it. Go with them and stone them.” Abdullah said: I was among those who stoned them, and he continued to smite her and protect her with the stones himself until he died. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the ruling of this verse. Is it valid today? Do the rulers have the option of ruling and considering between the People of the Covenant and the People of the Covenant if they refer their case to them, like what was given to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse? Or is it abrogated?

x: Some of them said: This is established today, nothing has abrogated it, and the rulers have the choice in every era with this verse, just as God gave to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah bin Al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Qais, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi:
m: If one of the polytheists brings a case before you regarding a judgment, then if you wish, then judge between them according to what God has revealed, and if you wish, then turn away from them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ibrahim, they said:
m: If the polytheists come to you and make you their judge,
h
then judge between them or turn away from them
. And if you judge, then judge according to the judgement of the Muslims, and do not refer it to anything else.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi:
m: Then
h
if they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them
, he said: If he wishes, he may judge, and if he wishes, he may not judge.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: If he wants, he will rule, and if he wants, he will not rule.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: If the People of the Book come to you with a matter between them, then judge between them according to the judgement of the Muslims, or leave them alone and let the people of their religion judge between them, except in the case of theft or murder.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Ata’ said to me: We have a choice. If we wish, we will judge between the People of the Book, and if we wish, we will turn away and not judge between them. If we judge between them, we will judge according to our judgment between us, or we will leave them and their judgment between them. Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Shu’ayb said something similar. This is His statement:
h
So judge between them or turn away from them

c: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Mughira told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, Amr bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
But if they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them

, they said: If they come to the ruler of the Muslims, then if he wishes he may judge between them, and if he wishes he may turn away from them. And if he judges between them, he judges between them according to what is in the Book of God.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If they come to you
, judge between them, meaning:
h
If they come to you

, judge between them according to what God has revealed, or turn away from them. So God gave him a concession in that, if He wills, he may judge between them, and if He wills, he may turn away from them.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi, they said:
m: If the polytheists come to you and make you judge between them, then judge between them according to the judgment of the Muslims and do not return to anything else, or turn away from them and leave them to the people of their religion.

x: Others said: Rather, the choice has been abrogated, and if the People of the Covenant refer the matter to the ruler, he must rule between them with justice, and he does not have the right to neglect to consider them.
Who said that? Surat al-Ma’idah 5:42 Listeners to falsehood, devourers of illicit gain. So
h
if they come to you
, either judge between them or turn away from them.
h
And if you turn away from them
, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri:
m: Then
h
if they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them
, was abrogated by His statement:
h
And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: It was abrogated by:
h
And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, they said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: It was abrogated by:
h
And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid ibn Harun told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Nothing was abrogated from Al-Ma’idah except these two verses:
h
But if they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them

, which was abrogated by: And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations (al-Ma’idah 5:49). And His statement: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God or the sacred month or the offerings or the garlands (al-Ma’idah 5:2), which was abrogated by: Kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It was abrogated by:
h
And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them

, meaning the Jews. So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to judge between them, and gave him permission to turn away from them if he wished. Then God, the Most High, revealed the verse that follows it: And We have revealed to you the Book until His statement:
h
So judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations (al-Ma’idah 5
:48). So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to judge between them by what God has revealed, after giving him permission, if he wished, to turn away from them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari:
m: That Omar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to Adi bin Adi: If the People of the Book come to you, then judge between them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: It was abrogated by His saying:
h
Then judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if they come to you
h
then judge between them or turn away from them

, he said: The Sunnah has been established that they should return their rights and inheritances to the people of their religion, unless they come desiring a punishment, in which case they should be judged according to the Book of God.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: When the verse,
h
Then judge between them or turn away from them

, was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, could judge between them if he wished, and turn away from them if he wished. Then he abrogated it and said, Then judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations (al-Ma’idah 5:48), and he was forced to judge between them.

c: Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Saeed ibn Sulayman told us, Ibad ibn al-Awam told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Two verses were abrogated from this surah, meaning al-Ma’idah, the verse of the necklaces, and His statement:
h
Then judge between them or turn away from them

. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a choice. If he wanted to judge, he could, and if he wanted to turn away from them, he would return them to their own arbitration, that he should judge between them according to what is in our Book.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: The ruling of this verse is established and has not been abrogated, and that the rulers have the option of ruling between the people of the covenant if they come to them and seek judgment, and leaving the ruling between them and the consideration, like what God made for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse. We said that this is the more correct of the two, because those who say that the ruling of this verse is abrogated claim that it was abrogated by His statement:
h
And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5

:49). We have demonstrated in our book, The Book of Explanation of the Principles of Rulings, that abrogation is not abrogation except in what is the negation of the ruling of another in all its meanings, so that it is not permissible for the ruling to be combined with both matters in its validity in any way, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

And since that was the case, and it was not impossible in speech to say: And that you judge between them by what God has revealed, and its meaning is: And that you judge between them by what God has revealed if you judge between them by your choice to judge between them, if you chose that, and did not choose to turn away from them, since the one to whom that was said had been informed by its speaker: that he has the choice to judge and to leave the judgement, it was known from that that there is no indication in his saying:
h
And that you judge between them by what God has revealed that it abrogates his saying
: “So
h
if they come to you
, judge between them or turn away from them.
h
And if you turn away from them

, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice,” because of what we have described of the possibility of that as we have explained. Rather, it is evidence for something similar to what his saying indicated: And if you judge, judge between them with justice.

Since there is no evidence in the apparent revelation that one of the two verses abrogated the other, nor that one of the two matters negated the ruling of the other, and there was no report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that one of them abrogates the other, nor is there a consensus among the Muslims on that, then what we said is correct, that each of the two matters supports the other, and its ruling agrees with its ruling, and there is no abrogation in one of them of the other. As for his saying:
h
And if you turn away from them

, they will not harm you at all, its meaning is: If you, O Muhammad, turn away from those who seek judgment from the People of the Book, and you refrain from looking into what they have sought judgment from you about, and do not judge between them, they will not harm you at all, he says: They will not be able to harm you in religion or in this world, so refrain from looking into what they have chosen to do.
As for his saying: And if you judge, judge between them with justice, its meaning is: If you choose to judge and consider, O Muhammad, between the people of the covenant when they come to you,
h
then judge between them with justice

, which is fairness, and that is the judgment that God has made a judgment in its likeness over all of His creation from the nation of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, a group of people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi:
m: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. They said: If you judge between them, judge according to what is in the Book of God.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And if you judge, judge between them with justice, he said: He ordered that they be judged by stoning.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi,
m: regarding his statement: And if you judge, judge between them with justice, he said: By stoning.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: With justice, with fairness.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then judge between them with justice
, he said: He ordered that judgment be passed between them by stoning. As for his saying:
h
God loves those who are just
, its meaning is:
h
God loves those who are just

in their rulings among people, who judge between them according to the ruling of God that He revealed in His Book and commanded His prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them. It is said: The judge was just in his ruling, if he was fair and ruled justly, he was just. As for qast, its meaning is: injustice, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: But as for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell (al-Jinn 72:15), meaning by that? those who deviate from the truth.

evidence.text: Then he recited this verse: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers (al-Ma’idah 5:44).

x: God Almighty means: How can these Jews, O Muhammad, make you judge among themselves, and be satisfied with you as a judge among them, while they have the Torah, which I sent down to Moses, which they acknowledge as true, and that it is My Book which I sent down to My Prophet, and that whatever ruling is in it is from My ruling, they know that and do not deny it or dispute it, and they know that My ruling in it for the married adulterer is stoning, and despite their knowledge of that, they turn away, meaning: they abandon ruling by it, after knowing My ruling in it, out of audacity towards Me and disobedience to Me. This, even though it was from God the Most High addressing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a rebuke from Him to the Jews about whom this verse was revealed. God the Most High says to them: How do you, O Jews, acknowledge the ruling of the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while you deny his prophethood and reject him, while you abandon My ruling which you acknowledge as a right and obligation upon you that Moses brought to you from God?

He says: Since you abandon My ruling that Moses brought to you, whose prophethood you acknowledge in My Book, then you are more likely to abandon My ruling that My Prophet Muhammad tells you is My ruling, while you deny his prophethood. Then the Most High said, informing about the state of these Jews whose description He described in this verse, and the state of their counterparts who transgressed against His rule and deviated from the path of truth: And those are not believers. He says: The one who did this action - that is, the one who turned away from the rule of God, which He ruled in His Book which He revealed to His Prophet, regarding His creation - is not the one who believed in God and His Messenger and acknowledged His Oneness and the Prophethood of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - because that is not the action of the people of faith.
The origin of turning away from something is turning away from it, as in:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer:
m: Then they turn away after that, he said: Their turning away is what they left of the Book of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: to his client: And how can they judge you while they have the Torah in which is the judgment of God, meaning: the limits of God, so God informed us of His judgment in the Torah.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And with them is the Torah
, in which is the judgment of God, meaning: God’s explanation of what they disputed about regarding their slain man, Then they turn away after that, the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said,
m: he said - meaning the Lord, may He be exalted - taunting them: And how can they judge you while they have the Torah in which is the judgment of God, he says: stoning.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is an explanation of what these Jews asked you about regarding the ruling on married adulterers, and a light, meaning: in it is the clarification of what was dark for them, and the illumination of what was unclear regarding the ruling, by which the prophets who submitted to God will judge, meaning: in what they referred to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the matter of adulterers, the prophets who submitted to God, and they are those who submitted to God’s ruling and acknowledged it. God Almighty meant by that our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his ruling on the married Jewish adulterers by stoning, and in his equalizing the blood of those killed by Nadir and Qurayzah in retaliation and blood money.
And before Muhammad, the prophets ruled according to what is in it from God’s ruling, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light, and the prophets who submitted to God judged by it, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when this verse was revealed: We judge the Jews and those other than them from the people of religions.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said, a man from Muzaynah told us
m: while we were with Saeed bin al-Musayyab, “on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: A Jewish man and a woman committed adultery, and some of them said to each other: Let us go to this prophet, for he is a prophet who was sent with leniency. If he issues a fatwa to us that is less than stoning, we will accept it and use it as evidence before God and say: The fatwa of one of your prophets! He said: So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among them who committed adultery? He did not say a word to them until he reached the house of their schools, and he stood at the door and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah regarding one who commits adultery if he is married? They said: He is to be stoned, flogged, and flogged. Flogging is that the two adulterers are carried on a donkey, their backs facing each other, and they are paraded around. A young man [among them] was silent, and when he saw him, he was silent. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O God, since You have asked us, we find stoning in the Torah!” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What was the first thing that you made permissible for God’s command? He said: “A man who was a relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so He delayed stoning him. Then a man committed adultery among the people, so he wanted to stone him, but his people prevented him and said: ‘Do not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him!’ So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Then I will rule according to what is in the Torah!’ So he ordered them to be stoned.” Al-Zuhri said: “They were informed that this verse was revealed about them: ‘Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it,’” and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was one of them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The prophets who submitted to Islam will judge by it
, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the prophets before him, judge by what is in it of truth.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The prophets who submitted to God will judge by it
, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for those who were Jews, meaning the Jews, so judge between them and do not fear them.

x: God Almighty says: And he rules by Surat al-Ma’idah 5:44 Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars [of Islam], by what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people, but fear Me,
h
and do not exchange My verses for a small price

. And whoever does not judge by what I have revealed Allah, then those are the disbelievers. the Torah and its rulings that God revealed in it in every era - according to what Muhammad passed by in ruling in it - with the prophets to whom Muhammad submitted, the rabbis and the scholars. The rabbis are the plural of rabbi, and they are the wise scholars who are insightful in the politics of people, managing their affairs, and looking after their interests, and the scholars are the rabbis.

We have explained the meaning of the rabbis in the past with evidence for this and the statements of the people of interpretation regarding it. As for al-Ahbar, they are the plural of Habr, which is the expert who knows something, and from this Ka’b was called: Ka’b al-Ahbar. Al-Farra’ used to say: I have heard the Arabs say ‘ahbar’ most often when referring to a scholar! “ahbar” with a kasra on the ha’.

Some of the interpreters said: What is meant by the rabbis and scholars in this place are the two sons of Suriya who acknowledged to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the ruling of God Almighty mentioned in the Torah regarding the married adulterers.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: There were two Jewish men, brothers, called the sons of Suriya, who followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but did not submit to Islam. They gave him a covenant that he would not ask them about anything in the Torah unless they told him about it. One of them was a rabbi and the other a rabbi. They only followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to learn from him. So he called them and asked them, and they told him how it was when the noble man committed adultery and the poor man committed adultery, and how they changed it. So God revealed: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Islam] judged by it for those who were Jews,” meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the rabbis and the rabbis, they were the sons of Suriya, for those who were Jews. Then he mentioned the sons of Suriya and said: And the rabbis and the rabbis, because they were entrusted with the Book of God and were witnesses thereto.

x: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God, the Most High, has informed us that the Torah is the law by which the Muslims of the prophets judge the Jews, and the rabbis from among His creation, and the rabbis. It is possible that he meant by that Ibn Suriya and others, but the Muslims of the prophets, and every rabbi and rabbi are included in the apparent meaning of the revelation, and there is no indication in the apparent meaning of the revelation that it is meant specifically from among the rabbis and rabbis, nor is there any proof that must be accepted. So every rabbi and rabbi is included in the verse by the apparent meaning of the revelation. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said in the interpretation of the rabbis.
Who said that?

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: The rabbis and scholars are their readers and jurists.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: The rabbis and scholars, the jurists and scholars.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The rabbis are the scholars and jurists, and they are above the rabbis.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The rabbis are the jurists of the Jews, and the scholars are their rabbis.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Yazid bin Dawud told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: The rabbis and scholars, all of them rule according to what is in it of truth.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, the rabbis are the governors, the rabbis are the scholars. As for his saying: With what they have been entrusted with of the Book of God, its meaning is: The prophets who converted to Islam rule according to the ruling of the Torah, and the rabbis and scholars - meaning the scholars - rule according to what they have been entrusted with knowledge of, such as the Book of God, which is the Torah. The letter Baa in his saying: because of what they have preserved, is related to the scholars. As for his saying: And they were witnesses over it, it means: that the rabbis and scholars, with what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, judge by the Torah with the prophets who submitted to those who were Jews, and they were witnesses over the judgment of the prophets who submitted to those who were Jews, that they judged them by the Book of God that He revealed to His Prophet Moses and His judgment over them, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: And they were witnesses over him, meaning the rabbis and scholars. They are the witnesses for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding what he said, that it is the truth that came from God, and he is the Prophet of God, Muhammad. The Jews came to him, so he judged between them with justice.

x: God Almighty says to the Jewish scholars and rabbis: Do not fear people in implementing My judgment that I have ruled upon My servants, and in carrying it out upon them as I have commanded, for they are not able to harm or benefit you except with My permission. And do not conceal the stoning that I have made a judgment in the Torah upon married adulterers, but fear Me more than any of My creation, for benefit and harm are in My hand.
And fear My punishment in concealing what you have been entrusted with of My Book, as:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: So do not fear the people, but fear Me, meaning: Do not fear the people and conceal what I have revealed. As for His statement:
h
And do not exchange My verses for a small price

, he says: And do not take, O rabbis, a small price for abandoning the ruling by the verses of My Book which I revealed to Moses, and that is the small price. Rather, the Most High intended to forbid them from eating ill-gotten gains because of their distortion of the Book of God, and their changing His ruling from what He ruled regarding married adulterers, and other rulings which they changed in order to obtain bribes, such as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And do not exchange My verses for a small price
, he said: Do not consume what is ill-gotten based on My Book. And he said another time, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement,
h
And do not exchange My verses for a small price
, he said: Do not take a bribe with it.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And do not exchange My verses for a small price
, and do not take a small amount of hope in order to conceal what I have revealed.

x: God Almighty says: And whoever conceals the judgment of God which He revealed in His Book and made it a judgment between His servants, and conceals it and judges by other than it, like the judgment of the Jews regarding married adulterers by casting off the dead body and blackening it, and their concealment of stoning, and their ruling regarding some of their dead with full blood money and in others with half the blood money, and regarding the nobles with retaliation, and regarding the lowly with blood money, and God has made all of them equal in the ruling upon them in the Torah, they are the disbelievers, meaning: These are the ones who did not rule by what God revealed in His Book, but changed and altered His judgment, and concealed the truth which He revealed in His Book, and they are the disbelievers, meaning: They are the ones who concealed the truth which they were supposed to reveal and clarify, and covered it up from the people, and showed them something other than it, and ruled by it, based on ill-gotten gain which they took from them.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of disbelief in this place.
Some of them said something similar to what we said about that, that he meant the Jews who distorted the Book of God and changed its ruling.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers

, “And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wicked (al-Ma’idah 5:47), regarding all of the disbelievers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Qasim told us, he said, Abu Hayyan told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, he said:
m: The three verses in Al-Ma’idah,
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
, “Then it is those who are the wrongdoers” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), Then it is those who are the wicked (al-Ma’idah 5:47), there is nothing of it for the people of Islam, it is for the disbelievers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers

, “the wrongdoers,” and the wicked. He said: These verses were revealed about the People of the Book. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated that al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated that he heard Imran ibn Hudayr say: Some people from Banu Amr ibn Sadus came to Abu Majlaz and said: O Abu Majlaz, do you think that God's statement,
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers is true

? He said: Yes! They said: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers (al-Ma’idah 5:45) is true? He said: Yes! They said: O Abu Majlaz, do these people judge by what God has revealed? He said: It is their religion that they follow, and it is what they say, and to which they call. If they abandon something of it, they will know that they have committed a sin! They said: No, by God, but you are different! He said: You are more deserving of this than I! I do not see it, and you see it and do not feel embarrassed, but it was revealed about the Jews, Christians, and polytheists, or something like that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, who said:
m: A group of Ibadis sat with Abu Majlaz and said to him: God says:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers

. “And it is those who are the wrongdoers.” (al-Ma’idah 5:45) And it is those who are the defiantly disobedient. (al-Ma’idah 5:47) Abu Majlaz said: They do what they do - meaning the rulers - and they know that it is a sin! Surat al-Ma’idah 5:44 Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars [of Islam], by what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people, but fear Me,
h
and do not exchange My verses for a small price

. And whoever does not judge by what I have revealed Allah, then those are the disbelievers. He said: This verse was revealed about the Jews and Christians. They said: By God, you know what we know, but you fear them. He said: You are more deserving of that than we are! As for us, we do not know what you know! They said: But you know it, but fear of them prevents you from carrying out your affairs!

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abi al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Hudhayfah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
, he said: What good brothers you have are the Children of Israel, if you have everything sweet and they have everything bitter!! And you will follow their path, the path of the traps.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
, “the wrongdoers,” and the wicked. He said: These verses were revealed about the People of the Book.

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, he said:
m: It was said to Hudhayfah: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then it is they who are the disbelievers. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abi Al-Bukhtari, he said:
m: A man asked Hudhayfah about these verses:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers

, “Then it is those who are the wrongdoers” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), Then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient (al-Ma’idah 5:47). He was asked: Is that about the Children of Israel? He said: What good brothers are you, the Children of Israel, if they have every bitterness and you have every sweetness! No, by God, you will follow their path, the path of the trap.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: These verses are about the People of the Book.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
. He mentioned to us that these verses were revealed regarding the murder of the Jews who was one of them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
, and the wrongdoers, and the wicked, for all the People of the Book, because of what they abandoned of the Book of God.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said:
m: “A Jewish man who had been flogged and had been slapped passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he called them and said: ‘Is this how you find the punishment for adultery?’ They said: ‘Yes!’ So he called one of their scholars and said: ‘I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book?’ He said: ‘No, and had you not asked me about this, I would not have told you. We find its punishment in our book as stoning, but it has become widespread among our nobles, so if we seized a noble person, we would leave him, and if we seized a lowly person, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: ‘Come, let us all gather together to flog and slap instead of stoning.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O God, I am the first to revive Your command when they killed it!’ So he ordered him to be stoned.” Then God revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you until His saying:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the disbelievers
. That is, The Jews: Then it is they who are the wrongdoers (al-Ma’idah 5:45) meaning the Jews: Then it is they who are the wicked (al-Ma’idah 5:47), for all the infidels.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
, he said: Whoever rules by his book that he wrote with his own hand, and abandons the Book of God, and claims that this book of his is from God, then he has disbelieved.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to the hadith of Al-Qasim on the authority of Al-Hasan, except that Hannad said in his hadith: So we said: Come, let us agree on something that we will implement on the noble and the weak, so we agreed on the blackening and flogging instead of stoning. And the rest of the hadith is similar to the hadith of Al-Qasim.

c: Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Al-Zinad narrated to us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: We were with Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Mas’ud, and a man mentioned in his presence:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the disbelievers

, “And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the wrongdoers,” (al-Ma’idah 5:45), And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is they who are the defiantly disobedient (al-Ma’idah 5:47). Ubaidullah said: By God, many people interpret these verses in a way that they were not revealed to, and they were only revealed about two tribes of Jews. Then he said: They are Qurayzah and An-Nadir, and that is because one of the two groups had invaded the other and subdued it before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, until they agreed and agreed that for every person killed by a powerful woman from a humiliated tribe, the ransom would be fifty wasqs, and for every person killed by a humiliated woman from a powerful woman, the ransom would be one hundred wasqs. So they gave them a difference and a loss. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came while they were in that state, and the two groups were humiliated by the arrival of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not prevail over them. While they were in that state, the humiliated one killed a man from the honorable one. The honorable one said: Give us a hundred wasqs! The humiliated one said: Has this ever happened in two tribes whose religion is one and whose country is one, and the blood money of some of them is double that of others? We gave you this only to separate you from us and to make Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) between us and you. So they agreed to make the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) between them. Then the honorable one discussed matters among themselves. She feared that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not give her from her companions double what she gave to her companions from it. So they sent their brothers from the hypocrites to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said to them: Tell us the opinion of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). If he gives us what we want, we will rule on it, but if he does not give us, we will warn him and not rule on it! The hypocrite went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they wanted from all of that matter. Ubaidullah said: Then God Almighty revealed about them: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, all of these verses, until he reached: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein, to the wicked. Ubaidullah read that verse by verse, and explained it according to what was revealed, until he finished explaining that to them in the verses. Then he said: What I meant by that was the Jews, and this description was revealed about them.

x: Some of them said: In the case of the infidels, the Muslims, and in the case of the oppressors, the Jews, and in the case of the immoral, the Christians.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: The disbelievers were revealed regarding the Muslims, the wrongdoers regarding the Jews, and the wicked regarding the Christians.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Safar, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: The unbelievers refer to the Muslims, the oppressors refer to the Jews, and the wicked refer to the Christians. Ibn Wakee’, Abu Al-Sa’ib, and Wasil bin Abd Al-A’la told us, they said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ibn Shabrama, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: A verse concerning us, and two verses concerning the People of the Book:
h
And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers

, concerning us, and concerning them: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, (al-Ma’idah 5:45), and the wicked, concerning the People of the Book.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer,
m: like the hadith of Zakariya on his authority.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Safar, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi:
m: h
And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
