, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another.
h
And whoever among you takes them as allies
, then indeed, he is of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed

, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever takes them as allies among you - indeed, he is one of them.” He said: When the Battle of Uhud took place, a group of people were in a difficult situation and feared that the infidels would prevail over them. So a man said to his companion: As for me, I will go to that Jew and take a guarantee of safety from him and convert to Judaism with him, for I fear that the Jews will prevail over us! And the other said: As for me, I will go to so-and-so the Christian in some part of the land of Ash-Sham, and take a guarantee of safety from him and convert to Christianity with him! So God, the Most High, revealed, forbidding them both: “
h
O you who have believed

, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever takes them as allies among you - indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.”

x: Others said: Rather, Abu Lubaba bin Abdul Mundhir meant by that, in his notification to Banu Qurayzah when they accepted Saad’s ruling: that it was slaughter.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
O you who have believed

, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir, from the Aws - and he was from Banu Amr ibn Awf - and he sent him to Qurayza when they broke the covenant. When they obeyed him by descending, he pointed to his throat: Slaughter, slaughter!

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God Almighty forbade all believers from taking the Jews and Christians as supporters and allies against the people of faith in God and His Messenger and others, and He informed us that whoever takes them as supporters, allies and guardians instead of God and His Messenger and the believers, then he is among them in his partisanship against God and His Messenger and the believers, and that God and His Messenger are innocent of him. It may be possible that the verse was revealed regarding Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and their Jewish allies. It may be possible that it was revealed regarding Abu Lubabah because of his actions against Banu Qurayzah. It may be possible that it was revealed regarding the two men of whom al-Suddi mentioned that one of them intended to join that Jew, and the other a Christian in Syria.

None of these three statements has been authenticated with a report that could be used as evidence, so it is acceptable to say that it is as it was said. If this is the case, then it is correct to rule that the apparent meaning of the revelation is general in what it is general, and what the people of interpretation have said about it is permissible, of the statement that we do not know of to the contrary. However, there is no doubt that the verse was revealed about a hypocrite who was loyal to Jews or Christians out of fear for himself from the vicissitudes of time, because the verse after this indicates that, and that is His statement: And you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may strike us’ Al-An’am 2:17. As for his saying:
h
Some of them are allies of others

, he meant by that: that some of the Jews are supporters of some of them against the believers, and one hand against all of them, and that the Christians are likewise, some of them are supporters of some of them against those who oppose their religion and creed, informing his believing servants by that: whoever is a friend of them or of some of them, then he is their friend against those who oppose their religion and creed from among the believers, just as the Jews and Christians are at war with them.

So the Most High said to the believers: So be you also allies of one another, and war with the Jew and the Christian as they are at war with you, and some of them are allies of one another, because whoever befriends them has shown war to the people of faith, and disavowed them, and has clearly severed their allegiance.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
And whoever among you takes them as allies

, then indeed he is one of them, and whoever takes the Jews and Christians as allies instead of the believers, then indeed he is one of them. He says: Whoever takes them as allies and supports them against the believers, then he is from the people of their religion and their faith, for no one takes anyone as an ally unless he is pleased with him and his religion and what he is upon. And if he is pleased with him and his religion, then he has opposed that which contradicts it and is angry with it, and it has become the wisdom of his judgment. Therefore, whoever among the people of knowledge ruled for the Christians of Banu Taghlib in their sacrifices and the marriage of their women and other matters of theirs, with the rulings of the Christians of Banu Israel, because of their allegiance to them, and their satisfaction with their faith and their support for them over it, even though their lineages were different from their lineages and the origin of their religion was different from the origin of their religion.

This is clear evidence of the correctness of what we say, that whoever professes a religion shall be subject to the ruling of the people of that religion, whether his religion was before the advent of Islam or after it. Except for whoever is a Muslim from the people of our religion and has converted to another religion, then he shall not remain in the religion he professed and has converted to it, but shall be killed for his apostasy from Islam and his abandonment of the religion of truth, unless he returns to the religion of truth before being killed. And the corruption of what he contradicts from the statement of the one who claims that the ruling of the People of the Two Books shall not be applied to whoever professes their religion, unless he is an Israelite or converted to their religion from someone other than them before the revelation of the Qur’an. As for whoever professes their religion after the revelation of the Qur’an, who was not one of them, whose lineage differs from their lineage and whose race differs from their race, then his ruling is contrary to their ruling.
Mention of those who said what we said about the interpretation.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman al-Ru’asi told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas was asked about the sacrifices of the Arab Christians, so he recited:
h
And whoever among you takes them as allies
, then indeed he is one of them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this verse: “
h
O you who have believed

, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them,” it is about sacrifices. Whoever enters the religion of a people is one of them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib4, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Eat from the slaughtered animals of Banu Taghlib, and marry their women, for God says in His Book: “
h
O you who have believed

, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you, then indeed, he is [one] of them.” And if they were not of them except through allegiance, then they would have been of them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Hisham, he said:
m: Al-Hasan saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Arab Christians or the marriage of their women, and he used to recite this verse: “
h
O you who have believed
, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another.
h
And whoever among you takes them as allies
, then indeed, he is of them.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Harun ibn Ibrahim, he said:
m: Ibn Sirin was asked about a man who sells his house to Christians who take it as a church. He said: So he recited this verse: Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies.

x: God Almighty means by that: God does not grant success to one who places guardianship in the wrong place, so he allies himself with the Jews and Christians - despite their enmity towards God, His Messenger, and the believers - against the believers, and he is their supporter and helper, because whoever allies himself with them is at war with God, His Messenger, and the believers. We have explained the meaning of injustice in other places, and that it is putting something in the wrong place, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Hisham, he said: Al-Hasan saw no harm in the sacrifices of the Arab Christians or the marriage of their women, and he used to recite this verse: “O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies.
He said: So he recited this verse: Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies.

x: The interpreters differed as to who is meant by this verse.
Some of them said: He meant Abdullah bin Abi bin Salul.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard my father, on the authority of Atiyah ibn Saʿd: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, hastening into them, into their guardianship, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may befall us,’ to the end of the verse: Then they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said, my father Ishaq bin Yasar told me, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit:
m: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease, meaning Abdullah bin Ubayy, hasten among them, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may strike us,’ because he said: I fear that a misfortune may strike me!
b.via: Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that a group of hypocrites who were advising the Jews and deceiving the believers, and saying: We fear that the Jews will have the upper hand over the believers!
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them, he said: The hypocrites, in their friendship with the Jews, their conversation with them, and their breastfeeding their children from them. And the statement of God Almighty: We fear that a misfortune may befall us, he said: He means: We fear that the misfortune may befall the Jews.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease to his statement
: regretful, people from the hypocrites who were friendly with the Jews and advised them, not the believers.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease, he said, doubt, hasten into them, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may strike us,’ and the misfortune is the appearance of those who are thorny upon them.

x: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is that it is from God, report about some hypocrites who were loyal to the Jews and Christians and deceived the believers, and they said: We fear that the tables will turn - either for the Jews and Christians, or for the polytheists who worship idols, or others - against the people of Islam, or that a calamity will befall these hypocrites, and we will have a need for them. It may be possible that this was from the words of ʿAbdullah bin Ubayy, and it may be possible that it was from the words of someone else, but there is no doubt that it was from the words of the hypocrites. The interpretation of the statement is: Then you see, O Muhammad, those in whose hearts there is sickness and faith in your prophethood and belief in what you have brought them from your Lord, hastening in them, meaning in the Jews and Christians, and by their haste in them he means their haste in befriending and treating them well, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may befall us,’ these hypocrites say: We only hasten to befriend these Jews and Christians out of fear of a misfortune that may befall us from our enemy.

i: It means the circle, the state, as the rajaz poet said:
x: May the destiny and the circles of time turn against you Meaning: That a state will prevail for a long time, and we will need their support for us, so we will support them for that.
So God Almighty said to them:
h
Perhaps God will bring about victory or a decision from Him
h
and they will become
, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful. (al-Ma’idah 5:52) Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Perhaps God will bring about victory or a decision from Him

, that perhaps God will bring about victory. Then they differed in the interpretation of the conquest in this place. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:52 Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into it, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us." But perhaps Allah will bring about victory or a decision from Him,
h
and they will become
, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful.
Some of them said: What he meant here is the judiciary.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Perhaps God will bring about victory, he said: with judgment.

x: Others said: He meant the conquest of Mecca.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Perhaps God will bring about victory, he said: The conquest of Mecca. In Arabic, victory is not judgment, as Qatada said, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth (al-A’raf 7:89). It may be possible that the decree that God promised His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when He said: Perhaps God will bring about the conquest, was the conquest of Mecca, because that was one of the great decrees of God, and His judgment separated the people of faith and disbelief, and it was established for the people of disbelief and hypocrisy that God exalts His word and weakens the plot of the disbelievers. As for his saying: or a command from Him, Al-Suddi used to say about that, what:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Or a command from Him, he said: The command is the jizya. It may be possible that the matter that God promised His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to bring about is the jizya, and it may be something else. However, whichever it is, it is one of the things that will give victory to the believers over the disbelievers in God and His Messenger, and one of the things that will upset the hypocrites and not please them. This is because God, the Most High, has informed us about them that when that matter comes, they will become regretful of what they kept secret within themselves. As for His statement:
h
And they will become

, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful, it means those hypocrites who were loyal to the Jews and Christians. God Almighty says: Perhaps God will bring a command from Him by which He will give victory to the believers over the disbelievers from among the Jews and Christians and other disbelievers, so that these hypocrites will become, over what they concealed within themselves of their friendship and love for the Jews and Christians, and their hatred and hostility towards the believers, regretful, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they will become
regretful of what they concealed within themselves, of their friendship with the Jews, and their deception of Islam and its people.

x: There is a difference in the reading of his statement:
h
And those who believe say

. So I read it as the people of Medina read: And they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful. “Those who believed will say, ‘Are these the ones who swore by God?’” without the waw. The interpretation of the speech according to this reading: So the hypocrites, when God brings victory or a command from Him, will become regretful over what they kept secret in their souls. The believers will say in amazement at them and their hypocrisy, lies, and their audacity towards God in their false oaths to God: These are the ones who swore to us by God that they were with us, and they are lying in their oaths to us?
And this is the meaning that Mujahid intended in his interpretation of that, which is:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Perhaps God will bring about victory or a decision from Him. Then, those who believed will say, ‘Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you?’ Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. The same is true in the copies of the Qur’an of the people of Medina without the letter waw.

x: Some of the Basrans read it as:
h
And those who believe say

, with the waw, and he put the word says in the accusative case in apposition to Perhaps God will bring about the conquest. The reader of that mentioned that he used to say: What is meant by that is: Perhaps God will bring about the conquest, and Perhaps those who believe say, and other than that is impossible. Rather, it is not permissible to say: And perhaps God will say those who believe, and he used to say: That is similar to their saying: I ate bread and milk, like the saying of poetry: And you saw your husband in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear. The interpretation of the speech according to this reading is: Perhaps God will bring victory to the believers, or a command from Him by which He will grant them victory over the disbelievers among their enemies, so that the hypocrites will become regretful for what they kept secret within themselves.

And perhaps those who believed will say at that time: These are the ones who swore falsely by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you? It is in the Mushafs of the people of Iraq with the letter waw:
h
And those who believe say
. The Kufians read it as
h
and those who believe say

with the waw, and they raised says with the future tense and freedom from the jussives and the nasibs. The interpretation of the one who reads it thus: Then they will regret what they concealed within themselves, and those who believed will say, and he will begin to say, and he will raise it.

Our reading that we are following is wa-yaqool with the addition of the waw in wa-yaqool, because it is like that in our copies of the Qur’an, the copies of the people of the East, with the waw, and raising ya-qul as the beginning. The interpretation of the statement - since our reading is as we have described - is: They will become regretful of what they kept secret in their souls, and the believers will say: These are the ones who swore to us by God with their most solemn oaths falsely that they were cursed. God Almighty says, informing about their condition before Him due to their hypocrisy and the evil of their actions, their actions have been nullified. He did not say: Their actions that they did in this world have been lost in vain, with no reward or recompense for them. Rather, they did them without certainty that they were an obligation imposed upon them by God, nor on the basis of sound faith in God and His Messenger.

Rather, they did them in order to repel the believers with them from themselves, their wealth, and their children. So God nullified their reward, since they were not for Him. So they became losers. He says: So these hypocrites, when the command of God came to give victory to the believers over the disbelievers, were clothed in their purchase of this world for the Hereafter, and their deal was disappointed, and they perished.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: And those who believe say.
So I read it as the people of Medina read: And they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful.
The interpretation of the speech according to this reading: So the hypocrites, when God brings victory or a command from Him, will become regretful over what they kept secret in their souls.
Some of the Basrans read it as: And those who believe say, with the waw, and he put the word says in the accusative case in apposition to Perhaps God will bring about the conquest.

The interpretation of the speech according to this reading is: Perhaps God will bring victory to the believers, or a command from Him by which He will grant them victory over the disbelievers among their enemies, so that the hypocrites will become regretful for what they kept secret within themselves.
The Kufians read it as and those who believe say with the waw, and they raised says with the future tense and freedom from the jussives and the nasibs.
The interpretation of the one who reads it thus: Then they will regret what they concealed within themselves, and those who believed will say, and he will begin to say, and he will raise it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: Our reading that we are following is wa-yaqool with the addition of the waw in wa-yaqool, because it is like that in our copies of the Qur’an, the copies of the people of the East, with the waw, and raising ya-qul as the beginning.

The interpretation of the statement - since our reading is as we have described - is: They will become regretful of what they kept secret in their souls, and the believers will say: These are the ones who swore to us by God with their most solemn oaths falsely that they were cursed.

x: God Almighty says to the believers in God and His Messenger:
h
O you who have believed

, meaning: they believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged what their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them, Whoever among you turns back from his religion, meaning: whoever among you turns back from the true religion that he is upon today, and changes it and alters it by entering into disbelief, whether in Judaism or Christianity or any other type of disbelief, then it will not harm God at all, and God will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him. He says: God will bring in their place, the believers who did not change, alter, or turn back, with a people better than those who turned back and altered their religion, whom God loves and who love God. This threat was from God to those who had foreknowledge that they would apostatize after the death of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Likewise, He promised to those among the believers what He promised in this verse, to those who had foreknowledge that they would not change or alter their religion, and would not apostatize. So when God took the soul of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, some people from the people of the hair and some of the mud apostatized, so God replaced the believers with better ones than them, as God the Most High said, and He fulfilled His promise to the believers, and carried out His threat against those of them who apostatized. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abdullah bin Ayyash told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b:
m: That Umar bin Abdul Aziz sent to him one day, and Umar was the governor of Medina at that time, and he said: O Abu Hamza, a verse kept me up last night! Muhammad said: What is it, O Prince? He said: The saying of God,
h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion… until he reached and do not fear the blame of a blamer. Muhammad said: O Prince, what God meant by those who believed were the governors from Quraysh, whoever reverted from the truth. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the individuals of the people whom God brought believers, and He replaced the believers with those of them who had apostatized.

x: Some of them said: It is Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq and his companions who fought the apostates until they entered through the door from which they left.
Who said that?

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Dahlam, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him, he said: This, by God, is Abu Bakr and his companions.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Dahlam, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Sahl, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him
, he said: Abu Bakr and his companions.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said:
m: Al-Hasan recited:
h
Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him
. He said: By God, it refers to Abu Bakr and his companions.

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Azdi told me, he said, Ahmad bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him
, he said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr and his companions.

c: Ali bin Saeed bin Masrouq Al-Kindi told me, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Then God will bring forth a people whom He will love and who will Surat al-Ma’idah 5
h
O you who have believed
, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are]
h
humble toward the believers

, powerful against the disbelievers, striving in the cause of Allah and not fearing the blame of a blamer. That is the bounty of Allah which He bestows upon whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing. love Him,
h
humble toward the believers
, powerful against the disbelievers;
h
they strive in the cause of God

and do not fear the blame of a blamer,” he said: This is Abu Bakr and his companions. When some of the Arabs apostatized from Islam, Abu Bakr and his companions fought them until he brought them back to Islam.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Whoever among you turns back from his religion, God will bring forth a people whom He will love and who will love Him, until His saying: And God is All-Encompassing and Knowing. God revealed this verse and He knew that apostates would turn back from among the people. So when God took the soul of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, most of the Arabs turned back from Islam - except for three mosques: the people of Medina, the people of Mecca, and the people of Bahrain from Abd al-Qays. They said: We pray but do not pay zakat, and by God, our wealth will not be seized! So Abu Bakr was spoken to about that and it was said to him: If they had understood this, they would have given it - or: paid it - so he said: No, by God, I do not differentiate between something that God has joined together, and if they withheld even a rope from what God and His Messenger have imposed, we would fight them over it! So God sent a group with Abu Bakr, and he fought as the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had fought, until he captured, killed, and burned with fire people who had apostatized from Islam and refused to pay the zakat. He fought them until they acknowledged the ma'un - which is the zakat - as small, worthless people. Then delegations of the Arabs came to him, and he gave them the choice between a shameful plan or a devastating war. So they chose the shameful plan, and it would have been easier for them to admit that their dead were in Hell, and that the dead believers were in Paradise, and that whatever money they had taken from the Muslims they would return to them, and whatever money the Muslims had taken from them was lawful for them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him. Ibn Jurayj said: They reverted when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, so Abu Bakr fought them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hisham told us, he said: Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion, he said: God knew the believers, and the meaning of evil fell upon the ignorant among them of the hypocrites and those in His knowledge that they would revert. He said:
h
O you who have believed
, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring, the apostates in their homes, with a people whom He will love and who will love Him, with Abu Bakr and his companions.

x: Others said: He means a group of people from Yemen. Some of those who said that said: They are the people of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Abdullah bin Qais.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of ʿIyad al-Ashʿari, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed,
h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pointed to Abu Musa with something he had with him, and said: They are this people.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, he said:
m: I heard Ayyad narrating on the authority of Abu Musa: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse:
h
Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him
, he said: He meant the people of Abu Musa.

c: Abu al-Sa’ib Salim ibn Junadah told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Shu’bah - Abu al-Sa’ib
m: said: Our companions said: It is on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, and I do not remember Samak - on the authority of Ayyad al-Ash’ari, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are the people of this one, meaning Abu Musa.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ayyadh al-Ash’ari,
m: the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Musa: They are the people of this, in his saying:
h
Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, Yazid told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, who said:
m: I heard ʿAyyadh al-Ashʿari say: When the verse, Then God will bring forth a people whom He will love and who will love Him, was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are your people, O Abu Musa! - or he said: They are the people of this one - meaning Abu Musa.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Sufyan Al-Himyari told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ayyadh - or:
m: Ibn Ayyadh - Then God will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, he said: He said: They are the people of Yemen.

c: Muhammad ibn Auf told us, Abu al-Mughira told us, Safwan told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr told us, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, who said:
m: When God revealed:
h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion to the end of the verse, Umar said: Is it me and my people, O Messenger of God? He said: No, rather this one and his people! meaning Abu Musa al-Ash’ari.

x: Others said: Rather, they are all the people of Yemen.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: He loves them and they love Him, he said: People from the people of Yemen.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They are the people of Saba.

c: Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said,
m: he told me from someone who heard Shahr bin Hawshab say: They are the people of Yemen.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abdullah bin Ayyash told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi:
m: From Umar bin Abdul Aziz, he sent to him one day, and he was the governor of Medina, asking him about that, and Muhammad said: God will bring a people, and they were the people of Yemen! Omar said: I wish I was one of them! He said: Amen!

x: Others said: They are the supporters of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him, he claims that they are the Ansar. The interpretation of the verse according to the opinion of those who said: God meant by His saying:
h
Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him

, Abu Bakr and his companions in their fight against the apostates after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, he will never harm God at all, and God will bring a people among you whom He will love and who will love Him, and He will take revenge on them through them at their hands. And thus came the report and narration from some of those who interpreted it in this way:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hisham told us, he said, Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love, he said, meaning: God will bring forth the apostates in their homes, a people He will love and who will love Him, with Abu Bakr and his companions. As for the saying of those who said: God meant the people of Yemen by that, then its interpretation is: O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, God will bring to the believers who have not turned back, a people whom He loves and who love Him, as helpers and supporters for them. And thus came the narration from some of those who interpreted it in this way:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
O you who have believed

, whoever of you should revert from his religion the verse, is a threat from God that whoever of you should revert from his religion, He will replace them with someone better than them. As for the one who said: He meant the Ansar by that, then his interpretation of that is similar to the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as meaning Abu Bakr and his companions.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is what was narrated in the hadith from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace): that they are the people of Yemen, the people of Abu Musa al-Ashʿari. Had it not been for the hadith that was narrated in this regard from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) based on the hadith that was narrated from him, I would have no opinion in this regard except the opinion of those who said: they are Abu Bakr and his companions. This is because he did not fight a people who had declared Islam during the time of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and then turned back as infidels, other than Abu Bakr and those who were with him from among those who fought the apostates with him after the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). However, we left the opinion in this regard for the hadith that was narrated in this regard from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) that he (may God bless him and grant him peace) was the source of clarification of the interpretation of what God revealed of His revelation and the verses of His Book.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: If the people whom God mentioned that He would bring - when those who had converted to Islam during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, apostatized from their religion - were the people of Yemen, then were the people of Yemen during the days of fighting Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, against the apostates, Abu Bakr’s helpers in fighting them, so that you find it permissible to direct the interpretation of the verse in the way it was Surat al-Ma’idah 5:54
h
O you who have believed
, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are]
h
humble toward the believers

, powerful against the disbelievers, striving in the cause of Allah and not fearing the blame of a blamer. That is the bounty of Allah which He bestows upon whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing. directed? Or were they not his helpers against them, so how could you find it permissible to direct the interpretation of the verse in that way, when you know that God does not break His promise?

God Almighty did not promise the believers that He would replace the apostates among them on that day with better apostates to fight the apostates, but He informed them that He would bring them better ones in their place. He did that to them recently, not long ago. He brought them during the time of Umar, and their position with Islam and its people was the best position. They were helpers to the people of Islam and more beneficial to them than those who had apostatized after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the rabble of the Bedouins and the rough people of the desert who were a burden to the people of Islam and no benefit.
There is a difference in the reading of his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, whoever among you should revert from his religion. So I read it as the people of Medina read:
h
O you who have believed

, whoever among you should revert from his religion, showing the doubling, with two dals, the last dal being in the jussive mood. And that is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an. As for the reading of the people of Iraq, they read it as: Whoever among you turns away from his religion, with assimilation, with one dal, and moving it to the fatha, based on the dual, because the jussive that appears to be doubled in the singular, if dualized, is assimilated. It is said for the singular: Return, O so-and-so, to so-and-so his right. If it is dual, it is said: Return his right to him, and it is not said: Ardadu. Likewise for the plural: Raddu, and it is not said: Ardadu. The Arabs sometimes base the singular on the dual, and sometimes doubling appears in the singular due to the sukoon of the verb’s lam.
Both languages are eloquent and well-known among the Arabs.

The reading of this according to us is as it is in our copies of the Qur’an and the copies of the people of the East, with one doubled dal, without showing the doubling, and with the opening of the dal, for the reason that was described.
God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Humble toward the believers
, that they are slaves to them and merciful to them. From the saying of the speaker: So-and-so was humbled by so-and-so, if he submitted to him and became submissive. And what he means by his saying:
h
Mighty against the disbelievers is harsh towards them

, rough with them. From the saying: So-and-so has shown me dignity, if he showed him dignity and showed him harshness and rudeness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Humble toward the believers
, people who are gentle toward the people of their religion, stern toward the disbelievers, people who are harsh toward those who differ with them in their religion.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Humble toward the believers
, mighty against the disbelievers, meaning by humble: the merciful.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Humble toward the believers
, he said: Merciful among themselves, Mighty against the disbelievers, he said: Severe with them.

c: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan said:
m: I heard Al-A’mash say about His statement:
h
Humble toward the believers
, mighty against the disbelievers, weak about the believers.

x: What God Almighty means by His statement,
h
They strive in the cause of God

, are these believers whom God promised the believers that He would bring to them in their place if any of them apostatized. They strive in fighting the enemies of God in the manner that God commanded them to be fought, and in the manner that He permitted them to do, and they strive against their enemy. That is their striving in the cause of God. And they do not fear the blame of a blamer, meaning: They do not fear anyone for the sake of God, and they are not prevented from doing what God commanded them to do in fighting their enemy by the blame of a blamer for that. As for his saying: That is the bounty of God, it means this description with which He, the Most High, described them, that they are humble towards the believers, powerful towards the disbelievers, striving in the way of God and not fearing the blame of any blamer in God’s cause.

It is the bounty of God that He bestowed upon them, and God gives His bounty to whomever He wills from among His creation, as a favor to him and out of generosity. And God is Bountiful, meaning: God is generous with His bounty to whomever He bestows it upon. He does not fear that His treasures will run out and his giving will be lost. Knowing, of the place of His generosity and giving, so He does not give it except to those who deserve it, and He does not give to those who deserve it except according to the benefit, because He knows where it is good for them and where it is harmful to them.

evidence.text: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, he said: I heard Ayyad narrating on the authority of Abu Musa: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him, he said: He meant the people of Abu Musa.
Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: O you who have believed, whoever among you should revert from his religion.
So I read it as the people of Medina read: O you who have believed, whoever among you should revert from his religion, showing the doubling, with two dals, the last dal being in the jussive mood.

As for the reading of the people of Iraq, they read it as: Whoever among you turns away from his religion, with assimilation, with one dal, and moving it to the fatha, based on the dual, because the jussive that appears to be doubled in the singular, if dualized, is assimilated.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading of this according to us is as it is in our copies of the Qur’an and the copies of the people of the East, with one doubled dal, without showing the doubling, and with the opening of the dal, for the reason that was described.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
Your protector is only God and His Messenger and those who believe that you

, O believers, have no protector except God and His Messenger, and the believers are those whose description is as God Almighty mentioned. As for the Jews and Christians, whom God has commanded you to disavow their protectorship and has forbidden you to take them as protectors, they are not your protectors or supporters, rather some of them are protectors of others, so do not take from them any protector or supporter. It was said that this verse was revealed about Ubadah bin al-Samit, in his disavowal of the authority of the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa and their alliance, to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers.
Who said that?

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, my father Ishaq bin Yasar told me, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said:
m: When Banu Qaynuqa’ fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Ubadah bin Al-Samit went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - and he was one of Banu Awf bin Al-Khazraj - and he renounced their alliance with the Messenger of God, and he expressed his displeasure to God and His Messenger from their alliance, and he said: I take God, His Messenger, and the believers as allies, and I disavow the alliance of the infidels and their allies! So the following verse was revealed about him: Your ally is only God and His Messenger
h
and those who believe
- those who establish prayer and give zakah, while they bow in prayer - because of Ubadah’s saying: I take God, His Messenger,
h
and those who believe
as allies, and he disavowed Banu Qaynuqa’ and their allies - until His saying: For the party of God - they will be the victorious.
b.via: Ubadah bin Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard my father, on the authority of Atiyah ibn Saʿd, he said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then he mentioned something similar to it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Your guardian is only God and His Messenger and those who believe
, meaning: whoever submits to Islam, God and His Messenger are his guardians. As for his saying:
h
And those who believe
, who establish prayer and give zakat, while they bow, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning.

x: Some of them said: He meant Ali bin Abi Talib.
Some of them said: He meant all believers.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Then he informed them
m: of who would be his guardian, saying:
h
Your guardian is only God and His Messenger and those who believe
, who establish prayer and give zakat, while they bow in prayer. These are all the believers, but Ali bin Abi Talib was passed by a beggar while he was bowing in the mosque, so he gave him his ring.

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, he said:
m: I asked him about this verse: Your ally is only God and His Messenger
h
and those who believe

, who establish prayer and give zakat, while they bow in prayer. I said: Who are those who believe? He said: Those who believe! We said: We have been informed that it was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib! He said: Ali is among those who believe.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Malik, he said:
m: I asked Abu Jaafar about the statement of God:
h
Your guardian is only God and His Messenger
, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Hannad, on the authority of Abdah.

c: Ismail bin Israel Al-Ramli told us, he said, Ayoub bin Suwaid told us, he said, Utbah bin Abi Hakim told us
m: regarding this verse: Your guardian is only God and Surat al-Ma’idah 5:55 Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger
h
and those who believe
, who establish prayer and give zakah, and they bow in prayer. His Messenger
h
and those who believe
, he said: Ali bin Abi Talib.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ghalib bin Ubaid God told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say about His statement:
h
Your guardian is only God and His Messenger
, the verse, he said: It was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, he gave charity while he was bowing.

x: This is an announcement from God Almighty to all of His servants - those who disavowed the alliance of the Jews and removed them out of satisfaction with the guardianship of God, His Messenger, and the believers, and those who held fast to their alliance and feared the circles of evil would turn on them, so they hastened to befriend them - that whoever trusts in God and befriends God, His Messenger, and the believers, and whoever is like him from the allies of God from the believers, they will have the victory, the circles, and the state over whoever opposes them and opposes them, because they are the party of God, and the party of God is the victorious, not the party of Satan, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: He informed them - meaning the Lord, may He be exalted - of the victorious one, and said: Do not fear the state or the cycle, and He said: And whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who have believed as allies - then indeed, the party of God - they are the victorious, and the party is the supporters. What he means by his saying:
h
Then the party of God is the supporters of God

, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: How can I shine while Bilal is my party member? What he meant by his saying: Adwaa, is to become weak and oppressed, from the weak thing. And what he meant by his saying: And Bilal is a partisan, means: a supporter.

x: God Almighty says to those who believe in Him and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who believe, meaning: those who believe in God and His Messenger, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, meaning the Jews and Christians to whom came the messengers and prophets, and to whom the Scriptures were sent before the mission of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and before the revelation of our Scripture, O you who believe, do not take them as supporters, brothers, or allies, for they will spare no effort to ruin you, because they show you affection and friendship. The actions of these Jews, about whom God told the believers that they took their religion as a mockery and a game with religion, as our Lord, the Most High, described them, was that one of them would show faith to the believers while he was still in disbelief, then he would revert to disbelief after a short period of time by showing that with his tongue in words, after he had shown faith with his tongue in words while he was concealing disbelief in playing with religion and mocking it, as God, the Most High, informed us about the actions of some of them in His saying: “
h
And when they meet those who believe
, they say, ‘We believe,’ but when they are alone with their evil ones, they say, ‘Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking.’
God mocks at them and prolongs them in their transgression while they wander blindly.” (al-Baqarah 2:14-15) In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report came from Ibn Abbas.

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, he said:
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit narrated to me, he said: Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Rafa’ah bin Zaid bin Al-Tabut and Suwaid bin Al-Harith had outwardly declared Islam, then they became hypocrites, and there were some men among the Muslims who were friendly to them, so God revealed about them: O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers until His saying: And God knows best what they were concealing. This report has demonstrated the truth of what we have said, that the taking of those who took the religion of God as a mockery and a game from the People of the Book whom God mentioned in this verse, was only due to their hypocrisy, and their showing faith to the believers while they were inwardly disbelief, and their saying to their Jewish devils when they were alone with them: We are with you. So God forbade friendship with them and their closeness to their alliance, and considering them as allies, and He informed them that they spare no effort in corrupting them, and in attacking their religion, and in humiliating it. As for the infidels whom God Almighty mentioned in His saying:
h
Of those who were given the Scripture before you and the infidels as allies

, they are the polytheists who worship idols. God forbade the believers from taking the People of the Scripture, the idol worshippers, and all the other infidels as allies, apart from the believers. Ibn Masoud was among those who said:

c: Ahmad Bani Yusuf told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Ibn Masoud,
m: he reads: Of those who were given the Scripture before you and of those who associated others with God. This is a statement of the correctness of the interpretation we have made in this regard. There are different readings of this.

x: A group of people from Hijaz, Basra and Kufa read it: And the disbelievers are allies, with the word the Surat al-Ma’idah 5:57 O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers. And fear Allah, if you are believers. disbelievers in the accusative case, meaning: O you who believe, do not take as allies those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and from among the disbelievers. Likewise, in the reading of Abi bin Kaab, as we have been informed: Of those who were given the Scripture before you and of the disbelievers are allies. The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: And the disbelievers are allies, in the accusative case, meaning: O you who believe, do not take those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement.
And the disbelievers, in apposition with (the disbelievers) to those who take.

The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings that agree on the meaning and are correct in their articulation. Scholars of the Qur’anic recitations have recited each one of them, so whichever one the reciter recites, he has done it right. Because the prohibition of taking a guardian from among the disbelievers is a prohibition of taking all of them as guardians. And the prohibition of taking all of them as guardians is a prohibition of taking some of them as guardians. This is because it is not difficult for any of the people of Islam that when God, the Most High, mentioned Himself, forbade the believers from taking a guardian from among the polytheists, He did not permit them to take all of them as guardians, nor when He forbade taking all of them as guardians, He did not specify the permissibility of taking some of them as guardians. So, in order to be difficult for them, it is necessary to seek evidence for the first of the two readings in this regard that is correct.
Since this is the case, whether the reciter recites in the accusative or in the genitive, for the reason we mentioned. As for his saying:
h
And fear God
, if you are believers, it means:
h
And fear God

, O believers, regarding those who have taken your religion as a mockery and a game from among those who were given the Scripture and from the disbelievers, lest you take them as allies and supporters, and fear His punishment for doing that if you do it after He has preceded you with the prohibition of it, if you believe in God and believe in His threat for disobeying Him.

evidence.text: A group of people from Hijaz, Basra and Kufa read it: And the disbelievers are allies, with the word the Surat al-Ma’idah 5:57 O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers.
Likewise, in the reading of Abi bin Kaab, as we have been informed: Of those who were given the Scripture before you and of the disbelievers are allies.

The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: And the disbelievers are allies, in the accusative case, meaning: O you who believe, do not take those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings that agree on the meaning and are correct in their articulation.
So, in order to be difficult for them, it is necessary to seek evidence for the first of the two readings in this regard that is correct.

x: God Almighty says: And when your muezzin calls to prayer, O believers, these infidels from among the Jews, Christians, and polytheists mock your call to it, and they play with that, that is because they are a people who do not reason. God Almighty means by His saying: that, the action that they do, which is their mockery and play with the call to prayer, and they only do it out of their ignorance of their Lord, and that they do not understand what is for them in their response if they respond to prayer, and what is against them in their mockery and play with the call to it, and if they had understood what punishment there is for whoever does that from them from God, they would not have done it.
Al-Suddi mentioned in his interpretation what:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And when you call to prayer, they treat it as mockery and amusement. There was a Christian man in Medina who, when he heard the caller calling: I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, would say: Burn the liar! One night his servant girl entered with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark fell and burned the house, and he and his family were burned.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians: O People of the Book, do you hate us or find fault with us in anything that you mock our religion? Why do you take our call as a mockery and a game when we call you to prayer? Except that we believe in God, meaning: Except that we believe and acknowledge God and declare Him One, and in what was revealed to us from God of the Book, and what was revealed to God’s prophets of the Books before our Book, and that most of you are wicked, meaning: Except that most of you are disobedient to God’s command, disobeying Him, and lying about Him. The Arabs say: I found and I hated you, and this is how the reciters of the Hijaz, Iraq and others read it. And I found and I hated, two languages - and we do not know of a reciter who read them - meaning: I found and I hated, and from this is the saying of Abdullah bin Qais al-Ruqayyat: They did not resent the Umayyads except that they were patient when they got angry.
It was mentioned that this verse was revealed because of a group of Jews.

Who said that? Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit narrated, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them Abu Yasir bin Akhtab, Rafi' bin Abi Rafi', Azar, Zaid, Khalid, Azar bin Abi Azar, and Ashya'. They asked him who among the messengers he believed in. He said: I believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him. When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: We do not believe in those who believe in him!

So God revealed about them: Say, 'O People of the Scripture! Do you blame us for anything except that we believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before? And because most of you are wicked.' In conjunction with that in His statement: except that we believe in God, because the meaning of the statement is: Do you blame us for anything other than our belief in God and your immorality?

evidence.text: The Arabs say: I found and I hated you, and this is how the reciters of the Hijaz, Iraq and others read it.

And I found and I hated, two languages - and we do not know of a reciter who read them - meaning: I found and I hated, and from this is the saying of Abdullah bin Qais al-Ruqayyat: They did not resent the Umayyads except that they were patient when they got angry.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who have taken your religion as a mockery and a game from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers, Shall I inform you, O group of People of the Scripture, of good report about the reward for what you blame us for, for our belief in God and what was revealed to us of God’s Book, and what was revealed before us of His Books?

i: And "Mathuba" is estimated as Maf'ula, but when the 'ayn of the verb was dropped, its vowel was transferred to Fa, which is Thaa from Mathuba, so it came out in the form of Maqūlah, Mahwārah, and Madhūfah, as the poet said:
x: And if my neighbor invited me to a guest house, I would roll up my sleeves until the one who was tired half-tucked my apron.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “Say:
h
Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a reward from God
?” He says: A reward from God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a reward from God

? He said: The reward is the reward, the reward of good, and the reward of evil, and he read better in reward (al-Kahf 18:44). As for min in his statement: whom God has cursed, it is in the accusative case, in response to his statement: more evil than that. So the interpretation of the statement, since that was the case, was: Say, Shall I inform you of someone who is worse than that in reward from God, whom God has cursed? If it was said: It is in the nominative case, it would be correct, as a resumption, meaning: That is the one whom God cursed, or: He is the one whom God cursed. If it was said: It is in the accusative case, it would not be invalid, meaning: Say, shall I inform you of the one whom God has cursed? So I inform you would be made the agent of whoever and would be applied to it. As for the meaning of his saying: He whom God has cursed, it means: He whom God has distanced and crushed from His mercy, and became angry with him and made of them apes and pigs, meaning: He became angry with him and made of them the transformed apes and pigs, out of His anger and wrath upon them, so He hastened for them disgrace and punishment in this world. As for the reason why God transformed some of them into monkeys, we have mentioned some of it in the past in this book of ours, and we will mention the rest of it, God willing, in a place other than this. As for the reason why God transformed some of them into pigs, it was due to: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, the freed slave of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: I was told that the transformation of the Children of Israel into pigs occurred when a woman from the Children of Israel was in a village of the Children of Israel, and the king of the Children of Israel was there. They had gathered together to destroy them, except that woman had a remnant of Islam that she held fast to. She began to call to God, until when people gathered around her and followed her in her matter, she said to them: You must strive for the religion of God and call your people to that, so go out, for I am going out. So she went out, and that king went out to her among the people, and he killed all of her companions, and she escaped from them. He said: She called to God until the people gathered around her, and when she was satisfied with them, she ordered them to go out, so they went out and she went out with them, and they were all killed, and she escaped from them. Then she called to God, and when men gathered around her and responded to her, she ordered them to go out. They went out and she went out, and they were all killed, and she escaped from among them. She returned, and she had despaired, and she said: Glory be to God, if this religion had a protector and a supporter, it would have prevailed after that! He said: So she spent the night sad, and the people of the village began to walk in its outskirts like pigs, whom God had transformed that night. So when she woke up and saw what she had seen, she said: Today I know that God has honored His religion and commanded His religion! He said: Alas, the transformation of the pigs among the Children of Israel was at the hands of that woman.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He made from them apes and pigs
, he said: They were transformed from Jews.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. The reason for the transformation is other than what we mentioned. We will mention it in its place, God willing.

x: There are different readings of this. So the people of Hijaz, Syria, Basra, and some of the Kufians read it as: And he worshipped the tyrant, meaning: And he made from them monkeys and pigs. And from the tyrant, meaning: worshipper, so he made worshipped a past tense verb from the connection of the implied word, and he put the tyrant in the accusative case, with worshipped falling upon it.

A group of Kufians read it as: And the servant of the tyrant with the opening of the ayn of abd and the closing of its ba, and the lowering of the tyrant by adding abd to it. They meant by that: and the servants of the tyrant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me that, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said, Hamza told me, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab,
m: that he read: And worshipped the Taghut, meaning: served. Abd al-Rahman said: And Hamza used to read it like that.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told me, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash:
m: that he used to read it like this. Al-Farra’ used to say: If there is a dialect in it like Hadhar and Wa Hadhar, and Ujal and Wajal, then it is correct, and God knows best. Otherwise, if he meant the saying of the poet: My son, your mother is a slave and your father is a slave This is a necessity of poetry, and this is permissible in poetry due to the necessity of rhymes, but not in reading.

x: Others read it as: And Abd al-Zaghut. This was mentioned by al-A’mash. It is as if the one who read it in this way wanted to collect the plural of the slave, as if he collected the slave as slaves, then collected the slaves as slave, like: fruits and fruit. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Jaafar al-Qari’ that he used to recite it: And the slave of the tyrant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us:
m: Abu Jaʿfar al-Nahwi used to read it: And the slave of the tyrant, as you would say: Abdullah struck.

x: This reading has no meaning, because God Almighty began the report by denouncing some people, and among the things He denounced them for was their worship of the tyrant. As for the report that the tyrant was worshipped, it is not of the same type as the report with which He began the verse, nor of the same type as what He concluded it with, so it has a face that can be directed towards its correctness. It was mentioned that Buraidah Al-Aslami used to recite it: And the worshipper of the tyrant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me that, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, a Basran sheikh told us:
m: that Buraidah used to recite it like that. If it had been read: And the slave of the tyrant, with the kasra, it would have a correct way of saying it in Arabic, even though I do not allow it to be read today, since the reading of the argument is from the reading that is different from it. The reason for its permissibility in Arabic is that what is meant by it is and the slaves of the tyrant, then the ha was deleted for the addition, as the rajaz poet said: He stood up and made her cry He wants: Her guardians stood up, so he deleted the ta from her guardians for the addition.

x: As for the reading of the Qur’an, it is according to one of the two aspects that I began by mentioning, which is: And the slave of the tyrant, with the accusative of the tyrant and the application of slave to it, and the direction of slave to it being a past tense verb from worship. The other: and the slave of the tyrant, on the example of faʿala, and the tyrant was lowered by adding slave to it. If the reading of the recitation is by one of these two faces and not by the other faces that are more correct in Arabic than them, then the first of them in terms of correctness of the reading is the reading of the one who read that and worshipped the taghut, meaning: and made from them monkeys and pigs and those who worshipped the taghut, because he mentioned that in the reading of Abi bin Ka’b and Ibn Mas’ud: and made from them monkeys and pigs and worshipped the taghut, meaning: and those who worshipped the taghut, then in that is clear evidence of the correctness of the meaning that we mentioned that what is meant by it is: and those who worshipped the taghut, and that the accusative with taghut is more appropriate, Surat al-Ma’idah 5:60 Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from God?

Those whom God has cursed and with whom He became angry and made from among them apes and pigs and who worshipped false gods. Those are worse in position and further astray from the soundness of the way." according to what I described in the reading, for the application of abd in it, since the other face was not widespread among the Arabs nor known in their speech. However, the Arabists find it objectionable to use something in the implied min and alladhi with min and fi if min or fi suffice from them, and they find it ugly, to the extent that some of them would reject it and not allow it. The one who rejects it would read it: and the servant of the tyrant, so according to him it is an error and an impermissible mistake.

Others of them considered it permissible, despite its ugliness. According to their statement, reading it in this way should be ugly. Despite their finding it ugly in speech, they chose to read it in this way, and to apply ja’ala to min, which is omitted with min. If we were to permit going against the group in something that they agreed upon, we would choose to read with something other than these two readings. However, what the Muslims came with is widespread among them and they do not deny it, so we do not permit deviating from it to something else. Therefore, we did not permit reading other than one of the two readings that we mentioned that they did not go beyond them. Since our reading is as we mentioned, the interpretation of the verse is: Say, Shall I inform you of those who are worse than that in reward from God? Those whom God has cursed and with whom He became angry, and made of them apes and pigs, and those who worship the tyrant.
We have explained the meaning of taghut previously with evidence from narrations and other things, so there is no need to repeat it here. As for his saying:
h
Those are the worst in position and further astray from the right path

, he means by his saying: those, those whom God Almighty mentioned, and they are those whose characteristics He described when He said: Those whom God has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and worshipped false gods, and all of that is from the characteristics of the Jews from the Children of Israel. God Almighty says: These people who are described like this, are worse in position in this world and the Hereafter with God than those you, O Jews, have resented for their belief in God and in what was revealed to them from God of the Book, and in what was revealed to the prophets before them, and are more astray from the straight path.
God Almighty says: And you, O Jews, are even more stubborn in following other than the straight path, and more astray from the path of guidance and the right path than they are.

This is from the grammatical errors in speech. That is because God, the Most High, intended with this report to inform the Jews, whose characteristics He described in the verses before this, of their ugly actions and reprehensible morals, and their incurring His wrath through their many sins and transgressions, to the point that He transformed some of them into monkeys and some into pigs, addressing them with that, alluding to the beautiful speech, and grammatically speaking to them what they knew the meaning of in speech with the best grammatical errors, and teaching His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the best of manners, so He said to him: Say to them, O Muhammad, are these believers in God and His Books whom you mock, worse, or those whom God has cursed? And He means the one to whom that was said.

evidence.text: So the people of Hijaz, Syria, Basra, and some of the Kufians read it as: And he worshipped the tyrant, meaning: And he made from them monkeys and pigs.
A group of Kufians read it as: And the servant of the tyrant with the opening of the ayn of abd and the closing of its ba, and the lowering of the tyrant by adding abd to it.
Abd al-Rahman said: And Hamza used to read it like that.
Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told me, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash: that he used to read it like this.
Others read it as: And Abd al-Zaghut.
It is as if the one who read it in this way wanted to collect the plural of the slave, as if he collected the slave as slaves, then collected the slaves as slave, like: fruits and fruit.
It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Jaafar al-Qari’ that he used to recite it: And the slave of the tyrant.
Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us: Abu Jaʿfar al-Nahwi used to read it: And the slave of the tyrant, as you would say: Abdullah struck.
Abu Jaʿfar said: This reading has no meaning, because God Almighty began the report by denouncing some people, and among the things He denounced them for was their worship of the tyrant.
It was mentioned that Buraidah Al-Aslami used to recite it: And the worshipper of the tyrant.
Al-Muthanna told me that, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, a Basran sheikh told us: that Buraidah used to recite it like that.

If it had been read: And the slave of the tyrant, with the kasra, it would have a correct way of saying it in Arabic, even though I do not allow it to be read today, since the reading of the argument is from the reading that is different from it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: As for the reading of the Qur’an, it is according to one of the two aspects that I began by mentioning, which is: And the slave of the tyrant, with the accusative of the tyrant and the application of slave to it, and the direction of slave to it being a past tense verb from worship.
