If the reading of the recitation is by one of these two faces and not by the other faces that are more correct in Arabic than them, then the first of them in terms of correctness of the reading is the reading of the one who read that and worshipped the taghut, meaning: and made from them monkeys and pigs and those who worshipped the taghut, because he mentioned that in the reading of Abi bin Ka’b and Ibn Mas’ud: and made from them monkeys and pigs and worshipped the taghut, meaning: and those who worshipped the taghut, then in that is clear evidence of the correctness of the meaning that we mentioned that what is meant by it is: and those who worshipped the taghut, and that the accusative with taghut is more appropriate, Surat al-Ma’idah 5:60 Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from God?

Those are worse in position and further astray from the soundness of the way." according to what I described in the reading, for the application of abd in it, since the other face was not widespread among the Arabs nor known in their speech.
The one who rejects it would read it: and the servant of the tyrant, so according to him it is an error and an impermissible mistake.
Despite their finding it ugly in speech, they chose to read it in this way, and to apply ja’ala to min, which is omitted with min.
If we were to permit going against the group in something that they agreed upon, we would choose to read with something other than these two readings.
Therefore, we did not permit reading other than one of the two readings that we mentioned that they did not go beyond them.
Since our reading is as we mentioned, the interpretation of the verse is: Say, Shall I inform you of those who are worse than that in reward from God?

x: God Almighty says: And when these hypocrites from among the Jews come to you, O believers, they say to you: We believe, meaning we believe in what your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought and we follow him in his religion, while they persist in their disbelief and misguidance. They have entered upon you with their disbelief that they believe in their hearts and conceal in their chests, and they falsely show belief in you with their tongues. And they have gone out with it, meaning: They have gone out with disbelief from you just as they entered upon you with it. They did not return with their coming to you from their disbelief and misguidance. They think that this is from their actions and is hidden from God, out of their ignorance of God. And God knows best what they were concealing, meaning: God knows best what they were concealing from you when they said to you with their tongues: We believe in God and Muhammad and we believe in what he brought - what they concealed from themselves of disbelief.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when they come to you

, they say, ‘We believe,’ the verse, some of the Jews used to enter upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tell him that they were believers and satisfied with what he had brought, while they were clinging to their misguidance and disbelief. And they would enter with that and leave with that from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And when they come to you

, they say, ‘We believe,’ but they entered in disbelief and they left in it, he said: These are people from the hypocrites who were Jews. He says: They entered as disbelievers and left as disbelievers.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when they come to you

, they say, ‘We believe,’ while they entered in disbelief and they have already left with it, and that they entered while speaking the truth, and disbelief was in their hearts, so he said: They entered in disbelief and they have already left with it.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when they come to you

, they say, ‘We believe,’ while they entered in disbelief and they have already exited in it, “And a party from the People of the Scripture say, ‘Believe in that which was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end that perhaps they will return.’”
r
(Al Imran 3:72)
. So when they return to their disbelievers from the People of the Scripture and their devils, they return with their disbelief. And these are the People of the Scripture from the Jews.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer:
m: And they entered with disbelief and they left with it, meaning: it is from them.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And you will see, O Muhammad, many, of these Jews whose story I told you about from the Children of Israel, hastening into sin and aggression, meaning: they hasten to commit sin. It was said: Sin in this context means disbelief.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you will see many of them hastening into sin and aggression
, he said: Sin means disbelief.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you will see many of them hastening into sin and aggression
, and this was regarding the Jewish rulers before you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
They hasten into sin and aggression
, he said: These are the Jews.
h
Evil is that which they do
, “Why do the rabbis not forbid them,” until His statement,
h
Evil is that which they do
, he said: They do and they do are one. He said to these when they did not forbid, just as He said to these when they did. He said: And that is the anointing.

x: This statement that we have mentioned from al-Suddi, even if it is a statement that is not refuted as being valid, what is more appropriate for the interpretation of the statement is that the people are described as rushing into all the sins of God, not avoiding any of them, neither disbelief nor anything else. Because God, the Most High, mentioned Himself, was general in describing them with what He described them with, that
h
they hasten into sin and aggression

, without specifying one sin over another. As for aggression, it is exceeding the limit that God has set for them in everything that He has set for them. The interpretation of this is that these Jews, whom God Almighty described in these verses as He described them, many of them hasten to disobey God and disobey His command, and they transgress the limits He has set for them in what He has permitted and forbidden them, in their consumption of unlawful gain, which is the bribe they take from people to rule against God’s ruling regarding them.
God Almighty says: How evil is what they were doing. He says: I swear that what these Jews were doing was evil, in their haste in sin and aggression, and their consumption of ill-gotten gains.

God Almighty says: Why do not these Jews from the Children of Israel, who hasten to sin and aggression and take bribes in judgment, their rabbis - who are their believing imams and their learned politicians with their politics - and their rabbis - who are their scholars and leaders, stop their sinful speech meaning: from saying lies and falsehood, because they used to rule among them by other than the judgment of God, and they used to write books with their own hands and then say: This is from the judgment of God, and this is from His books. God says: So woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn (al-Baqarah 2:79). As for his saying: And their consumption of ill-gotten gains, he means by that the bribe that they took for their rulings other than the Book of God for those for whom they ruled according to it. We have explained the meaning of rabbis and rabbis and the meaning of illicit gain with evidence of that in the past, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

How evil is what they were doing. This is an oath from God, by which He swore. God Almighty says: I swear: How evil is what these rabbis and scholars were doing, in their failure to forbid those among them who were hastening to sin, transgression, and consuming ill-gotten gains, from what they were doing of that.
The scholars used to say: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is more severe in rebuking scholars than this verse, nor is it more frightening for them than it.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abdullah bin Dawud told us, he said, Salamah bin Nabit told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from their sinful speech
? He said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that I fear more than: We are not forbidden.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Atiyah told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Khalid bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is more severe in rebuke than this verse:
h
Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful
? Evil is that which they have been doing. He said: This is how he recited it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Why do not the rabbis and scholars forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful? He said: The rabbis and scholars, their jurists, reciters, and scholars. He said: Then Ad-Dahhak says: How frightening this verse is to me.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful
? Evil is that which they do, meaning: the rabbis, that they: Evil is that which they do.

evidence.text: He said: This is how he recited it.
He said: The rabbis and scholars, their jurists, reciters, and scholars.

x: This is report from God Almighty about the audacity of the Jews towards their Lord, and their description of Him with what is not His description, as a rebuke to them for that, and as a declaration from Him to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their ancient ignorance and deception of Him, and their denial of all His good deeds towards them, and His frequent pardon of them and His forgiveness of their great crimes, and as an argument for His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he is a prophet sent and a messenger sent:

c: that this report that he informed them
m: of was from the hidden and hidden knowledge of their knowledge that no one knew except their rabbis and scholars, not to mention the illiterate nation of the Arabs who did not read a book, nor did they comprehend any knowledge of the People of the Book, so God informed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, to establish his truthfulness among them, and thus cut off their argument. God Almighty says:
h
And the Jews said
, from the Children of Israel,
h
The hand of God is chained

, meaning that God’s goodness is withheld and His giving is restricted from being extended to them, as God Almighty said in disciplining His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor extend it completely (al-Isra’ 17:29). The Almighty described the hand with this meaning, and the meaning is giving, because people’s giving and offering of their good deeds is mostly done by their hands. So people used to describe each other, if they described someone as generous and kind, or stingy, miserly and narrow, by adding whatever of that was from the description of the described to his hands, as Al-A’sha said in praising a man: Your hands are the hands of glory, a useful hand and a hand that spends if it is stingy with provisions So he added what was the description of the owner of the hand of spending and benefit to the hand. And there is more like that in the speech of the Arabs in their poetry and proverbs than can be counted. So God addressed them with what they know and discuss among themselves in their speech, saying:
h
And the Jews say
h
The hand of God is chained

.’ Meaning by that: They said: God is stingy with us, and prevents us from His bounty, so He does not give, like the one whose hand is chained, who is not able to extend it with giving or offering good. God is exalted above what they said, the enemies of God! Then God, the One who denied them and informed them of His wrath against them, said: Their hands are chained, meaning: their hands are held back from doing good deeds and are restrained from giving gifts, and they are cursed for what they said, and they were distanced from God’s mercy and grace because of what they said of disbelief, and they fabricated lies and falsehoods against God, Rather, His hands are extended, meaning: Rather, His hands are extended with giving and bestowing and the provisions of His servants and the sustenance of His creation, neither chained nor restrained,
h
He spends as He wills
, meaning: He gives to this one and withholds from that one, so He is stingy with him. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the Jews say
h
The hand of God is chained
.’ Chained are their hands, Surat al-Ma’idah 5:64
h
And the Jews say
, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they said. Rather, His hands are extended;
h
He spends as He wills

. And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast between them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindle a fire, For war Allah has extinguished it, and they strive to cause corruption in the land, and Allah does not like corrupters. and cursed are they for what they say. He said: They do not mean by that that
h
the hand of God is chained
, but rather they say: He is miserly and withholds what He has. God is far above what they say, far above.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
The hand of God is chained
, they said: God has exhausted us - meaning: God has exhausted us - O Children of Israel, until God put his hand to his throat! And they lied!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The hand of God is chained
, he said: The Jews say it: God has exhausted us, O Children of Israel and O People of the Book, until His hand is to His throat, Rather, His hands are extended,
h
He spends as He wills

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And the Jews say
h
The hand of God is chained
.’ Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they said to And God does not like corrupters. As for his statement:
h
The hand of God is chained
, they said: God is stingy and not generous! God said: Rather, His hands are extended;
h
He spends as He wills

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And the Jews said
h
The hand of God is chained

.’ Chained are their hands and cursed for what they said. Rather, His hands are extended, spending as He wills.” They said: God has placed His hand on His chest, and He will not extend it until He returns our kingdom to us. As for his saying:
h
He spends as He wills
, he says: He provides as He wills.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ikrimah said:
m: h
And the Jews said
h
The hand of God is chained
.’ The verse was revealed about Phinehas the Jew.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Abu Tamila narrated to us, on the authority of Ubaid bin Sulayman, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The hand of God is chained

, they say: He is stingy and not generous! God said: Their hands are chained, their hands are held back from spending and doing good. Then He said, meaning Himself: Rather, His hands are extended, spending as He wills. And He said: And do not make your hand chained to your neck (al-Isra’ 17:29), meaning: Do not hold your hand back from spending.

x: The people of debate differed in the interpretation of his statement: Rather, His hands are extended.

Some of them said: What he meant by that is His two blessings. He said: That means: The hand of God is upon His creation, and that is His blessings upon them. He said: The Arabs say: You have a hand with me, meaning by that: a blessing.
Others of them said: He meant strength by that. They said: This is similar to the words of God Almighty: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, possessors of strength
r
Others of them said: Rather, His hand means His kingdom. He said: The meaning of His statement,
h
And the Jews said
h
The hand of God is chained

’ is His kingdom and His treasuries. They said: This is like what the Arabs say about kings: He is the property of his right hand, and So-and-so has the marriage contract of so-and-so in his hand, meaning he owns that, and like the saying of God Almighty: Then present before your private conversation a charity (Al-Mujadilah: 12).

Others among them said: Rather, the hand of God is an attribute of His attributes. It is a hand, but it is not a limb like the limbs of the sons of Adam. They said: That is because God Almighty mentioned that He singled Adam out with what He singled him out with in His creation of him with His hand. They said: If the meaning of the hand was grace, power, or kingship, then there would be no clear explanation for it being specific to Adam, since all of His creation was created by His power, and His will in His creation was a grace, and He is the owner of all of them. They said: Since God Almighty mentioned Adam specifically by mentioning his creation with His hand, and not with any other of His servants, it was known that He only mentioned him specifically for a reason that made him different from all other creation. They said: If that is the case, then the statement of the one who said: The meaning of the hand of God is power, grace, or kingship, in this place is invalidated.
They said: It is more appropriate that if it were as those who claim that the hand of God in His statement,
h
And the Jews say
h
The hand of God is chained

,’ is His blessing, it would have been said: Rather, His hand is extended, and not said: Rather, His hands, because the blessings of God are innumerable in number. And thus came the revelation, God Almighty says: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them (Ibrahim 14:34 - al-Nahl 16:18). They said: Even if there were two blessings, they would have been counted. They said: If someone thinks that the two blessings mean many blessings, then he is mistaken, because the Arabs use the word one to express one’s gender, as in the saying of God Almighty:
“By the declining day. Indeed, man is in loss”
and His saying: Indeed, We created man (al-Hijr 15:26), and His saying:
h
And the disbeliever
is, against his Lord, a supporter (al-Furqan 25:55).
He said: So, in these places, the human being
h
and the disbeliever

did not mean a specific human being, nor a disbeliever who is referred to and present, rather, it meant all of humanity and all of the disbelievers, but the one expressed its gender, as the Arabs say: How many dirhams are in the hands of people. And likewise His saying:
h
And the disbeliever

(al-Furqan 25:55), meaning: And those who disbelieved were. They said: As for if the noun is dual, it does not represent the genus, and it only represents two of them specifically, not all of them and not others. They said: It is a mistake in the speech of the Arabs to say: How many dirhams are in people’s hands, meaning: How many dirhams are in their hands. They said: This is because when the dirham is dual, it only refers to two specific individuals in her speech. They said: It is not impossible: How many dirhams are in people’s hands, and how many dirhams are in their hands, because one pays for all.

They said: In the statement of God Almighty: Rather, His hands are spread out, while informing His servants that His blessings are innumerable, along with what we described as it being unreasonable in the speech of the Arabs that two people would perform for everyone - which indicates the error of the statement of the one who said: The meaning of the hand, in this place, is the blessing - and the correctness of the statement of the one who said: The hand of God is an attribute of Him. They said: And this is what the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has shown, and the scholars and people of interpretation have said this.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: This which We have informed you of from the hidden affairs of these Jews, which none knows except their scholars and rabbis, is an argument against them for the authenticity of your prophethood, and to cut off the excuse of one of them who says: No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us (al-Ma’idah 5:19): And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. What is meant by transgression is the exaggeration in denying what they have known to be true of the prophethood of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and persisting in that, and disbelief. He says: And what increases them, along with their exaggeration in denying that, is their denial of the greatness of God and their description of Him with other than His attribute, by attributing miserliness to Him, and saying:
h
The hand of God is chained

God Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they were people of insolence and rebellion against their Lord, and that they would not submit to the truth even if they knew it was true, but they would oppose it. Thus, He consoled His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his distress at their turning away from God and denying Him. I have explained the meaning of tyranny in the past with evidence, so there is no need to repeat it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. The envy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Arabs led them to disbelieve in him, even though they found it written down in their books.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection
, between the Jews and the Christians, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection
, the Jews and the Christians.

x: How was it said:
h
And We cast among them enmity and hatred
, making the ha’ and the mim in His statement: among them, a metaphor for the Jews and Christians, and not mentioning the Jews and Christians?
They were mentioned, and that is His saying: “
h
Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies
. They are allies of one another” (al-Ma’idah 5:51). The report was reported in some verses about the two groups, and in some about one of them, until it ended with His saying:
h
And We cast among them enmity and hatred
. Then He intended by His saying:
h
We cast among them
, the report about the two groups.

God Almighty says: Whenever their affair is united on something and becomes straight and level, and they want to oppose those who oppose them, God disperses them and corrupts them, due to the evil of their actions and the wickedness of their intentions, like the one who:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding His statement: “
h
You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice

, and you will surely reach great haughtiness. But when the first of the two promises comes to pass, We will send against you servants of Ours of great might, and they will penetrate into the dwellings, and it will be a promise fulfilled. Then We will give you back the upper hand against them” (al-Isra’ 17:4-6), he said: The first corruption occurred, so God sent an enemy against them, and they violated the dwellings, took the women for marriage, enslaved the children, and destroyed the mosque. So they Surat al-Ma’idah 5:64
h
And the Jews say
, "The hand of Allah is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they said. Rather, His hands are extended;
h
He spends as He wills

. And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast between them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindle a fire, For war Allah has extinguished it, and they strive to cause corruption in the land, and Allah does not like corrupters. remained in ruins for a period of time, then God sent a prophet among them, and their situation returned to the best it had been. Then the second corruption occurred when they killed the prophets, until they killed John the son of Zechariah, so God sent against them Bukht Nasr, and he killed those of them whom He killed, took those whom He took captive, and destroyed the mosque. So Bukht Nasr was the second corruption - he said: And corruption is disobedience - then he said, So when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, they will disfigure your faces and enter the temple as they entered it the first time until His saying: And if you return, We will return (al-Isra’ 17:7-8). So God sent to them Ezra, and he had learned the Torah and memorized it in his chest and wrote it down for them. So that generation established it, and they remained and forgot. And Ezra died, and there were events, and they forgot the covenant and were stingy with their Lord, and they said: “
h
The hand of God is chained
. Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they said. Rather, His hands are extended;
h
He spends as He wills

.” And they said about Ezra: God took him as a son, and they used to criticize the Christians for that in what they said about the Messiah, so they disobeyed what they were forbidden to do, and did what they used to disbelieve in, so a word came from God at that time that they would not prevail over an enemy until the end of time, so He said: Every time they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it, and they strive to cause corruption in the land, and God does not love corrupters. So God sent against them the third Magi as lords, and they continued like that with the Magi on their necks, and they said: Oh, if only we had caught up with this prophet whom we find written about with us, so that God may free us through him from the Magi and the humiliating punishment! So he sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace - his name is Muhammad, and his name in the Gospel is Ahmad - and when he came to them and they recognized him, they disbelieved in him. He said: Then the curse of God be upon the disbelievers (al-Baqarah 2:89), and he said: So they incurred wrath upon wrath (al-Baqarah 2:90).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Whenever they kindled a fire for war
, God extinguished it, they are the Jews.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Whenever they kindle the fire of war, God extinguishes it. And they strive to cause corruption in the land.” Those are the enemies of God, the Jews. Whenever they kindle the fire of war, God extinguishes it. You will not find the Jews in a country except that you will find them among the most humiliated of its people. Islam came when it came, and they were in the hands of the Magians, the most hated of its creation to Him.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
Whenever they kindled a fire for war

, God extinguished it, he said: Whenever they agreed on something, God scattered it, extinguished their fire and their fire, and cast terror into their hearts. Mujahid said: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Whenever they kindled a fire for war
, God extinguished it, he said: The war of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: God Almighty says: These Jews and Christians commit acts of disobedience to God, disbelieve in His signs, deny His messengers, and disobey His commands and prohibitions. This is their attempt to cause corruption in it. And God does not love corrupters, meaning: God does not love those who commit acts of disobedience to Him on His earth.

God Almighty says: And if the People of the Scripture had believed in God and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believed in him and followed what was revealed to him, and feared what God forbade them from and avoided, We would have removed from them their misdeeds, meaning: We would have erased their sins and covered them up, and would not have disgraced them because of them, and would have admitted them to gardens of pleasure, meaning: We would have admitted them to gardens in which they would enjoy themselves in the Hereafter. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared God
, meaning: had believed in what God revealed and feared what God has forbidden, We would have removed from them their misdeeds.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel

, and if they had acted according to what is in the Torah and the Gospel, and what was revealed to them from their Lord, meaning: and had acted according to what was revealed to them from their Lord of the Criterion that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them.
How do they establish the Torah, the Gospel, and what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when these books differ and some of them abrogate others?

Even though it is like this in some of its rulings and laws, it is in agreement in the command to believe in the messengers of God, and to believe in what they brought from God. So the meaning of their establishing the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is their belief in what is in them, and working with what they agree upon, and with each one of them at the time when working with it was made obligatory. As for the meaning of his saying:
h
They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet

, it means: God would have sent down rain from the sky upon them, and the earth would have produced for them its grain and plants, and would have brought forth its fruits. As for His statement: and from under their feet, He, the Most High, means: they would have eaten from the blessing of what is under their feet of the earth, and that is what the earth produces of its grain, plants, fruits, and everything else that is eaten from what the earth produces. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel

and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed from above them, meaning: He would have sent down abundant rain upon them, and from beneath their feet, meaning the earth would produce its blessings.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel
and what was revealed to them from their Lord,
h
they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet
, meaning: Then the sky would have given them its blessing, and the earth its vegetation.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel
and what was revealed to them from their Lord,
h
they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet

. He says: If they had acted upon what was revealed to them, which Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them, We would have sent down rain upon them, and the fruit would have grown.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And if they had established the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, as for establishing the Torah, it means acting upon it. As for what was revealed to them from their Lord, it means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was revealed to him. He says:
h
They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet

. As for from above them, it means I sent rain upon them. As for from beneath their feet, it means I would have caused to grow for them from the earth from My provision what would make them independent of means.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet
, he said: The blessings of the sky and the earth. Ibn Jurayj said: They would have eaten from above them, the rain, and from beneath their feet, from the plants of the earth.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: from above them and from beneath their feet, meaning: they would have eaten from the provision that descends from the sky, and from beneath their feet, meaning: from the earth.

x: Some of them said: What is meant by his saying:
h
They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet is an expansion

, just as someone says: He is in better condition from his head to his feet. The interpretation of the people of interpretation is contrary to what we mentioned of this statement, and that is sufficient evidence of its corruption.

What God Almighty meant by His statement: Among them is a community, among them is a group, moderate, meaning moderate in their statement about Jesus, son of Mary, saying that he is the truth, the Messenger of God and His Word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, not exaggerating, saying that he is the son of God, God is exalted above what they say of that, nor falling short, saying that he is not on the right path. And many of them, meaning: of the Children of Israel from the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, evil is what they do, meaning: many of them are evil in their actions, and that is because they disbelieve in God, so the Christians deny Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and claim that the Messiah is the son of God, and the Jews deny Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon them. So God Almighty said about them, blaming them: Evil is what they do, in that of their actions.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Among them is a moderate nation
, and they are the Muslims of the People of the Book, but many of them are evil in what they do.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, he said, Abdullah bin Kathir told us:
m: He heard Mujahid say: The Children of Israel split into groups, and one group said: Jesus is the son of God, and another group said: He is God, and another group said: He is the servant of God and His spirit, and they are the moderate ones, and they are the Muslims of the People of the Book.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God said:
h
Among them is a moderate nation
, meaning: on His Book and His command. Then He condemned most of the people, saying: But many of them - evil is what they do.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Among them is a moderate nation
, he said: a believing nation.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Among them is a moderate nation
, but many of them - evil is what they do, he said: The moderate ones are the people of obedience to God. He said: And these are the People of the Book.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Among them is a moderate nation

, but many of them are evil in what they do, he said: This is the moderate nation, those who are neither harsh in religion nor extreme. He said: Extremism is aversion to it, and immorality is falling short of it.

x: This is an order from God, the Most High, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform these Jews and Christians from the People of the Book, whose stories He, the Most High, has related in this Surah, and in which He has mentioned their faults and the evil of their religions, their audacity towards their Lord, their attack on their prophets, their alteration of His Book, their distortion of it, the poor quality of their food and their eating, and all the polytheists besides them, of what was revealed to him regarding them of their faults, their disparagement of them, their shortcomings, their slander of them, and what He has commanded them to do and forbidden them from doing, and that he should not feel himself wary of them afflicting him with something bad in himself as he has done with them by the command of God, nor out of fear of their large number and the small number of those with him, and that he should not fear anyone for the sake of God, for God, the Most High, is sufficient for him from every one of His creation, and He has warded off from him the harm of everyone who seeks to harm him.

c: And God Almighty informed him that
m: if he fell short of conveying something that was revealed to them, then in his failure to convey it - even if it was little and not exaggerated - he is in the same position as if he had not conveyed anything of what was revealed to him. And what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message,” meaning: If you conceal a verse of what has been revealed to you from your Lord, you have not conveyed My messages.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, the verse. God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would suffice him from the people and protect him from them, and He commanded him to convey the message. It was mentioned to us that “it was said to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why don’t you veil yourself! He said: By God, I will reveal my end to the people as long as I keep company with them.”

c: Al-Harith bin Muhammad told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: When the verse, Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, was revealed, he said: I am only one, what should I do? People will gather around me! Then the verse, And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, was revealed.

c: Hanad and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Tha’laba, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: When the verse was revealed: “O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people,” the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not guard me, for my Lord has protected me.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was being followed by some of his companions. When the verse, ‘And God will protect you from the people,’ was revealed, he went out and said: O people, go back to where you are going, for God has protected me from the people.”

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Asim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was being guarded by his companions, so God Almighty revealed: ‘O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message,’” to the end of it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Al-Harith bin Ubaid Abu Qudamah Al-Ayyadi told us, he said, Saeed Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guarding, until this verse was revealed: ‘And God will protect you from the people.’ She said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stuck his head out of the dome and said: O people, go away, for God has protected me.”

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Qurazi:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to guard until God revealed: ‘And God will protect you from the people.’”

x: The interpreters differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed.
Some of them said: It was revealed because of an Arab who intended to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but God spared him from doing so.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Maʿshar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi and others, he said:
m: “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would stop at a place, his companions would choose a shady tree for him to take a nap under. Then a Bedouin came to him, drew his sword, and said: Who will protect you from me? He said: God! The Bedouin’s hand trembled and the sword fell from him. He said: He hit his head against the tree until his brain was scattered, and God revealed: ‘And God will protect you from the people.’”
b.via: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi and others

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed because he feared the Quraysh, so he felt safe from that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared the Quraysh, but when the verse, ‘And God will protect you from the people,’ was revealed, he lay down and then said: Whoever wants to let me down, let him let me down, two or three times.”

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq, he said,
m: “Aisha said: Whoever Surat al-Ma’idah 5:67 O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people. tells you that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed something from the revelation has lied! Then she recited: ‘O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you,’” the verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said, Aisha said:
m: Whoever says that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed something, has lied and has committed a great slander against God! God Almighty said: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord verse.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, he said, Aisha said:
m: Whoever claims that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed anything from the Book of God, has greatly slandered God! And God says: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Khalid told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Jahm, on the authority of Masruq bin Al-Ajda’, he said:
m: I entered upon Aisha one day and heard her say: What a great lie it is to say that Muhammad concealed something of the revelation! And God says: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. What he means by his saying:
h
And God will protect you from people is that He will prevent you from being harmed by them

. Its origin is from the word asam al-qirbah, which is what is tied with, such as a string or thread. From this comes the poet’s saying: I said: Malik is your guardian, Malik will protect you, if there is a guardian among the people. It means: it prevents you. As for his saying: Indeed, God does not guide the disbelieving people, it means: God does not guide to the right path those who deviate from the path of truth, stray from the straight path, deny what I have brought to them from God, and do not adhere to God’s command and obey Him in what He has imposed upon them and made obligatory.

x: This is an order from God the Most High, mentioned by His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform the Jews and Christians who were among his immigrants. God the Most High says to him: Say, O Muhammad, to these Jews and Christians, O People of the Scripture, the Torah and the Gospel, You are not upon anything, of what you claim to be upon, of what Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to you, you Jews, nor of what Jesus, you Christians, brought to you, until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord, of what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to you of the Criterion, so you act upon all of that, and believe in what is in it of belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and confirm him, and acknowledge that all of that is from God, so do not deny any of it, and do not differentiate between the Messengers of God, believing in some and disbelieving in others, because disbelieving in one of them is disbelief in all of them, because the Books of God confirm each other, so whoever denies some of them has denied all of them.
The effect came in a similar manner to what we said about it.

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to us, he said:
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “Rafi’ bin Haritha, Salam bin Mishkam, Malik bin Al-Saif, and Rafi’ bin Huraymila came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Muhammad, do you not claim that you are on the religion and faith of Abraham, and that you believe in what we have of the Torah, and that you testify that it is the truth from God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, but you have innovated and denied what was in it from what was taken from you of the covenant, and you have concealed from it what you were commanded to make clear to the people, and I am innocent of your innovations. They said: We will take what is in our hands, for we are on the truth and guidance, and we do not believe in you, nor will we follow you! So God, the Most High, revealed: “Say: O People of the Scripture, you are upon nothing until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord” to: “
h
So do not grieve
over The unbelieving people.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord,’” he said: We have become among the People of the Scripture, the Torah, for the Jews, and the Gospel, for the Christians, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord, what was revealed to us from our Lord, meaning: You are not upon anything until you uphold, until you act according to what is in it.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief

, and He swore: “And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of these Jews and Christians whose stories are related in these verses, the Book which I have revealed to you, O Muhammad,” in transgression, meaning: transgression and going to extremes in denying you, as they were upon you before the revelation of the Criterion, and disbelief, meaning: and denial of your prophethood. We have already explained the meaning of tyranny. As for his saying:
h
So do not grieve over the disbelieving people
, he means by his saying:
h
So do not grieve
, do not be sad. It is said: So-and-so is sad about such-and-such, if he is sad and grieves, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: His eyes welled up with grief.

God Almighty says to His Prophet: Do not be sad, O Muhammad, about the denial of you by these infidels from among the Jews and Christians from among the Children of Israel, for such a thing is a habit and a characteristic of their prophets, so how about you? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief, he said: The Criterion, he says:
h
So do not grieve

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So do not grieve over the disbelieving people
, he said: Do not be sad.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messenger, and they are the people of Islam, and those who were Jews, and they are the Jews, and the Sabians, and we have explained their matter, and the Christians—whoever believes in God and the Last Day, and believes in the resurrection after death, and does, from the work, righteousness, for his afterlife, there will be no fear concerning them, in what they have done of the horrors of the Resurrection, nor will they grieve, for what they have left behind of the world and its life, after they have witnessed what God has honored them with of His abundant reward. We have explained the reason for its parsing previously, so there is no need to repeat it.

God Almighty says: I swear: We took a covenant from the Children of Israel to be sincere in their belief in Our Oneness, to act in accordance with what We commanded them to do, and to refrain from what We forbade them from doing. We sent messengers to them for this purpose, and We promised them on the tongues of Our messengers to them, for acting in obedience to Us, a great reward, and We promised them, for acting in disobedience to Us, a severe punishment. Whenever a messenger of Ours came to them with something that their souls did not desire or agree with their love, they denied a group of them, and they killed a group of them, in violation of Our covenant that We took from them, and in audacity towards Us and in opposition to Our command.

God Almighty says: And these Israelites, whose description God Almighty described: That He took a covenant from them, and that He sent messengers to them, and that whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, they denied a group and killed a group, thought that there would be no trial and test from God for them with hardships of punishments for what they were doing, so they were blind and deaf, meaning: They were blind to the truth and to fulfilling the covenant that I took from them, of sincere worship of Me, and adhering to My commands and prohibitions, and working in obedience to Me, in their opinion and assumption, and they were deaf to it, then I repented of them. He says: Then I guided them with kindness from Me to them until they repented and turned back from what they were doing of sins and disobedience to My command and doing what I dislike from them, to doing what I love and adhering to My obedience and command and prohibition, Then many of them became blind and deaf, He says: Then they also became blind to the truth and fulfilling My covenant that I took from them: of working in obedience to Me, adhering to My command, and avoiding my sins, And many of them became deaf, He says: Many of those from whom I took a covenant from the Children of Israel, to follow My messengers and do what I revealed to them from My books, became blind to the truth and became deaf, after My repentance to them and My rescue of them from destruction, And God is Seeing of what they do, He says Seeing, so He sees their deeds, both good and evil, and He will reward them on the Day of Resurrection for all of them, if good then good, and if evil then evil.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they thought that there would be no trial
, the verse, he says: The people thought that there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf, whenever a trial presented itself to them, they were afflicted with it, and they perished in it.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they thought that there would be no trial
, so they became blind and deaf, meaning: They thought that they would not be afflicted, so they became blind to the truth and deaf.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And they thought that there would be no trial
, he said: A calamity.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they thought that there would be no trial
, he said: polytheism.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they thought that there would be no trial
, so they became blind and deaf, he said: The Jews.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So they became blind and deaf, he said: Jews. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, he said: This verse is for the Children of Israel. He said: And trial is the trial and the test.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about some of the things that He tempted the Israelites with, about whom He informed us that they thought that there would be no temptation. God, the Most High, says: Among the things that I tested them with - and they broke My covenant and changed My covenant that I had taken from them that they would not worship anyone other than Me, and would not take anyone as a lord other than Me, and that they would make Me One and cease to obey Me - was My servant Jesus, son of Mary. I created him and carried out through his hand what I carried out through many of My messengers. They said, out of disbelief, He is God. This is what the Jacobite Christians say, upon them is the wrath of God. God the Almighty says: So when I tested them and afflicted them with what I afflicted them with, they associated partners with Me, and they said to a creation of Mine, and a slave like them from among My slaves, and a human being similar to them whose lineage and origin are known, born from among humans, calling them to My Oneness, and commanding them to worship and obey Me, and acknowledging to them that I am his Lord and their Lord, and forbidding them to associate anything with Me: He is their God, out of their ignorance of God and disbelief in Him, and it is not appropriate for God to be a father nor to be born.
And what he means by his saying:
h
And the Messiah said

, O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord, he says: make worship and humility for the One to whom everything is humbled, and to whom everything that exists is subject, My Lord and your Lord, he says: my Owner and your Owner, and my Master and your Master, who created me and you, Indeed, whoever associates others with God, God has forbidden him Paradise, to dwell in it in the Hereafter, and his refuge is the Fire, he says: and his return and his place - to which he will return and become in his afterlife, whoever makes a partner for God in his worship - is the fire of Hell, and for the wrongdoers, he says: and for whoever does other than what God has permitted him, and worships other than the One to whom creation is worshipped, there are no helpers, who will support him on the Day of Resurrection from God, and save him from Him when he leads him to Hell.

This is also report from God Almighty about another group of the Israelites whose characteristics He described in the verses before: that when He tested them after they thought that they would not be tested or tried, they said, in disbelief in their Lord and polytheism: God is the third of three. This is what the majority of Christians believed before the Jacobites, the Melkites, and the Nestorians split. As far as we know, they said: “The ancient God is one essence encompassing three hypostases: a father who is a begetter and not begotten, a son who is a begetter and not a father, and a spouse who follows them.” God the Most High says, belying them in what they said: And there is no god except one God, meaning: You have no god, O people, except one god, and He is the One who is neither the father of anything nor the begotten, but rather He is the Creator of every father and begotten thing, and if they do not desist from what they say, meaning: if the speakers of this statement do not desist from what they say of their statement: God is the third of three, “a painful punishment will afflict those among them who disbelieve,” meaning: those who say this statement and those who say the other statement: He is the Messiah, son of Mary, will afflict them, because both groups are disbelievers and polytheists.

Therefore, He returned in the threat of punishment to the generality, and did not say: a painful punishment will afflict them, because if that were said thus, the threat from God the Most High would be specific to the speaker of the second statement, and they are the speakers of the statement: God is the third of three, and those who say: The Messiah is God would not be included among them. So the threat of God Almighty includes every disbeliever, so that those addressed by these verses may know that God’s threat includes both groups of the Children of Israel, and whoever among the disbelievers is like them.
If the matter is as you described, then to whom do the ha and mim in his statement: of them refer?

On the Children of Israel. The interpretation of the statement, since the matter is as we have described: If these Israelites do not cease what they say about God of the great words, then those of them who say: The Messiah is God, and those who say: God is the third of three, and every disbeliever who follows their path, will be afflicted with a painful punishment, because of their disbelief in God.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said, that he meant the Christians by these verses.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three.’ He said: The Christians said: He and the Messiah and his mother. So that is the saying of God Almighty: Did you say to the people, ‘Take me and my mother as gods besides God?’ (al-Ma’idah 5:116).

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said:
m: They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three,’ something similar.

x: God Almighty says: Will not these two disbelieving groups, one of whom said: God is the Messiah, the son of Mary, and the other who said: God is the third of three, return from what they said of that, and repent for what they said and uttered of their disbelief, and ask their Lord for forgiveness for what they said, And God is Forgiving, of the sins of those of His creation who repent, who turn to His obedience after their disobedience, Merciful to them, in accepting their repentance and their turning back to what He loves from what He hates, so He thereby pardons their actions for what they have done before that of their crimes.

This is report from God Almighty, as an argument for His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the Christian sects in what they say about the Messiah. He says - refuting the Jacobites in their saying: He is God and the others in their saying: He is the son of God -: The saying is not as these infidels said about the Messiah, but he is the son of Mary, born as mothers give birth to their sons, and that is from the description of human beings, not from the description of the Creator of human beings, but he is a messenger to God like all of His messengers who were before him and then passed away and departed, He performed through his hand whatever signs and lessons He willed to perform upon them, as proof for him of his truthfulness, and that he is a messenger to God to whomever He sent him from among His creation, just as He performed through the hands of the messengers before him of signs and lessons, as proof for them of the truth of their truthfulness in that they are messengers to God, and his mother is a friend, God Almighty says, and the mother of the Messiah is a friend.

And the friend is the active participle, from the truth, and likewise their saying: So-and-so is a friend, the active participle from the truth, and from it is the saying of the Most High: And the truthful and the martyrs
r
(An-Nisa’: 70)

. It was said that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, was called Al-Siddiq because of his truthfulness. It has been said that he was called Siddiq because he believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his journey in one night to the Holy House from Mecca, and his return to it. His saying:
h
They were eating food

, is report from God Almighty about the Messiah and his mother: that they were people in need of what would nourish them and sustain their bodies from food and drink like all other human beings from the children of Adam. For whoever is like that, is not a god, because the one who needs food is sustained by something other than it.
And in his sustaining himself by something other than it and his need for what sustains him, there is clear evidence of his helplessness. And the helpless can only be a servant, not a lord.

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him): Look, O Muhammad, how We explain to these infidels from among the Jews and Christians, the signs, which are the evidence, signs, and arguments for the length of what they say about the prophets of God, and their slander against God, and their claim that He has a son, and their testimony for some of His creation that they have a Lord and a God, and then they are not deterred from their lies and falsehood, and they are not deterred from their slander against their Lord and their great ignorance, despite the decisive arguments that prove their excuse for them. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him): Then look, O Muhammad, how they are deluded, meaning: Then look, with Our explaining to them Our signs despite their lengthy words, in what way do they turn away from Our explanation that We explain to them?

And how do they go astray from the guidance to which We guide them from the truth? The Arabs say for everything that is spent on something: He is Ma'fook 'anhu. It is said: Qad Affakat Fulan 'an Dhat, meaning: I diverted him from it, Fana Affakahu Affak, and he is Ma'fook. And Qad Affakat Al-Ard, if the rain is diverted from it.

This is also an argument from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the Christians who say about Christ what was described of what they said about him before. God the Almighty says to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to these infidel Christians who claim that Christ is their Lord and who say that God is the third of three, “Do you worship other than God, who has the power to harm and benefit you, and who created you and provided for you, and who gives you life and causes you to die, something that has no power to harm or benefit you?” God the Almighty informs them that Christ, whom some Christians claim is a god, and whom some claim is the son of God, has no power to ward off harm from them if God brings it upon them, nor to bring them benefit if God does not decree it for them. God the Almighty says: How can someone with these attributes be a lord and a god?

Rather, the Lord who is worshipped is the One in whose hand is everything and who is capable of everything. So worship Him and devote your worship to Him alone, and not to any other helpless one who can neither benefit you nor harm you. As for his saying:
h
And God is the All-Hearing
, the All-Knowing, He, the Most High, means by that:
h
And God is the All-Hearing

, for their seeking forgiveness if they sought His forgiveness for what He informed us they would say about the Messiah, and for other things of their speech and the speech of His creation, the All-Knowing, of their repentance if they repented from it, and other things of their affairs.

This is a speech from God Almighty to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these Christians who are extreme in their belief in Christ, O People of the Book, meaning by the Book, the Gospel, Do not go to extremes in your religion, meaning: Do not go to extremes in what you believe in regarding Christ, so that you go beyond the truth to falsehood, so that you say about him: He is God, or: He is his son, but say: He is the servant of God and His Word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and do not follow the inclinations of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray, meaning: And do not also follow in Christ the inclinations of the Jews who had gone astray before you from the path of guidance in saying about him, so that you say about him as they said: He is not right, and slander his mother as you slandered her with a lie while she was a friend, and they led many astray, meaning: And these Jews led many people astray, so they deviated them from the path of truth, and led them to disbelieve in God and deny Christ, and they went astray from the right path, meaning: And these Jews went astray from the right path, They rode a path other than the right path.

What God Almighty means by this is their disbelief in God, their denial of His messengers: Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their departure from faith and their distance from it. That was their misguidance with which God described them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And they have strayed from the right path, he said: Jews.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Do not follow the desires of a people who went astray before and led many astray, they are those who went astray and led their followers astray, and went astray from the right path, from the justice of the path.

x: According to the words of God Almighty to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to these Christians whose characteristics God Almighty described: Do not go to extremes and say about Christ something other than the truth, and do not say about him what the Jews said, whom God cursed through the tongues of His prophets and messengers, David and Jesus, son of Mary.
And God’s curse was on their tongues, like the one who:

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus

, the son of Mary, he said: They were cursed by every tongue: they were cursed during the time of Moses in the Torah, they were cursed during the time of David in the Psalms, they were cursed during the time of Jesus in the Gospel, and they were cursed during the time of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Qur’an.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus
, son of Mary, meaning: They were cursed in the Gospel by the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary, and they were cursed in the Psalms by the tongue of David.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus

, son of Mary. He said: They mixed with them after the prohibition in their trade, so God struck the hearts of some of them with others, so they are cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Hiseen, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus
, son of Mary. He said: They were cursed by the tongue of David and became monkeys, and they were cursed by the tongue of Jesus and became pigs.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: Ibn Abbas said, his statement:
h
Cursed are those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel

, is by every language they were cursed in: during the time of Moses in the Torah, during the time of David in the Psalms, during the time of Jesus in the Gospel, and they were cursed by the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Qur’an. Ibn Jurayj said: Others said:
h
Cursed are those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel

by the tongue of David, during his time, so they were cursed by his call. He said: David passed by a group of them while they were in a house and said: Who is in the house? They said: Pigs. He said: O God, make them pigs!, so they were pigs. He said: Then his curse befell them. And Jesus called down a curse upon them and said: O God, curse those who slandered me and my mother, and make them despised apes!

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel the verse
, God cursed them on the tongue of David in his time, so He made them despised apes, and in the Gospel on the tongue of Jesus, so He made them pigs.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me, he said, Abu Muhsin Husayn bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Husayn - meaning:
m: Ibn Abd al-Rahman - on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed on the tongue of David, he said: They were transformed into monkeys on the tongue of David, and into pigs on the tongue of Jesus.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When a man from the Children of Israel saw his brother committing a sin, he would forbid him from doing so as an excuse. But the next day, what he saw of him did not prevent him from being his eater, his companion, or his drinker. When he saw that from them, he struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them on the tongues of their prophet David and Jesus, son of Mary, ‘That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.’ He Surat al-Ma’idah 5:78
h
Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus

, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors. said: ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must seize the hand of the wrongdoer and force him to adhere to the truth, or God will strike the hearts of some of you against others, and curse you as He cursed them.’” Ibn Humayd narrated, Al-Hakam bin Bashir bin Salman narrated, Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i narrated, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When evil spread among the Children of Israel, a man would meet another man and say: O man, fear God! But that would not prevent him from eating and drinking with him. When God saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, then He sent down a book about them: “Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors. They used not to forbid one another from the evil they were doing. Evil indeed was that which they were doing.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, then he sat up and said: No, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, until they forced the oppressor to adhere to the truth.

c: Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told us, he said, al-Mu’ammil bin Ismail told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Ali bin Badhima told us, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah,
m: I think on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When evil became apparent among the Children of Israel, a man would see his brother, neighbor, or companion committing evil, and he would forbid him, but that would not prevent him from being his eater, drinker, or companion. So God struck the hearts of some of them against others, and they were cursed on the tongues of David and Jesus, son of Mary, ‘That is because they disobeyed and were transgressors,’ to ‘disobedient.’ Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, then he sat up straight, and became angry and said: No, by God, not until you seize the hand of the oppressor and force him to do what is right.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, he said,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Children of Israel were deficient, a man would see his brother in doubt and forbid him from it. But the next day, what he saw of him did not prevent him from being his eater, drinker, and companion.
