c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: From their hardship and their ease.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: From their hardship and their ease.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: h
From the average of what you feed your families
, he said: their food.

c: Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Absi, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
From the average of what you feed your families
, he said: their food.

c: Abu Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salim told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Ubayd al-Absi, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
From the best of what you feed your families
, he said: They used to prefer the free man over the slave, and the old over the young, so the verse was revealed:
h
From the best of what you feed your families

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said,
m: they used to feed the old what they did not feed the young, and they used to feed the free man what they did not feed the slave, so he said:
h
From the average of what you feed your families

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
From the average of what you feed your families
, he said: If you are going to satisfy your family, then satisfy them. And if you are not going to satisfy them, then according to that.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Shaiban Al-Nahwi told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: From the middle of what you feed your families, he said: from their hardship and ease.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: A man would feed some of his family with a poor diet, and some of them with ample diet, so God said:
h
From the average of what you feed your families
, bread and oil.

x: The most correct interpretation of his statement,
h
From the average of what you feed your families
, according to us, is the statement of those who say:
h
From the average of what you feed your families

in terms of little and much. This is because the rulings of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding all expiations have been reported in this regard. This is like his ruling, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the expiation for shaving the head from harm by distributing food among six poor people, for each poor person half a saʿ, and like his ruling regarding the expiation for intercourse in the month of Ramadan by distributing fifteen saʿ among sixty poor people, for each poor person a quarter of a saʿ. Nothing is known of his, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding expiations. He ordered the feeding of bread and condiments, nor lunch and dinner.

If that is the case, and the expiation for an oath is one of the expiations that are required of the one who is obligated to do so, then its method is the method of what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took over the ruling on: that what is required of the one who expiates it is food, estimated for the ten poor people, limited by a measure, without gathering them together for a baked and prepared lunch or dinner, since his Sunnah, may God bless him and grant him peace, was like that in all other expiations. So if what we said is correct, based on what we cited as evidence, then it is clear that the interpretation of the statement is: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn in oaths. Its expiation is feeding ten poor people from the most just of what you feed your families. And that the ma in His statement:
h
from the average of what you feed your families
is in the sense of the source, not in the sense of the names.

If this is the case, then the most just food for the wealthy person is two mudds, which is half a sa’ of food, and a quarter of it is a condiment. This is the highest that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled for expiation for feeding the poor. And the most just food for the poor person is one mudd, which is a quarter of a sa’, and this is the lowest that he ruled for expiation for feeding the poor. As for those who saw feeding the poor in expiation for an oath, bread and meat and what we mentioned about them before, and those who saw that they should eat or have dinner, and those who saw that they should eat in the morning and have dinner, then they went to the interpretation of his saying:
h
from the average of what you feed your families
, from the average food that you feed your families, so they made what is in his saying:
h
from the average of what you feed your families
, a noun and not a source, so they obligated the one who is expiating to feed the poor from the most equitable food that he feeds his family.

And that is a doctrine, were it not for what we mentioned from the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in expiations other than it, the forms of which must be attached to it, and that the expiation for an oath has a counterpart and similar that must be attached to it.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: or their clothing.

God Almighty means by that: The expiation for the oaths you have made is to feed ten poor people, or clothe them. He says: Either you feed them or clothe them. And the choice in that is up to the one making the expiation.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the clothing that God Almighty meant by His saying: or their clothing.
Some of them said: He meant by that: covering one garment.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding clothing the poor in expiation for an oath: The lowest garment is a garment.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The lowest part is a garment, and the highest part is whatever you wish.

c: Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said
m: regarding the expiation for an oath in his statement: or their clothing, a garment for each poor person.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Wahib, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: Or their clothing, he said: a garment.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ubaidah told us, and Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: or their clothing, he said: a garment.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Or their clothing, he said: A garment, a garment. Mansur said: The shirt, or the cloak, or the lower garment.

c: Abu Kuraib and Hannad told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja’far,
m: regarding his statement: Or their clothing, he said: Winter and summer clothing, one garment after another.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Omar bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement: Or their clothing, he said: A garment, a garment for every poor person.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement: or clothed them, he said: If he clothed them with a garment, it would suffice for him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Hammad, who said:
m: One garment or two garments, and one garment is necessary.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Surat al-Ma’idah 5:
m: 89 Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for your deliberate oaths. Its expiation is the feeding of ten needy persons
h
from the average of what you feed your families

, or clothing them, or the freeing of a slave. But whoever cannot find [that], then a fast of three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. You have sworn, and keep your oaths. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful. Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A garment is a garment for every person. And the cloak was a substitute for clothing at that time.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Saleh, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Or their clothing, he said: The clothing is a cloak for every poor person, or a shawl.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, he said:
m: A garment, or a shirt, or a robe, or a loincloth.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If the one on the right chooses the garment, he will clothe ten people, each person with a cloak.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said,
m: I heard Ata’ say regarding his statement: Or their clothing, clothing is a garment.

x: Some of them said: He meant by that: clothing, two garments, two garments.
Who said that?

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ubaidah told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, regarding his statement: Or their clothing, he said: A cloak and a turban.

c: Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Wakiʿ told us, and Ibn Wakiʿ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, he said:
m: A turban with which to wrap his head, and a cloak with which to cover himself.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, they said:
m: Two garments, two garments.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Two garments.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Abu Kuraib and Hannad told us, they said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Two garments, two garments for every poor person.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Musa,
m: that he swore an oath, and he was clothed in two garments from the Muqaddah of Bahrain.

c: Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: Abu Musa was clothed in two garments from the Bahraini fabric.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd al-A’la 87:
m: That Abu Musa al-Ash’ari swore an oath, and he decided to atone, so he did, and he clothed ten people in two garments.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad:
m: Abu Musa swore an oath and then broke it, so he clothed ten poor people with two garments each.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said:
m: A cloak and a turban for every poor person.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, he said: A man said
m: in the presence of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab: Or I clothed them. Saeed said: No, it is: Or I clothed them. I said: O Abu Muhammad, what is their clothing? He said: Every poor person has an cloak and a turban: an cloak to cover himself with, and a turban to tie around his head.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Or their clothing, he said: Clothing is for every poor person a cloak and a lower garment, like what he finds of ease and poverty.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was that he clothed them in a comprehensive garment, like a blanket or a cloak, and something suitable for wearing and sleeping.
Who said that?

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The kiswa is a comprehensive garment.

c: Hanad and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement: or their clothing, he said: a comprehensive garment. He said, and Mugheerah said: the comprehensive garment is the blanket or cloak or something similar, and we do not see the armor, shirt, veil, and something similar as comprehensive.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mugheera, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: A comprehensive garment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mugheera, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: A comprehensive garment.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Or their clothing, he said: A garment for every poor person.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan and Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement: Or their clothing, he said: A comprehensive garment.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughira,
m: the same.

x: Others said: What he meant by that was: a garment of a loincloth, a robe, and a shirt.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Burda, on the authority of Rafe’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said
m: regarding clothing: In expiation, a loincloth, a cloak, and a shirt.

x: Others said: Whatever he covers is sufficient, and the verse is general.
Who said that?

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abd al-Salam bin Harb told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Everything is sufficient as expiation for an oath except straw.

c: Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: A turban is sufficient as expiation for an oath.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Uwais al-Sayrafi, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, he said, Salman said:
m: The best garment is the taban.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said:
m: A turban that is wrapped around his head.

x: The most correct of the opinions on this, in our view, and the most similar to the interpretation of the Qur’an, is the opinion of those who said: What is meant by His statement, or their clothing, is what is called clothing, which is a garment or more, because what is less than a garment, there is no disagreement among all the proofs that it is not included in the ruling of the verse. So what is less than that amount is excluded from what God Almighty meant, according to the widespread transmission. And the garment and what is above it is included in the ruling of the verse, since there was no revelation from God Almighty, nor from His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there was no consensus among the nation that it is not included in its ruling. And it is not permissible to exclude what the verse appears to be from the ruling of the verse, except with a proof that must be accepted.
And there is no proof for that.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: or the freeing of a slave.
God Almighty means by that: or freeing a slave from the bondage and humiliation of slavery.

i: The origin of liberation is release from captivity, and from it is the saying of Al-Farazdaq bin Ghalib:
x: My son Ghadana, I have freed you and given you to Atiya bin Ja'al.

He means by his saying: I have freed you, I have freed your necks from the humiliation of satire and the necessity of shame. It was said, Freeing a neck, and the freedman is the one with the neck, because it was the custom of the Arabs, when they captured a prisoner, to tie his hands to his neck with a stick or a rope or something else, and when they released him from captivity, they released his hands and freed them from what they were tied with to the neck. So the talk, when they released the prisoner, was about releasing his hands from his neck, and they meant the report about releasing him from his captivity, as it is said: So-and-so held his hand back from so-and-so, if he held his hand from giving him his gift - and extended his tongue against him, if he said something bad about him - so the action is attributed to the limb by which that action occurs, not its doer, because people use that among themselves, and they know its meaning.

Likewise, in the statement of God Almighty: or the freeing of a slave, “freeing” was added to the neck, even if there was no shackle on his neck or a handcuffing it. What was meant by freeing was the slave himself, as we have described, as a result of people using it among themselves because of their knowledge of its meaning.
Is this meant for all necks or some of them?

Rather, what is meant by that is every neck that is free from crippling, blindness, muteness, amputation of the hands or their paralysis, complete insanity, and similar things. If a neck has that or some of it, there is no disagreement among all of them regarding the proof that it is not sufficient in expiation for an oath. So it was known from that that God, the Most High, mentioned Him, did not mean him by liberation in this verse. As for the young and the old, Surat al-Ma’idah 5:89 Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for your deliberate oaths. Its expiation is the feeding of ten needy persons
h
from the average of what you feed your families
, or clothing them, or the freeing of a slave.

But whoever cannot find [that], then a fast of three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. You have sworn, and keep your oaths. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful. the Muslim and the disbeliever, they are meant by it.
A group of scholars said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Hanad told us...
m: he said, Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim: that he used to say: If someone has a slave who is obligated to be freed, and he buys a soul, he said: If he frees it from work, it is sufficient for him, and it is not permissible to free someone who does not work. As for the one who works, it is the one-eyed person and the like. As for the one who does not work, it is not sufficient, the blind person and the crippled person.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: He disliked freeing a person with a mental disorder as part of any of the expiations.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: He did not think that freeing someone who was mentally impaired was sufficient for any of the expiations.

x: Some of them said: Only a healthy person is sufficient for expiation, and a young person is sufficient for it.
Who said that?

c: Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: Nothing is sufficient for a slave except a healthy one.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: A child born in Islam is sufficient as a slave.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Al-Aʿmash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Whatever is mentioned in the Qur’an about a believing slave
r
(An-Nisa’: 92)
, then nothing is sufficient except what fasts and prays. And whatever is not a believing slave, then a boy is sufficient.

x: Some of them said: The newborn is not called a neck until after a period of time has passed.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Yazid Al-Rafa’i told me, he said, Yahya bin Zakariya bin Abi Zaida told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Shu’ayb bin Shabur, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Al-Mundhir, on the authority of Sulayman, who said:
m: When a boy is born, he is a soul, and when he turns from his back to his stomach, he is a slave, and when he prays, he is a believer.

x: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is to say: God Almighty mentioned the neck in general, meaning every neck, so any neck that the expiator of his oath frees in his expiation, he has fulfilled what he was required to do, except what we mentioned, that the evidence is unanimously agreed upon that God Almighty mentioned, and did not mean it by freeing, so that is outside the ruling of the verse, and other than that it is permissible to free it in expiation according to the apparent meaning of the revelation. The person who makes expiation has the choice to expiate his oath in which he broke it in one of these three cases that God mentioned in His Book, and that is: feeding ten poor people from the average of what he feeds his family, or clothing them, or freeing a slave, by consensus of all, and there is no disagreement among them on that. If someone thinks that what we said, that it is a consensus of everyone, is not as we said, because: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawareb narrated, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad narrated, Sulayman Al-Shaibani narrated, Abu Al-Dhaha narrated, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Maqal bin Muqrin came to Abdullah and said: I have sworn off women and bed!

Abdullah recited this verse: “Do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” (al-Ma’idah 5:87). Maqal said: I only asked you to read this verse last night. Abdullah said: Go to women and sleep, and free a slave, for you are well off.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Jarir ibn Hazim told me: Sulayman al-A'mash told him, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Nakha'i, on the authority of Hammam ibn al-Harith:
m: Nu'man ibn Muqrin asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, saying: I swore that I would not sleep in my bed for a year. Ibn Mas'ud said: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you (al-Ma’idah 5:87). Atone for your oath and sleep in your bed! He said: How do I atone for my oath? He said: Free a slave, for you are well off. And similar to this from the reports that were narrated from Ibn Masoud, Ibn Omar and others, for that from them was in the form of recommendation for those who were ordered to atone for what they were ordered to atone for in terms of slaves, not that atonement was not sufficient for the wealthy person except by a slave, because no one transmitted from any of them that for money: atonement is not sufficient for the wealthy person except by a slave. And all of the scholars of the countries, ancient and modern, are in agreement that atonement with other than slaves is permissible for the wealthy person. So in that we are satisfied with citing evidence for the correctness of what we said about that with other sources.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And whoever does not find it
, then he should fast for three days.

God Almighty says: But whoever cannot find, for the expiation for his oath, which he must expiate with food, clothing, and slaves, what he can expiate with according to what we have imposed upon him and made obligatory in our book and on the tongue of our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
then fasting for three days
, meaning: he must fast for three days. Then the scholars differed regarding the meaning of his statement:
h
And whoever does not find
, and when does the person who broke his oath and was required to pay expiation deserve the name not finding, so that he is among those who are permitted to fast in that case.

Some of them said: If the person who broke his oath at the time of expiation for his oath only has enough to sustain himself and his family for a day and a night, then he may expiate by fasting. If he has enough at that time to sustain himself and his family for a day and a night, and some of the surplus is enough to feed ten poor people or clothe them, then he must expiate by feeding or clothing them, and fasting will not be sufficient for him in that case.
Among those who said this is Al-Shafi’i:

c: Al-Rabi' told us
m: about it. This statement, God willing, is intended to mean that whoever makes food obligatory on someone who has two dirhams must make it obligatory on someone who has three dirhams. And something similar to that:

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Abd al-Karim, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: If he has only three dirhams, he should feed them. He said: He meant as expiation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told me:
m: I said to Umar bin Rashid: A man swears an oath and he has only enough food to atone for it. He said: Qatada used to say: He fasts for three days.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, Yunus bin Ubayd told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: If he has two dirhams.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Abdul Karim Abu Umayya, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: Three dirhams.

x: Others said: It is permissible for someone who does not have two hundred dirhams to fast, even though he is one of those who cannot find anything.

Others said: It is permissible for someone who does not have any surplus money beyond his capital that he can use for his livelihood, which would atone for his oath by feeding others, to fast unless he has enough money, and some of the money he can use for his livelihood, and some of the surplus money he can use to atone for his oath. This is a statement that some of the later jurists used to say.

The correct opinion in this regard, according to us, is that whoever, when he broke his oath, had only enough to sustain himself and his dependents for a day and a night, with no surplus, should fast for three days. He is one of those who cannot find anything to feed, clothe, or free. If he had at that time enough to feed or clothe ten poor people for a day and a night, or to free a slave, then fasting is not sufficient for him, because one of the three cases in this case, whether feeding, clothing, or freeing, is a right that God, the Most High, has made obligatory on his wealth, as a debt is obligatory. Evidence has been established that if a bankrupt person distributes his wealth among his creditors, he should not be left that day except what he needs for his food and the food of his dependents for a day and a night. The same is the ruling for the one who is destitute because of the debt that God, the Most High, has made obligatory on his wealth because of the expiation that is required of his wealth.
Scholars differed regarding the nature of the fasting that God has made obligatory as expiation for an oath.
Some of them said: Its description is that it should be continuous between the three days, not separated.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Every fast in the Qur’an is consecutive, except for making up for Ramadan, which is a number of days from another.

c: Abu Kuraib and Hannad told us, they said: Waki’ told us, and Ibn Waki’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, he said:
m: My father bin Ka’b used to recite: Then fast three consecutive days.

c: Abdul-A’la bin Wasil Al-Asadi told us, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-A’aliyah, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b:
m: that he used to recite: Then fast three consecutive days.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Qaza’ah, on the authority of Suwaid, on the authority of Saif bin Sulayman, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: In Abdullah’s recitation: Then fasting for three consecutive days.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: In our recitation: then fasting three consecutive days.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding the reading of the companions of Abdullah: Then fasting for three consecutive days. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:89 Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for your deliberate oaths. Its expiation is the feeding of ten needy persons
h
from the average of what you feed your families

, or clothing them, or the freeing of a slave. But whoever cannot find [that], then a fast of three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. You have sworn, and keep your oaths. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.

c: Hanad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: In Abdullah’s reading: Then fasting for three consecutive days.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad bin Hamid told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq,
m: regarding Abdullah’s reading: Then fasting for three consecutive days.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad bin Hamid told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said:
m: The companions of Abdullah used to recite: Then fast three consecutive days.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, he said,
m: I heard Sufyan say: If he breaks up fasting for three days, it does not count. He said: And I heard him say about a man who fasted as expiation for an oath and then broke his fast, he said: He should start fasting again.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then fasting for three days
, he said: If he does not find food, and it was in some of the recitation, then fasting for three consecutive days. And Qatada used to take it from this.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He has the choice in these three, the first then the first, and if he does not find anything of that, then he should fast three consecutive days.

x: Others said: It is permissible for the one who fasts them to fast them however he wants, together or separately.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said, Malik said:
m: Everything that God mentioned in the Qur’an about fasting, if it is fasted consecutively it is more amazing. But if it is fasted separately, I hope that it will suffice for it.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God Almighty has made it obligatory for the one who is obligated to make expiation for an oath, if he cannot find a way to make expiation by feeding, clothing, or freeing a slave, to make expiation by fasting three days, and He did not stipulate that they be consecutive. So however the expiator fasts them, separately or consecutively, it is sufficient for him. Because God Almighty has only made it obligatory for him to fast three days, so whatever he does by fasting them is sufficient. As for what was narrated from Abi and Ibn Masoud regarding their reading: Fasting for three consecutive days, this is contrary to what is in our copies of the Qur’an. It is not permissible for us to testify that something that is not in our copies of the Qur’an is from the Book of God. However, I prefer that the one who is fasting, in the expiation of an oath, should follow the three days and not separate them.

Because there is no disagreement among all that if he does that, it will suffice for him as expiation, and they differ on other matters. So doing what there is no disagreement about its permissibility is more beloved to me, since the other is permissible.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
This is the expiation for your oaths when you swear
, and guard your oaths.
Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.”

God Almighty means by His saying: That, that which I mentioned to you is the expiation for your oaths, from feeding ten poor people, or clothing them, or freeing a slave, and fasting for three days if you do not find anything of that - it is the expiation for the oaths that you made when you swore - and guard, O you who believe, your oaths, lest you break them, then waste the expiation for them with what I described to you, thus does God make clear to you His signs, just as He made clear to you the expiation for your oaths, thus does God make clear to you all of His signs - meaning the signs of His religion, and He explains them to you - lest the one who neglects and is excessive in what God has obligated him to do say: I did not know the ruling of God in that, that you may be grateful, meaning: so that you may thank God for His guidance to you and His success for you.

evidence.text: The majority of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as: But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have made, with a shaddah on the qaf, meaning: you have made oaths and rejected them.
Abdullah recited this verse: “Do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress.
Maqal said: I only asked you to read this verse last night.
Hanad told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: In our recitation: then fasting three consecutive days.
Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding the reading of the companions of Abdullah: Then fasting for three consecutive days.

Bishr bin Muadh told us, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Then fasting for three days, he said: If he does not find food, and it was in some of the recitation, then fasting for three consecutive days.
As for what was narrated from Abi and Ibn Masoud regarding their reading: Fasting for three consecutive days, this is contrary to what is in our copies of the Qur’an.

x: This is a statement from God, the Most High, to those of the Prophet's companions who forbade themselves women, sleep, and meat, imitating the priests and monks. God sent down His Book to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbidding them from doing so, saying: O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you (al-Ma’idah 5:87). Thus, He forbade them from forbidding what God has made lawful for them of good things. Then He said: And do not transgress My limits, making lawful what I have forbidden to you, for that is not permissible for you, just as it is not permissible for you to forbid what I have made lawful, and I do not like transgressors.

c: Then He informed them
m: of what He had forbidden them, which if they permitted it and went beyond it, they would be among the transgressors in His limits. He said to them: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, indeed the wine which you drink, and the gambling which you use, and the idols which you slaughter at, and the arrows by which you cast lots, are an abomination, meaning: a sin and a stench due to God’s anger and dislike for you, from the work of Satan, meaning: your drinking of wine, your gambling on the islands, your slaughtering at idols, and your casting lots with arrows, are from Satan’s beautification of you, his calling you to him, and his making it seem good to you. It is not from the deeds that your Lord has urged you to do, nor from what He is pleased with for you. Rather, it is from what He is angry with you. So avoid it, meaning: leave it and reject it and do not do it, that you may succeed, meaning: so that you may succeed and attain success with your Lord by leaving it. We have previously explained the meaning of wine, gambling, and arrows, so we disliked repeating it. As for al-Ansab, it is the plural of Nasab, and we have explained the meaning of Nasab with its evidence, previously.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding the meaning of filth in this context, as follows: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
An abomination from the work of Satan
, meaning: displeasure. Ibn Zayd said about that, what: - Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement:
h
An abomination from the work of Satan
, he said: The abomination is evil.

x: God Almighty says: Satan only wants you to drink alcohol and play with lots, and to make that seem good to you, wanting to cause enmity and hatred between you through your drinking alcohol and playing with lots, so that you may become hostile to one another and hate one another, and so that your affairs may be scattered after God has united you through faith and brought you together through the brotherhood of Islam, and to turn you away from the remembrance of God, meaning: and to turn you away through the prevalence of this alcohol by intoxicating you upon you, and by your preoccupation with this gambling, from the remembrance of God through which your worldly and afterlife are improved, and from the prayer, which your Lord has enjoined upon you,
h
so will you not desist

? He says: Will you desist from drinking this and playing with this, and will you act according to what your Lord has commanded you to do by performing the prayer that He has enjoined upon you at its appointed times, and by adhering to His remembrance through which your requests in your worldly and afterlife will succeed?
The interpreters differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed because of something that happened to Omar bin Al-Khattab, which is that he mentioned the unpleasant consequences of drinking it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he asked God to prohibit it.
Who said that?

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Wakee’ narrated to us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, who said: Umar said:
m: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine! He said: Then the verse in Al-Baqarah was revealed: “They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, “In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.”
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:219)

. He said: So Umar was summoned and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine! Then the verse in Al-Nisa’ was revealed: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying.
r
(Al-Nisa’ 4:43)

. He said: The crier of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to call out when the time for prayer came: The drunkard should not approach prayer! He said: So Umar was summoned and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine! He said: Then the verse in Al-Ma’idah was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement until His saying:
h
Will you then desist
? When he reached his saying:
h
Will you then desist

? Omar said: We have desisted, we have desisted!! - Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, he said, Omar said: O God, give us a clear explanation of wine, for it takes away the mind and wealth! Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Wakee’.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, he said, Umar ibn al-Khattab said:
m: O God, make it clear to us, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father,
m: and Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, the same.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Zakariya bin Abi Zaida told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab,
m: the same.

c: Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, saying: Abu Maʿshar al-Madani narrated to me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, who said:
m: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, the people came to him and they were drinking alcohol and gambling. They asked him about that, so God, the Most High, revealed: “They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit.’” (al-Baqarah 2:219) They said: This is something for which a concession has been given. We eat gambling and drink alcohol, and we ask God’s forgiveness for that! Until a man came to the Maghrib prayer and began to recite: Say, ‘O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, nor will you worship what I worship.’ (al-Kafirun 109:1-3). So he did not allow that, and he did not know what he was reading. Then God revealed: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated.
r
(An-Nisa’: 143)

So the people would drink alcohol until the time for prayer came, then they would stop drinking it and come to prayer knowing what they were saying. They continued like that until God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, wine, gambling, idolatry, and divining arrows until His saying:
h
Will you then desist
? They said: We have desisted, O Lord!

x: Others said: This verse was revealed because of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas. He was arguing with a man over a Surat al-Ma’idah 5:91 Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer.
h
So will you not desist

? drink they had, so his companion hit him with the jawbones of a camel, causing his nose to split, so this verse was revealed about them. The novel mentioned that: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Musʿab ibn Saʿd, on the authority of his father Saʿd, that he said: A man from the Ansar made food and invited us. He said: We drank wine until we became intoxicated, and the Ansar and Quraysh boasted. The Ansar said: We are better than you! He said: Then a man from the Ansar took the jawbone of a camel and struck Saʿd’s nose with it, causing it to split.
Saʿd had the most split nose. He said: Then this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants and gambling to the end of the verse.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, he said, Sa’d said:
m: I drank with some of the Ansar and I struck one of them, I think - with the jawbone of a camel - and I broke it, so I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, and I did not hesitate to confirm the prohibition of alcohol: O you who believe, indeed, intoxicants and gambling are but fornication, to the end of the verse.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Musʿab bin Saʿd, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I drank wine with some people from the Ansar, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, that Ibn Shihab told him, that Salim ibn Abdullah told him:
m: The first time wine was forbidden, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and his companions drank and fought, and they broke Saʿd’s nose, so God revealed: Indeed, wine and gambling are only forbidden, the verse.

x: Others said: It was revealed about two tribes of the Ansar.

Who said that? Al-Husayn ibn Ali Al-Sada’i narrated, Hajjaj ibn Al-Munhal narrated, Rabia ibn Kulthum ibn Jabr narrated, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed concerning two tribes of the Ansar who drank until they became drunk, and some of them played with each other. When they sobered up, one of them would see the marks on his face and beard and say: My brother so-and-so did this to me! - and they were brothers, and there was no grudge in their hearts - By God, if He had been kind and merciful towards me, He would not have done this to me! Until grudges fell into their hearts, then God revealed: Intoxicants and gambling are only until His saying:
h
Will you then desist

Some of the pretenders said: There is an abomination in the stomach of so-and-so who was killed on the day of Badr, and so-and-so was killed on the day of Uhud! Then God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten (al-Ma’idah 5:193), the verse. Muhammad bin Khalaf narrated, Saeed bin Muhammad Al-Jarmi narrated, on the authority of Abu Tamila, on the authority of Salam, the freed slave of Hafs Abu Al-Qasim, on the authority of Ibn Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: While we were sitting on a sandy beach, three or four of us, and we were drinking halal wine, I got up to go to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and greet him. The prohibition of wine had been revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, to the end of the two verses,
h
So will you not desist
So I came to my companions and recited it to them until His saying:
h
So will you not desist

? He said: And some of the people had his drink in their hand, he had drunk some and some remained in the vessel, so he put the vessel under his upper lip as a cupper does. Then they poured out what was in their basins and said: We have stopped, our Lord! We have stopped, our Lord!

Others said: The enmity and hatred that existed between those about whom this verse was revealed was due to gambling, not due to the intoxication that would result from drinking alcohol. That is why God forbade them from gambling.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us
m: - Bishr said: I heard it from Yazid and he told it to me - and he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: A man in the pre-Islamic era would gamble with his family and his money, and he would sit around, robbed and plundered, looking at his money in the hands of others, so it would cause enmity and hatred between them, so God forbade that and advanced it. And God knows best who will reform His creation.

x: The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that God Almighty has called these things that He called in this verse filth, and He has commanded us to avoid them.

The people of interpretation differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed. It is possible that it was revealed because of the supplication of Omar may God be pleased with him regarding the matter of alcohol. It is possible that it was revealed because of what happened to Saad from the Ansari when they were intoxicated from drinking. It is possible that it was because of the enmity and hatred that would befall one of them when his money was lost through gambling. We do not have any conclusive information as to which of these was the excuse. However, whichever of these was the case, the ruling of the verse is binding on all those who are accountable, and ignorance of the reason for which this verse was revealed will not harm them. Alcohol, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are all abominations from the work of Satan. It is obligatory upon all those who receive the verse of accountability to avoid all of these, as God the Almighty says: So avoid them that you may be successful.

evidence.text: He said: So Umar was summoned and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine!
He said: So Umar was summoned and it was recited to him, and he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine!
So I came to my companions and recited it to them until His saying: So will you not desist?

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it, “and obey God and obey the Messenger,” in avoiding that, and following His command in what He has commanded you to do in order to be deterred from what He has forbidden you from in these meanings that He has explained to you in this verse and others, and disobey Satan in his command to you to disobey God in that and in other matters, for he only seeks for you enmity and hatred between you through wine and gambling, and beware, meaning: and fear God and watch Him lest He sees you when He forbids you from these matters that He has forbidden you in this verse and others, or misses you when He has commanded you, so that you will ruin yourselves and destroy them, and if you turn away, meaning: if you do not do what We have commanded you to do, and desist from what We have forbidden you from, and you turn back from what you are upon of faith and belief in God And with His Messenger, and following what your Prophet brought you, Know that the duty of Our Messenger is only to convey the clear message, meaning: Know that the one we sent to you with warning has no duty other than to convey to you the message with which he was sent to you, explaining to you a statement that clarifies for you the path of truth, and the way that you were commanded to follow. As for the punishment for turning away and taking revenge for disobedience, that is upon the one to whom it was sent, not the messengers.

This is a warning from God Almighty to those who turn away from His commands and prohibitions. God Almighty says to them: If you turn away from My commands and prohibitions, then expect My punishment and beware of My wrath.

God Almighty says to the people who said - when God revealed the prohibition of alcohol with His saying: Indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it: What about those of our brothers who perished while they were drinking it? And about us when we used to drink it? -There is no blame upon those among you who believe and do righteous deeds for what they drink of that, in the case when God the Most High has not forbidden it to them, if they fear God and believe and do righteous deeds, meaning: if the living among them fear God, fear Him, and observe Him in avoiding what He has forbidden them from, and believe in God and His Messenger in what He has commanded them and forbidden them, so they obey them in all of that, and do righteous deeds, meaning: and they acquire from the deeds what pleases God in that of what their Lord has charged them with, then fear God and believe, meaning: then they fear God and observe Him by avoiding what He has forbidden after that charge as well, so they remain steadfast in fearing God in that and believing in Him, and they do not change or alter, then fear God and do good, meaning: then they fear God, so their fear of God called them to do good, and that doing good is doing what He has not imposed upon them of deeds, but rather they are voluntary acts by which they draw closer to their Lord, seeking His pleasure.
And to escape His punishment,
h
And God loves the doers of good

, He says: And God loves those who draw near to Him through voluntary deeds that please Him. The first piety is piety by accepting and believing in God’s command, and by adhering to it and acting upon it. The second piety is piety by remaining steadfast in belief and avoiding alteration and change. The third piety is piety by doing good and drawing closer to God through voluntary deeds.
What is the evidence that the third type of piety is piety through voluntary acts of worship, without that being through obligatory acts of worship?

God Almighty informed us about His placing the blame on those who drank alcohol before He prohibited it, if they feared God in drinking it after it was prohibited, and believed in God and His Messenger in prohibiting it, and did righteous deeds from the obligatory duties. There is no reason to repeat that, as it was mentioned in one verse. In a manner similar to what we said, that this verse was revealed in the context in which we mentioned that it was revealed, the report came from the Companions and the Followers.
Who said that?

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb told us, they said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, they said: O Messenger of God, what about our companions who died while drinking alcohol? So the verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds
, and the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel,
m: with his chain of transmission, something similar. Muhammad bin Bashar narrated, Abdul Kabir bin Abdul Majeed narrated, Ibad bin Rashid narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: While I was passing the cup around to Abu Talha, Abu Ubaidah bin Al Jarrah, Muadh bin Jabal, Suhayl bin Bayda, and Abu Dujana, until their heads were tilted from the mixture of unripe dates and dates, we heard a crier calling out: Beware, wine has been forbidden! No one entered or left until we had poured out the drink, broken the jugs, performed ablution, washed, and obtained some of Umm Sulaym’s perfume. Then we went out to the mosque, and suddenly the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reciting: “
h
O you who have believed

, indeed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful,” until His saying:
h
Will you then desist
? A man said: O Messenger of God, what is the status of one of us who dies while drinking it? Then God the Almighty revealed:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten

Al-Baqarah 2:17. A man said to Qatada: Did you hear that from Anas ibn Malik? He said: Yes! A man said to Anas ibn Malik: Did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes!

c: And someone who did not lie told me.
m: By God, we did not lie, and we do not know what lying is!

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, he said:
m: When wine was forbidden, they said: What about our companions who died while drinking wine? Then the verse was revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do Surat al-Ma’idah 5:93 There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten if they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves the doers of good. righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Bukhari.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: Al-Baraʿ said:
m: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died while they were drinking alcohol. When its prohibition was revealed, some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What about our companions who died while they were drinking it? Then this verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds
, the verse.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten
was revealed regarding those who were killed at Badr and Uhud with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, he said, Ali bin Masaher told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: When the verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten

, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It was said to me: You are one of them. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Jamiʿ bin Hammad narrated, Yazid narrated, Saʿid narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten
, to His statement:
h
And God loves the doers of good

.* When God, the Most High, revealed the prohibition of alcohol in Surat Al-Ma’idah, after Surat Al-Ahzab, some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about that: So-and-so was afflicted on the day of Badr, and so-and-so on the day of Uhud, and they were drinking it! So we bear witness that they are among the people of Paradise! So God, the Most High, revealed: “
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten
, if they fear God and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear God and believe, then fear God and do good.
h
And God loves the doers of good
.” He said: The people drank it out of fear of God and doing good, and it was permissible for them on that day, then it was forbidden after them, so there is no blame upon them for that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten
, they said: O Messenger of God, what do we say to our brothers who have passed away? They used to drink alcohol and gamble! So God revealed:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten
, meaning before it was forbidden, if they were good and righteous. And He said another time:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten

of what is forbidden before it was forbidden to them, and then feared God and did good, after it was forbidden, which is His statement: But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, (al-Baqarah 2:275).

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten

, meaning men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who died while drinking alcohol before alcohol was forbidden. There was no blame upon them for it before it was forbidden, but when it was forbidden they said: How can it be forbidden to us when our brothers died while drinking it? So God, the Most High, revealed:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten
, if they fear God and believe and do righteous deeds, meaning: There is no blame upon them for what they used to drink before I forbade it, if they were doers of good and righteous,
h
and God loves the doers of good

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten
, for those who drank alcohol and were killed with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Badr and Uhud.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds

, the verse. This is regarding alcohol. When it was forbidden, they asked the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Our brothers who died while drinking it? Then God, the Most High, revealed this verse.

x: God Almighty says:
h
O you who have believed
in God and His Messenger, God will surely test you with something of the game. He says: God will surely test you, with something of the game, meaning: with some of the game.

c: God Almighty informed them that
m: He would test them with something, because He did not test them with sea catch, but rather He tested them with land catch, so the test is with some, not all. His saying: Your hands can reach it, means: either by hand, like eggs and chicks, or by hitting arrows and spears, like donkeys, cows, and gazelles. So He tests you with it while you are in a state of ihram for your Umrah or your Hajj.

x: A group of interpreters said something similar.
Who said that?

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears may reach
, he said: Your hands means small game, taking chicks and eggs, and the spears he said: large game.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Your hands and spears will reach it, he said: The arrows, your spears, will reach the large game, and your hands! will reach the small game, taking the chicks and eggs.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears can reach, he said: That which you cannot separate from the game.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: your hands and your spears, he said: It is the weak and small game, with which God Almighty tests His servants during their state of ihram, so that if they wanted to, they could reach it with their hands. But God forbade them from approaching it.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Hamid al-Araj and Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears may reach
, he said: chicks and eggs, and what cannot escape.

x: God Almighty means: God will test you, O believers, with some hunting while you are in a state of ihram, so that He may know who are the people of obedience to God and faith in Him, and who adhere to His limits, commands and prohibitions, and who fears God and avoids what He has forbidden and avoids it for fear of His punishment, in the unseen, meaning: in this world, such that He does not see it. We have shown that the unseen is the source of the saying of the speaker, This matter is hidden from me, so it is hidden, unseen, and that what is not witnessed, the Arabs call it unseen. The interpretation of the statement is: So that the guardians of God may know who fears God and avoids the prohibitions that He has forbidden him, such as hunting and other things, such that he does not see or witness it. As for his saying:
h
But whoever transgresses after

that, he means: whoever transgresses the limit that God set for him, after he was afflicted with the prohibition of hunting for him while it was forbidden, and he made lawful what God had forbidden for him by taking it and killing it, for him is a painful punishment, from God, meaning: painful and hurtful.

God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, Do not kill game, which I have explained to you, and it is game on land, not game on the sea, while you are in a state of ihram, meaning: while you are in a state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah. Al-Haram is the plural of Haram, and both males and females are pronounced the same. You say: This is a forbidden man and This is a forbidden woman.
Muharram, the woman is called: Muharram. Ihram is entering into it.

The people entered into ihram if they entered the forbidden month, or into the sanctuary. The interpretation of the words: Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah. And His saying: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, this is an announcement from God Almighty to His servants of the ruling on the one who kills the game that He forbade him from killing intentionally. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of deliberate killing for which God obligated its owner to pay expiation and penalty for killing game.

Some of them said: It is the intentional killing of the game, while the killer forgot that he was in a state of ihram when he killed it. He said: If he killed it while remembering that he was in a state of ihram and deliberately killed it, then there is no judgment against him, and his matter is up to God. They said: This is too great a matter for him to be judged, or for him to have an expiation.
Who said that?

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed in livestock. Whoever among you kills him forgetting that he is in a state of ihram, intentionally killing him, then he is the one who is judged. But if he kills him remembering that he is in a state of ihram, intentionally killing him, then he is not judged.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the one who kills game intentionally while knowing that it is in a state of ihram, and intentionally kills it, he said: He is not to be judged, and he does not have to perform Hajj. And his statement, And whoever among you kills it intentionally, he said: It is the deliberate act that requires expiation, and in it is expiation and error, that he strikes it while forgetting his state of ihram, intentionally killing it, or he strikes it while intending something else. So he is judged once.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. And whoever among you kills it intentionally,” not forgetting its sanctity, nor intending anything else, then it is permissible, and he has no dispensation. And whoever kills it forgetfully, or intending something else but mistakenly, then that is the deliberate act that leads to expiation. Surat al-Ma’idah 5:95 O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. And whoever among you kills it intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering delivered to the Ka'bah, or as an expiation, the feeding of poor people, or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the evil consequences of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past. And whoever returns [to sin] - Allah will take vengeance on him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.

c: Yaqub told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, he said: intentionally killing him, forgetting his state of ihram.

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Al-Fudayl bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Deliberate is the mistake that leads to expiation.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Laith told us, Mujahid said:
m: God’s statement:
h
And whoever among you kills him intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock

, he said: The intentional killing that God mentioned is that he hits the game while intending something else and he hits it, so this is the intentional killing that requires expiation. As for the one who kills it without realizing or intending something else, then he is not judged. This is too great for him to be judged.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, they said, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of al-Haytham, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: that he said
m: regarding this verse: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, he said: He kills him intentionally to kill him, forgetting his ihram.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Haytham, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, not forgetting his sanctity or intending something else, then it is permissible, and he has no concession. And whoever kills him forgetting his sanctity, or intending something else but made a mistake, then that is the deliberate act that leads to expiation.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, while hunting, forgetting his state of ihram, then whoever transgresses after that, intentionally while hunting, remembering his state of ihram.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, Ismail bin Muslim told us:
m: Al-Hasan used to issue a fatwa regarding someone who killed game intentionally while remembering that he was in a state of ihram: He should not be judged. Ismail said: Hammad said, on the authority of Ibrahim, something similar. Amr ibn Ali narrated, Affan ibn Muslim narrated, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated: Jaʿfar ibn Abi Wahshiyah ordered me to ask Amr ibn Dinar about this verse:
h
And whoever among you kills him intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock

, the verse. So I asked him, and he said: Ata’ used to say: He has the choice, whatever he wants he can do. If he wants he can offer a sacrifice, or feed others, or fast. So I told Jaʿfar about it and said: What did you hear about it? He hesitated for a while, then he started laughing and did not tell me, then he said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr used to say: He is required to offer a sacrifice from livestock to the Kaʿbah, but food and fasting were made expiation, so this does not amount to the price of the sacrifice, and fasting for it is from three to ten days.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ ibn Yazid told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, he said, Mujahid said:
m: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, not forgetting his sanctity, nor intending anything other than that, then it is permissible, and there is no dispensation for him. And whoever kills him forgetfully, or intending something other than that but made a mistake, then that is the deliberate act that leads to expiation.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: As for the one who deliberately hunts while forgetting its sanctity, or is ignorant that killing it is not forbidden, these are the ones who are judged. As for the one who kills it deliberately after God has forbidden it, and he knows that it is forbidden, and that it is forbidden, then he is entrusted to God’s vengeance, and that is the one upon whom God has placed the vengeance.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, he said: intentionally killing him, forgetting his ihram.

x: Others said: Rather, this is the intentional killing of game by a pilgrim in ihram, remembering its sanctity.
Who said that?

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us
m: - and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us - on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: He is judged in the case of deliberate, accidental, and forgetful acts.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, and Amr ibn Ali told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Tawus said:
m: By God, God only said: And whoever among you kills him intentionally.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, some of our companions told me, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, that he said:
m: The Qur’an was revealed regarding intentional killing, and the Sunnah applies to error, meaning: regarding a pilgrim who hits game.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram, he said: If he kills it intentionally or forgetfully, he is punished. But if he does it again intentionally, the punishment is hastened for him, unless God forgives.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: The expiation was only made for deliberate killing, but it was made more severe for them in the case of an accident so that they would be cautious.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah and Waki’ told us, they said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Nafi’ bin Yazid told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said:
m: Tawus used to say: By God, God only said: And whoever among you kills him intentionally.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, has forbidden the killing of game on land for every pilgrim in a state of ihram as long as he is in a state of ihram, by His saying: O you who believe! Do not kill game. Then He explained the ruling for whoever kills such game while in a state of ihram. Rather, the revelation made it general in requiring the penalty for every intentional killer of game while in a state of ihram. It is not permissible to refer the apparent meaning of the revelation to an inner interpretation that is not indicated by a text in the Book, nor a report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor a consensus from the ummah, nor any indication from any of these aspects. If this is the case, then whether the one who killed the game was one of the people in ihram, intentionally killing it while in ihram, or intentionally killing it while forgetting his ihram, or intending to kill someone else and killing it while remembering his ihram, then all of them must pay the penalty that our Lord, the Most High, mentioned, has said, which is: the equivalent of the livestock he killed, to be judged by two just Muslims, or the expiation of feeding the poor, or the equivalent of that in fasting.
