evidence.text: The majority of the people of Medina and some of the people of Basra read it as: Then the recompense is like that which was killed of the livestock, by adding the recompense to the like, and lowering the like.

The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as: Then the penalty is like what he killed with the tanween of the penalty and the raising of the like, with the interpretation: then upon him is the penalty like what he killed.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: Then the recompense is like what he killed with the tanween of the recompense and the raising of the example because the recompense is the example, so there is no reason to add the thing to itself.
I think that those who read it with the addition saw that it is obligatory for the one who kills the game to reward the like of it in game with the like of it in livestock.
For this reason, no reader we know read it with the tanween and the accusative of the like.
Likewise the reward if it were not the example, then the reading of the example in the accusative case would be expanded if the reward was put in the noon case.

But that was too narrow, so no one read it with the tanween of al-jaza’ and the accusative of al-mithl, since al-mithl was al-jaza’, and the meaning of the statement was: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, upon him is a penalty equal to what he killed of livestock.
There are different readings of this: So I read it as the people of Medina generally read it, or as an expiation for feeding the poor in addition.
As for the reading of the people of Iraq, most of them read it with the tanween of expiation and raising the food: or expiation of feeding the poor.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of the one who reads with the tanween of expiation and the raising of the food, for the reason we mentioned in his statement: Then the recompense is like that of the livestock killed.
Then he recited this verse: “But if he returns, God will take vengeance on him.

x: God Almighty says: Lawful for you, O believers, is sea game, which is what is caught fresh, such as:

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Umar ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab told you about his statement:
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
, he said: Its game, whatever is caught from it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Samak, he said,
m: I was told on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: It is permissible for you to hunt in the sea. He said: So hunting is what is taken.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
, he said: Its game, whatever is caught from it.

c: Sulayman bin Umar bin Khalid Al-Raqi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Salamah Al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
, he said: Its game, fresh.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hudhayl bin Bilal told us, Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea
, he said: Its game, whatever is hunted.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
, he said: The sea urchin.

c: Ibn Wakeeʿ told us, he said, Al-Hasan ibn ʿAli Al-Hanafi told us
m: - or: Al-Husayn, Abu Jaʿfar was not sure - on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, he said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: The game of the sea is what is caught.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Permissible for you is the game of the sea. He said: Fresh.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Badr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said:
m: Sea game means what is caught.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Permissible for you is the game of the sea. He said: Fresh.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: It is permissible for you to catch fish from the sea, he said: fresh fish.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Permissible for you is sea fishing. As for sea fishing, it is the fish, which are whales.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said:
m: His prey, what you hunt fresh - Muammar said, and Qatada said: His prey, what you hunt.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
, he said: its whales.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, he said:
m: Saeed was asked about sea hunting, so he said, Makhul said, Zaid bin Thabit said: Its hunting, what you hunt.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and for the travelers
, he said: The pilgrim and the non-pilgrim may hunt from the sea and eat from their catch.

c: Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Abu Bakr said:
m: The food of the sea is everything in it. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: Whatever is uncovered, eat. And he said: Everything in it, meaning Surat al-Ma’idah 5:96
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered. everything that is caught.

c: Saeed ibn al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr,
m: he heard Ikrimah say: Abu Bakr said:
h
And its food is provision for you and for the travelers
, he said: It is everything in it. In this context, the word sea refers to all rivers. The Arabs call rivers seas, as God Almighty said: Corruption has appeared on land and sea (al-Rum 30:41).

x: The interpretation of the statement is: It is permissible for you, O believers, to eat fresh river fish that you caught during your time of pilgrimage and your sanctuary, and what you did not catch of its food that it killed and then threw on its shore.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of his saying: and his food.
Some of them said: What he meant by that is: what was thrown to its shore dead, similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Samak, he said,
m: I was told on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: Lawful for you is the hunting of the sea and its food as
h
provision for you
, and its food is what is thrown up.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Umar ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: I was in Bahrain, and they asked me about what the sea casts up. He said: I gave them a fatwa that they should eat it. When I came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, I mentioned that to him, and he said to me: What did you give them a fatwa on? I said: Did you give them a fatwa that they should eat it? He said: If I had given them a fatwa other than that, I would have beaten you with a whip! He said: Then he said: God Almighty said in His Book:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
. So its game is what is caught from it, and its food is what is cast up.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
and its food as
h
provision for you
, he said: Its food is what is thrown up.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food
, he said: Its food is what is thrown up.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hussain bin Ali told us, on the authority of Zaida, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: His food is everything that the sea throws up.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Hasan bin Ali told us
m: - or: Al-Hussein bin Ali Al-Hanafi, Abu Jaafar was not sure - on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: His food is what he expels from his dead body.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hudhayl bin Bilal told us, Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
and its food, he said: Its food is what is found dead on the shore.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: His food is what he threw away.

c: Saeed bin al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr,
m: he heard Ikrimah say: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: And his food is
h
provision for you
, he said: His food is everything in it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Amr ibn Dinar told me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Bakr said: And his food is a
h
provision for you
, he said: His food is his dead body. Amr said: I heard Abu al-Sha’tha’ say: I did not think his food was anything but his salt.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ad-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Umar bin Saad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And its food is provision for you
, he said: Its food is its dead body.

c: Humaid bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And his food is
h
provision for you
. He said: His food is what he threw up.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muammar ibn Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I heard Ubaydullah, on the authority of Nafi', he said: Abd al-Rahman came to Abdullah and said: The sea has thrown up many whales? He said: So he forbade him from eating them, then he said: O Nafi', bring me the Qur'an! So I brought it to him, and he recited this verse:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
. I said: Its food is what it has thrown up. He said: So catch up with it and order it to eat it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’:
m: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayrah asked Ibn Umar, saying: The sea has thrown up many dead whales, so can we eat them? He said: Do not eat them! So when Abdullah returned to his family, he took the Qur’an and read Surat al-Ma’idah, and he came to this verse:
h
And its food is provision for you and for the travelers
. He said: Go and tell him to eat it, for it is his food.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ad-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Amr bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, he said, Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, said:
h
And its food is provision for you
, he said: its dead body. Amr said: I heard Abu Al-Shatha’ say: I did not think its food was anything but its saltiness.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Ad-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Nafi’ told us:
m: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hurayrah asked Ibn Umar about many whales that the sea had thrown up, Are they dead? He said, Yes! So he forbade him from doing so, then he entered the house and called for the Qur’an and recited the following verse:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
. He said, “Its food, everything taken out of it, so eat it, there is no harm in it. And everything in it may be eaten, dead or on its shores.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, Qatada said:
m: (His food is what he ejaculates from it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, he said:
m: Whatever the sea throws up is its food, even if it is dead.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr, he said:
m: Abu Ayoub was asked about the statement of God Almighty:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food
as provision, he said: It is what the sea throws up.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying: and its food is the salty fish, so the interpretation of the speech according to that is their interpretation: The fish of the sea and its salty fish are permissible for you in every case, in the case of your being in ihram and in the state of your being in ihram.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman bin Omar bin Khalid Al-Raqi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And his food, he said: his food, the salty part of it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And its food is a
h
provision for you
, meaning: with its food, its saltiness, and what the sea throws up of it, its saltiness.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And its food is a
h
provision for you
, and it is salty.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Majma’ al-Taymi, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
For your enjoyment
, he said: The beautiful.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas and Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: The handsome man Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And his food is a
h
provision for you
, he said: The good, and what is the wording.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
, he said: A man comes to the people of the sea and says: Feed me!

x: If he says: A fish, they cast their net and catch it for him. And if he says: Feed me from your food, they feed him from their salted fish.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed:
m: Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food. He said: The abandoned fish, the salted fish.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And his food, he said: salty.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And his food, he said: It is his food. Then he said: What he slandered.

c: Ibn Muadh told us, he said, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And his food, he said: salted fish.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Al-Thawri told me, on the authority of Mansur, he said:
m: Ibrahim used to say: His food is good fish. Then he said after that: What he threw away.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: His food is good.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: His food is good fish.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And its food is provision for you
, he said: The salty water. Shuʿbah said, so I said to Abu Bishr: What is the salty water? He said: The salty water.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Hisham bin Al-Waleed told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Wahshiyya, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr,
m: Surat al-Ma’idah 5:96
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered. regarding his statement:
h
And its food is provision for you
, he said: The salty food. I said: What is the salty food? He said: The salty food.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And his food is a
h
provision for you
, he said: As for his food, it is salty.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab:
m: And his food is
h
provision for you
, he said: His food is what you take with you salted on your journey.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid and Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, he said, Jaber bin Zaid said:
m: We used to say that his food was good, but we disliked what was floating around in it.

x: Others said: (His food) is what is in it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Seafood is what is in it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Harith, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And his food is
h
provision for you
, he said: What the sea brings with its waves, like this.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Hassan bin Saleh, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: His food is everything that is hunted from it.

x: The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: His food is what the sea throws up, or what is uncovered and found dead on its shore. This is because God Almighty mentioned before it the game that is hunted, and said:
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea

, so what must be connected to it in the concept is what is not hunted from it, so He said: Lawful to you is what you hunt from the sea, and what you do not hunt from it. As for the salty, whatever is salty after being caught is included in the statement,
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
, so there is no point in repeating it, as there is no benefit in it. And He, the Most High, has informed His servants that what is caught from the sea is lawful by His statement,
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea

. So there is no benefit in saying to them after that, And the salty which is caught is lawful to you, because whatever is caught from it, He has made lawful, whether it is fresh or salty, by His statement,
h
Lawful to you is the game of the sea
, and God is too exalted to address His servants with what does not benefit them.

It has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what we have mentioned, even though some of its transmitters depend on the one who transmitted it from him from the Companions, and that is what:

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, he said, Abu Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said,
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food as
h
provision for you
. He said: Its food, whatever it throws up dead is its food.

x: Some of them attributed this hadith to Abu Hurairah.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food
, he said: its food is what it throws up dead.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
For your enjoyment

, a benefit for whoever among you is a resident or present in his country, who enjoys its food and benefits from it, and for the traveler, meaning: And also a benefit and enjoyment for those traveling from one land to another, and travelers who take it as a good provision for their journey. And 1 for a car, plural car. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Ishaq told me on the authority of Ikrimah that he said
m: regarding his statement: Provisions for you and for the travelers, he said: for those who are by the sea, and for the travelers, the journey.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Abi ʿAruba, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And its food is provision for you and for the travelers
, what the sea throws up, and what they take with them on their journeys from this salty food, he interprets it in this way.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Jami’ bin Hammad told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And its food is provision for you and for the travelers
, salted fish, what they stock up on during their travels.

c: Sulayman bin Umar bin Khalid Al-Raqi told us, he said, Maskeen bin Bakir told us, he said, Abd Al-Salam bin Habib Al-Najjari told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement: and for the travelers, he said: They are the ones who are in ihram.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And its food is provision for you and for the travelers
. As for its food, it is the salty part of it, a provision that travelers eat from it on journeys.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And its food is provision for you and for the travelers

, he said: Its food is its saltiness, and what the sea throws up of it, which the traveler takes as provisions. And he said another time: its saltiness, and what the sea throws up. So its saltiness is what the traveler takes as provisions.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And its food is provision for you and for the travelers
, meaning: the salt-eater takes provisions from it. Mujahid used to say about this:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And its food is provision for you
, he said: the people of the villages, and for the travelers, the people of the cities.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Provision for you

, he said: for the people of the villages, and for the travelers, he said: the people of the cities, and the whales are for all people. What Mujahid said: that the travelers are the people of the cities, has no clear basis, unless he meant by his saying: they are the people of the cities, the travelers from the people of the cities, so it must be included in that every traveler, whether they are from the people of the cities or from the people of the villages. As for the travelers, we do not understand it: those residing in their cities.

x: God Almighty means: And God has forbidden you, O believers, to hunt on land, as long as you are in a state of ihram, meaning: As long as you are in a state of ihram, you have not yet ended your state of ihram. Then the scholars differed about the meaning that God Almighty meant by His saying,
h
He has forbidden you to hunt on land
Some of them said: He meant by that that he forbade us all meanings of hunting on land: hunting, eating, killing, selling, buying, holding, and owning.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Uthman bin Affan performed Hajj, and Ali performed Hajj with him. He said: Then some meat of game that he had hunted was brought to Uthman, and he ate from it, but Ali did not eat. Uthman said: By God, we did not hunt, nor did we command, nor did we advise! Ali said: And hunting on land is forbidden to you as long as you are in a state of ihram. Ibn Hamid narrated, Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Subaih ibn Abdullah al-Absi, who said: Uthman ibn Affan sent Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith to the battlefield. He stopped at Qudayd and a man from the Levant passed by with a hawk and a falcon. He borrowed them from him and hunted some jaguars with them and put them in a pen. When Uthman passed by, he cooked them and brought them to him. Uthman said: Eat!

x: Some of them said: Until Ali ibn Abi Talib comes, may God have mercy on him. When he came and saw what was in front of them, Ali said: We will not eat it! Uthman said: Why don’t you eat it? He said: It is game, and it is not permissible to eat it while I am in a state of ihram! Uthman said: Explain it to us! Ali said: O you who believe! Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. Uthman said: Did we kill it? So he recited to him:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
and for travelers. But forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in a state of ihram.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir and Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Qanad narrated to us, they said: Ishaq Al-Azraq informed us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Subaih bin Abdullah Al-Absi, he said:
m: Uthman bin Affan appointed Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith over the prosody, then he mentioned something similar and added to it, he said: Uthman stayed as long as God willed him to stay, then he came and it was said to him in Mecca: Would you like to have a donkey’s udder presented to Ibn Abi Talib so he can eat from it! So Uthman sent to him and asked him about eating udder, he said: As for you, you eat it, but as for us, you forbid us? He said: It is the game of the first year and I am lawful, so there is no harm in eating it, and I hunted that - meaning the Yaqoob - while I was in a state of ihram, and slaughtered it while I was in a state of ihram.

c: Imran bin Musa Al-Qazzaz told us, he said, Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Omar bin Al-Khattab did not see anything wrong with the meat of game for the pilgrim, and Ali bin Abi Talib disliked it, may God be pleased with them both.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told us, he said, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab:
m: Ali disliked the meat of game for the pilgrim in all cases.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith:
m: That he witnessed Uthman and Ali being brought meat, and Uthman ate it but Ali did not. Uthman said: Did we hunt or was it hunted for us? So Ali recited this verse:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
and for travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in a state of ihram.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Umar ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Uthman ibn Affan performed Hajj, and Ali performed Hajj with him. Then some game meat was brought to him that he had hunted while in a state of ihram, so he ate some of it while in a state of ihram, but Ali did not eat any of it. Uthman said: It was hunted before we entered the state of ihram! Ali said to him: We have come down and our families are lawful for us, Surat al-Ma’idah 5:96
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you
and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered. so will it be lawful for us today?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abd al-Karim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal:
m: Ali was brought a piece of a donkey’s rump while he was in a state of ihram, and he said: I am in a state of ihram.

c: Ibn Buzayʿ told us, he said, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Yaʿla ibn Hakim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he disliked it in all cases, as long as it was forbidden.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Nafi’ told us:
m: Ibn Umar disliked everything from hunting that was forbidden, whether it was taken for him or not, and the Shaiqa and other things.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Abdullah, he said, Nafi’ told me:
m: Ibn Omar did not eat game while he was in a state of ihram, even if it was hunted by a lawful person.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Al-Hasan bin Muslim bin Yanaq told me:
m: That Tawus used to forbid the forbidden from eating game, and the Shaiqa and other things, that he had hunted and had not hunted for him.

c: Abdul A’la told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Al-Ash’ath told us, Al-Hasan said:
m: If someone hunts game and then enters ihram, he should not eat its meat until he becomes halal. If he eats it while in ihram, Al-Hasan does not see anything wrong with him. Ibn Humayd narrated that Hakam and Harun narrated on the authority of Anbasa on the authority of Salim who said: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about game caught by a lawful person, can a person in ihram eat from it? He said: I will tell you about that. God the Almighty said: O you who believe! Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram, and He forbade killing it. Then He said: And whoever among you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from sacrificial animals, then He the Almighty said:
h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you

and for travelers, he said: A man comes to the people of the sea and says: Feed me, and if he says: Gharidh, they cast their net and catch for him, and if he says: Feed me from your food, they feed him from their salted fish. Then He said: And forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in a state of ihram, and it is forbidden to you, whether you hunt it or it is hunted by a lawful person.

x: Others said: What God Almighty meant by His statement: And forbidden to you is the game of land as long as you are in a state of ihram, is what the pilgrim hunts and slaughters while in a state of ihram, or what is newly slaughtered for him in that state. As for what he slaughters, which is lawful and for the lawful, there is no problem for the pilgrim to eat it. Likewise, what was in his possession before his state of ihram, it is not forbidden for him to keep it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie’ told us, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, Saeed told us, Qatada told us: Saeed bin al-Musayyab told him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah:
m: He was asked about game that was hunted by a lawful person, can a person in ihram eat it? He said: So he gave him a fatwa allowing him to eat it, then he met Umar bin al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, and informed him of what had happened to him, so he said: If you had given them a fatwa other than this, I would have given you a headache.

c: Ahmad bin Abda Al-Dhabi told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Omar bin Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Uthman bin Affan, may God have mercy on him, stopped at Al-Arj while he was in a state of ihram, and the owner of Al-Arj gave him a cat as a gift. He said: So he said to his companions: Eat, for it was hunted in my name. He said: So they ate, but he did not eat.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Al-Musayyab:
m: Abu Hurairah was in Al-Rabdhah, and they asked him about the meat of game that he had hunted that was permissible, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Buzay’ on the authority of Bishr.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saʿid Ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of Umar,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Sha’tha’, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Umar about the meat of game that is given as a gift from the lawful to the unlawful. He said: Umar ate it, and he saw no harm in it. I said: Do you eat it? He said: Umar is better than me.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, he said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Sha’tha’, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Umar about game that was hunted by lawful animals and that was eaten by unlawful animals. He said: Umar used to eat it. I said: What about you? He said: Umar was better than me.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: A man from the people of Ash-Sham asked me about the meat of game that he had caught while he was in a state of ihram, so I ordered him to eat it. Then I went to Umar ibn Al-Khattab and said to him: A man from the people of Ash-Sham asked me about the meat of game that he had caught while he was in a state of ihram. He said: What is your fatwa? I said: I told him to eat it. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I had told him anything else, I would have beaten you with a whip! Umar said: I was only forbidden from hunting it. Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Musʿab bin Al-Muqaddam narrated, he said: Kharijah narrated, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ, on the authority of Kaʿb, he said: I came with some people in ihram, and we found the meat of a wild donkey. The people asked me about eating it, so I gave them a fatwa permitting them to eat it while they were in ihram.

c: So we went to ʿUmar and told him that
m: I had given them a fatwa permitting them to eat the meat of a wild donkey while they were in ihram. ʿUmar said: I have ordered it over you until you return.
b.via: So we went to ʿUmar and

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: I passed by Ar-Rabadha, and its people asked me about a person in ihram eating what a person in ihram hunted.

c: So I told them that
m: they should eat. I met Umar bin Al-Khattab and mentioned that to him. He said: What did you tell them? He said: I told them that they should eat. He said: If you told them anything else, I would have opposed you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Abu al-Sha’tha’ al-Kindi, who said:
m: I said to Ibn Umar: What do you think of a people who are forbidden and who meet people who are lawful and have with them the meat of game, so they either sell it to them or feed it to them? He said: It is lawful.

c: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Saeed narrated to us, he said: Hisham - meaning Ibn Urwah - narrated to us, he said: Urwah narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Hatib: Abd Al-Rahman narrated to him:
m: He performed Umrah with Uthman bin Affan in a group that included Amr bin Al-Aas, until they stopped at Al-Rawha’, and a bird drank to them while they were in the state of Ihram, so Uthman said to them: Eat, for I will not eat it! Amr bin Al-Aas said: Are you ordering us to do something that I will not eat? Uthman said: If I did not think that it was hunted because of me, I would have eaten! So the people ate.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Hisham Ibn ʿUrwah, on the authority of his father:
m: Al-Zubayr used to stock up on the meat of wild animals while he was in a state of ihram.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Whatever is hunted or slaughtered while you are lawful is lawful for you, and whatever is hunted or slaughtered while you are unlawful is unlawful for you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Whatever is hunted while you are in a state of ihram is forbidden to you, and whatever is hunted while you are in a state of ihram is permissible for you.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram, so he made the game forbidden for the pilgrim to hunt and eat as long as he is in the state of ihram. If the game was hunted before the man entered the state of ihram, then it is permissible. But if a pilgrim hunts it for a permissible reason, then it is not permissible for him to eat it.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us:
m: I asked Abu Bishr about the person in ihram eating what a lawful person hunted. He said: Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid used to say: Whatever is hunted before he becomes ihram may be eaten, and whatever is hunted after he becomes ihram may not be eaten.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us:
m: When Ata’ was asked publicly: Can the forbidden person eat the dried meat? he would say to himself: “I cannot explain to you in a gathering. If it was slaughtered before we declared it forbidden, then eat it. Otherwise, do not sell its meat or purchase anything.”

x: Others said: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And He has forbidden you to hunt on land while you are in a state of ihram

, and He has forbidden you to hunt it. They said: As for buying it from someone who owns it, slaughtering it, and eating it, after he has owned it for a purpose other than hunting it, and selling and buying it is permissible. They said: The prohibition from God Almighty is to hunt it while in a state of ihram, not the other meanings.
Who said that?

c: Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwaih told me, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said: Yahya bin Ayoub told us, he said: Yahya told me:
m: Abu Salamah bought a cat while he was in Al-Arj, and he was in a state of ihram, and Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir was with him, and he ate it. So the people criticized him for that.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, mentioned that He prohibited all types of land hunting for the pilgrim in his state of ihram, without specifying one thing over another.

All types of hunting are forbidden for the pilgrim as long as he is in ihram, including selling it, buying it, hunting it, killing it, and other types of hunting, unless he finds it slaughtered by someone lawful for someone lawful, in which case it is permissible for him to eat it, based on the established report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said:

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Abdul Malik ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir informed me, on the authority of Muadh ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman, on the authority of his Surat al-Ma’idah 5:
m: h
Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you

and the travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered. father Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman, saying: We were with Talhah ibn Ubaydullah while we were in ihram, and a bird was given to us as a gift. Some of us ate it, and some of us were cautious and did not eat it. When Talhah woke up, he rewarded those who ate it and said: We ate it with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).

x: What do you say about what was narrated on the authority of al-Sa’ib ibn Jaththama that a man gave the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) a wild donkey dripping with blood, but he returned it and said: We are in ihram? And what was narrated on the authority of Aisha that a young gazelle was given as a gift to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was in ihram, so he returned it, and similar reports?

There is no statement in any of these reports that came with this meaning that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rejected what he rejected, and the slaughterer slaughtered it, as he slaughtered it while it was permissible for someone who was permissible, then he presented it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while it was forbidden, so he returned it and said: It is not permissible for us because we are in a state of ihram. Rather, it was mentioned in it that the meat of a hunted animal was presented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he returned it. It may be permissible that he rejected it because the slaughterer slaughtered it or the hunter hunted it for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in a state of ihram. Jabir’s report on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained his saying: The meat of game on land is permissible for the pilgrim in ihram, except for what he hunted or what was hunted for him. The meaning of all of this is: Since both reports are authentic in their source, it is obligatory to believe them, and to direct each one of them to the correct one from the aspect, and to say: (Return what he returned from that because it was hunted for him, and his permission to eat what he permitted to eat from it, because it was not hunted by a pilgrim nor was it hunted by a pilgrim, so the meaning of both reports is correct.
They differed about the description of the game that God Almighty meant by prohibition in His saying: And forbidden to you is the game of land as long as you are in the state of ihram.
Some of them said: The game of land is everything that lives on land and in the sea, and the game of the sea is what lives in the water rather than on land and takes refuge in it.
Who said that?

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: And hunting on land is forbidden to you as long as you are in a state of ihram. He said: Whatever lives on land and in the sea, do not hunt it, but whatever lives in the water, that is it.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Whatever lives in the desert and is struck by something forbidden, then it is upon him to pay the penalty, such as turtles, crabs, and frogs.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Qais, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: Everything that lives on land or in the sea and is touched by a person in ihram must pay expiation.

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: We went out as pilgrims with a man from the people of al-Sawad who had a water bird with him, and my father said to him when we entered ihram: Separate this from us.
b.via: Abd al-Malik ibn Sa’id ibn Jubayr

c: Abu Kuraib told us
m: about it another time. He said, Ibn Idris told us. He said, I heard Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad say, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’: He disliked for the pilgrim to slaughter a Negro chicken, because it has a root in the land.

x: Some of them said: Land hunting is what is hunted on land more than at sea.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said:
m: I asked Ata’ about the offspring of water, is it hunted on land or in the sea? And about the likes of it? He said: Wherever it is more, it is its hunt.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Waki’ told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, who said:
m: It is most often found where it spawns, so it is from it.

x: This is an advance from God, the Most High, to His creation to warn against His punishment for His disobedience. God, the Most High, says: “And fear God, O people, and beware of Him by obeying Him in what He has commanded you of His obligations, and in what He has forbidden you from in these verses that He revealed to your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the prohibition of alcohol, gambling, idols, and arrows, and from hunting and killing game in the land while you are in a state of ihram and at other times, for your final destination and return is to God, so He will punish you for your disobedience to Him, and He will reward you and reward you for your obedience to Him.”

evidence.text: So I brought it to him, and he recited this verse: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you.
So Ali recited this verse: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and for travelers, but forbidden to you is game from the land as long as you are in a state of ihram.

x: God Almighty says: God made the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House, a support for people who have no leader to protect their strong from their weak, their evildoers from their good, and their oppressors from their oppressed,
h
and the sacred month

, and the offerings, and the garlands. So with each one of these He protected some of them from others, since they had no support other than it, and He made them landmarks for their religion and the interests of their affairs. The Kaaba was called, as it is said, Kaaba because of its square shape.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: It was called the Kaaba because it is square.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Mu’addab, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: It was called the Kaaba because of its squareness. It was said: Qiyaman li-nas with a ya’, and it is one of the words with a waw, because of the kasra of the qaf, which is the fa’ of the verb, so the ‘ayn was made from it with a kasra ya’, as was said in the source: qamat (qiyam) and samat (siyaman), so the ‘ayn was changed from the verb: which is a waw to a ya’ because of the kasra of its fa’. Rather, it is originally: qamat qiwaman and samat sawaman, and likewise his saying:
h
God made the Kaaba

, the Sacred House, a place of standing for people, so its waw was changed to a ya’, because it is qawam. This came from their speech, stated according to its origin, which is its origin. The rajaz poet said: The foundation of the world and the foundation of religion So he brought it with the letter waw according to its origin. God Almighty made the Kaaba, the sacred month, the sacrificial animals, and the necklaces a pillar for those Arabs who forbade that, and with His greatness, he was like a leader who carries out the affairs of his followers. As for the Kaaba, it is the entire sanctuary. God Almighty called it sacred because He forbade it from being hunted, or secluded in its wasteland, or cutting its trees. We have already explained this with evidence in what came before. And His statement:
h
And the sacred month

, and the offerings, and the garlands, God Almighty says: And He made the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands also a means of support for the people, just as He made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of support for them. The people who made this a cause for them are different.

x: Some of them said: God made that in the pre-Islamic era a means of support for all people.

Some of them said: Rather, He meant the Arabs in particular. And the people of interpretation said the same as what we said in the interpretation of the standing, the people of interpretation mentioned. He mentioned those who said: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
God made the Kaaba
, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, the standing, in the same way as we said.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said,
m: we were told by someone who heard Khasif narrating on the authority of Mujahid regarding:
h
God made the Kaaba
, the Sacred House, a support for the people, he said: a support for the people.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Standing for the people, he said: improving their religion.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding:
h
God made the Kaaba
, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, he said: When they neither hope for Paradise nor fear Hell, then God made that more severe with Islam.

c: Hanad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his saying:
h
God made the Kaaba
, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, he said: a means of strengthening their religion.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God has made the Kaaba
, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, he said, its support means that whoever turns towards it is safe.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
God made the Kaaba
, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people,
h
and the sacred month
, and the offerings, and the garlands, meaning: a means of support for their religion, and landmarks for their pilgrimage.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
God made the Kaaba

, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, and the Sacred Month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands. God made these four means of support for the people, and they are the foundation of their affairs.

x: Although the wording of these statements differed among those who said them, their meanings lead to what we said about that, that the foundation of a thing is that by which it is improved, just as the greatest king is the foundation of his subjects and those under his authority, because he is the manager of their affairs, and prevents their oppressors from their oppressed, and defends them from the hatred of those who rebel against them and are hostile to them. Likewise, the Kaaba, the Sacred Month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands were the foundation of the Arabs’ affairs, by which they were improved in the pre-Islamic era. In Islam, they are landmarks for its people in their pilgrimage and rituals, and the direction of their prayers, and their qiblah by which their obligation is fulfilled.
A group of the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Jami' bin Hammad narrated, Yazid bin Zari' narrated, Sayyid narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
God has made the Ka'bah
, the Sacred House, a means of support for mankind,
h
and the sacred month

, the offerings, and the garlands, barriers that God left between people in the Age of Ignorance. If a man committed any crime and then sought refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary, he would not touch it or come near it. If a man met his father's killer in the sacred month, he would not attack him or come near him. When a man wanted to enter the House, he would wear a necklace of hair that would protect him and prevent him from people. When he fled, he would wear a necklace of idhkhir or samr bark that would prevent him from people until he reached his family. Barriers that God left between people in the Age of Ignorance.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
God has made the Kaaba
, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people,
h
and the sacred month

, and the offerings, and the garlands, he said: All the people had kings among them who would defend one another. He said: There were no kings among the Arabs who would defend one another, so God, the Most High, made the Sacred House a means of support for them, by which they defend one another,
h
and the sacred month
likewise, God defends one another by the sacred months, and the garlands. He said: And a man meets the killer of his brother or cousin and does not confront him. And all of this has been abrogated.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the necklaces, people used to wear tree bark during the pre-Islamic era when they wanted to perform Hajj, and they were known by that. We have already mentioned the sacred month, the sacrificial animals, and the necklaces in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here.

x: God Almighty means by His saying: That, that He made the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House, a place of standing for the people,
h
and the sacred month

, the offerings, and the necklaces. God Almighty says: I have made that a place of standing for you, O people, so that you may know that He who has introduced for you what He has introduced for your worldly interests, by which you are sustained, out of His knowledge of your benefits and harms, He thus knows all that is in the heavens and on the earth of what is good for you in this world and the next, and so that you may know that He is All-Knowing of everything, nothing of your affairs and deeds is hidden from Him, and He is the Keeper of their records for you, until He rewards the doer of good among you for his good, and the doer of evil among you for his evil.

God Almighty says: Know, O people, that your Lord, who knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and nothing of your secret or public deeds is hidden from Him, and He counts them for you in order to reward you for them, is severe in His punishment of whoever disobeys Him and rebels against Him, for his disobedience to Him, and He is Forgiving of the sins of whoever obeys Him and turns to Him, so He covers them up and leaves his disgrace because of them, and He is Merciful towards him, so that He does not punish him for his past sins after his repentance and repentance from them.

This is a threat and warning from God, the Most High, to His servants. God, the Most High, says: There is nothing upon Our Messenger whom We sent to you, O people, with warning you of Our punishment before a severe torment, and Our excuse to you that would cut off your arguments, except that he delivers Our message to you, then to Us is the reward for obedience, and to Us is the punishment for disobedience, And God knows what you reveal and what you conceal, meaning: And it is not hidden from Us the obedient among you, who accepts Our message, who does what We have commanded him to do, from the disobedient who rejects Our message, who abandons doing what We have commanded him to do, because We know what the worker among you has done and shown with his limbs and uttered with his tongue, and what you conceal, meaning: and what you hide in yourselves of faith and disbelief, or certainty and doubt and hypocrisy. God Almighty says: Whoever is like this, nothing is hidden from him of the secrets of the chests, nor the outward actions of the souls, of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and in his hand is reward and punishment, so he deserves to be feared, and to be obeyed and not disobeyed.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad: The bad and the good, the righteous and the wicked, the obedient and the disobedient are not equal, even if the abundance of the wicked pleases you, meaning: The disobedient and the obedient to God are not equal in the sight of God, even if the people of disobedience were many and you were amazed by their abundance, because the people of obedience to God are the successful ones who win God's reward on the Day of Resurrection, even if they are few, unlike the people of disobedience to Him, and the people of disobedience to Him are the greatest losers and disappointments, even if they are many.

God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be amazed at the number of those who disobey God, and He gives them respite and does not hasten to punish them, for the good end is for those who obey God, with Him, but not them, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: The wicked and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the wicked pleases you. He said: The wicked are the polytheists, and the good are the believers. Although this statement is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is intended for some of his followers, as indicated by his statement: So fear God, O you of understanding, that you may succeed.

x: God Almighty says: And fear God by obeying Him in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, and beware lest Satan take control of you by making you admire the abundance of evil, so that you become one of them, O you of understanding, meaning by that the people of reason and wisdom who acted upon God’s verses and recognized the locations of His proofs, that you may succeed, meaning: Fear God so that you may succeed, that is, so that you may succeed in your pursuit of what is with Him.

It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of questions that people would ask him, sometimes as a test and sometimes as a mockery.

Some of them would say to him: Who is my father? And some of them would say to him when his she-camel got lost: Where is my she-camel? So God, the Most High, said to them: Do not ask about things like that, like the question of Abdullah bin Hudhafah to him about his father, If it were revealed to you, it would distress you, meaning: If We revealed to you the truth of what you are asking about, it would distress you to start it and reveal it. In a manner similar to what we said about that, the report from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has become clear. The novel mentioned that: Abu Kuraib narrated, Hafs ibn Baghail narrated, Zuhair ibn Muawiyah narrated, Abu al-Juwayriyah narrated, Ibn Abbas said to a Bedouin from Banu Salim: Do you know why this verse was revealed:
h
O you who have believed
, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, may distress you?

Until he finished the verse, then he said: There were people who used to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in mockery. A man would say, Who is my father? or a man would lose his camel and say, Where is my camel? So God revealed this verse about them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Abu Amir and Abu Dawud told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said:
m: The people asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they surrounded him with questions. He ascended the pulpit one day and said: Do not ask me about anything except that I will explain it to you! Anas said: “I looked right and left and saw everyone wrapping his garment and weeping. Then a man arose who, when he argued, was called by someone other than his father. He said: O Messenger of God, who is my father? He said: Your father is Hudhafah! Then Umar arose and said: We are pleased with God as our Lord, Islam as our religion, and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as our Messenger. I seek refuge in God from the evil of trials!” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: I have never seen evil and good as they are today! Paradise and Hell were made to appear to me until I saw them behind the wall. Qatada used to mention this hadith when he saw this verse: Do not ask about things which, if made clear to you, would distress you.

c: Muhammad bin Muammar Al-Bahrani told me, he said, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Musa bin Anas told me, he said,
m: I heard Anas say, a man said: O Messenger of God, who is my father? He said: Your father is so-and-so! He said: Then this verse was revealed:
h
O you who have believed
, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated to us, Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
O you who have believed
, do not ask about things which, if made known to you, may distress you, he said: So he narrated to us that Anas bin Malik narrated to them: Surat al-Ma’idah 5:101
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are made clear to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Forbearing. That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked until they surrounded him with questions, so he came out to them one day and ascended the pulpit and said: Do not ask me today about anything except that I will explain it to you! The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were afraid that something was about to happen before him, so I would not turn to the right or to the left except that I would find everyone with his head wrapped in his garment and weeping. Then a man who was being argued with and called to someone other than his father arose and said: O Prophet of God, who is my father? He said: Your father is Hudhafah! Then Umar stood up - or he said: Umar arose - and said: We are pleased with God as our Lord, with Islam as our religion, and with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as our Messenger, seeking refuge in God - or he said: I seek refuge in God - from the evil of trials! He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have never seen such good and evil as today. Heaven and Hell were pictured to me until I saw them beyond the wall.

c: Ahmad bin Hisham and Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, they said: Muadh bin Muadh told us, he said: Ibn Awn told us, he said:
m: I asked Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, about the words of God:
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. He said: That was the day when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among them and said: Do not ask me about anything but that I will inform you of it! A man stood up, and the Muslims disliked his standing that day, so he said: O Messenger of God, who is my father? He said: Your father is Hudhafah. He said: Then this verse was revealed.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: The verse: Do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you was revealed about a man who said: O Messenger of God, who is my father? He said: Your father is so-and-so. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: They asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they overwhelmed him with questions. He stood up angrily and delivered a sermon, saying: Ask me, for by God, as long as I am in this position, you will not ask me about anything except that I will tell you! A man stood up and said: Who is my father? He said: Your father is Hudhafah. His anger became intense and he said: Ask me! When the people saw that, they cried a lot. Umar knelt down and said: We are satisfied with God as our Lord - Muammar said, Al-Zuhri said, Anas said something similar: Umar knelt down and said: We are satisfied with God as our Lord, Islam as our religion, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as our Messenger. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, Paradise and Hell were pictured for me just now across this wall, and I have never seen anything like today in good and evil. Al-Zuhri said: Umm Abdullah ibn Hudhafah said: I have never seen a more disobedient son than you! Do you trust that your mother did what the people of ignorance did, and you disgrace her in front of people!! He said: By God, if he put me in a black slave position, I would join him.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry one day, so he stood up to deliver a sermon and said: Ask me, for you do not ask me about anything except that I will inform you about it! A man from the Quraysh, from Banu Sahm, called Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, who used to slander him, stood up and said: O Messenger of God, who is my father? He said: Your father is so-and-so! So he called him to his father. Umar stood up and kissed his foot and said: O Messenger of God, we are pleased with God as our Lord, with you as our Prophet, with Islam as our religion, and with the Qur’an as our leader, so pardon us, may God pardon you! So he kept on at him until he was pleased. On that day he said: The child belongs to the bed and the adulterer will be stoned.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out angry and his face was red, until he sat on the pulpit. A man stood up and said: Where is my father? He said: In the Fire. Another stood up and said: Who is my father? He said: Your father is Hudhafah! Then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: We are pleased with God as our Lord, Islam as our religion, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as our Prophet, and the Qur’an as our Imam. O Messenger of God, we are recent converts from ignorance and polytheism, and God knows who our fathers were! His anger subsided, and the verse was revealed:
h
O you who have believed
, do not ask about things which, if made known to you, will distress you.

x: Others said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of a question from a questioner who asked him about something related to the Hajj.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Mansur bin Wardan Al-Asadi told us, he said: Ali bin Abdul A’la told us:
m: When this verse was revealed: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses
r
(Al Imran 3:97)

, they said: O Messenger of God, is it every year? He was silent. Then they said: Is it every year? He was silent. Then he said: No, and if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory! Then God revealed this verse:
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you. Abu Kuraib narrated that Abd al-Raheem ibn Sulayman narrated on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri on the authority of Abu Ayyad on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has prescribed Hajj for you. A man said: Is it every year, O Messenger of God? He turned away from him until he came back two or three times. Then he said: Who is the questioner? He said: So-and-so. He said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory. If it were obligatory for you, you would not have been able to do it, and if you left it, you would have disbelieved.” Then God revealed this verse:
h
O you who have believed
, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you, until the end of the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told me,
m: he heard my father say, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, he said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us and said: O people, God has prescribed Hajj for you. Then Muhsin Al-Asadi stood up and said: Every year, O Messenger of God? He said: If I had said yes, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory and then you abandoned it, you would have gone astray. Be silent about me as I have been silent about you, for those who came before you were destroyed because of their questions and their disagreements with their prophets! Then God, the Most High, revealed:
h
O you who have believed
, do not ask about things which, if they are made clear to you, may distress you, to the end of the verse.
b.via: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, who said:
m: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a sermon, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Then Ukasha bin Muhsin Al-Asadi stood up.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abaan Al-Masri narrated to us, Abu Zaid Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Ghamr narrated to us, Abu Mutee Muawiyah bin Yahya narrated to us, on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, who said: Salim bin Aamer narrated to me,
m: who said: I heard Abu Umamah Al-Bahili say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among the people and said: Hajj has been prescribed for you! A Bedouin man stood up and said: Every year? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped talking and became silent, and became angry. He remained silent for a long time, then he spoke and said: Who is the questioner? The Bedouin said: I am! He said: Woe to you! What assures you that I will not say yes! If I said yes, it would be obligatory, and if it were obligatory, you would disbelieve! Indeed, those who came before you were destroyed by the leaders of hardship. By God, if I were to make lawful for you everything on earth and prohibit for you a small spot of it, you would fall into it! He said: Then God, the Most High, revealed:
h
O you who have believed
, do not ask about things, to the end of the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you. That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people and said: O my people, Hajj has been prescribed for you! A man from Banu Asad stood up and said: O Messenger of God, is it every year? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became very angry and said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory you would not have been able to do it, and then you would have disbelieved. So leave me as I have left you, so if I command you to do something, do it, and if I forbid you from something, refrain from it! Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed:
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you. He forbade them from asking about something like what the Christians asked from the table, and because of that they became disbelievers. God Almighty forbade that and said: Do not ask about things that if the Qur’an is revealed in a harsh manner, it will upset you. Rather, wait, and when the Qur’an is revealed, you will not ask about anything except that you will find its clarification.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, he said, Ali bin Abi Talha told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you. But if you ask about them when the Qur’an is being revealed, they will be shown to you,” he said: When the verse about Hajj was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to the people and said: O people, God has prescribed Hajj for you, so perform Hajj. They said: O Messenger of God, once a year or every year? He said: No, rather once a year. If I had said every year, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory, you would have disbelieved. Then God, the Most High, said:
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you, he said: They asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about some things, so he admonished them and they stopped.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned Hajj, and it was said: Is it obligatory, O Messenger of God, every year? He said: No, if I said it would be obligatory, and if it were obligatory you would not be able to do it, and if you were not able to do it you would disbelieve. Then he said: Ask me, for no man in this gathering of mine asks me about anything except that I will tell him, even Surat al-Ma’idah 5:101
h
O you who have believed

, do not ask about things which, if they are made clear to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you. Allah has pardoned them, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Forbearing. if he asks me about his father! A man stood up and said: Who is my father? He said: Your father is Hudhafah ibn Qays. Then Umar stood up and said: O Messenger of God, we are pleased with God as our Lord, with Islam as our religion, and with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as our Prophet, and we seek refuge in God from His wrath and the wrath of His Messenger.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed because they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the bahīrah, the sa’ibah, the wasīlah, and the hami.
Who said that?

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me, he said, Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Do not ask about things, he said: They are Al-Bahira, Al-Sa’ibah, Al-Wasilah, and Al-Hami. Don’t you see that he says after that: God has not made such and such? He said: As for Ikrimah, he said: They used to ask him about the signs, but they were forbidden from doing so.
